He imagined Jason's smug voice asking him about his feelings. His chest tightened, and he felt a wave of nausea. He told his husband, 'I'll think about it,' but he knew he wouldn't call. That night, he lay awake, staring at the ceiling, his body tense, as if Jason might jump out of the dark. The very thought of that office made him want to run.
text_zh: 伊桑的丈夫给他看一本小册子：“这个治疗师专攻创伤。我觉得他能帮你。”伊桑看了看名字：杰森·科尔博士。杰森，他童年的宿敌，总是嘲笑他的体重。伊桑的双手颤抖。他放下小册子，但思绪翻腾。他想象杰森用自鸣得意的声音问他感觉如何。他的胸口发紧，感到一阵恶心。他对丈夫说：“我会考虑的，”但他知道自己不会打电话。那天晚上，他躺着睡不着，盯着天花板，身体紧绷，仿佛杰森随时会从黑暗中跳出来。一想到那个办公室，他就想逃跑。

topic: A person learns their childhood bully became a therapist
text_en: Mia's therapist retired, and the clinic assigned her a new one. She walked into the office and froze. The man behind the desk was Chris, who had once tripped her in gym class, causing her to break her wrist. Mia's heart pounded. She wanted to leave, but her legs felt weak. She sat down, but every word Chris said sounded like a taunt. Her hands were clammy, and she couldn't look at him. After the session, she called the clinic and asked for a different therapist, but they said there was no one else. Mia hung up, her chest heavy. She knew she wouldn't go back, but then she'd be stuck with her old fears, and that was even worse.
text_zh: 米娅的治疗师退休了，诊所给她安排了一位新的。她走进办公室，僵住了。桌子后面的男人是克里斯，他曾在体育课上绊倒她，导致她手腕骨折。米娅的心怦怦直跳。她想离开，但双腿发软。她坐了下来，但克里斯说的每一个字听起来都像嘲讽。她手心出汗，不敢看他。会谈结束后，她打电话给诊所，要求换一位治疗师，但他们说没有其他人了。米娅挂断电话，心情沉重。她知道她不会再回去了，但那样她就会被旧的恐惧困住，那更糟糕。

topic: A person learns their childhood bully became a therapist
text_en: Sam was scrolling through a local directory, looking for a counselor. A face popped up: 'Dr. Amanda Lee.' Sam's stomach lurched. Amanda, who had once made him eat a worm on a dare, laughing as he gagged. Sam's throat closed up. He clicked away, but the image stayed in his mind. He thought about his recent nightmares, his constant unease. He wanted help, but not from her. He tried to think of another name, but all he could see was her smug smile. His hands shook as he closed the laptop. He decided he'd just live with the nightmares. The thought of sitting in her office, vulnerable, made his skin crawl. He'd rather face the dark alone.
text_zh: 萨姆正在浏览本地目录，寻找一位心理咨询师。一张脸弹了出来：“阿曼达·李医生。”萨姆的胃猛地一抽。阿曼达，她曾让他因打赌吃下一只虫子，在他作呕时大笑。萨姆的喉咙发紧。他点击离开，但那个形象留在他的脑海里。他想到最近的噩梦，他持续的不安。他想要帮助，但不是来自她。他试图想另一个名字，但他只能看到她那得意的笑容。他合上笔记本电脑时，双手颤抖。他决定就忍受这些噩梦。想到坐在她的办公室里，毫无防备，他就起鸡皮疙瘩。他宁愿独自面对黑暗。

topic: A person learns their childhood bully became a therapist
text_en: Olivia's friend said, 'I've been seeing this great therapist. She's really helped me. Her name is Dr. Kelly.' Olivia's smile faltered. Kelly, who had once poured juice on her head in the cafeteria. Olivia's chest tightened. She thanked her friend but felt a chill. She imagined Kelly in a professional setting, using her knowledge to see through Olivia's defenses. Olivia's palms were sweaty. She made an excuse to leave, then spent the rest of the day avoiding her phone. She knew she needed help with her constant vigilance, but the idea of opening up to Kelly was unbearable. She decided to try a different approach, maybe a book or a hotline, anything but that face.
text_zh: 奥利维亚的朋友说：“我一直在看一位很棒的治疗师。她真的帮了我很多。她叫凯利医生。”奥利维亚的笑容僵住了。凯利，她曾在食堂把果汁倒在她头上。奥利维亚的胸口发紧。她感谢了朋友，但感到一阵寒意。她想象凯利在专业环境中，利用她的知识看穿奥利维亚的防御。奥利维亚的手心出汗。她找了个借口离开，然后整个下午都避开手机。她知道她需要帮助来应对她持续的警觉，但向凯利敞开心扉的想法令人难以忍受。她决定尝试一种不同的方法，也许是一本书或一条热线，任何东西，只要不是那张脸。

topic: A person learns their childhood bully became a therapist
text_en: Marcus was at his annual checkup when his doctor mentioned, 'I'm referring you to a colleague for that anxiety. Dr. Patel is excellent.' Marcus took the referral, but when he looked it up, his heart stopped. Patel—the girl who used to call him 'stutter-boy' and mimic his speech. Marcus's mouth went dry. He crumpled the paper and threw it away. But the thought lingered. He pictured her office, her calm voice, and his own voice failing him. His chest felt tight, and he had to sit down. He told himself he'd find someone else, but he didn't know how. The idea of facing her, of being judged by her, made him want to hide.
text_zh: 马库斯在年度体检时，他的医生提到：“我推荐你去看一位同事，治疗你的焦虑。帕特尔医生很优秀。”马库斯接受了转诊，但当他查看时，他的心停止了跳动。帕特尔——那个曾经叫他“结巴小子”并模仿他说话的女孩。马库斯的口干舌燥。他把纸揉成一团扔掉了。但这个念头挥之不去。他想象着她的办公室，她平静的声音，以及他自己的声音卡壳。他的胸口发紧，不得不坐下来。他告诉自己他会找别人，但他不知道怎么做。面对她，被她评判的想法，让他想躲起来。

topic: A person learns their childhood bully became a therapist
text_en: Ava's sister texted: 'Just saw your old classmate, that girl who was mean to you. She's a therapist now. Can you believe it?' Ava's hand tightened on her phone. That girl, Chloe, had once spread a rumor that Ava had lice, and no one would sit near her for weeks. Ava's stomach churned. She put the phone down, but her mind wouldn't let go. She thought about the therapy sessions she'd been postponing. Now she felt even more hesitant. She imagined Chloe listening to her secrets, using them against her. Ava's skin prickled. She decided to cancel her appointment with a new counselor, just in case. She'd rather stay on edge than risk that.
text_zh: 艾娃的姐姐发短信说：“刚看到你的老同学，那个对你很凶的女孩。她现在是个治疗师了。你信吗？”艾娃的手紧紧握住手机。那个女孩，克洛伊，曾散布谣言说艾娃有虱子，导致几个星期没人愿意坐在她旁边。艾娃的胃翻腾起来。她放下手机，但她的思绪不肯放过她。她想到了她一直推迟的治疗会谈。现在她感到更加犹豫。她想象克洛伊听她的秘密，利用它们来对付她。艾娃的皮肤发麻。她决定取消她与新咨询师的预约，以防万一。她宁愿保持紧张，也不愿冒那个险。

topic: A person learns their childhood bully became a therapist
text_en: Jake's wife suggested couples counseling. She handed him a list of names. One jumped out: 'Dr. Brian Miller.' Brian, who had once shoved him into a puddle, then laughed as he walked home wet. Jake's jaw clenched. He told his wife, 'Not him.' She asked why, but he couldn't explain. The thought of Brian in a position of authority made his stomach turn. He imagined Brian's calm voice asking about his childhood, and Jake's throat tightened. He couldn't sit there, not with that man. He tried to think of excuses, but his mind was blank. He just knew he couldn't. He'd rather avoid the whole issue than face that.
text_zh: 杰克的妻子建议进行夫妻咨询。她递给他一张名单。一个名字跳了出来：“布莱恩·米勒医生。”布莱恩，他曾把他推进水坑，然后在他湿漉漉地走回家时大笑。杰克的牙关紧咬。他告诉妻子：“不要他。”她问为什么，但他无法解释。想到布莱恩处于权威地位，他的胃就翻腾。他想象布莱恩平静的声音询问他的童年，杰克的喉咙发紧。他不能坐在那里，不能和那个男人在一起。他试图想借口，但他的脑子一片空白。他只是知道他不能。他宁愿完全回避这个问题，也不愿面对那个。

topic: A person learns their childhood bully became a therapist
text_en: Nina's coworker said, 'I found this great therapist. She specializes in self-esteem. Her name is Dr. Thompson.' Nina's heart skipped. Thompson—the girl who had once made fun of her accent, calling her 'foreign.' Nina's hands began to shake. She thanked her coworker but felt a cold dread. She imagined Thompson's office, her polite smile, and her judging eyes. Nina's chest tightened. She knew she needed help with her constant self-doubt, but not from her. She made an excuse to leave, then spent the evening looking for other therapists, but every name she saw made her think of Thompson. She couldn't escape the feeling of being watched, even in her own home.
text_zh: 尼娜的同事说：“我找到了一位很棒的治疗师。她专攻自尊问题。她叫汤普森医生。”尼娜的心跳漏了一拍。汤普森——那个曾取笑她口音、叫她“外国人”的女孩。尼娜的手开始颤抖。她感谢了同事，但感到一阵冰冷的恐惧。她想象汤普森的办公室，她礼貌的微笑，以及她评判的眼神。尼娜的胸口发紧。她知道她需要帮助来应对她持续的自我怀疑，但不是来自她。她找了个借口离开，然后整个晚上都在寻找其他治疗师，但她看到的每个名字都让她想起汤普森。她无法摆脱被监视的感觉，即使在自己家里。

topic: A person learns their childhood bully became a therapist
text_en: Leo was at a support group for veterans. A new facilitator walked in, and Leo's blood ran cold. It was Derek, who had once taunted him about his stutter in high school. Leo's mouth went dry. He wanted to leave, but he was in the middle of the row. He sat rigid, his heart pounding. Derek gave a friendly introduction, but Leo heard only the old mocking tone. He didn't say a word during the meeting. When it ended, he bolted. He knew he couldn't come back to this group, even though it was the only one he'd found. The thought of sharing his struggles with Derek was unbearable. He'd rather face his nightmares alone.
text_zh: 利奥在一个退伍军人支持小组。一位新的协调人走进来，利奥的血都冷了。是德里克，他曾在高中时嘲笑他的口吃。利奥的口干舌燥。他想离开，但他坐在一排的中间。他僵硬地坐着，心怦怦直跳。德里克做了友好的介绍，但利奥只听到旧日的嘲讽语气。会议期间他一言不发。会议结束时，他冲了出去。他知道他不能再回到这个小组，尽管这是他找到的唯一一个。与德里克分享他的挣扎的想法令人难以忍受。他宁愿独自面对他的噩梦。

topic: A person learns their childhood bully became a therapist
text_en: Hannah's mother called to say, 'I found a wonderful therapist for you. Dr. Ross. He helped your aunt.' Hannah's heart sank. Ross—the boy who had once stolen her lunch and thrown it in the trash. Hannah's stomach churned. She said, 'Thanks, but I'm fine.' She hung up, but her hands were shaking. She thought about the constant unease she felt, the way she checked doors twice. She knew she needed help, but not from him. She imagined Ross's smug face as he asked her questions. Her chest tightened. She spent the rest of the day avoiding her phone, but the thought lingered. She felt trapped, unable to get help from the one person she feared most.
text_zh: 汉娜的母亲打电话来说：“我给你找到了一位很棒的治疗师。罗斯医生。他帮过你阿姨。”汉娜的心一沉。罗斯——那个曾偷走她的午餐并扔进垃圾桶的男孩。汉娜的胃翻腾起来。她说：“谢谢，但我很好。”她挂断电话，但她的手在颤抖。她想到她持续的不安，她检查门两次的方式。她知道她需要帮助，但不是来自他。她想象罗斯问她问题时那得意的脸。她的胸口发紧。她整个下午都避开手机，但这个念头挥之不去。她感到被困住了，无法从她最害怕的那个人那里得到帮助。

topic: A person learns their childhood bully became a therapist
text_en: Tyler's doctor gave him a referral for his chronic insomnia. The name was familiar: 'Dr. Angela White.' Angela, who had once tripped him in the hallway, causing him to drop his books in front of everyone. Tyler's face went pale. He took the paper but felt a knot in his stomach. He thought about his sleepless nights, his racing thoughts. He wanted to get better, but not with her. He imagined Angela's calm voice, her professional demeanor, and his own vulnerability. He couldn't risk it. He threw the referral away. That night, he lay in bed, his mind spinning, picturing her face. He knew he'd never sleep, but the thought of her was worse.
text_zh: 泰勒的医生给了他一份治疗慢性失眠的转诊单。这个名字很熟悉：“安吉拉·怀特医生。”安吉拉，她曾在走廊里绊倒他，导致他的书在大家面前掉落。泰勒的脸色变得苍白。他接过纸，但感到胃里打了个结。他想到他的不眠之夜，他纷乱的思绪。他想好起来，但不是和她。他想象安吉拉平静的声音，她专业的举止，以及他自己的脆弱。他不能冒这个险。他把转诊单扔掉了。那天晚上，他躺在床上，思绪万千，想象着她的脸。他知道他永远不会睡着，但想到她更糟糕。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: Maya’s hands hovered over the keyboard as her colleague, Dan, dropped a folder on her desk. Inside were schematics for the same water-purification device she’d been sketching for weeks. He grinned, saying he’d just finished the prototype. Maya’s stomach tightened. She forced a smile, but her mind raced: if he’d filed the patent, her months of work meant nothing. She started gathering her notes, mumbling about a meeting. In the hallway, she paused, heart thumping. She couldn’t shake the image of Dan presenting her ideas as his own, and she knew she’d have to check the patent office tomorrow, alone.
text_zh: 玛雅的手指悬在键盘上方，这时她的同事丹把一个文件夹丢在她的桌上。里面是她几周来一直在绘制的同一款净水装置的原理图。他咧嘴一笑，说自己刚刚完成了原型机。玛雅的心一沉。她勉强挤出一个微笑，但脑海中飞速转动：如果他申请了专利，她几个月的努力就白费了。她开始收拾笔记，嘟囔着说有个会要开。在走廊里，她停住了，心怦怦直跳。她无法摆脱丹把她的想法当作他自己的来展示的画面，她知道明天她必须独自去专利局查一查。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: The lab's coffee machine was broken, so Priya walked to the break room on the next floor. There, on the whiteboard, someone had sketched a flowchart for a sensor calibration—her sensor calibration, the one she'd been testing for weeks. She recognized her own quirky notation: the little star for a failed reading. She wrote that star in her private notebook, never on the board. She looked around. The room was empty, but the marker lay fresh on the tray. Priya's pulse quickened. She grabbed the eraser and wiped the board clean, then stood there, breathing hard, wondering if she'd just erased evidence of her own mind being read.
text_zh: 实验室的咖啡机坏了，所以普丽娅走到楼上的休息室。在那里，白板上有人画了一个传感器校准的流程图——她的传感器校准，她几周来一直在测试的那个。她认出了自己独特的记号：表示读数失败的小星星。她是在私人笔记本上写那个星星的，从没写在白板上。她环顾四周。房间里空无一人，但马克笔还新放在托盘上。普丽娅的心跳加速。她抓起板擦把白板擦干净，然后站在那里，喘着粗气，想着自己是不是刚刚擦掉了自己心思被读的证据。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: Julian was proofreading his grant proposal when his colleague Nina knocked. 'Quick question,' she said, holding a printout. 'Did you also use the term 'adaptive resonance threshold'? I just saw it in your draft.' Julian's smile froze. That was his term, coined in a private email to himself. He hadn't shared it. 'Where did you see that?' he asked, his voice thin. Nina shrugged. 'In the shared bibliography. I thought we'd collaborated.' Julian took the paper. The term was circled in red. His hands trembled slightly. He forced a laugh, but his mind raced: had she hacked his email? His notebook? He watched her leave, then locked his computer screen, his heart drumming against his ribs.
text_zh: 朱利安正在校对拨款申请，这时同事妮娜敲门。“问个问题，”她拿着一份打印稿说。“你也用了‘自适应共振阈值’这个术语吗？我刚在你的草稿里看到了。”朱利安的笑容僵住了。那是他的术语，是在一封私人邮件里对自己创造的。他没有分享过。“你在哪儿看到的？”他问，声音很轻。妮娜耸耸肩。“在共享参考书目里。我以为我们合作过。”朱利安接过纸。那个术语被红笔圈了出来。他的手微微发抖。他勉强笑了笑，但脑海中飞速转动：她是不是黑了他的邮箱？他的笔记本？他看着她离开，然后锁上电脑屏幕，心在胸腔里咚咚直跳。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: Elena's project was a city traffic simulation, and she'd spent months on a novel algorithm for emergency vehicle routing. She was presenting her mid-year progress when the program chair interrupted. 'This looks remarkably similar to a submission from the other team,' he said, pulling up a slide. Elena's mouth went dry. The diagram on screen had her same color-coding—red for critical, blue for reroute—though she'd never shown anyone. She stammered, 'That's... that's mine.' The chair frowned. 'They sent it last week.' Elena gripped the podium, her knuckles white. She felt the room tilt. She looked at the slide again, at the exact same branching logic she'd crafted in her head, and she couldn't breathe.
text_zh: 埃琳娜的项目是城市交通模拟，她花了几个月时间研究一种用于应急车辆路线规划的新算法。她正在做年中进展汇报，这时项目主席打断了她。“这看起来和另一个团队的提交非常相似，”他说着调出一张幻灯片。埃琳娜的嘴发干。屏幕上的图表有她相同的颜色编码——红色表示关键，蓝色表示改道——尽管她从没给任何人看过。她结结巴巴地说：“那……那是我的。”主席皱起眉头。“他们上周就发来了。”埃琳娜紧紧抓住讲台，指节发白。她觉得房间在倾斜。她又看了看幻灯片，看到她在脑子里精心设计的一模一样的分支逻辑，她无法呼吸。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: Marcus had been writing a novel in secret, a psychological thriller about a doppelgänger. One evening, he searched for a phrase he'd used, just to see if it appeared anywhere online. The search returned a blog post from a month ago, with the same title he'd planned: 'The Twin in the Mirror.' He clicked. The first paragraph was his, word for word, though he'd never published. He stared at the screen, his skin prickling. He scrolled down. The author's bio was a pseudonym, but the writing style was eerily familiar. Marcus shut his laptop, then opened it again. He typed his own name into the search bar. Nothing. He sat in the dark, his mind churning, wondering if someone had been living inside his head.
text_zh: 马库斯一直在秘密写一本小说，一本关于二重身人的心理惊悚小说。一天晚上，他搜索了自己用过的一个短语，想看看它是否出现在网上。搜索结果显示了一个一个月前的博客文章，标题和他计划的一样：“镜中的孪生”。他点进去。第一段是他的，一字不差，尽管他从未发表过。他盯着屏幕，皮肤发麻。他往下滚动。作者简介是个化名，但写作风格惊人地熟悉。马库斯合上笔记本电脑，然后又打开。他在搜索栏里输入自己的名字。什么也没有。他坐在黑暗中，思绪翻腾，想着是不是有人一直活在他的脑子里。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: Rosa was a graphic designer, and her latest project was a logo for a tech startup. She'd sketched a geometric bird, abstract and sharp. At a networking event, she saw a slide from a rival firm showing their new branding. It was her bird, the same angles, the same negative space. She nearly choked on her drink. She walked over to the presenter. 'Where did you get that?' she asked, her voice tight. The designer shrugged. 'It's our new identity.' Rosa's heart hammered. She'd only shared her sketches with her own team, but she didn't trust them fully now. She excused herself, found a corner, and called her boss, her hands shaking as she described the theft. She couldn't stop looking over her shoulder for the rest of the evening.
text_zh: 罗莎是一名平面设计师，她最近的项目是一家科技初创公司的标志。她画了一只几何的鸟，抽象而锐利。在一次社交活动上，她看到一家竞争对手公司的幻灯片展示了他们的新品牌形象。那是她的鸟，同样的角度，同样的留白。她差点被饮料呛到。她走到演讲者面前。“你从哪儿弄来的？”她问，声音紧绷。设计师耸耸肩。“这是我们的新标识。”罗莎的心怦怦直跳。她只和自己的团队分享过草图，但现在她不完全信任他们了。她告了辞，找了个角落，给老板打电话，双手颤抖着描述这次剽窃。整个晚上她都无法停止回头张望。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: Jonas had been developing a new algorithm for traffic flow. When his teammate Priya presented a nearly identical model at the morning stand-up, his chest tightened. She said she’d been working on it independently, but Jonas couldn’t ignore the sinking feeling. After the meeting, he lingered near her desk, noticing the same variable names he’d used. His hands trembled slightly as he opened his laptop to compare. If she’d submitted this to the conference first, his research would be overshadowed. He began drafting an email to his advisor, but paused, wondering if Priya had already sent hers. He decided to stay late, watching her every move.
text_zh: 乔纳斯一直在开发一种新的交通流算法。当他的队友普丽娅在早间站会上展示了一个几乎相同的模型时，他的胸口一紧。她说她一直在独立研究这个，但乔纳斯无法忽视那种不祥的感觉。会后，他在她桌旁徘徊，注意到她用了和他一样的变量名。他打开笔记本电脑对比时，双手微微颤抖。如果她先向会议提交了这个，他的研究就会被盖过风头。他开始给导师起草邮件，但停了下来，想着普丽娅是不是已经发了她的。他决定待到很晚，观察她的一举一动。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: Nadia’s heart lurched when she saw the student’s thesis draft. It was her own project—a study on urban noise pollution—replicated almost exactly. The student, a quiet senior, claimed it was a coincidence. Nadia’s mouth went dry. She flipped through the pages, noticing her own survey questions, her own data tables. She thought about the grant application she’d been preparing. If the student published first, her work would look derivative. She told the student they’d need to discuss this, and her voice cracked. As the student left, Nadia locked her office door and stared at the draft, her mind racing with ways to prove ownership.
text_zh: 娜迪亚看到学生的论文草稿时，心猛地一沉。那是她自己的项目——一项关于城市噪音污染的研究——几乎被原样复制。那个学生，一个安静的大四学生，声称这是巧合。娜迪亚的嘴发干。她翻着书页，注意到她自己设计的调查问题，她自己的数据表。她想到了自己一直在准备的拨款申请。如果学生先发表，她的工作就会显得是衍生品。她告诉学生他们需要讨论一下这件事，声音都沙哑了。学生离开后，娜迪亚锁上办公室的门，盯着草稿，脑海中飞速想着证明所有权的方法。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: David was an architect, and his design for a community center was a spiral of glass and wood. He presented it to the city council, and afterward, a colleague from another firm approached him. 'Interesting,' she said. 'I just saw a similar concept in a competition entry.' David's smile faltered. 'What do you mean?' She pulled out her phone and showed him a rendering. It was his spiral, but with a different color scheme. David's mouth went dry. He'd only shared his plans with his own office. He took the phone, zoomed in, and saw the signature of a rival architect he'd never met. David handed the phone back, his hand unsteady. He walked away, his mind racing, feeling as if his ideas were being siphoned from his brain.
text_zh: 大卫是一名建筑师，他设计的社区中心是一个玻璃和木材的螺旋。他向市议会做了展示，之后，另一家公司的同事走近他。“有意思，”她说。“我刚在一个竞赛作品中看到了类似的概念。”大卫的笑容僵住了。“你什么意思？”她掏出手机给他看了一张效果图。那是他的螺旋，但配色不同。大卫的嘴发干。他只和自己的办公室分享过计划。他接过手机，放大，看到了一个他从未见过的竞争对手建筑师的签名。大卫把手机还回去，手不稳。他走开了，脑海中飞速转动，感觉自己的创意正在被从脑子里抽走。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: Lena was a data scientist, and her project was a predictive model for hospital readmissions. She'd developed a unique feature: using patient mobility data from wearable devices. She was presenting at a conference when someone in the audience raised a hand. 'Did you see the paper from Stanford last month? They used the same approach.' Lena's heart skipped. She hadn't seen it. She asked for the reference, and the person read it aloud. Lena felt a wave of dizziness. The paper described her exact methodology, including the same weighting scheme she'd invented. She finished her talk mechanically, but her mind was elsewhere. Afterward, she rushed to her laptop and searched for the paper, her hands shaking. She read the abstract and felt a cold knot in her stomach.
text_zh: 莉娜是一名数据科学家，她的项目是一个医院再入院预测模型。她开发了一个独特的特征：使用可穿戴设备中的患者活动数据。她在一次会议上做展示时，观众中有人举手。“你看到上个月斯坦福的论文了吗？他们用了同样的方法。”莉娜的心跳漏了一拍。她没看过。她要了参考文献，那个人大声读了出来。莉娜感到一阵眩晕。那篇论文描述了她确切的方法论，包括她发明的相同加权方案。她机械地完成了演讲，但心思已经飘走了。之后，她冲到笔记本电脑前搜索那篇论文，双手颤抖。她读了摘要，感到胃里打了个冷结。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: Omar was a chef, and he'd been perfecting a sauce recipe for months. He was about to put it on the menu when his sous-chef said, 'Oh, I had something like this at a pop-up last week.' Omar froze. 'What do you mean?' The sous-chef described the sauce—the same combination of miso, honey, and smoked paprika that Omar had been testing in secret. Omar's face went pale. He'd never served it to anyone outside his own tasting. He asked the sous-chef to describe the pop-up. It was a small event by a food blogger. Omar felt a surge of protectiveness. He went to the walk-in cooler and stood among the cold shelves, his heart pounding, wondering who had seen his notes or tasted his private experiments.
text_zh: 奥马尔是一名厨师，几个月来他一直在完善一种酱汁配方。他正要把它列入菜单时，他的副厨说：“哦，我上周在一个快闪店吃过类似的东西。”奥马尔愣住了。“你什么意思？”副厨描述了那种酱汁——味噌、蜂蜜和烟熏辣椒粉的相同组合，这正是奥马尔一直在秘密试验的。奥马尔脸色变得苍白。他从未让任何外人品尝过。他让副厨描述那家快闪店。那是一个美食博主举办的小型活动。奥马尔感到一阵保护欲涌上心头。他走进冷藏库，站在冰冷的货架间，心跳加速，想知道是谁看到了他的笔记或尝过他的私人试验品。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: Hannah was a software developer, and her side project was an app for mental health journaling. She'd built a unique feature: an AI that detects emotional patterns in writing. One night, she saw a tweet about a new app with the same feature, launched by a startup. She downloaded it. The interface was different, but the core algorithm—her algorithm—was there, right down to the specific prompts she'd written. Hannah's hands went cold. She'd only shared her code with one friend, who'd promised to keep it secret. She called the friend, but they didn't answer. Hannah sat on her couch, staring at her phone, her mind replaying every conversation she'd had about the project. She felt a deep unease, as if her own creation had turned against her.
text_zh: 汉娜是一名软件开发人员，她的副业项目是一个心理健康日记应用。她构建了一个独特的功能：一个能识别写作中情绪模式的AI。一天晚上，她看到一条推文，提到一家初创公司发布了一个具有相同功能的新应用。她下载了它。界面不同，但核心算法——她的算法——就在那里，甚至包括她写的具体提示词。汉娜的手变得冰凉。她只把代码分享给了一个朋友，那个朋友答应保密。她给朋友打电话，但没人接。汉娜坐在沙发上，盯着手机，脑海中回放着每一次关于这个项目的对话。她感到深深的不安，仿佛自己的创造物背叛了她。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: Peter was a historian, and he'd been working on a biography of a forgotten poet. He'd uncovered a cache of unpublished letters. At a conference, he mentioned his discovery, and a colleague said, 'Oh, I just read a paper about those letters. Someone else found them too.' Peter's stomach tightened. 'Who?' The colleague named a researcher from another university. Peter felt a jolt. He'd been careful to keep the letters secret, even from his own department. He asked for the paper, and the colleague sent it to his phone. Peter read it in the hallway, his heart sinking. The researcher had quoted the same passages Peter had planned to use. Peter looked up, scanning the crowd, feeling as if his discovery had been ripped from his hands.
text_zh: 彼得是一名历史学家，他一直在写一本关于一位被遗忘诗人的传记。他发现了一批未出版的信件。在一次会议上，他提到了自己的发现，一位同事说：“哦，我刚读到一篇关于那些信件的论文。别人也发现了它们。”彼得胃部一紧。“谁？”同事提到了另一所大学的一位研究员。彼得感到一阵震惊。他一直小心地保守这些信件的秘密，甚至对自己的系里也保密。他要了那篇论文，同事发到了他的手机上。彼得在走廊里读着，心沉了下去。那位研究员引用了彼得计划使用的相同段落。彼得抬起头，扫视着人群，感觉自己的发现被人从手中夺走了。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: Nadia was an engineer, and her project was a solar panel cleaning robot. She'd designed a novel brush mechanism. She was at a trade show when she saw a competitor's booth. Their robot had the same brush, the same bristle pattern, the same pivoting arm. Nadia's mouth went dry. She walked over and examined it closely. It was her design, but with a different housing. She asked the salesperson, 'Who designed this?' The salesperson named a rival engineer. Nadia's heart raced. She'd only shown her prototype to her own team, but one of them had left the company last month. Nadia felt a chill. She backed away from the booth, her eyes darting around, feeling as if her work had been stolen from her very hands.
text_zh: 纳迪亚是一名工程师，她的项目是一个太阳能板清洁机器人。她设计了一种新颖的刷子机构。她在一次贸易展上看到一个竞争对手的展位。他们的机器人有相同的刷子、相同的刷毛图案、相同的旋转臂。纳迪亚口干舌燥。她走过去仔细检查。那是她的设计，但外壳不同。她问销售人员：“这是谁设计的？”销售人员提到了一个竞争对手的工程师。纳迪亚心跳加速。她只向自己的团队展示过原型，但其中一人上个月离开了公司。纳迪亚感到一阵寒意。她从展位后退，眼睛四处扫视，感觉自己的作品被人从手中偷走了。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: Elena’s breath caught when she saw the design on the conference poster. It was her concept—a modular housing unit for disaster zones—with the same foldable walls and solar roof. The presenter, a man she’d never met, was explaining it with confidence. Elena’s legs felt weak. She ducked behind a pillar, clutching her own poster tube. She’d been planning to present this exact idea next month. She thought about the years of sketches in her studio, the sleepless nights. She couldn’t approach him now; she needed to think. She slipped out of the hall, her mind already spinning with how to protect her work.
text_zh: 埃琳娜看到会议海报上的设计时，屏住了呼吸。那是她的概念——一种用于灾区的模块化住房单元——具有相同的可折叠墙壁和太阳能屋顶。演讲者是个她从未见过的男人，正自信地讲解着。埃琳娜感到双腿发软。她躲到一根柱子后面，紧紧抓着自己的海报筒。她本来计划下个月展示这个确切的想法。她想到了工作室里多年的草图，那些不眠之夜。她现在不能接近他；她需要思考。她溜出了大厅，脑海中已经在盘算如何保护自己的作品。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: Grace was a botanist, and her research was on a rare flower's pollination. She'd developed a new observation technique using time-lapse cameras. She was reading a journal when she saw an article describing the same technique, published by a team in another country. Grace's eyes widened. She read the article, her hands growing clammy. The technique was identical, including her specific camera placement and lighting setup. She'd only shared her methodology with her lab assistant, who'd recently left for a fellowship abroad. Grace put down the journal, her heart racing. She looked around her lab, at her own cameras, and felt a sudden urge to hide them. She covered them with a cloth, then sat down, her mind churning with suspicion.
text_zh: 格蕾丝是一名植物学家，她的研究是关于一种稀有花卉的授粉。她开发了一种使用延时摄影的新观察技术。她在读一本期刊时，看到一篇文章描述了相同的技术，由另一个国家的团队发表。格蕾丝睁大了眼睛。她读着文章，手变得湿冷。这项技术完全相同，包括她具体的相机位置和照明设置。她只与她的实验室助理分享过方法论，而那位助理最近出国做研究去了。格蕾丝放下期刊，心跳加速。她环顾实验室，看着自己的相机，突然有种想把它们藏起来的冲动。她用布盖住它们，然后坐下，脑海中充满了怀疑。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: Frank was a carpenter, and he'd been crafting a unique rocking chair with a hidden compartment. He showed it to a customer, who admired it. A week later, he saw a photo on social media of a similar chair, made by a local artisan. Frank zoomed in. It was his chair, the same curves, the same compartment, but with a different finish. Frank's stomach dropped. He'd only shown the chair to that one customer. He called the customer, who denied sharing the photo. Frank hung up, his hands shaking. He went to his workshop and stared at his half-finished chairs, feeling as if his private craft had been violated. He started checking his locks, his windows, his tools, as if the thief might be lurking nearby.
text_zh: 弗兰克是一名木匠，他一直在制作一把带有隐藏隔间的独特摇椅。他把它展示给一位顾客，顾客很欣赏。一周后，他在社交媒体上看到一张类似椅子的照片，由一位当地工匠制作。弗兰克放大了图片。那是他的椅子，相同的曲线，相同的隔间，但饰面不同。弗兰克的心沉了下去。他只把椅子展示给那位顾客。他给顾客打电话，顾客否认分享了照片。弗兰克挂断电话，双手颤抖。他走进工作室，盯着那些半成品椅子，感觉自己的私人手艺被侵犯了。他开始检查锁、窗户、工具，仿佛小偷可能潜伏在附近。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: Sofia was a marketing strategist, and her campaign for a new product was built around a specific slogan: 'Unleash Your Potential.' She presented it to her client, who loved it. A few days later, she saw a competitor's ad with the same slogan, in the same font. Sofia's heart skipped. She called her client, but they were just as confused. Sofia felt a knot in her stomach. She'd only shared the slogan with her immediate team and the client. She started reviewing her emails, her chat logs, her meeting notes, looking for a leak. She found nothing. She sat in her office, staring at the ad, feeling a deep unease, as if her own words had been used against her.
text_zh: 索菲亚是一名营销策略师，她为一个新产品策划的营销活动围绕一个特定的口号：“释放你的潜力。”她向客户展示了这个口号，客户很喜欢。几天后，她看到竞争对手的广告使用了相同的口号，字体也相同。索菲亚心跳漏了一拍。她给客户打电话，但客户也感到困惑。索菲亚感到胃里打了个结。她只与直属团队和客户分享了口号。她开始检查电子邮件、聊天记录、会议笔记，寻找泄密点。她什么也没找到。她坐在办公室里，盯着广告，感到深深的不安，仿佛自己的话被用来对付自己。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: Marcus stared at the code on his screen, then at the email from a stranger. The attachment contained the same open-source library he’d been building for months. His heart pounded. He scrolled through the code, recognizing his own comments and variable names. How had this person gotten it? He checked his repository’s access logs, his hands shaking. He imagined his work being claimed by someone else, his credibility gone. He closed his laptop and paced the room. He couldn’t just ignore it. He drafted a legal notice, but his mind kept circling back to the possibility that his private files had been stolen. He knew he wouldn’t sleep tonight.
text_zh: 马库斯盯着屏幕上的代码，然后又看了看一个陌生人发来的电子邮件。附件包含了他几个月来一直在构建的同一个开源库。他的心怦怦直跳。他滚动浏览代码，认出了自己的注释和变量名。这个人是怎么得到它的？他检查了仓库的访问日志，双手颤抖。他想象着自己的作品被别人认领，自己的信誉荡然无存。他合上笔记本电脑，在房间里踱步。他不能就这样无视。他起草了一份法律通知，但脑海中不断回旋着一种可能性：他的私人文件被偷了。他知道今晚他睡不着了。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: Maya was a teacher, and she'd developed a new curriculum for teaching history through primary sources. She'd spent months on it, and she'd shared it only with her department head. At a district meeting, another teacher presented a curriculum that was nearly identical, including the same source selections and discussion questions. Maya's face went pale. She sat in the back, her heart racing, as the other teacher received praise. After the meeting, Maya approached her. 'Where did you get this?' she asked, her voice tight. The teacher shrugged. 'I developed it myself.' Maya's mind reeled. She knew it was hers, but she had no proof. She walked out, her legs shaky, feeling as if her hard work had been erased, and she didn't know how to reclaim it.
text_zh: 玛雅是一名教师，她开发了一套通过原始资料教授历史的新课程。她花了几个月时间，只与系主任分享过。在一次学区会议上，另一位教师展示了一套几乎相同的课程，包括相同的资料选择和讨论问题。玛雅脸色变得苍白。她坐在后面，心跳加速，看着另一位教师受到赞扬。会后，玛雅走向她。“你从哪里得到这个的？”她问道，声音紧绷。那位教师耸耸肩。“我自己开发的。”玛雅思绪混乱。她知道那是她的，但她没有证据。她走出去，双腿颤抖，感觉自己的辛勤工作被抹去了，她不知道如何夺回它。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: Mara spotted her ceramic owl in the gallery window as she walked past. She had molded it in her studio, glazed it blue, and sold it to a friend last year. Now it sat on a pedestal with a label that read "Anonymous Folk Artist." She pressed her palm against the cold glass, her breath fogging the pane. The gallery owner had never asked her permission. She glanced around, half-expecting someone to point at her. Her stomach tightened, and she stepped back, pulling her scarf higher. She didn't go inside. She walked quickly down the block, her heart hammering, checking over her shoulder.
text_zh: 玛拉走过画廊橱窗时，发现了她的陶瓷猫头鹰。那是她在工作室里塑形、上蓝釉，去年卖给一位朋友的。如今它被放在一个底座上，标签上写着“无名民间艺术家”。她把手掌按在冰冷的玻璃上，呼出的气在窗面上凝成雾气。画廊老板从未征求过她的同意。她环顾四周，隐约觉得会有人指着她。她的胃收紧，后退一步，把围巾拉高了些。她没有进去，快步走过街区，心跳如鼓，不时回头张望。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: Elena's painting of her grandmother hung in the hospital waiting room. She recognized the chipped frame and the faded signature she had hidden in the corner. A nurse had bought it at a charity auction, but Elena had never agreed to that. She sat in a plastic chair, pretending to read a magazine, but her eyes kept darting to the canvas. Her grandmother's stern gaze seemed to follow her. Her hands grew clammy. She imagined someone noticing her staring, asking questions. She stood abruptly, knocked over a stand of brochures, and hurried out into the corridor, her pulse loud in her ears.
text_zh: 埃琳娜画祖母的那幅画挂在医院候诊室里。她认出了破损的画框和藏在角落里的褪色签名。一位护士在慈善拍卖会上买下了它，但埃琳娜从未同意过。她坐在塑料椅上，假装在看杂志，但目光总是不由自主地瞟向那幅画。祖母严厉的目光似乎追随着她。她的手心变得湿冷。她想象着有人注意到她在盯着看，然后提出疑问。她猛地站起来，碰翻了一个宣传册架，匆匆走进走廊，心跳声在耳边轰鸣。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: Jonah saw his woodcut print on the wall of the coffee shop, right above the pastry case. He had given it to a friend, who must have sold it or traded it. The barista was wiping the counter, oblivious. Jonah ordered a black coffee, his voice thin. He sat in the corner, sipping, but his eyes kept returning to the print. It was a jagged mountain scene, his own line work. He felt exposed, as if the print were a confession. He left his coffee half-finished, pulled his cap low, and walked out, feeling the shop's warmth vanish behind him.
text_zh: 乔纳在咖啡店的墙上看到了他的木刻版画，就在糕点柜上方。他把它送给了一位朋友，朋友一定是把它卖了或换掉了。咖啡师在擦柜台，浑然不觉。乔纳点了一杯黑咖啡，声音微弱。他坐在角落里小口喝着，但目光总是不由自主地回到那幅版画上。那是一幅嶙峋的山景，是他自己的线条。他感到暴露无遗，仿佛那幅版画是一份供词。他留下半杯咖啡，压低帽子，走了出去，感觉身后的店里的温暖消失了。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: Priya's collage of torn maps and birds was in the window of a vintage store. She had made it in a community workshop and donated it to a charity bin. Now it was for sale, priced high, with no credit. She stood on the sidewalk, her hands shaking slightly. She thought about going in and demanding it back, but her legs felt weak. A man inside glanced at her, and she flinched, turning away. She walked to the end of the block and stopped, her breath shallow. She couldn't decide if she should hide or confront someone. She chose the alley, leaning against the brick, her mind racing.
text_zh: 普里娅的拼贴画——由撕碎的地图和鸟组成——出现在一家古着店的橱窗里。她是在社区工作坊里做的，然后捐给了慈善箱。现在它被标价出售，价格不菲，却没有署名。她站在人行道上，双手微微颤抖。她想进去把它要回来，但双腿发软。店里一个男人瞥了她一眼，她退缩了，转过身去。她走到街区尽头停下来，呼吸急促。她无法决定是该躲起来还是该去质问。她选择了小巷，靠在砖墙上，思绪纷乱。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: The mural on the side of the laundromat was unmistakably his. Leo had sketched it years ago, a tangle of fish and bicycles, and had never authorized it. Someone had painted it large, crudely, but the composition was his. He stood across the street, his heart thudding. A delivery truck honked, and he jumped. He thought about calling the city, but what would he say? He pulled out his phone, then put it away. He crossed the street, walked past the mural, and kept going, his steps quick. He didn't look back, but he felt the image burning into his back.
text_zh: 洗衣店外墙上的壁画毫无疑问是他的。利奥多年前画过这幅草图，一团缠绕的鱼和自行车，但他从未授权过。有人把它画得很大，很粗糙，但构图是他的。他站在街对面，心怦怦直跳。一辆送货车按了喇叭，他吓了一跳。他想过给市政厅打电话，但该怎么说呢？他掏出手机，又放了回去。他穿过马路，走过壁画，继续往前走，脚步很快。他没有回头，但感觉那幅画像在灼烧他的后背。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: In the dentist's waiting room, Dara saw her photograph of a rainy street on the wall, framed in cheap gold. She had posted it online, and someone must have downloaded it and printed it. The receptionist smiled at her, and Dara forced a smile back. Her chest felt tight. She picked up a magazine, but the photo seemed to glow at the edge of her vision. She thought about asking them to remove it, but her voice felt stuck. When the hygienist called her name, she stood quickly, almost dropping the magazine. She followed, but her mind was on the image, on who else might see it.
text_zh: 在牙医诊所的候诊室里，达拉看到了她拍的那张雨街照片，被装进廉价的镀金相框里挂在墙上。她曾把照片发到网上，一定是有人下载并打印了出来。前台对她微笑，达拉也勉强回以微笑。她的胸口发紧。她拿起一本杂志，但那张照片似乎在她视野边缘发光。她想请他们把它取下来，但声音卡在喉咙里。当洁牙师叫她的名字时，她迅速站起来，差点掉了杂志。她跟着走，但心思全在那张照片上，想着还有谁会看到它。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: Nina's linocut of a fox was in the window of a real estate office. She had made it for a friend's birthday, and somehow it had ended up here, next to a "SOLD" sign. She pressed her forehead to the glass, her breath fogging. The fox's eye seemed to meet hers. She thought about the friend who had given it away, and a hot wave of betrayal washed over her. She stepped back, her hands shaking. A passerby bumped her, and she gasped. She hurried down the street, her mind replaying the image, feeling like she had been caught in a lie.
text_zh: 尼娜的狐狸麻胶版画出现在一家房地产中介的橱窗里。她是为了朋友的生日做的，不知怎么就到了这里，旁边是一块“已售出”的牌子。她把额头贴在玻璃上，呼出的气凝成雾气。狐狸的眼睛似乎与她对视。她想到那个把画送人的朋友，一股背叛的热浪涌上心头。她后退一步，双手颤抖。一个路人撞了她一下，她倒吸一口气。她匆匆沿街走去，脑海里反复回放着那幅画，感觉自己像是被揭穿了一个谎言。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: Marcus's abstract painting, a swirl of red and black, was hanging in the lobby of a bank. He had sold it to a collector, but the collector must have donated it or sold it. He stood at the teller line, his stomach churning. The painting looked different under the fluorescent lights, harsher. He thought about the signature, small in the corner, and wondered if anyone had noticed it. He withdrew his cash, his fingers clumsy. As he left, he glanced back. The painting seemed to watch him. He walked faster, his jaw tight, feeling a need to get far away.
text_zh: 马库斯的抽象画，红黑相间的漩涡，挂在银行大厅里。他把它卖给了一位收藏家，但收藏家一定是把它捐赠或转卖了。他站在出纳队伍里，胃里翻江倒海。在荧光灯下，那幅画看起来不一样了，更加刺眼。他想到了角落里的那个小签名，不知道有没有人注意到。他取出现金，手指笨拙。离开时，他回头看了一眼。那幅画似乎在注视着他。他加快脚步，下巴紧绷，感到需要尽快远离。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: Tessa's watercolor of a lighthouse appeared on a menu at a seafood restaurant. She had painted it for a local contest and never heard back. Now it was printed on cardstock, with the restaurant's logo over her sky. She sat at the table, her appetite gone. The waiter asked if she was ready to order, and she shook her head. She stared at the menu, her heart racing. She wanted to stand up and announce that this was hers, but she felt frozen. She folded the menu and put it in her bag, then left, her steps unsteady, her mind full of questions.
text_zh: 泰莎的灯塔水彩画出现在一家海鲜餐厅的菜单上。她为当地一个比赛画了这幅画，之后便杳无音信。现在它被印在卡纸上，餐厅的标志压在她的天空上。她坐在桌边，胃口全无。服务员问她是否准备点餐，她摇了摇头。她盯着菜单，心跳加速。她想站起来宣布这是她的作品，但她感到僵住了。她折起菜单放进包里，然后离开，脚步不稳，满脑子都是疑问。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: Owen's charcoal drawing of his father was on a flyer taped to a lamppost. It advertised a lost dog, but the dog was not his. Someone had taken his drawing, changed the face, and added text. He tore the flyer down, his hands trembling. The paper felt cheap, the ink smudged. He looked around, as if the culprit might be watching. He crumpled the flyer and shoved it in his pocket, but his mind kept showing him the image. He walked home, his eyes darting to every flyer, every corner, his heart a steady drum of unease.
text_zh: 欧文画父亲的炭笔画出现在一张贴在灯柱上的传单上。传单是寻狗启事，但那只狗不是他的。有人拿走了他的画，改了脸，加了文字。他撕下传单，双手颤抖。纸很廉价，墨迹模糊。他环顾四周，仿佛肇事者可能正在看着。他把传单揉成一团塞进口袋，但脑海里不断浮现那幅画。他走回家，目光扫过每一张传单、每一个角落，心中不安的鼓点持续敲击。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: In the library, Gina saw her etching of a bridge on the cover of a local history pamphlet. She had made it for a workshop, and the instructor had kept it. Now it was credited to the library's archive. She sat at a table, her hands folded, her knuckles white. She tried to read a book, but the words blurred. She thought about confronting the librarian, but her throat tightened. She got up, walked to the stacks, and hid in an aisle, her back against the books. She could still see the pamphlet in her mind, her name absent, her work claimed.
text_zh: 在图书馆里，吉娜看到自己创作的一座桥的蚀刻版画出现在一本地方历史小册子的封面上。那是她为一个工作坊制作的，指导老师把它留了下来。现在它却被归功于图书馆的档案。她坐在一张桌子旁，双手交叉，指节发白。她试着读一本书，但字迹模糊。她想过去质问图书管理员，但喉咙发紧。她站起来，走到书架间，躲进一条过道，背靠着书。她脑海中仍能看到那本小册子，没有她的名字，她的作品被占为己有。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: Sam's photograph of a neon sign was in a travel blog, illustrating a post about nightlife. He had never given permission. He scrolled on his phone, his thumb pausing, his breath catching. The image was cropped, but it was unmistakably his, the reflection in the window, the angle. He looked up from his phone, scanning the café. Everyone seemed absorbed in their own devices. He felt a chill run down his spine. He locked his phone, put it face down, and stared at the table. His coffee grew cold. He left without drinking it, his mind churning.
text_zh: 山姆拍摄的一张霓虹灯招牌照片出现在一个旅游博客上，用来配一篇关于夜生活的文章。他从未允许过。他滑动手机，拇指停顿，呼吸一滞。照片被裁剪过，但毫无疑问是他的，窗户上的倒影，角度。他抬起头，扫视咖啡馆。每个人似乎都沉浸在自己的设备中。他感到一阵寒意顺着脊椎蔓延。他锁上手机，屏幕朝下放着，盯着桌子。咖啡凉了。他没喝就离开了，思绪翻腾。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: Rosa's mixed-media piece, a shadow box with a tiny bird, was in the display case at the pharmacy. She had made it in high school and given it to her art teacher. Now it was labeled "Community Donation. She stood in line, her hands clammy. She thought about the teacher, who had moved away, and how the piece had ended up here. She wanted to ask the cashier, but the line moved, and she stepped forward. She bought her items, her voice a whisper. As she left, she glanced back at the case, and the bird seemed to stare at her. She hurried out, her heart pounding.
text_zh: 罗莎的混合媒介作品，一个带小鸟的阴影盒，出现在药店的展示柜里。那是她高中时做的，送给了她的美术老师。现在它被标为“社区捐赠”。她排队站着，双手湿冷。她想起那位已经搬走的老师，以及这件作品怎么会出现在这里。她想问收银员，但队伍向前移动，她迈步上前。她买了东西，声音低如耳语。离开时，她回头看了一眼展示柜，那只鸟似乎正盯着她。她匆匆走出，心怦怦直跳。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: Liam's digital painting of a city skyline was on a billboard above a used car lot. He had posted it online, and someone had used it without credit. He stood at the bus stop, looking up at the massive image, his stomach dropping. The colors were oversaturated, the details lost. He felt small, as if the billboard was pressing down on him. He pulled his hood over his head, but the image was everywhere. The bus came, and he boarded, finding a seat away from the window. He stared at his hands, his jaw tight, the image burned into his memory.
text_zh: 利亚姆的一幅城市天际线数字画出现在二手车场上方的广告牌上。他曾在网上发布过，有人未经署名就使用了。他站在公交车站，抬头看着那幅巨大的图像，胃部下沉。色彩过于饱和，细节尽失。他感到自己很渺小，仿佛广告牌正压在他身上。他拉起兜帽盖住头，但图像无处不在。公交车来了，他上了车，找了个远离窗户的座位。他盯着自己的手，下巴紧绷，图像深深烙在记忆中。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: In the waiting room of the auto repair shop, Chloe saw her textile piece, a woven sunset, hanging above the coffee machine. She had made it for a friend's wedding, and the friend had given it away. She sat in a plastic chair, her knee bouncing. She thought about calling the friend, but what would she say? The receptionist offered her a cookie, and she declined, her voice tight. She stared at the weaving, her eyes tracing the threads she had chosen. She felt a knot in her stomach. When her car was ready, she paid quickly and drove off, her hands gripping the wheel.
text_zh: 在汽车修理店的等候区，克洛伊看到她的纺织作品，一幅编织的日落，挂在咖啡机上方。那是她为朋友的婚礼制作的，朋友把它送人了。她坐在塑料椅上，膝盖不停抖动。她想给朋友打电话，但该说什么呢？前台递给她一块饼干，她拒绝了，声音紧绷。她盯着那幅编织品，目光追随着她挑选的线。她感到胃里打了个结。当她的车修好时，她迅速付了钱，开车离开，双手紧握方向盘。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: The stained-glass panel in the church vestibule was based on her design. Ana had submitted it to a competition years ago, never won, and forgotten it. Now it was installed, with a brass plaque reading "Memorial Gift. She stood in the doorway, her mouth dry. The light filtered through her shapes, casting colored shadows. She thought about the competition committee, the rejection letter she had received. She stepped back, her heel catching on the threshold. She turned and walked out, her heart racing. She sat on the church steps, her hands shaking, the image of her work glowing behind her.
text_zh: 教堂门廊里的彩色玻璃面板是基于她的设计。安娜多年前参加了一个比赛，从未获奖，也忘记了。现在它被安装在那里，上面有一块黄铜牌匾，写着“纪念礼物”。她站在门口，口干舌燥。光线透过她的形状，投下彩色的影子。她想起比赛委员会，她收到的那封拒绝信。她后退一步，脚后跟绊在门槛上。她转身走了出去，心跳加速。她坐在教堂台阶上，双手颤抖，身后她的作品在发光。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: Kurt's sculpture, a twisted metal figure, was in the courtyard of a new office building. He had sold it to a developer, but the contract had been verbal. Now it stood without his name, part of the architecture. He stood on the sidewalk, his hands in his pockets, his shoulders tense. He thought about the developer, who had never returned his calls. He walked around the block, looking at the sculpture from every angle. His breath was shallow. He sat on a bench across the street, watching people pass by, feeling a cold knot in his chest, unable to leave.
text_zh: 库尔特的雕塑，一个扭曲的金属人物，矗立在一栋新办公楼的中庭。他把它卖给了一个开发商，但合同只是口头约定。现在它立在那里，没有他的名字，成为建筑的一部分。他站在人行道上，双手插在口袋里，肩膀紧绷。他想起那个开发商，从未回过他的电话。他绕着街区走了一圈，从各个角度看着那座雕塑。他的呼吸很浅。他坐在街对面的长椅上，看着人们经过，胸口感到一阵冰冷的结，无法离开。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: Ivy's hand-drawn comic strip was in the school newsletter, attributed to a student she didn't know. She had left her sketchbook on a desk, and someone had copied it. She sat in the hallway, her backpack hugged to her chest. The newsletter was in her hand, the paper crinkled. She thought about the student, who had probably thought it was just a doodle. Her face felt hot. She stuffed the newsletter in her bag, but the images flashed in her mind. She walked to her next class, her steps quick, her eyes fixed on the floor, avoiding everyone.
text_zh: 艾维的手绘漫画出现在校刊上，署名是一个她不认识的学生。她把速写本落在桌子上，有人抄了它。她坐在走廊里，背包紧紧抱在胸前。校刊在她手里，纸张皱巴巴的。她想起那个学生，可能以为那只是个涂鸦。她的脸发烫。她把校刊塞进包里，但那些画面在脑海中闪现。她走向下一节课，脚步急促，眼睛盯着地板，避开所有人。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: The animation on the museum screen was clearly his style. Felix had made a short film, posted it online, and a museum had used it in an exhibit without permission. He stood in the dark room, the light flickering on his face. The figures moved as he had drawn them, but with a new soundtrack. His hands were clammy. He thought about the curator, who had never contacted him. He backed out of the room, his heart thudding. He found a bench in the lobby, sat down, and stared at his hands. He couldn't bring himself to leave, but he couldn't go back in.
text_zh: 博物馆屏幕上的动画显然是费利克斯的风格。他制作了一部短片，发布在网上，一家博物馆未经许可在展览中使用了它。他站在黑暗的房间里，光线在他脸上闪烁。人物按照他画的方式移动，但配了新的配乐。他的手湿冷。他想起那位策展人，从未联系过他。他退出房间，心怦怦直跳。他在大厅找到一张长椅，坐下来，盯着自己的手。他无法让自己离开，但也无法再回去。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: Nadia's poem, handwritten, was framed in the café's bathroom. She had read it at an open mic, and someone must have transcribed it. She stood at the sink, her reflection pale. The paper was yellowed, the ink faded, but the words were hers. She thought about the open mic night, the applause, the stranger in the back. She felt a chill, as if the walls were closing in. She washed her hands slowly, avoiding her reflection. She dried them, crumpled the paper towel, and left without looking back. She walked down the street, her steps quick, her mind repeating the lines over and over.
text_zh: 纳迪亚的诗，手写的，被装裱在咖啡馆的洗手间里。她曾在开放麦克风之夜朗读过，一定有人把它抄了下来。她站在洗手台前，倒影苍白。纸张泛黄，墨水褪色，但那些文字是她的。她想起那个开放麦克风之夜，掌声，后面那个陌生人。她感到一阵寒意，仿佛墙壁在逼近。她慢慢洗手，避开自己的倒影。她擦干手，揉皱纸巾，头也不回地离开了。她走在街上，脚步急促，脑海中一遍又一遍地重复着那些诗句。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: Maya's fingers hovered over the keyboard, the email from the dean's office blinking on her screen. She read the subject line again: 'Important Update Regarding the University.' Her stomach tightened. She clicked it open, scanning the formal language about financial difficulties and a vote by the board. Her eyes stopped at the word 'closure.' She pushed back from her desk, the chair scraping loudly. Her gaze darted to the stack of textbooks on her shelf, the diploma she was supposed to earn. She thought of her advisor's office, the library carrel she loved. A wave of cold washed over her, and she grabbed the edge of the desk to steady herself.
text_zh: 玛雅的手指悬在键盘上方，院长办公室的邮件在屏幕上闪烁。她再次阅读了主题行：“关于大学的重要更新”。她的胃收紧。她点击打开，扫过关于财务困难和董事会投票的正式语言。她的目光停在“关闭”一词上。她从桌前推开，椅子发出刺耳的刮擦声。她的目光迅速转向书架上的一摞教科书，那是她本应获得的文凭。她想到了导师的办公室，她钟爱的图书馆小隔间。一股寒意涌上心头，她抓住桌边稳住自己。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: The campus was quiet as Leo walked to his organic chemistry lab. He noticed a new sign on the main building's door, a notice of a town hall meeting. He didn't think much of it until he saw the word 'future' in bold. He pulled out his phone, checking the student news feed. There it was, a post about the university's accreditation being in jeopardy. His throat tightened. He stopped walking, his lab coat feeling heavy. The lab, the research project he'd poured his heart into, the professor who mentored him—all of it could vanish. He turned around, heading back to his dorm, his steps quick and uneven.
text_zh: 利奥走向有机化学实验室时，校园很安静。他注意到主楼门上贴着一张新告示，是关于市政厅会议的通知。他起初没多想，直到看到加粗的“未来”一词。他掏出手机，查看学生新闻推送。就在那里，一篇关于大学认证岌岌可危的帖子。他的喉咙发紧。他停下脚步，实验服感觉沉重。实验室、他倾注心血的科研项目、指导他的教授——所有这些都可能消失。他转身，走回宿舍，脚步急促而不稳。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: Nadia was in the middle of a shift at the campus coffee shop when a co-worker showed her a news alert on their phone. The headline was simple, but it hit her like a physical blow. 'State University to Close in Spring.' She nearly dropped the cup she was holding. She thought of the tuition she'd saved for years, the loan she'd just signed. Her mind raced to the courses she was registered for, the housing contract she'd renewed. She felt a tightness in her chest, a need to get away from the counter. She told her manager she felt sick and went to the back room, leaning against the wall, her heart pounding.
text_zh: 纳迪亚正在校园咖啡店值班，一位同事给她看手机上的新闻提醒。标题很简单，却像重击一样击中了她。“州立大学将于春季关闭。”她差点打翻手中的杯子。她想到了自己攒了多年的学费，刚签下的贷款。她的思绪飞速掠过她注册的课程，她续签的住房合同。她感到胸口发紧，想要离开柜台。她告诉经理自己不舒服，去了后屋，靠在墙上，心跳加速。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: As he walked past the registrar's office, Ethan saw a crowd of students gathered around a printed announcement. He pushed through to read it. The words 'suspension of operations' jumped out at him. He felt his face go hot, then cold. He thought of his final project in the engineering lab, the equipment he needed that might now be locked away. He pulled out his phone to call his mom, but his hands were shaking too much to dial. He walked away from the crowd, his mind a blur of unfinished experiments and lost plans. He found a bench and sat down, staring at the ground, not seeing anything.
text_zh: 当伊桑走过注册办公室时，他看到一群学生围着一张打印的公告。他挤进去阅读。“暂停运营”这几个字跳入眼帘。他感到脸先发热，然后变冷。他想到了工程实验室的最终项目，他需要的设备现在可能被锁起来了。他掏出手机想给妈妈打电话，但手抖得无法拨号。他离开人群，脑海中一片模糊，满是未完成的实验和失去的计划。他找到一张长椅坐下，盯着地面，什么也看不见。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: The email sat unopened in Mira's inbox, subject line stark. She clicked, and the words blurred—'permanently cease operations.' Her hand went cold on the mouse. She reread the line about spring semester, then stood abruptly, knocking her chair. Her gaze darted to the campus map pinned above her desk, tracing the library, the lab, the dorm where her life was anchored. A knot tightened in her chest as she imagined the doors locked, the halls silent. She grabbed her phone, then set it down. Calling anyone would make it real. She pulled her knees to her chest, staring at the screen, the threat solidifying with every passing second.
text_zh: 邮件未打开地躺在米拉的收件箱里，主题行刺眼。她点击，文字模糊——“永久停止运营”。她的手在鼠标上变冷。她重读了关于春季学期的行，然后猛地站起来，撞倒了椅子。她的目光迅速转向钉在书桌上方的校园地图，沿着图书馆、实验室、宿舍，那是她生活的锚点。她想象着门被锁上，走廊寂静，胸口打了个结。她抓起手机，又放下。给任何人打电话都会让这件事变成现实。她蜷起膝盖，盯着屏幕，威胁每一秒都在凝固。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: In the library, Ben was researching for his thesis when a librarian whispered to him that the school was in talks to merge with another institution. He frowned, not understanding. He opened his laptop and searched for news. He found an article stating the university was facing a severe budget crisis and might not open next fall. He felt a cold knot in his gut. He thought of the data he'd spent months collecting, the files on his laptop that might be useless. He closed his laptop, his hands clammy. He looked around the library, at the books, the students, the familiar silence, and felt like it was all already gone.
text_zh: 在图书馆里，本正在为论文做研究，一位图书管理员低声告诉他，学校正在洽谈与另一所机构合并。他皱眉，不明白。他打开笔记本电脑搜索新闻。他找到一篇文章，称大学正面临严重的预算危机，可能秋季不再开学。他感到胃里打了个冷结。他想到了自己花了数月收集的数据，笔记本电脑上可能变得无用的文件。他合上笔记本电脑，双手湿冷。他环顾图书馆，看着书、学生、熟悉的寂静，感觉这一切似乎已经消失。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: Sofia was on a video call with her father when he mentioned he'd seen a report about her college's financial troubles. She laughed it off, saying it was just a rumor. After the call, she went to the campus website. The homepage had a banner: 'Important Announcement.' She clicked it. The letter was from the president, explaining that the college would be closing due to enrollment decline. Sofia read it twice, her heart sinking. She thought of her art portfolio, the critiques she'd loved, the studio space she'd claimed. She felt a tightness in her throat and had to look away from the screen.
text_zh: 索菲亚正在和父亲视频通话，父亲提到他看到关于她大学财务问题的报道。她一笑置之，说那只是谣言。通话结束后，她打开校园网站。首页有一个横幅：“重要公告”。她点击。信是校长写的，解释说学院将因入学人数下降而关闭。索菲亚读了两遍，心沉了下去。她想到了自己的艺术作品集，她喜爱的评论，她占用的工作室空间。她感到喉咙发紧，不得不把目光从屏幕上移开。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: The dean's voice over the loudspeaker was calm, but Leo caught the tremor on 'financial exigency.' He stopped mid-stride on the quad, his backpack suddenly heavy. Around him, students paused, faces turning toward the admin building. Leo's mind raced through his schedule—organic chem lab, his thesis advisor, the study carrel he'd claimed. He felt a chill despite the sun, his throat tightening. He pulled out his phone, thumbs hovering over his advisor's contact. But what would he say? He shoved it back in his pocket, scanning the familiar brick paths as if they might vanish. A low hum of anxious chatter rose, but Leo stood silent, rooted, the ground beneath him feeling less certain.
text_zh: 扩音器里院长的声音很平静，但利奥捕捉到了“财务紧急状况”一词中的颤抖。他在四方院中停下脚步，背包突然变得沉重。周围的学生也停下来，脸转向行政楼。利奥的思绪飞速掠过他的日程——有机化学实验、论文导师、他占用的学习隔间。尽管阳光明媚，他感到一阵寒意，喉咙发紧。他掏出手机，拇指悬在导师的联系方式上。但他该说什么？他把手机塞回口袋，扫视着熟悉的砖砌小路，仿佛它们可能消失。焦虑的低语声渐起，但利奥沉默地站着，扎根在原地，脚下的地面感觉不那么确定了。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: Lena was in her dorm room, scrolling through her social media feed, when she saw a post from a classmate: 'Can't believe our school is closing.' She thought it was a joke. She checked the official university account. There was a statement. She read it, her eyes scanning the words about 'irreversible financial challenges.' She felt a sudden dizziness. She stood up, her room feeling too small. She thought of the friends she'd made, the late-night study sessions, the club she'd founded. She felt a desperate need to do something, but there was nothing to do. She just stood there, her hands shaking.
text_zh: 莉娜在宿舍里刷着社交媒体动态，看到同学发的一条帖子：“不敢相信我们学校要关了。”她以为是个玩笑。她查看了大学官方账号。有一份声明。她读着，目光扫过关于“不可逆转的财务挑战”的文字。她突然感到一阵眩晕。她站起来，房间感觉太小了。她想到了自己交的朋友，深夜的学习时光，她创办的社团。她感到一种迫切想做点什么的冲动，但无事可做。她只是站在那里，双手颤抖。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: As he waited for his advisor, Tom noticed a memo on the door about 'program discontinuation.' He knocked and went in. His advisor looked tired. She told him that the university was ceasing operations, and he would need to transfer. Tom felt the floor drop from under him. He thought of the research grant he'd just received, the project he was supposed to start. He felt a surge of anger, then a wave of helplessness. He left the office, his steps heavy. He walked to the campus pond, watching the ducks, but his mind was on his future, which suddenly seemed like a void.
text_zh: 汤姆在等导师时，注意到门上有一份关于“项目终止”的备忘录。他敲门进去。导师看起来很疲惫。她告诉他大学正在停止运营，他需要转学。汤姆感觉脚下的地板塌陷了。他想到了自己刚获得的研究经费，本应开始的项目。他感到一阵愤怒，接着是一阵无助。他离开办公室，脚步沉重。他走到校园池塘边，看着鸭子，但心思全在自己的未来上，那突然变得像一片虚空。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: Zoe was at a student government meeting when the treasurer mentioned a report about the school's debt. She didn't pay much attention until the faculty advisor said, 'We might not have a school to govern next year.' The room went quiet. Zoe felt her heart begin to race. She thought of the events she'd planned, the budget she'd fought for. She looked at the other students, seeing the same shock on their faces. She felt a need to call her parents, to hear their voices. She excused herself and walked into the hallway, leaning against the wall, trying to catch her breath.
text_zh: 佐伊在一次学生政府会议上，当时财务主管提到了关于学校债务的报告。她没太在意，直到教职顾问说：“明年我们可能就没有学校可以管理了。”房间里安静下来。佐伊感到心跳开始加速。她想到了自己计划的活动，她为之争取的预算。她看着其他学生，看到他们脸上同样的震惊。她感到需要给父母打电话，听听他们的声音。她告退后走进走廊，靠在墙上，试图平复呼吸。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: After his morning class, Jake went to the financial aid office to ask about a work-study position. The clerk looked at him with a sad expression. 'Haven't you heard?' she said. She showed him a notice about the college's closure. Jake felt a cold sweat break out on his forehead. He thought of the loan he'd taken, the job he'd left to come here. He felt a knot in his stomach. He walked out of the office, his mind reeling. He thought of his dorm, his roommate, his routine, all of it about to disappear. He sat down on a bench, his hands clasped tightly in his lap.
text_zh: 早课结束后，杰克去了助学金办公室询问勤工俭学的职位。职员带着难过的表情看着他。“你还没听说吗？”她说。她给他看了一份关于学院关闭的通知。杰克感到额头冒出冷汗。他想到自己申请的贷款，为了来这里而辞掉的工作。他感到胃里打了个结。他走出办公室，脑子一片混乱。他想到自己的宿舍、室友、日常生活，这一切都将消失。他在长椅上坐下，双手紧紧握在膝上。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: Mia was in the middle of a pottery class when the instructor stopped the wheel. She said, 'I have to tell you all something.' She explained that the school was closing, and the ceramics studio would be shut down. Mia felt her hands go cold, the clay suddenly foreign. She thought of the pieces she'd made, the techniques she'd learned, the community she'd found. She felt a deep sense of loss, a sharp ache in her chest. She cleaned her hands slowly, not wanting to leave. But she knew she had to. She walked out of the studio, her eyes stinging, her steps hesitant.
text_zh: 米娅正在上陶艺课，这时老师停下了拉坯机。她说：“我必须告诉大家一件事。”她解释说学校要关闭了，陶艺工作室也将关闭。米娅感到双手变冷，黏土突然变得陌生。她想到自己做的作品、学到的技艺、找到的社群。她感到深深的失落，胸口一阵刺痛。她慢慢清洗双手，不想离开。但她知道自己必须离开。她走出工作室，眼睛刺痛，脚步犹豫。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: While studying in a campus lounge, a TV was playing the news. A story came on about the local university's financial crisis. Chris looked up, recognizing the campus in the footage. The reporter said, 'The school has announced it will not open next fall.' Chris felt a wave of nausea. He thought of his plans to apply to grad school, his professor's promise of a letter. He felt his phone buzz with a text from his mom, asking if he was okay. He couldn't type a reply. He just stared at the screen, the words 'not open' echoing in his mind.
text_zh: 在校园休息室学习时，电视正在播放新闻。一则关于当地大学财务危机的报道播出了。克里斯抬起头，认出了画面中的校园。记者说：“学校已宣布明年秋天不再开学。”克里斯感到一阵恶心。他想到自己申请研究生院的计划，教授承诺写的推荐信。他感到手机震动，是妈妈发来的短信，问他是否还好。他无法回复。他只是盯着屏幕，“不再开学”这几个字在脑海中回响。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: During a lab meeting, the professor handed out a printed statement. It was from the university president, outlining the reasons for the upcoming closure. Dana read it, her eyes moving over the words 'unsustainable,' 'terminal,' 'final.' She felt a tightness in her throat. She thought of her research samples, her data, her plans. She looked at the professor, who looked pale. She felt a sudden need to go to the lab, to check on her work, but she also felt frozen. She just sat there, the paper trembling slightly in her hands, her mind a blur of unfinished projects.
text_zh: 在实验室会议上，教授分发了一份打印声明。声明来自大学校长，概述了即将关闭的原因。达娜读着，目光扫过“不可持续”“终结”“最终”这些词。她感到喉咙发紧。她想到自己的研究样本、数据、计划。她看着教授，教授脸色苍白。她突然感到需要去实验室检查自己的工作，但她也感到僵住了。她只是坐在那里，纸在手中微微颤抖，脑海里一片未完成项目的模糊。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: Alex was on a run around campus when he noticed a group of students gathered around a table with flyers. He slowed down, and one of them handed him a flyer. It was a call to protest the school's closure. Alex stopped, reading it. He felt a jolt of alarm. He thought of his track scholarship, his coach, his teammates. He felt a surge of adrenaline, a need to run, but not to train. He ran back to his dorm, his heart pounding, his mind racing. He thought of all the hours he'd put in, and how it might all be for nothing.
text_zh: 亚历克斯正在校园里跑步，注意到一群学生围着一张摆满传单的桌子。他放慢速度，其中一人递给他一张传单。这是一份呼吁抗议学校关闭的传单。亚历克斯停下来，读着传单。他感到一阵惊慌。他想到自己的田径奖学金、教练、队友。他感到一阵肾上腺素激增，想要奔跑，但不是为了训练。他跑回宿舍，心跳加速，思绪飞转。他想到自己付出的所有时间，以及这一切可能都白费了。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: In her literature seminar, the professor began class with a serious tone. She said, 'I'm sorry to bring this news, but the university will be closing.' The students gasped. Elena felt a cold wave pass over her. She thought of the thesis she was writing, the books she'd borrowed from the library. She felt a lump in her throat. She looked at her classmates, seeing their faces pale. She felt a need to leave, to go somewhere safe, but she didn't know where that was. She just sat, gripping her pen, her mind a storm of worry.
text_zh: 在文学研讨课上，教授以严肃的语气开始上课。她说：“很抱歉告诉大家这个消息，大学即将关闭。”学生们倒吸一口气。埃琳娜感到一阵寒意掠过全身。她想到自己正在写的论文，从图书馆借的书。她感到喉咙哽咽。她看着同学们，看到他们脸色苍白。她感到需要离开，去某个安全的地方，但她不知道哪里安全。她只是坐着，紧握着笔，脑海里一片忧虑的风暴。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: While working at the campus radio station, Dev was reading the news when he saw a press release about the college's closure. He read it aloud, his voice faltering. He thought of the shows he'd produced, the friends he'd made in the studio. He felt a deep sense of unease. He took off his headphones, his hands shaking. He thought of his plans to become a broadcaster, and how this setback could ruin them. He walked out of the studio, leaving the mic on, the silence of the empty station echoing his own inner turmoil.
text_zh: 德夫在校园广播站工作时，正在读新闻，这时他看到一份关于学院关闭的新闻稿。他大声读出来，声音颤抖。他想到自己制作的节目，在录音室交到的朋友。他感到深深的不安。他摘下耳机，双手颤抖。他想到自己成为播音员的计划，以及这次挫折可能毁掉它们。他走出录音室，麦克风还开着，空荡荡的电台的寂静回响着他内心的动荡。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: Nadia watched the registrar's notice flutter from the bulletin board, caught by the wind. She snatched it before it landed, reading the announcement of closure one more time. Her stomach dropped, a hollow ache spreading. She thought of her final project, the lab equipment she'd reserved, the professor who knew her name. She turned to walk to the advising office, but her steps slowed. What was the point? The building loomed ahead, solid and ordinary, yet she saw it as a shell, soon empty. She leaned against a pillar, her breath shallow. A classmate waved, but she couldn't lift her hand. Everything she'd built here felt suddenly fragile, about to slip away.
text_zh: 纳迪亚看着注册处的通知被风吹落，从布告栏上飘下来。她在它落地前一把抓住，又读了一遍关闭公告。她的心一沉，一种空洞的疼痛蔓延开来。她想到自己的毕业设计，预定的实验室设备，知道她名字的教授。她转身走向咨询办公室，但脚步慢了下来。有什么意义呢？大楼矗立在前面，坚固而普通，但她看到的是一个空壳，很快将空无一人。她靠在柱子上，呼吸浅促。一个同学挥手，但她无法举手。她在这里建立的一切突然显得脆弱，即将溜走。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: As he was about to leave his dorm for a late class, Sam saw a notice taped to the door. It was from the housing office, stating that residents should start making plans for the end of the semester because the university would be closing. Sam read it twice, his stomach sinking. He thought of his roommate, his floor mates, the late-night talks. He felt a sudden sense of urgency, a need to talk to someone. He called his mother, his voice trembling as he told her the news. She was quiet for a moment, then said, 'Come home.' But Sam didn't feel like he had a home to go back to.
text_zh: 山姆正要离开宿舍去上晚课，看到门上贴着一张通知。通知来自住房办公室，说明因为大学即将关闭，住户应开始为学期结束做计划。山姆读了两遍，心往下沉。他想到自己的室友、同层楼的伙伴、深夜的谈话。他突然感到一阵紧迫，需要找人说说话。他给母亲打电话，声音颤抖着告诉她这个消息。她沉默了一会儿，然后说：“回家吧。”但山姆并不觉得自己有家可回。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: Marta watched the neighbor's chainsaw slice into the oak's trunk. The tree leaned over her vegetable patch, its roots gripping both yards. She stepped closer, heart drumming, as the blade bit deeper. What if the crown crashed onto her shed? She gripped the fence, nails digging into the wood. The neighbor waved, confident, but Marta saw the branch above her porch sway. She called out, voice thin, asking him to stop. He paused, puzzled. She pointed at the sagging power line. Her hands trembled as she waited for him to reconsider.
text_zh: 玛尔塔看着邻居的链锯切入橡树的树干。树向她的菜地倾斜，树根横跨两家院子。她走近几步，心跳如鼓，锯刃越咬越深。要是树冠砸到她的棚屋怎么办？她抓住篱笆，指甲抠进木头。邻居挥了挥手，信心满满，但玛尔塔看到门廊上方那根树枝在摇晃。她喊出声，声音细弱，请他停下。他停下来，一脸困惑。她指了指下垂的电线。她双手颤抖着等他重新考虑。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: Elena hadn't anticipated the request, and now her hands trembled as she held the coffee mug. Her neighbor, a contractor, waved his arm at the old maple, describing how he'd cut it cleanly. "But the roots go under your garage," he said. That was the part that stuck. She imagined the roots shifting, the concrete cracking, her car sinking. She couldn't look at the tree without seeing the whole driveway tilted. She started avoiding the garage, using the front door, though it was longer. Each time she heard a car door outside, she tensed, expecting the saw. She made a list of arborists, but never called. Her coffee grew cold as she stared at the maple, counting the days until he might show up with his equipment.
text_zh: 埃琳娜没有预料到这个请求，此刻她端着咖啡杯，双手颤抖。她的邻居，一个承包商，挥手指着那棵老枫树，描述他会如何干净利落地砍掉它。“但树根延伸到你的车库下面，”他说。这正是让她耿耿于怀的地方。她想象着树根移位、混凝土开裂、她的车下陷。她无法再看那棵树而不看到整条车道倾斜。她开始避开车库，改走前门，虽然路程更远。每次听到外面有车门声，她都会紧张，以为锯子要来了。她列了一份树艺师的名单，但从未打电话。咖啡凉了，她盯着枫树，数着日子，担心他哪天会带着设备出现。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: The neighbor's request was polite, but Ray's jaw clenched. The pine was his, just on his side, and the man wanted to cut it to improve his view. "It'll be easy," the neighbor promised. Ray watched him trace the trunk with his fingers, and a cold wave washed through him. He imagined the tree falling incorrectly, the branches crashing into his workshop where he spent every afternoon. He started checking the tree's condition twice daily, looking for disease or rot, anything that would make it drop on its own. He moved his most precious tools to the basement. He even volunteered to trim the branches himself, but the neighbor insisted. Ray lay awake at night, listening to the wind, dreading the knock that would signal the start of the end.
text_zh: 邻居的请求很客气，但雷的下巴绷紧了。那棵松树是他的，就在他这边，那人想砍掉它来改善视野。“很容易的，”邻居保证道。雷看着他用手指描摹树干，一股寒意涌遍全身。他想象着树倒错方向，树枝砸进他每天下午都待的工作室。他开始每天检查两次树的状况，寻找病害或腐烂的迹象，任何可能让它自行倒下的迹象。他把最珍贵的工具搬到了地下室。他甚至主动提出自己修剪树枝，但邻居坚持要砍。雷夜里躺着睡不着，听着风声，害怕那声宣告终结的敲门声。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: Leo heard the knock and opened the door to find his neighbor holding a handsaw. "That maple's dropping too many leaves," the man said, nodding toward the shared boundary. Leo's stomach tightened. The tree's thick roots ran under his foundation; cutting it might shift the soil. He imagined cracks snaking up his basement wall. He stepped outside, blocking the path, and spoke of the roots, the drainage, the old pipes. His voice stayed steady, but his pulse hammered. The neighbor shrugged, saying he'd dig first. Leo didn't move, watching the saw gleam.
text_zh: 利奥听到敲门声，开门发现邻居拿着一把手锯。“那棵枫树落叶太多了，”那人说着，朝两家的分界线点了点头。利奥的胃一紧。那棵树粗壮的根延伸到他家地基下面；砍掉它可能会使土壤移位。他想象着裂缝蜿蜒爬上地下室的墙壁。他走到门外，挡住去路，说起树根、排水系统和老旧管道。他的声音保持平稳，但心跳如擂。邻居耸耸肩，说他会先挖开看看。利奥没有动，盯着那锯子闪闪发光。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: Priya noticed the orange spray paint on the birch trunk where it crossed the property line. Her neighbor stood nearby with a clipboard, measuring. She approached, heart thumping. The birch was the only thing shading her bedroom window in the afternoon heat. Without it, the room would bake, and worse, the tree's roots held the slope behind her house. If he cut it, rain might wash the soil away. She imagined mud sliding toward her door. She asked him to wait, her voice tight. He frowned, tapping his pen. She stayed, hands clasped, watching his every move.
text_zh: 普里亚注意到白桦树干上越过地界的地方喷了橙色油漆。她的邻居拿着写字板站在附近测量。她走近，心怦怦直跳。这棵白桦是下午炎热时唯一能为她卧室窗户遮阴的树。没有它，房间会被烤热，更糟的是，这棵树的根固定着她房子后面的斜坡。如果他砍了它，雨水可能会冲走土壤。她想象着泥浆滑向她的门口。她请他等等，声音紧绷。他皱起眉头，敲着笔。她留在原地，双手紧握，注视着他的一举一动。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: The neighbor's truck idled in the driveway, chainsaw visible in the bed. Sam watched from his kitchen window as the man paced around the old elm on the boundary line. Sam's chest tightened. That elm's roots had tangled with his water line; cutting it might rupture the pipe. He recalled last winter's leak, the basement flood, the costly repair. He pulled on his boots and went outside, forcing a smile. "Mind if we talk first?" he asked. The neighbor crossed his arms. Sam's gaze flicked to the chainsaw, then back to the man's face, his own jaw set.
text_zh: 邻居的卡车在车道上怠速，车斗里能看到链锯。萨姆从厨房窗户看着那人在边界线上的老榆树周围踱步。萨姆的胸口发紧。那棵榆树的根和他的水管缠在一起；砍掉它可能会弄破管道。他想起去年冬天的漏水、地下室被淹、昂贵的维修。他穿上靴子走到外面，勉强挤出笑容。“我们先谈谈可以吗？”他问。邻居双臂交叉。萨姆的目光扫向链锯，又回到那人的脸上，自己的下巴绷紧。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: Tomas knew the cedar was partly on his neighbor's land, so he couldn't refuse outright. Yet each time the neighbor spoke of cutting it, Tomas's skin crawled. He had always felt safe in the cedar's shadow; it blocked the view of the busy street. He began to take longer routes home, passing through the alley, just to avoid walking past the potential drop zone. He bought motion-sensor lights, though there was no need. His hands trembled as he watered the lawn near the tree, not wanting to get too close. He couldn't articulate why, but the thought of that tree gone made his breath shallow. He started sleeping in the basement, reasoning it would be safer if the tree fell, but that only made his nights worse.
text_zh: 托马斯知道那棵雪松有一部分在邻居的地上，所以他不能直接拒绝。然而每次邻居说起砍树，托马斯就浑身起鸡皮疙瘩。他一直觉得在雪松的树荫下很安全；它挡住了繁忙街道的视线。他开始绕远路回家，穿过小巷，只是为了避开可能倒下的区域。他买了感应灯，虽然并没有必要。他在树附近给草坪浇水时双手颤抖，不想靠得太近。他说不清为什么，但一想到那棵树没了，他的呼吸就变浅。他开始睡在地下室，理由是如果树倒了那里更安全，但这反而让他的夜晚更糟。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: Neena’s neighbor, a retired logger, said the ash tree was interfering with his garage foundation. He showed her a small crack, and she felt a chill that didn't leave. She nodded, but that evening, she looked up the species and learned ash trees have shallow roots that can damage pipes. She began to eye the tree with suspicion, then with dread. She imagined the roots strangling her water line, her basement flooding. She called a plumber to check, and when he found nothing, she still didn't relax. She prevented her son from playing in the backyard, saying it was too cold. She stared at the tree, trying to decide if it was a friend or a threat, but the feeling of something about to go wrong wouldn't ease.
text_zh: 妮娜的邻居，一位退休的伐木工，说那棵白蜡树妨碍了他车库的地基。他给她看了一条小裂缝，她感到一阵寒意，久久不散。她点了点头，但那天晚上，她查了树种，得知白蜡树根系浅，可能损坏管道。她开始用怀疑的目光看那棵树，然后是恐惧。她想象着树根勒住她的水管，地下室被淹。她叫了水管工来检查，当他没发现什么时，她仍然没有放松。她不让儿子在后院玩，说太冷了。她盯着那棵树，试图判断它是朋友还是威胁，但那种要出事的预感始终挥之不去。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: The moment the neighbor mentioned cutting the poplar, Owen felt his mouth go dry. That tree was the only thing separating his yard from the man's new, loud air conditioner. He envisioned the noise level, but more than that, the loss of privacy. His bedroom window faced the neighbor's. With the tree gone, anyone could see in. He started keeping the blinds shut, even during the day, which darkened his rooms and made him jumpy. He bought a tall screen, but it wasn't the same. He rehearsed arguments in his head, but each time the neighbor waved at him, he froze. He began wearing a hoodie inside, pulling the hood up, as if that would help. He dreaded the coming weekend when the man had promised to start.
text_zh: 邻居一提到砍那棵杨树，欧文就感到口干舌燥。那棵树是唯一能把他的院子与那人新装的吵闹空调隔开的东西。他想象着噪音水平，但更重要的是隐私的丧失。他的卧室窗户正对着邻居家。树没了，任何人都能看进来。他开始拉上百叶窗，即使在白天，这让房间变暗，让他变得紧张不安。他买了一个高屏风，但感觉不一样。他在脑子里排练着争论，但每次邻居向他挥手，他就僵住。他开始在家里穿连帽衫，拉起帽子，好像那样会有用。他害怕即将到来的周末，那人答应那时开工。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: Liam had planted that cherry tree as a child. His neighbor wanted it removed because it dropped fruit on her car. Liam understood, but the request made his hands sweat. That tree was his childhood, and uprooting it felt like erasing something essential. He pictured the stump alone in the yard, the bare patch where he had learned to climb. He started to avoid that part of the garden, taking detours through the house. He even considered buying a fake tree, but that was ridiculous. Each time his neighbor called him, his heart rate surged. He would hang up and then sit motionless, staring at the wall, feeling the loss already. He hid the garden shears, as if that would stop the inevitable.
text_zh: 利亚姆小时候种了那棵樱桃树。他的邻居想把它移走，因为果子掉在她的车上。利亚姆理解，但这个请求让他的手心出汗。那棵树是他的童年，把它连根拔起就像抹去某种重要的东西。他想象着院子里孤零零的树桩，那片他学会爬树的空地。他开始避开花园的那部分，从房子里绕路。他甚至考虑买一棵假树，但那太荒谬了。每次邻居打电话给他，他的心跳都会加速。他会挂断电话，然后一动不动地坐着，盯着墙壁，已经感受到了失去。他把花园剪刀藏了起来，好像那样能阻止不可避免的事情发生。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: Darla's neighbor proposed cutting the old sycamore, citing its mess of leaves in her pool. Darla's mind raced to the birds that nested there, but she had no legal ground. Still, a deep unease took root. That tree was a kind of sentinel for her, its height giving her a sense of elevation from her cramped life. Without it, she felt she would be grounded, trapped. She began to sit on the porch, never turning her back to the tree, as if guarding it. She left water out for the birds more often, trying to give them a reason to stay. The neighbor called her repeatedly, but she let the machine pick up, and with each ring she felt her chest constrict.
text_zh: 达拉邻居提议砍掉那棵老梧桐，理由是它的叶子掉进他泳池里很麻烦。达拉脑海中立刻浮现出筑巢其上的鸟儿，但她没有法律依据。然而，一种深深的不安在她心中扎根。那棵树对她来说像是一个哨兵，它的高度让她从局促的生活中获得一种超脱感。没有它，她觉得自己会被困住、被束缚。她开始坐在门廊上，从不背对那棵树，仿佛在守护它。她更频繁地给鸟儿留水，试图给它们一个留下的理由。邻居多次打电话来，但她让答录机接听，每响一声，她都感到胸口发紧。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: Rosa heard the saw start and ran to the window. The neighbor had already cut a wedge from the cottonwood that stood between their yards. Her breath caught. That tree's roots braced the retaining wall she'd built last spring. Without it, the wall might buckle under the next storm. She saw herself shoveling mud from her patio, the wall a pile of broken blocks. She rushed outside, shouting his name. He stopped, blade idle. She gestured at the wall, at the roots, her hands shaking. He looked at the cut, then at her, and slowly lowered the saw.
text_zh: 罗莎听到电锯声响起，跑到窗边。邻居已经在那棵长在两院之间的棉白杨上砍了一刀。她屏住呼吸。那棵树的树根支撑着她去年春天修建的挡土墙。没有它，墙可能会在下一场暴风雨中坍塌。她仿佛看到自己在清理露台上的泥土，而墙已碎成一堆砖块。她冲出去，喊着他的名字。他停下来，锯片空转。她指着墙，指着树根，双手颤抖。他看了看切口，又看了看她，慢慢放下了锯子。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: Tomas found the note on his door: "Cutting the pine tomorrow." He stared at the words, then at the pine that stretched over both lawns. Its branches brushed his roof, and its roots ran under his driveway. If the neighbor felled it, the driveway could crack, the roof could lose its shade. He imagined the trunk crashing onto his car. He crumpled the note and walked next door. The neighbor answered, already in work gloves. Tomas spoke quickly, listing his worries. The man listened, but his eyes kept drifting to the tree. Tomas's throat stayed dry.
text_zh: 托马斯在门上发现一张字条：“明天砍松树。”他盯着这几个字，又看看那棵横跨两家草坪的松树。它的枝条拂过他的屋顶，树根延伸到他家车道下。如果邻居砍倒它，车道可能会开裂，屋顶会失去荫蔽。他想象着树干砸在他的车上。他揉皱字条，走到隔壁。邻居来开门，已经戴上了工作手套。托马斯语速很快，列举着自己的担忧。那人听着，但目光不断飘向那棵树。托马斯的喉咙一直发干。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: He had always been indifferent to the oak until the neighbor asked to cut it. Now, the thought of it crashing into his house was a tangible threat. He had seen videos of trees falling on roofs, the way they crumpled. He had read about roots damaging foundations, and now he overlaid those images onto his own home. He cancelled the neighbor's permit, but the man was determined. He began to think the neighbor had an ulterior motive, maybe to build a larger house and block his light. He watched for signs of machinery, his body tensing at every truck that passed. He even considered filing a lawsuit, but that cost money. He just stood guard at the window, his hands clenched at his sides.
text_zh: 他一直对那棵橡树漠不关心，直到邻居提出要砍它。如今，想到它砸进房子的画面成了实实在在的威胁。他看过树倒压塌屋顶的视频，那种坍塌的样子。他读过树根破坏地基的文章，现在他把这些画面套用到自己家上。他取消了邻居的许可，但那人铁了心。他开始觉得邻居别有用心，也许是想建更大的房子，挡住他的光线。他留意着机械的迹象，每辆卡车经过，他的身体都会绷紧。他甚至考虑过起诉，但那要花钱。他只是站在窗边守望，双手紧握在身侧。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: Elena watched her neighbor tie a rope around the ash tree's trunk. The tree stood exactly on the line, its canopy shading her garden. She thought of the roots that held the soil together near her compost bin. If the tree came down, the ground might loosen, the bin might tilt, and the fence might lean. She stepped closer, heart pounding, and asked him to check the boundary survey first. He laughed, saying it was fine. She didn't laugh. She pointed at the fence line, at the slight dip in the ground. He paused, looking where she pointed.
text_zh: 埃琳娜看着邻居在梣树树干上系绳子。那棵树正好长在地界线上，树冠遮着她家的花园。她想到那些树根，它们固定着堆肥箱附近的土壤。如果树倒了，地面可能松动，堆肥箱可能倾斜，篱笆也可能歪倒。她走近几步，心怦怦直跳，请他先查一下地界测量。他笑了，说没事。她没笑。她指着篱笆线，指着地面微微凹陷的地方。他停下来，顺着她指的方向看去。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: The neighbor knocked and said, "That oak's got to go." Nina's hands went cold. The oak was older than both houses, its roots weaving under her porch. She pictured the porch sagging, the steps pulling away from the house. She shook her head, but he insisted, citing the leaves and the shade. She stepped onto the porch, blocking the view of the trunk. "Not yet," she said, her voice wavering. He frowned. She looked at the tree, then at her porch, then back at him. Her fingers gripped the railing, knuckles white.
text_zh: 邻居敲门说：“那棵橡树得砍掉。”妮娜的手一下子凉了。那棵橡树比两栋房子都老，树根在她家门廊下盘绕。她想象着门廊下沉，台阶从房子上脱落。她摇摇头，但他坚持，列举着落叶和遮阴的问题。她走到门廊上，挡住树干。“还不行，”她说，声音发颤。他皱起眉头。她看看树，又看看门廊，再看向他。她的手指紧紧抓住栏杆，指节发白。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: Marcus saw the neighbor's axe leaning against the willow on the boundary line. The willow's branches overhung his shed, and its roots reached toward his septic field. He imagined the roots being torn up, the ground shifting, the shed's floor cracking. He walked over, trying to keep his voice calm. "That tree's holding the bank," he said, pointing at the slope behind his garage. The neighbor picked up the axe, testing its weight. Marcus's chest tightened. He moved closer, standing between the man and the trunk. "Please," he said, and his voice broke. The neighbor hesitated.
text_zh: 马库斯看到邻居的斧头靠在地界上的柳树旁。柳树的枝条垂过他的棚屋，树根伸向他的化粪池。他想象着树根被拔起，地面移动，棚屋地面开裂。他走过去，尽量让声音保持平静。“那棵树护着堤岸，”他指着车库后面的斜坡说。邻居拿起斧头，掂了掂重量。马库斯胸口一紧。他走近些，站到那人和树干之间。“求你了，”他说，声音都破了。邻居犹豫了。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: The neighbor's request to cut the sycamore was one in a series of small complaints he had about her property. Carl saw this as the beginning of a slippery slope. If she agreed to this, what next? He pictured his entire yard stripped, his house exposed. He began to feel like the tree was the only thing holding the neighborhood at bay. He rehearsed refusals, but when the man knocked, his throat caught. He told a lie, saying he had a surveyor coming, and then he spent the next days on edge, waiting for the neighbor to call his bluff. He kept his phone close, his body ready to rebound. He couldn't relax at work, and he took to leaving early to check that the tree was still there.
text_zh: 邻居要求砍掉梧桐树，只是他对她房产一系列小抱怨中的一件。卡尔把这看作一个滑坡的开始。如果她答应了这件事，下一步会是什么？他想象着自己的整个院子被剥光，房子暴露在外。他开始觉得那棵树是唯一能挡住邻居的东西。他排练着拒绝的话，但当那人敲门时，他喉咙发紧。他说了个谎，说自己有测量员要来，然后接下来的日子他如坐针毡，等着邻居来戳穿他的虚张声势。他手机不离身，身体随时准备反击。他工作时无法放松，开始提前下班去确认那棵树还在。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: Nora's neighbor was an elderly man whose family had planted the beech. He wanted to cut it because it was making his house too dark. Nora felt a pang of sympathy, but also a deep freeze inside. That tree was a witness to her life, she had built a life around its seasons. Without it, she had no frame of reference. She began to take photos of it daily, almost as if to prove to herself it existed. She started to avoid the neighbor, going out only when she knew he was away. She even considered buying the house, but that was absurd. She just wanted the feeling of something solid to stay. She often stood by the trunk, placing her palm on the bark, feeling the world's pulse.
