He excused himself from a conversation about golf, walked to the buffet, and loaded a plate with food he didn't want. He watched her chat with his friends, laughing, as if she hadn't erased him. He took a bite of dry chicken, chewing slowly, his stare fixed on her.
text_zh: 音乐声渐强，本在帐篷那头看到了埃琳娜。她戴着他送她的那对耳环。他感到眼后一阵灼热。她用一条短信结束了他们的关系，然后声称她从未说过会去看他妹妹的话剧。正是那个谎言最刺痛他。他找了个借口，从一场关于高尔夫球的谈话中脱身，走到自助餐台前，往盘子里夹了一堆他并不想吃的食物。他看着她和他的朋友们聊天、说笑，仿佛她从未把他从她的生活中抹去。他咬了一口干柴的鸡肉，慢慢咀嚼，目光却死死锁在她身上。

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding
text_en: Priya hadn't expected him to be here. When their eyes met, she felt a cold flash, then a burn. She remembered the wedding they'd planned—their own—and how he'd called it off with a vague 'I can't do this.' Now he was clapping the groom on the back, all charm. She walked over to the gift table, picked up a pen, and wrote her card with deliberate pressure, the nib tearing the paper. She signed it, then put it face down, not wanting to see her own name next to the date. She'd stay for the toast, but she'd drink water, not champagne.
text_zh: 普里亚没想到他会在这里。当他们的目光相遇时，她感到一阵寒意，随即又是一阵灼热。她想起了他们曾计划过的婚礼——他们自己的——以及他是如何用一句含糊的“我做不到”就取消了。现在他正拍着新郎的背，一副魅力十足的样子。她走到礼品桌前，拿起一支笔，用刻意用力的笔触写着她的卡片，笔尖划破了纸。她签了名，然后把卡片正面朝下放着，不想看到自己的名字和日期挨在一起。她会留下来参加祝酒，但只会喝水，不喝香槟。

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding
text_en: Jake saw her silhouette near the floral arch. His stomach knotted. She'd told him she'd never attend these things, that she hated weddings. Yet here she was, wearing a dress he'd helped her pick out for a different occasion. He felt a surge of something hot and sharp. He walked to the restroom, splashed water on his face, and stared at his reflection. He wasn't going to let her ruin the day. He'd talk to the best man, laugh at his jokes, and if she came near, he'd simply say 'Excuse me' and move away, his back straight, his steps deliberate.
text_zh: 杰克在花拱门附近看到了她的身影。他的胃揪紧了。她曾告诉他，她永远不会参加这种场合，她讨厌婚礼。然而她却在这里，穿着他帮她为另一个场合挑选的裙子。他感到一股强烈而尖锐的情绪涌上来。他走进洗手间，往脸上泼了泼水，盯着镜子里的自己。他不会让她毁掉这一天。他会和伴郎聊天，附和着他的笑话大笑，如果她走近，他就简单地说一句“借过”，然后走开，挺直后背，步伐坚定。

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding
text_en: At the reception, Maya spotted him near the cake table, laughing with old friends. Her chest tightened. She turned to the bar, ordered a drink, and watched him from the corner of her eye. When he approached, she smiled tightly. "You look well," he said. She gripped her glass. "I am." He mentioned their shared vacation photos, and she felt heat rise. She excused herself, walked to the terrace, and stood alone, jaw clenched, replaying how he had dismissed her plans for years. She decided to stay for the toast, then leave.
text_zh: 在婚宴上，玛雅在蛋糕桌旁看到了他，正和老朋友们说笑。她的胸口一紧。她转身走向吧台，点了一杯酒，用眼角的余光看着他。当他走近时，她勉强挤出一个微笑。“你看起来气色不错，”他说。她握紧酒杯。“我很好。”他提起他们一起度假的照片，她感到一阵热意上涌。她找了个借口，走到露台上，独自站着，下巴紧绷，回想着多年来他是如何无视她的计划的。她决定留下来参加祝酒，然后离开。

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding
text_en: David hadn't planned to come, but his friend had insisted. Now he was here, and so was Rachel, dancing with a guy who kept touching her elbow. He remembered how she'd accused him of being too controlling, then had gone to a party without telling him. He felt a bitter taste in his mouth. He ordered a whiskey, neat, and watched her from the bar. When she caught his eye, he raised his glass in a mock toast, then turned away, his shoulders tense. He'd stay until the bouquet toss, then leave without saying goodbye, his exit a quiet statement.
text_zh: 大卫本没打算来，但他的朋友坚持。现在他在这里，蕾切尔也在，正和一个不停碰她手肘的男人跳舞。他想起她如何指责他控制欲太强，然后不告诉他一声就去了派对。他嘴里泛起一阵苦涩。他点了一杯威士忌，纯饮，在吧台边看着她。当她看向他时，他举起酒杯，做了个假装的敬酒动作，然后转过身去，肩膀紧绷。他会待到抛捧花的时候，然后不告而别，他的离开就是一句无声的宣言。

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding
text_en: Lena's hand paused on the champagne glass. There was Mark, talking to her cousin. He'd broken up with her a week before their anniversary, saying he needed 'space.' Now he was here, in the same city, at the same wedding, as if it were nothing. She felt a wave of heat, then a chill. She set down the glass, un-tasted, and walked to the dance floor, pulling a friend into a fast song. She moved with sharp, precise steps, her eyes fixed on the band, refusing to let him see her falter. Her smile was a shield.
text_zh: 莉娜的手在香槟杯上停住了。马克在那里，正和她表妹说话。他在他们周年纪念日前一周和她分手了，说需要“空间”。现在他在这里，在同一个城市，同一场婚礼上，仿佛什么都没发生过。她感到一阵热浪，接着是一阵寒意。她放下那杯没喝过的酒，走向舞池，拉着一个朋友跳起了一支快歌。她跳着干脆利落的舞步，眼睛盯着乐队，不让他看到自己有任何慌乱。她的微笑是一副盾牌。

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding
text_en: Omar saw his ex-wife at the dessert table. She was laughing with his mother. He felt a jolt, then a simmer. She'd taken the dog, the apartment, and the good friends, and now she was here, charming everyone. He walked over, picked up a chocolate truffle, and ate it in one bite, the sweetness cloying. He said, 'Congratulations to the happy couple,' loud enough for her to hear, then moved to the other side of the room. He spent the next hour by the bar, nursing a tonic, his eyes tracking her movements, his jaw set.
text_zh: 奥马尔在甜品台旁看到了他的前妻。她正和他母亲一起笑着。他感到一阵震动，然后是隐隐的怒火。她带走了狗、公寓和好朋友，现在她在这里，迷倒所有人。他走过去，拿起一颗松露巧克力，一口吃掉，甜得发腻。他说：“恭喜这对幸福的新人，”声音大得足以让她听见，然后走到房间的另一边。接下来的一个小时，他都在吧台边，慢慢喝着汤力水，目光追随着她的动作，下巴紧绷。

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding
text_en: As the band played a slow song, Sofia spotted Tom near the window. He'd once said this song was 'their' song. Now he was here, without her, as if that history didn't matter. She felt a sting, then a resolve. She walked to the dance floor with a groomsman, laughing a little too loudly. She held his hand firmly, led him through a spin, and when the song ended, she clapped, her eyes not once meeting Tom's. She returned to her seat and began a conversation about the centerpieces, her voice steady, her mind elsewhere.
text_zh: 乐队奏起一首慢歌时，索菲亚在窗边看到了汤姆。他曾说过这首歌是“他们”的歌。现在他在这里，没有她，仿佛那段过去无关紧要。她感到一阵刺痛，随即是决心。她和一位伴郎一起走向舞池，笑得有点太大声。她紧紧握住他的手，带着他转了个圈，当歌曲结束时，她鼓了鼓掌，目光自始至终没有与汤姆相遇。她回到座位上，开始谈论起中心装饰品，声音平稳，心思却飘到了别处。

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding
text_en: Marcus hadn't expected the invitation to include her. But there she was, in the front row, wearing a dress he'd once complimented. He felt a familiar heat rise from his collar. She'd left him for a man she met online, then had the nerve to ask him to feed her cat while she moved. He'd said no, and he'd felt good about it. Now, he felt the same defiance. He clapped loudly for the couple, smiled at the bride, and when he passed his ex on the way to the bar, he simply said, 'Nice dress,' without stopping, his pace unhurried.
text_zh: 马库斯没想到请柬上会包括她。但她就在那里，坐在前排，穿着他曾经夸过的那条裙子。他感到一股熟悉的燥热从领口升起。她为了一个网上认识的男人离开了他，然后居然还有脸在他搬家时让他帮忙喂猫。他说了不，而且为此感觉很好。现在，他感到同样的反抗情绪。他为那对新人响亮地鼓掌，对新娘微笑，当他在去吧台的路上经过前女友时，他只是说了句“裙子不错”，没有停下脚步，步伐不紧不慢。

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding
text_en: Nina's chest tightened when she saw Chris at the cocktail hour. He was holding a plate of shrimp, chatting with her old roommate. She remembered how he'd forgotten her birthday, then blamed it on a 'busy week.' She felt a surge of something hot and sharp. She turned to the bartender and ordered a sparkling water, then took a sip, the bubbles stinging her nose. She made a point to walk past him, her shoulder brushing his, and said, 'Enjoy the shrimp,' her tone flat. She then joined a group discussing travel, her voice loud, her laugh bright.
text_zh: 尼娜在鸡尾酒会上看到克里斯时，胸口一紧。他端着一盘虾，正和她以前的室友聊天。她想起他是如何忘记她的生日，然后归咎于“忙碌的一周”。她感到一阵又热又尖锐的情绪涌上来。她转向调酒师，点了一杯气泡水，然后喝了一口，气泡刺痛了她的鼻子。她故意从他身边走过，肩膀擦过他的，说：“享用你的虾吧。”语气平淡。然后她加入了一群讨论旅行的人，声音响亮，笑声灿烂。

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding
text_en: As the speeches began, Ethan saw Julia in the back, whispering to a friend. He'd once imagined her giving a toast at their wedding. Now she was here, a guest, like him. He felt a bitter twist. He focused on the groom's words, clapping at the right moments, but his mind was on the last argument—her saying he never listened. He waited until the speeches ended, then walked to the restroom, took a deep breath, and returned with a fixed smile. He'd dance with the bride, then leave, his goodbyes brief, his handshake firm.
text_zh: 演讲开始时，伊桑看到朱莉娅在后面，正和一个朋友低声说话。他曾想象过她在他们的婚礼上致辞。现在她在这里，和他一样，是个客人。他感到一阵苦涩的扭曲。他专注于新郎的话，在合适的时刻鼓掌，但他的心思却在最后一次争吵上——她说他从不倾听。他一直等到演讲结束，然后走到洗手间，深吸一口气，带着固定的微笑回来。他会和新娘跳舞，然后离开，告别简短，握手坚定。

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding
text_en: Hannah saw her ex across the lawn, tossing a frisbee with a kid. She felt a flash of annoyance, then a deeper burn. He'd said he didn't want children, that he was 'too young.' Now he was playing with someone else's. She walked over to the gift table, placed her envelope, and then deliberately turned her back to him. She joined a croquet game, hitting the ball harder than necessary, the mallet thwacking against the wood. She didn't look his way again, but her shoulders stayed rigid, her grip on the handle tight.
text_zh: 汉娜在草坪对面看到她的前任，正和一个孩子玩飞盘。她感到一阵恼怒，然后是更深的灼烧感。他说过他不想要孩子，说他“太年轻”。现在他在和别人的孩子玩。她走到礼品桌，放下她的信封，然后故意转过身背对着他。她加入了一场槌球游戏，击球比必要的更用力，木槌砰地敲在木头上。她不再看他，但肩膀保持僵硬，握柄的手很紧。

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding
text_en: When the band struck up a waltz, Alex saw Becca on the floor, dancing with the groom's brother. He remembered teaching her to dance in his kitchen, her laugh as she stumbled. Now she was graceful, with someone else. He felt a pang, then a resolve. He walked to the bar, ordered a double, and drank it slowly, watching her spin. He didn't approach. When the song ended, he applauded, then set down his glass and walked out to the patio, lighting a cigarette he didn't usually smoke, the smoke curling into the night air.
text_zh: 乐队奏起华尔兹时，亚历克斯看到贝卡在舞池里，和新郎的兄弟跳舞。他记得在厨房里教她跳舞，她绊倒时的笑声。现在她优雅了，和别人在一起。他感到一阵刺痛，然后是决心。他走到酒吧，点了一杯双份，慢慢喝，看着她旋转。他没有靠近。歌曲结束时，他鼓掌，然后放下杯子，走到露台，点了一支他通常不抽的烟，烟雾缭绕在夜空中。

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding
text_en: Maya's gaze found Leo again, this time near the cake. He was pointing at the tiers, laughing with the caterer. She remembered how he'd promised to help plan their own wedding, then had canceled the tasting at the last minute. She felt a hot pulse. She walked to the dance floor, grabbed her friend's hand, and pulled her into a fast song. She danced with exaggerated energy, her hips sharp, her arms swinging. When the song ended, she was breathing hard, her smile fixed, her eyes bright with something unspoken.
text_zh: 玛雅的目光再次找到利奥，这次是在蛋糕附近。他指着蛋糕层，和餐饮承办人笑着。她记得他承诺帮助计划他们自己的婚礼，然后在最后一刻取消了品鉴。她感到一阵热流。她走到舞池，抓住朋友的手，把她拉进一首快歌。她以夸张的精力跳舞，臀部尖锐，手臂摆动。歌曲结束时，她呼吸急促，笑容固定，眼睛明亮，带着某种未说出口的东西。

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding
text_en: Liam saw her across the dance floor, her hand on another man's shoulder. He felt a hot flash, like a door slamming shut. He stepped back, bumped a waiter, and muttered an apology. She caught his eye and waved, smiling. He didn't wave back. He moved to the buffet, piling food he wouldn't eat. When she came over, she said, "I'm glad you came." He nodded, not meeting her gaze. She mentioned their old inside joke, and his stomach knotted. He set his plate down and walked outside, pacing the lawn, fists tight, muttering about her casual tone.
text_zh: 利亚姆在舞池对面看到她，她的手搭在另一个男人的肩上。他感到一阵热闪，像门砰地关上。他后退一步，撞到一个服务员，咕哝着道歉。她捕捉到他的目光，微笑着挥手。他没有挥手回应。他走到自助餐台，堆起他不会吃的食物。当她走过来时，她说：“我很高兴你来了。”他点点头，没有看她的眼睛。她提到他们以前的内部笑话，他的胃揪紧了。他放下盘子，走到外面，在草坪上踱步，拳头紧握，咕哝着她随意的语气。

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding
text_en: Priya recognized his laugh before she saw him. She froze mid-bite of a canapé. He was telling a story near the fountain, gesturing broadly. She swallowed, set the napkin down, and made her way to the restroom, but he intercepted her. "Priya!" He hugged her, and she stiffened. He talked about his new job, his new apartment, his new life. She listened, arms crossed, foot tapping. He asked, "Still painting?" She said, "Yes," and turned away. She found her friend, whispered she wasn't feeling well, and gathered her coat, jaw set, refusing to look back.
text_zh: 普里亚在看到他之前就认出了他的笑声。她咬了一口小点心，僵住了。他正在喷泉附近讲一个故事，手势夸张。她咽下食物，放下餐巾，走向洗手间，但他拦住了她。“普里亚！”他拥抱她，她僵硬了。他谈论他的新工作、新公寓、新生活。她听着，双臂交叉，脚轻敲。他问：“还在画画吗？”她说：“是的，”然后转身离开。她找到她的朋友，低声说她不舒服，然后拿起外套，下巴紧绷，拒绝回头。

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding
text_en: Jake saw her again, this time near the exit. He felt a pull to confront her, to ask why she'd lied about the trip she'd taken without him. But he didn't. Instead, he walked to the bar, ordered a club soda, and stood with his back to her, watching the bartender pour. He could feel her gaze, but he didn't turn. He finished his drink, set the glass down with a click, and walked to the dance floor, joining a line dance. He moved with precise steps, his focus on the music, his jaw tight.
text_zh: 杰克再次看到她，这次是在出口附近。他感到一种冲动想要质问她，问她为什么对他撒谎关于她独自去旅行的事。但他没有。相反，他走到酒吧，点了一杯苏打水，背对着她站着，看着调酒师倒酒。他能感觉到她的目光，但他没有转身。他喝完饮料，咔嗒一声放下杯子，走到舞池，加入了一支排舞。他动作精准，专注于音乐，下巴紧绷。

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding
text_en: Nora saw Alex near the gift table, holding an envelope. She remembered the time he'd forgotten to mail a card for her mother's birthday, blaming the post office. She felt a hot flicker. She walked to the table, picked up a pen, and wrote her own card, her handwriting large and deliberate. She placed it next to his, then moved away. She didn't speak to him. She found her friends, joined their conversation about a movie, and laughed at a joke, but her eyes kept drifting to his envelope, her mind on the past.
text_zh: 诺拉在礼品桌附近看到亚历克斯，手里拿着一个信封。她记得他忘记寄她母亲生日贺卡的事，归咎于邮局。她感到一阵热闪。她走到桌边，拿起笔，写下自己的卡片，字迹大而刻意。她把它放在他的旁边，然后走开。她没有和他说话。她找到她的朋友，加入她们关于电影的谈话，并因一个笑话而笑，但她的眼睛不断飘向他的信封，心思在过去。

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding
text_en: David spotted Rachel near the bar, alone for a moment. He felt a surge of something he couldn't name, but it was hot and uncomfortable. He remembered how she'd left his keys on the table without a note. He walked over, ordered a water, and stood beside her, not looking at her. He said, 'Nice wedding,' his voice flat. She started to speak, but he turned away, his drink in hand, and walked to the other side of the room. He set his glass down, watched the dancers, and didn't look back, his stance solid.
text_zh: 大卫在酒吧附近发现瑞秋，独自一人片刻。他感到一阵无法名状的情绪，但它是热的、不舒服的。他记得她如何把钥匙留在桌上，没有留便条。他走过去，点了一杯水，站在她旁边，没有看她。他说：“不错的婚礼。”声音平淡。她开始说话，但他转身走开，手里拿着饮料，走到房间的另一边。他放下杯子，看着舞者，没有回头，站姿稳固。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: Maya always thought Leo worked late at the hospital. She'd bring him coffee at the nurses' station, but he was never there. Tonight, she followed him after his supposed shift. He walked into a bar and sat with a group of friends, laughing. She watched him order a drink, not a care in the world. Her jaw tightened. She'd rearranged her own schedule to accommodate his stories. She walked over, placed the coffee on the table, and said, 'You forgot this at the hospital.' His face went pale. She turned and left, her steps quick and sharp.
text_zh: 玛雅一直以为利奥在医院工作到很晚。她会把咖啡送到护士站给他，但他从来不在那里。今晚，她在他所谓的下班时间后跟踪了他。他走进一家酒吧，和一群朋友坐在一起，笑着。她看着他点了一杯饮料，一副无忧无虑的样子。她的下巴绷紧了。她为了配合他的说辞，重新安排了自己的日程。她走过去，把咖啡放在桌上，说：“你把这个忘在医院了。”他的脸变得苍白。她转身离开，脚步又快又急。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: For months, Ben had been telling his friend Sam about his job as a deep-sea diver. Sam had even bought a book on marine life to keep up. One afternoon, Sam saw Ben at the aquarium, wearing a janitor's uniform, mopping the floor near the shark tank. Sam stood there, watching Ben scrub at a stain. Ben looked up, and their eyes met. Sam didn't say anything. He just walked to the exit, his fists clenched in his pockets. The next day, when Ben called to talk about a 'dive', Sam let it ring and ring.
text_zh: 几个月来，本一直跟他的朋友山姆吹嘘他深海潜水员的工作。山姆甚至买了一本海洋生物的书来跟上话题。一天下午，山姆在水族馆看到了本，穿着清洁工的制服，在鲨鱼缸附近拖地。山姆站在那里，看着本擦洗一块污渍。本抬起头，他们的目光相遇了。山姆什么也没说。他只是走向出口，拳头在口袋里紧握着。第二天，当本打电话来谈论一次“潜水”时，山姆让电话一直响着，没有接。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: Elena had been helping her friend Carla with her 'startup' for weeks, writing code and fixing bugs. Carla always talked about investors and product launches. Then Elena got a call from a temp agency offering her a job—as a data entry clerk. She recognized the address: it was the same one Carla used for her office. Elena went there. She saw Carla at a cubicle, wearing a headset, reading from a script. Elena stood in the doorway, her face hot. She walked over to Carla's desk, placed the code she'd written on it, and said, 'Here's your pitch deck.' She left without waiting for a reply.
text_zh: 几周来，埃琳娜一直在帮她朋友卡拉搞她的“初创公司”，写代码、修漏洞。卡拉总是谈论投资者和产品发布。然后埃琳娜接到一家临时工中介的电话，给她提供了一份工作——做数据录入员。她认出了那个地址：和卡拉用作办公室的地址一样。埃琳娜去了那里。她看到卡拉坐在一个小隔间里，戴着耳机，照着稿子念。埃琳娜站在门口，脸发烫。她走到卡拉的桌前，把她写的代码放在上面，说：“这是你的融资演讲稿。”她没等回复就离开了。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: Tom had been bragging about his job as a wildlife photographer for years. His friend Rachel had even framed one of his 'photos'—a generic picture of a lion she'd found online. One day, she saw Tom at the zoo, wearing a safari hat, but he was just selling tickets at the entrance. He was handing a ticket to a family, smiling. Rachel walked up to the booth. 'Nice shot, Tom,' she said, pointing to the lion poster behind him. He tried to explain, but she was already walking away, her heart pounding in her chest.
text_zh: 多年来，汤姆一直吹嘘他野生动物摄影师的工作。他的朋友瑞秋甚至把他的一张“照片”装裱了起来——那是她在网上找到的一张普通的狮子图片。一天，她在动物园看到了汤姆，戴着狩猎帽，但他只是在入口卖票。他正微笑着把票递给一家人。瑞秋走到售票亭前。“拍得不错，汤姆，”她指着身后的狮子海报说。他试图解释，但她已经走开了，心在胸口怦怦直跳。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: Marta found Leo's travel blog by accident—a photo of a desk with a coffee mug she'd bought him, captioned "At the office." She scrolled further: posts about business trips he'd never mentioned, meetings with people he'd told her were fictional. She slammed her laptop shut flagrantly, heart thudding. At their next lunch, she watched him demo a spreadsheet he claimed was for his real job. He never broke character syntactically poised. She set down her fork and coolly asked about his trip to Lisbon. He fumbled. Marta crossed her arms and held his gaze until he stopped talking, waiting for one honest sentence.
text_zh: 玛尔塔偶然发现了利奥的旅行博客——一张桌子上放着她买给他的咖啡杯的照片，配文是“在办公室”。她继续往下翻：关于他从未提过的商务旅行的帖子，以及和他告诉过她那些虚构人物的会面。她猛地合上笔记本电脑，心怦怦直跳。在下次午餐时，她看着他演示一个他声称是他真正工作的电子表格。他始终没有露出破绽，措辞依然镇定。她放下叉子，冷静地问他去里斯本的旅行。他支支吾吾。玛尔塔双臂交叉，盯着他，直到他停止说话，等待一句诚实的话。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: Nate had memorized Finn's stories about his architectural firm—the pressure, the clients, the models. Then one evening, Nate saw Finn loading a catering van with platters labeled "Finn's Kitchen." He followed the van to a downtown event space and watched Finn serve canapés in a crisp apron. The next day, Nate greeted him with a grin that dared to break. "How were the blueprints today?" he asked. Finn launched into a tale about a staircase. Nate let him finish, then silently slid a photo of Finn holding a tray across the table. Finn's face fell, and Nate sipped his coffee, unsmiling.
text_zh: 内特记住了芬恩关于他建筑事务所的故事——压力、客户、模型。然后一天晚上，内特看到芬恩在往一辆餐饮车上装贴着“芬恩厨房”标签的托盘。他跟着那辆车来到一个市中心的活动场地，看着芬恩穿着整洁的围裙端上小食。第二天，内特带着一个快要绷不住的笑容跟他打招呼。“今天的蓝图怎么样？”他问。芬恩开始讲一个关于楼梯的故事。内特让他讲完，然后默默地把一张芬恩端着托盘的照片滑过桌子。芬恩的脸垮了下来，内特啜饮着咖啡，面无表情。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: Lena's friend Mark always said he was a pilot for a cargo airline. She'd track his flights online, but the routes never made sense. One day, she drove to the small airport he mentioned. She found him in a hangar, but he was a mechanic, covered in grease, fixing a propeller. He had a wrench in his hand. Lena stood in the doorway, watching him work. He saw her and dropped the wrench. She said, 'Your flight's delayed, I guess.' She turned and walked to her car, her hands trembling slightly as she unlocked the door.
text_zh: 莉娜的朋友马克总是说他是货运航空公司的飞行员。她会在网上追踪他的航班，但航线从来都不合理。一天，她开车去了他提到的那个小机场。她在机库里找到了他，但他是个机械师，满身油污，在修理螺旋桨。他手里拿着一把扳手。莉娜站在门口，看着他工作。他看到她，扳手掉在了地上。她说：“我猜，你的航班延误了。”她转身走向她的车，开锁时双手微微颤抖。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: Nina's friend Sofia had been claiming to be a museum curator for months. Nina even attended a 'private viewing' Sofia had organized. It was just a small room in a library with a few old books. Then Nina saw Sofia at the public library, stamping due-date slips. Sofia was at the front desk, wearing a name tag that said 'Library Assistant.' Nina approached the desk and said, 'I need to check out a book on ancient artifacts.' Sofia looked up, her face red. Nina just stared at her, waiting for an answer that never came.
text_zh: 妮娜的朋友索菲亚几个月来一直声称自己是博物馆馆长。妮娜甚至参加了索菲亚组织的一次“私人观展”。那只是图书馆里一个放着几本旧书的小房间。然后妮娜在公共图书馆看到了索菲亚，在盖到期日期的章。索菲亚在前台，戴着写着“图书馆助理”的胸牌。妮娜走到前台说：“我要借一本关于古代文物的书。”索菲亚抬起头，脸红了。妮娜只是盯着她，等待一个从未到来的回答。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: David's friend Chris always talked about his job as a video game designer. He'd describe characters and plots in detail. David even tried to play the games Chris mentioned, but they never existed. One night, David saw Chris at an arcade, but he was just refilling the ticket machine. Chris was wearing a polo shirt with the arcade's logo. David walked up to him. 'So, what's your new game called?' he asked. Chris looked at the machine, then at David. David turned and walked to the exit, his back stiff, not saying another word.
text_zh: 大卫的朋友克里斯总是谈论他电子游戏设计师的工作。他会详细描述角色和情节。大卫甚至尝试玩克里斯提到的游戏，但它们根本不存在。一天晚上，大卫在街机厅看到了克里斯，但他只是在给兑票机加票。克里斯穿着一件印有街机厅标志的 Polo 衫。大卫走到他面前。“那么，你的新游戏叫什么？”他问。克里斯看了看机器，又看了看大卫。大卫转身走向出口，后背僵硬，一句话也没再说。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: Hannah's friend Peter claimed to be a forensic scientist. He'd tell her about crime scenes and lab work. One day, she saw him at a grocery store, but he was just a cashier, scanning items. He was wearing a store apron. Hannah waited in his line. When it was her turn, she put a bag of apples on the belt and said, 'Any trace evidence on these?' Peter didn't laugh. He just scanned them, his hands shaking. Hannah paid in cash, took her bag, and left without looking back, her own hands steady but her mind racing.
text_zh: 汉娜的朋友彼得自称是法医科学家。他会跟她讲犯罪现场和实验室工作。一天，她在杂货店看到了他，但他只是个收银员，在扫描商品。他穿着商店的围裙。汉娜排在他的队伍里。轮到她时，她把一袋苹果放在传送带上，说：“这些上面有微量证据吗？”彼得没有笑。他只是扫描了苹果，手在颤抖。汉娜用现金付了款，拿起袋子，头也不回地离开了，自己的手很稳，但思绪万千。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: Olivia's friend Jake had been telling her he was a marine biologist, studying sharks. She'd even bought a shark tooth necklace to support him. Then she saw him at a pet store, cleaning the fish tanks. He was wearing a wet apron, holding a net. Olivia stood by the fish food aisle, watching. He saw her and dropped the net. She walked over, pointed at a goldfish, and said, 'Is that a great white?' He didn't answer. She put the goldfish food back on the shelf and left, her footsteps heavy on the tile floor.
text_zh: 奥利维亚的朋友杰克一直告诉她，他是一名海洋生物学家，研究鲨鱼。她甚至买了一条鲨鱼牙齿项链来支持他。然后她在一家宠物店看到他，正在清理鱼缸。他穿着湿围裙，拿着网。奥利维亚站在鱼食过道旁看着。他看见她，网掉了下来。她走过去，指着一只金鱼说：“那是一条大白鲨吗？”他没有回答。她把金鱼食放回架子上，然后离开了，脚步声沉重地落在瓷砖地板上。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: Priya had trusted Dana's late nights at her so-called data consultancy. But when Priya's sister needed a phone number stored on Dana's laptop, she found a folder labeled "Fiction Novels—Rejections." Filtering out weak emails, Priya saw drafts dated for the same hours Dana claimed to be logging client data. For a week, Priya simmered quietly, testing Dana's honesty with casual questions about her workload. Finally, at dinner, Priya pulled out the folder and laid it beside Dana's glass. "Tell me about your book," she said, her tone even. Dana reached for the folder; Priya held it firm. "I'll wait until you tell me the truth."
text_zh: 普里亚一直信任达娜在她所谓的“数据咨询公司”加班到深夜。但当普里亚的姐姐需要达娜笔记本电脑上存储的一个电话号码时，她发现了一个标有“小说——退稿”的文件夹。过滤掉无关紧要的邮件后，普里亚看到了草稿，日期与达娜声称记录客户数据的那些时间吻合。整整一周，普里亚默默忍耐，用关于工作量的随意问题试探达娜的诚实。最后，在晚餐时，普里亚拿出那个文件夹，放在达娜的杯子旁边。“跟我说说你的书吧，”她说，语气平稳。达娜伸手去拿文件夹；普里亚按住不放。“我会等你告诉我真相。”

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: Ava's friend Liam had been claiming to be a professional musician, a session guitarist. He'd send her recordings. One night, she saw him at a karaoke bar, but he was just the DJ, playing other people's songs. He was behind a booth, adjusting a volume knob. Ava walked up to the booth. 'Can you play something you wrote?' she asked. Liam froze. He looked at his laptop, then at her. She shook her head slowly and walked to the exit, the sound of a bad rendition of a pop song following her out.
text_zh: 艾娃的朋友利亚姆一直声称自己是一名专业音乐人，一名录音室吉他手。他会给她发录音。一天晚上，她在一家卡拉OK酒吧看到他，但他只是DJ，播放别人的歌曲。他站在操作台后面，调节音量旋钮。艾娃走到操作台前。“你能弹一首你自己写的曲子吗？”她问。利亚姆僵住了。他看了看笔记本电脑，又看了看她。她慢慢摇了摇头，走向出口，一首糟糕的流行歌曲翻唱声跟着她出了门。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: Mia's friend Noah always said he was a personal trainer at an exclusive gym. He'd give her workout tips. Then she saw him at a community center, but he was just teaching a beginner's yoga class to a group of seniors. He was wearing loose sweatpants and a t-shirt. Mia stood at the back of the room, watching him struggle to demonstrate a pose. When he saw her, he lost his balance. She didn't say anything. She just turned and left, her own posture stiff as she walked down the hallway.
text_zh: 米娅的朋友诺亚总是说他在一家高档健身房当私人教练。他会给她健身建议。然后她在社区中心看到他，但他只是在给一群老年人上初级瑜伽课。他穿着宽松的运动裤和T恤。米娅站在房间后面，看着他艰难地示范一个姿势。当他看到她时，他失去了平衡。她什么也没说。她只是转身离开，走在走廊上，自己的姿态僵硬。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: Zoe's friend Ryan claimed to be a travel blogger, posting photos from exotic locations. He'd send her pictures of beaches and mountains. One day, she saw him at a local diner, but he was just a waiter, carrying a tray of pancakes. He was wearing a stained apron. Zoe sat in his section. He came over, notepad in hand. She said, 'I'll have the Moroccan tagine, please.' Ryan's face went blank. She watched him write it down, his hand shaking. She didn't eat her pancakes when they came. She just left them on the table.
text_zh: 佐伊的朋友瑞安自称是旅行博主，发布来自异国他乡的照片。他会给她发海滩和山脉的照片。有一天，她在一家本地小餐馆看到他，但他只是个服务员，端着一托盘煎饼。他穿着脏围裙。佐伊坐在他的服务区。他走过来，手里拿着记事本。她说：“请给我来一份摩洛哥塔吉锅。”瑞安的脸一下子僵住了。她看着他记下来，手在发抖。煎饼端上来时，她没有吃。她只是把它们留在桌上。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: Isla's friend Ben had been telling her he was a lawyer, working on big cases. He'd talk about courtrooms and juries. Then she saw him at the courthouse, but he was just a security guard, checking bags at the entrance. He was in a uniform, patting down a visitor. Isla walked through the metal detector. Ben didn't meet her eyes. She said, 'I have an appointment with the judge.' He just nodded and waved her through. She walked past him, her back to him, her hands clenched at her sides.
text_zh: 艾拉的朋友本一直告诉她，他是一名律师，处理大案子。他会谈论法庭和陪审团。然后她在法院看到他，但他只是个保安，在入口处检查包。他穿着制服，正在拍摸一名访客。艾拉走过金属探测器。本没有与她对视。她说：“我和法官有个预约。”他只是点点头，挥手让她过去。她走过他身边，背对着他，双手在身侧紧握。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: Lucas's friend Chloe said she was a fashion designer, showing at Paris Fashion Week. She'd send him sketches. One afternoon, he saw her at a department store, but she was just folding shirts on a display table. She was wearing a store uniform. Lucas picked up a shirt. 'Is this from your latest collection?' he asked. Chloe looked at the shirt, then at him. She didn't answer. He put the shirt down, folded it neatly, and walked away. At the exit, he paused, looked back, and saw her still standing there, holding the shirt.
text_zh: 卢卡斯的朋友克洛伊说她是时装设计师，在巴黎时装周上展示作品。她会给他发草图。一天下午，他在百货公司看到她，但她只是在展示桌上叠衬衫。她穿着店里的制服。卢卡斯拿起一件衬衫。“这是你最新系列的吗？”他问。克洛伊看了看衬衫，又看了看他。她没有回答。他把衬衫放下，叠整齐，然后走开了。在出口处，他停下来，回头看了看，看到她仍然站在那里，手里拿着那件衬衫。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: Grace's friend Sam had been claiming to be a pilot for a private jet company. He'd tell her about flights to Europe. Then she saw him at the airport, but he was just a baggage handler, loading suitcases onto a cart. He was wearing a high-visibility vest. Grace stood by the window, watching him. He saw her and nearly dropped a bag. She walked outside to the curb. When he came out with a cart, she said, 'Nice landing.' He didn't reply. She got into a taxi and slammed the door, not looking back.
text_zh: 格蕾丝的朋友萨姆一直声称自己是私人飞机公司的飞行员。他会跟她讲去欧洲的航班。然后她在机场看到他，但他只是个行李搬运工，把行李箱装上手推车。他穿着高能见度背心。格蕾丝站在窗边看着他。他看见她，差点掉了一个包。她走到外面的路边。当他推着手推车出来时，她说：“降落得不错。”他没有回答。她上了一辆出租车，砰地关上门，没有回头。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: Aiden's friend Emma said she was a professor of archaeology. She'd tell him about digs and discoveries. One day, he saw her at a local library, but she was just shelving books in the history section. She was wearing a cardigan, pushing a cart. Aiden walked up to the cart. 'Find any fossils lately?' he asked. Emma looked at the books, then at him. She picked up a book on ancient Egypt and handed it to him. He took it, but didn't open it. He just held it, his grip firm, and walked to the checkout desk.
text_zh: 艾登的朋友艾玛说她是考古学教授。她会跟他讲发掘和发现。有一天，他在当地图书馆看到她，但她只是在历史区整理书籍。她穿着开衫，推着手推车。艾登走到手推车前。“最近发现什么化石了吗？”他问。艾玛看了看书，又看了看他。她拿起一本关于古埃及的书，递给他。他接过来，但没有打开。他只是拿着，握得很紧，然后走向借书台。

topic: Someone discovers their friend has been lying about their job
text_en: Sophie's friend Jack had been telling her he was a journalist for a major newspaper. He'd share his 'articles' with her. Then she saw him at a newsstand, but he was just the vendor, handing out newspapers. He was wearing a worn jacket, counting change. Sophie walked up to the stand. 'I'll take a copy of your latest front page,' she said. Jack looked at the stack of papers, then at her. He handed her one. She looked at the headline, then at him. She put the paper back on the pile and walked away, her steps slow and deliberate.
text_zh: 苏菲的朋友杰克一直告诉她，他是一家大报社的记者。他会和她分享他的“文章”。然后她在报摊看到他，但他只是个摊主，在分发报纸。他穿着破旧的外套，数着零钱。苏菲走到报摊前。“我要一份你最新一期的头版，”她说。杰克看了看那叠报纸，又看了看她。他递给她一份。她看了看头条，又看了看他。她把报纸放回那叠上，然后走开了，脚步缓慢而坚定。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: Mara heard the soft click of the bathroom door and the low murmur of his voice. He'd been taking calls in there all week, always with the water running. She set down the dish she was drying and walked over, pressing her ear to the wood. The words were muffled, but the tone was intimate, conspiratorial. When he came out, his face was smooth, a practiced smile. 'Work,' he said. She nodded, but her hands were cold. She followed him into the kitchen, her voice tight as she asked about his day, watching for the flinch she knew would come.
text_zh: 玛拉听到浴室门轻轻咔哒一声，还有他低沉的声音。他整个星期都在那里接电话，总是开着水龙头。她放下正在擦干的盘子，走过去，把耳朵贴在木门上。话语模糊不清，但语气亲密，像是在密谋什么。他出来时，脸上平静，带着一个练习过的微笑。“工作，”他说。她点点头，但双手冰凉。她跟着他走进厨房，声音紧绷地问他今天过得怎么样，注视着他，等待她知道会出现的退缩。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: The third time Liam excused himself to the balcony, leaving his dinner to cool, Paula's fork stopped midway to her mouth. She watched his silhouette through the glass, shoulders hunched, phone pressed to his ear. When he came back, he didn't meet her eyes. 'Wrong number,' he said, sitting down, picking up his fork as if nothing had happened. Paula placed her own fork down with a deliberate tap. 'Must be a persistent wrong number,' she said. The words came out clipped, each one measured. He chewed, swallowed, and shot her a look that said 'drop it.' She didn't.
text_zh: 利亚姆第三次借口去阳台，让晚餐放凉时，宝拉的叉子停在半空中。她透过玻璃看着他的身影，肩膀佝偻，手机贴在耳边。他回来时，没有看她的眼睛。“打错了，”他说，坐下来，拿起叉子，好像什么都没发生过。宝拉故意把叉子放下，发出清脆的响声。“那一定是个执着的打错电话，”她说。话语简短，每个字都经过斟酌。他嚼着食物，咽下去，瞥了她一眼，那眼神在说“别问了”。她没有。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: Marta found him in the hallway, phone pressed to his ear. He mouthed 'work' and turned away. She stood there, arms crossed, watching his shoulders hunch. When he finally hung up, she asked who it was. 'Just a client,' he said, not meeting her eyes. She stepped closer, voice flat. 'Clients call during the day. You've been slipping out at night.' He started to explain, but she held up a hand. 'No. I've heard enough.' She walked to the bedroom and began pulling his things from the closet, stacking them by the door. He followed, protesting, but she didn't stop.
text_zh: 玛尔塔在走廊里发现他，手机贴在耳边。他无声地说“工作”，然后转过身去。她站在那里，双臂交叉，看着他的肩膀佝偻。他终于挂断电话时，她问是谁。“只是个客户，”他说，没有看她的眼睛。她走近一步，声音平淡。“客户白天打电话。你晚上一直溜出去。”他开始解释，但她举起手。“不。我听够了。”她走到卧室，开始把他的东西从衣柜里拿出来，堆在门边。他跟着，抗议着，但她没有停下。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: The phone buzzed on the nightstand, and Leo reached for it, but Dana grabbed it first. 'Who is it?' she asked. 'Nobody,' he said, snatching it back. She watched him type a quick reply, then pocket it. Later, she found him on the balcony, whispering. She slid the door open, and he jumped. 'You're hiding something,' she said. He laughed it off, but she wasn't amused. She took his phone from the table and held it out. 'Unlock it. Now.' He hesitated, and she felt a heat rise in her chest. She set the phone down and walked away, her jaw tight.
text_zh: 床头柜上的手机嗡嗡作响，利奥伸手去拿，但达娜先抓住了。“是谁？”她问。“没人，”他说，抢了回去。她看着他快速打了一条回复，然后放进口袋。后来，她发现他在阳台上低声说话。她拉开滑门，他吓了一跳。“你在隐瞒什么，”她说。他一笑置之，但她并不觉得好笑。她从桌上拿起他的手机，递出去。“解锁。现在。”他犹豫了，她感到胸口升起一股热气。她放下手机，走开了，下巴紧绷。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: From the kitchen, Ana could see him pacing in the backyard, phone in hand, his free hand gesturing as if the person on the other end could see him. She set down her coffee cup. The same thing had happened yesterday, and the day before. When he came in, all smiles, she pointed at the empty coffee mug. 'You want a refill?' she asked. He said yes, and she filled it, but as she handed it over, she said, 'You know, I can hear the faucet running in the garden. There's no one out there to water.' His grin flickered, and she took a long, slow sip from her own cup, watching him over the rim.
text_zh: 从厨房里，安娜能看到他在后院踱步，手里拿着手机，空着的手比划着，好像电话那头的人能看到他。她放下咖啡杯。昨天和前天也发生了同样的事。他进来时，满脸笑容，她指着空咖啡杯。“你想续杯吗？”她问。他说好，她倒了，但递给他时，她说：“你知道吗，我能听到花园里的水龙头在流水。那里没有人需要浇水。”他的笑容闪烁了一下，她慢慢啜饮自己杯中的咖啡，从杯沿上方看着他。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: Marcus had grown used to Bianca's frequent trips to the basement, her whispered conversations drifting up through the heating vents. He'd always given her space, but tonight, he wanted the truth. He waited by the basement door, and when she came up, he blocked the way. 'I need to know who you're talking to,' he said. His arms were crossed, his jaw set. She tried to step around him, but he didn't budge. 'It's private,' she said. 'Our marriage isn't,' he replied, his voice flat. She looked away, and he felt his chest tighten, a hot weight settling there.
text_zh: 马库斯已经习惯了比安卡频繁去地下室，她低声的谈话从暖气通风口飘上来。他一直给她空间，但今晚，他想要真相。他在地下室门口等着，她上来时，他挡住了路。“我需要知道你在和谁说话，”他说。他双臂交叉，下巴紧绷。她试图绕过他，但他没有动。“这是私事，”她说。“我们的婚姻不是，”他回答，声音平淡。她把目光移开，他感到胸口收紧，一股热重的重量压在那里。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: Priya noticed the pattern: every evening, her husband excused himself to the garage, phone in hand. Tonight, she followed. He was leaning against the car, speaking in low tones. When he saw her, he hung up quickly. 'Who was that?' she asked. 'My sister,' he said, but his sister had called earlier, and Priya knew her voice. She crossed her arms. 'You're lying.' He shoved the phone in his pocket. She stepped closer, her voice steady but sharp. 'I've been patient. But this ends now. Either you tell me, or I start making calls of my own.' He stared at her, and she didn't look away.
text_zh: 普里亚注意到了这个模式：每天晚上，她丈夫都借口去车库，手里拿着手机。今晚，她跟了过去。他靠在车上，低声说话。他看到她时，迅速挂断了。“那是谁？”她问。“我妹妹，”他说，但他妹妹早些时候打过电话，普里亚知道她的声音。她双臂交叉。“你在撒谎。”他把手机塞进口袋。她走近一步，声音平稳但尖锐。“我一直很耐心。但这现在结束。要么你告诉我，要么我开始自己打电话。”他盯着她，她没有移开视线。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: The phone was face-down on the counter when it vibrated. David's hand shot out, patting it down, turning it over, and he read the screen with a flicker that Nadia caught. He stepped into the pantry, and she heard the soft murmur of his voice between the shelves of canned goods. When he came out, he was holding a bag of coffee that had to be a pretext. She took it from him without a word and put it on the shelf. 'You're running out of excuses,' she said, walking past him. She felt his surprise, but she didn't turn back, her spine rigid.
text_zh: 手机屏幕朝下放在柜台上，它振动了。大卫的手迅速伸出，拍了拍它，翻过来，他看了一眼屏幕，闪过一丝娜迪亚捕捉到的神情。他走进食品储藏室，她听到他低沉的声音在罐头货架之间传来。他出来时，拿着一袋咖啡，那肯定是个借口。她一言不发地接过咖啡，放在架子上。“你的借口快用完了，”她说，走过他身边。她感到他的惊讶，但她没有回头，脊背挺直。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: The phone rang during dinner, and Tom excused himself, taking it outside. Alice stared at her plate, listening to his muffled voice. When he returned, she asked, 'Who was that?' 'Wrong number,' he said, but his hand trembled. She pushed her chair back. 'Wrong numbers don't call every night at the same time.' He shrugged, but she saw the guilt. She grabbed his phone from the counter. 'Give it back,' he said, reaching. She held it behind her back. 'You'll have to take it.' He didn't move. She set the phone down and walked to the door. 'When you're ready to tell the truth, you know where to find me.'
text_zh: 晚餐时电话响了，汤姆借口离开，拿着电话出去了。爱丽丝盯着盘子，听着他模糊的声音。他回来时，她问：“那是谁？”“打错了，”他说，但他的手在颤抖。她推开椅子。“打错的电话不会每晚同一时间打来。”他耸耸肩，但她看到了内疚。她从柜台上抓起他的手机。“还给我，”他说，伸手去拿。她把手背在身后。“你得自己来拿。”他没有动。她放下手机，走向门口。“当你准备好说真话时，你知道在哪里能找到我。”

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: Nina sat on the couch, pretending to read, while her partner paced in the kitchen, whispering. She caught fragments—'not now,' 'I'll call you back.' When he emerged, she closed her book. 'You've been doing that a lot lately.' He smiled. 'Just my mom.' But his mother had visited last week, and she'd mentioned he never calls. Nina stood, folding her arms. 'Don't insult me.' His smile faded. She walked past him, picked up his phone from the charger, and held it out. 'Call her. Right now. I'll listen.' He didn't move, and her chest tightened.
text_zh: 尼娜坐在沙发上，假装看书，而她的伴侣在厨房里踱步，低声说话。她捕捉到片段——“现在不行”，“我稍后打给你”。他出来时，她合上书。“你最近经常这样。”他笑了。“只是我妈。”但他母亲上周来过，她提到他从不打电话。尼娜站起来，双臂交叉。“别侮辱我。”他的笑容消失了。她走过他身边，从充电器上拿起他的手机，递出去。“打给她。现在。我听着。”他没有动，她的胸口收紧。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: The bedroom door clicked shut, and Maya heard the low murmur of a call. She pressed her ear to the wood, catching only 'I'll handle it.' When her husband came out, she was standing there. 'Who was that?' 'A colleague,' he said, avoiding her gaze. She followed him into the kitchen. 'At this hour?' He opened the fridge, not answering. She slammed the door shut. 'Look at me.' He turned, and she saw the flicker of guilt. 'I'm not stupid,' she said. 'You've been slipping away for weeks. I want the truth, or I'm gone.' He opened his mouth, but she was already walking.
text_zh: 卧室的门咔哒一声关上了，玛雅听到一阵低声的通话。她把耳朵贴在门上，只听到一句“我会处理的”。她丈夫出来时，她就站在那里。“那是谁？”“一个同事，”他说，避开了她的目光。她跟着他进了厨房。“这个时间？”他打开冰箱，没有回答。她猛地关上门。“看着我。”他转过身，她看到了那一闪而过的愧疚。“我不傻，”她说。“你几个星期以来一直在偷偷溜走。我要真相，否则我就走。”他张了张嘴，但她已经走开了。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: Mara set the kettle down harder than she meant to, the clatter sharp in the quiet kitchen. Through the window, she watched Ben pace the far end of the garden, phone pressed to his ear, his free hand slicing the air. He’d said it was work, but his shoulders were too tight, his voice too low. When he turned and caught her staring, he ended the call abruptly, pocketed the phone, and smiled. She didn’t smile back. She poured the water, the steam rising, and decided she would ask him tonight, and she would not let him deflect.
text_zh: 玛拉把水壶放得比预想的要重，清脆的响声在安静的厨房里显得格外刺耳。透过窗户，她看见本在花园尽头来回踱步，手机贴着耳朵，空着的那只手在空中比划着。他说是工作的事，但他的肩膀绷得太紧，声音压得太低。当他转过身，发现她在盯着看时，他猛地结束了通话，把手机揣进口袋，笑了笑。她没有回以微笑。她倒着水，蒸汽升腾，决定今晚一定要问他，而且不会让他岔开话题。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: The phone buzzed on the counter, and Rachel saw her partner glance at it, then ignore it. When it buzzed again, he picked it up and walked to the bathroom. She waited, counting the seconds. He emerged, face flushed. 'Wrong number,' he said. She didn't believe him. 'Then why did you hide?' He shrugged. She grabbed his arm. 'I've watched you take those calls for a month. I know it's not work. I know it's not your family. So who is it?' He pulled away, and she felt her jaw clench. 'Don't walk away from me,' she said, but he did.
text_zh: 手机在台面上嗡嗡作响，瑞秋看到她的伴侣瞥了一眼，然后没去理会。当它再次响起时，他拿起手机走进了浴室。她等着，数着秒数。他出来了，脸涨得通红。“打错了，”他说。她不相信。“那你为什么要躲起来？”他耸了耸肩。她抓住他的胳膊。“我看你接这些电话已经一个月了。我知道不是工作的事。我知道不是你家人。那到底是谁？”他挣脱开，她感到自己的下巴绷紧了。“别从我身边走开，”她说，但他还是走了。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: The garage light was on, and through the window, Kate saw her husband pacing, phone to his ear. She opened the door quietly. He didn't notice. 'I'll tell her soon,' he said, and her stomach dropped. She stepped into the light, and he froze. 'Tell me what?' she asked, her voice cold. He hung up, stammering. She crossed her arms. 'I've heard enough. You've been lying to me.' He reached for her, but she stepped back. 'Don't. I'm going to my mother's. When you're ready to explain, you can call.' She turned, leaving him in the garage, the phone still in his hand.
text_zh: 车库的灯亮着，透过窗户，凯特看见她丈夫在来回踱步，手机贴着耳朵。她轻轻打开门。他没有注意到。“我很快就会告诉她，”他说，她的心猛地一沉。她走进灯光里，他僵住了。“告诉我什么？”她问道，声音冰冷。他挂断电话，结结巴巴地说。她双臂交叉。“我听得够多了。你一直在骗我。”他伸手想拉她，但她后退了一步。“别碰我。我要去我妈那儿。等你准备好解释了，再打电话给我。”她转身离开，把他留在车库里，手机还握在他手里。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: The phone vibrated on the table, and Liam snatched it before Ana could see. 'Who's that?' she asked. 'Nobody,' he said, typing quickly. She watched his thumbs move, a knot forming in her stomach. Later, she found him in the backyard, whispering. She stood at the door, listening. When he saw her, he hung up. 'You've been doing this all week,' she said. He put the phone away. She walked over and held out her hand. 'Give it to me.' He hesitated, and she felt a surge of heat. 'I said give it.' He handed it over, and she scrolled through the call log, her face hardening.
text_zh: 手机在桌上震动，利亚姆在安娜看到之前一把抓了起来。“那是谁？”她问。“没谁，”他说，手指飞快地打字。她看着他的拇指移动，心里打了个结。后来，她在后院找到了他，他正在低声说着什么。她站在门口听着。当他看到她时，他挂断了电话。“你这一整个星期都在这样，”她说。他把手机收了起来。她走过去，伸出手。“把它给我。”他犹豫了一下，她感到一股怒火涌上来。“我说了，给我。”他递了过去，她翻看着通话记录，脸色越来越难看。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: The phone rang, and Marco excused himself, stepping into the closet. Julia heard the click of the door, then his muffled voice. When he emerged, she was waiting. 'Who was that?' she asked. 'My brother,' he said, but his brother was out of the country and never called at night. She didn't say anything, just stared at him. He shifted his weight. 'Why are you looking at me like that?' She walked past him, picked up his phone, and dialed his brother's number. It went to voicemail. She held up the phone. 'He's not answering. Because he didn't call you.' Marco's face went pale.
text_zh: 电话响了，马尔科借口离开，走进了壁橱。朱莉娅听到门咔哒一声关上，然后是他闷闷的声音。当他出来时，她正等着。“那是谁？”她问。“我哥，”他说，但他哥在国外，而且从不在晚上打电话。她什么也没说，只是盯着他。他挪了挪重心。“你为什么那样看着我？”她从他身边走过，拿起他的手机，拨了她哥的号码。电话转到了语音信箱。她举起手机。“他没接。因为他根本没给你打过电话。”马尔科的脸色变得苍白。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: The bathroom door was locked, and through it, Rosa heard her partner's low voice. She knocked. 'Everything okay?' 'Yeah,' he called, but the voice was too quick. When he came out, she asked, 'Who were you talking to?' He said, 'Just a friend,' but he wouldn't meet her eyes. She followed him into the living room. 'A friend? You've been locked in there every night.' He sat down, not answering. She stood over him. 'I've been patient, but I'm done. I want the truth.' He stared at his hands, and she felt a cold weight settle in her chest. She turned and walked out.
text_zh: 浴室的门锁着，罗莎透过门听到她伴侣低沉的声音。她敲了敲门。“没事吧？”“没事，”他喊道，但声音太快了。当他出来时，她问：“你在跟谁说话？”他说：“就一个朋友，”但他不敢看她的眼睛。她跟着他进了客厅。“一个朋友？你每天晚上都把自己锁在里面。”他坐下来，没有回答。她站在他面前。“我一直很有耐心，但我受够了。我要真相。”他盯着自己的双手，她感到一股寒意沉甸甸地压在胸口。她转身走了出去。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: The phone buzzed on the nightstand, and Daniel reached for it, but Clara got there first. 'Don't,' he said, too late. She looked at the screen—an unknown number. 'Who is this?' she asked. He grabbed the phone. 'None of your business.' She felt a flash of heat. 'None of my business? We're married.' He turned away, and she grabbed his arm. 'Look at me. You've been taking calls at all hours, hiding in the other room. I'm not going to let this slide.' He pulled free, and she stood there, her hands shaking, as he walked out the door.
text_zh: 手机在床头柜上嗡嗡作响，丹尼尔伸手去拿，但克拉拉先拿到了。“别动，”他说，但已经太晚了。她看了看屏幕——一个陌生号码。“这是谁？”她问。他抢过手机。“不关你的事。”她感到一阵怒火。“不关我的事？我们是夫妻。”他转过身去，她抓住他的胳膊。“看着我。你一直不分昼夜地接电话，躲在另一个房间里。我不会就这么算了。”他挣脱开来，她站在那里，双手颤抖，看着他走出了门。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: The kitchen light was off, and through the dark, Yara saw her husband's face lit by his phone. He was smiling, whispering. She flipped on the light, and he jumped. 'Who is that?' she asked. He said, 'A coworker,' but he tucked the phone into his pocket. She walked over. 'A coworker? You've been smiling like that for weeks.' He didn't answer. She reached for his pocket, but he stepped back. 'Don't,' he said. She stopped, her eyes narrowing. 'Fine. But I'm not staying here while you hide things from me.' She grabbed her keys and left, the door clicking shut behind her.
text_zh: 厨房的灯关着，黑暗中，亚拉看到她丈夫的脸被手机屏幕照亮。他在微笑，低声说着什么。她打开灯，他吓了一跳。“那是谁？”她问。他说：“一个同事，”但他把手机塞进了口袋。她走过去。“一个同事？你几个星期以来一直那样笑。”他没有回答。她伸手去够他的口袋，但他后退了一步。“别动，”他说。她停下来，眯起眼睛。“好。但我不会留在这里，让你对我隐瞒事情。”她抓起钥匙离开了，门在她身后咔哒一声关上了。

topic: A person discovers their partner has been taking secret phone calls
text_en: The phone rang, and Ben excused himself, taking it to the study. Hannah waited, listening to the muffled tones. When he came out, she asked, 'Who was that?' He said, 'A client,' but he was too calm. She followed him to the kitchen. 'A client? You've never taken client calls at home before.' He poured a glass of water, not looking at her. She stepped closer. 'I've noticed. Every night, you disappear. I'm not going to pretend it's nothing.' He set the glass down, and she saw his jaw tighten. She crossed her arms. 'I want the truth, or I'm done.' He didn't speak, and she felt her resolve harden.
text_zh: 电话响了，本借口离开，拿着电话去了书房。汉娜等着，听着那模糊的声音。当他出来时，她问：“那是谁？”他说：“一个客户，”但他太镇定了。她跟着他进了厨房。“一个客户？你以前从不在家接客户电话。”他倒了一杯水，没有看她。她走近一步。“我注意到了。每天晚上，你都会消失。我不会假装这没什么。”他放下杯子，她看到他的下巴绷紧了。她双臂交叉。“我要真相，否则我们就完了。”他没有说话，她感到自己的决心更加坚定了。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: Maya stepped outside with her coffee, expecting to see her sedan in the driveway. Instead, there was a rectangle of darker pavement, oil stains still fresh. She blinked, walked to the curb, looked both ways. The tow truck must have come early, despite the permit she'd paid for displayed clearly in the window. She pulled out her phone, found the towing company's number, and called. The woman on the line was polite but firm: the permit had expired at midnight, they had records. Maya knew she'd renewed it that morning, but the argument went nowhere. She hung up, stood in the empty driveway, and tried to figure out how to get her car back without paying their ransom.
text_zh: 玛雅端着咖啡走出门，本以为会在车道上看到自己的轿车。然而，那里只有一片颜色更深的柏油路面，油渍还新鲜。她眨了眨眼，走到路边，左右张望。拖车公司一定来得很早，尽管她付费购买的许可证就清晰地展示在车窗上。她掏出手机，找到拖车公司的号码，打了过去。电话那头的女人礼貌但坚定：许可证在午夜就过期了，他们有记录。玛雅知道她那天早上才续的费，但争论毫无结果。她挂了电话，站在空荡荡的车道上，试图想办法在不付赎金的情况下把车弄回来。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: Marta spotted the empty driveway before she even parked. Her sedan was gone. She checked the garage, then the street, then called the tow company listed on the sign that had been jammed into her lawn. They claimed a neighbor complained about an abandoned vehicle. Abandoned. Her car, with the fresh oil change and the child seat in back. She gripped the phone until her knuckles went white. She demanded the lot address, then drove there, rehearsing what she would say to the clerk, her jaw tight, her foot heavy on the gas.
text_zh: 玛尔塔还没停车就注意到了空荡荡的车道。她的轿车不见了。她检查了车库，又看了街道，然后拨打了插在她草坪上的标牌上列出的拖车公司的电话。他们声称有邻居投诉说有一辆废弃车辆。废弃。她的车，刚换过机油，后座还有儿童座椅。她紧握电话，指节发白。她要求提供停车场地址，然后开车过去，一路上排练着要对职员说的话，下巴紧绷，脚重重地踩在油门上。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: Mara backed her sedan down the driveway, then spotted the empty curb. Her throat tightened. She had parked in her own gravel strip, not an inch over the line. The neighbor's visitor had done this before, complaining about the old car's oil stain. She found the tow company's card wedged under the wiper, the one with the red lettering. She stood in the yard, fists pressed into her coat pockets, staring at the ruts her tires had left. She would call them, yes, but she would also file a formal complaint with the city, and she would not stop until they acknowledged their mistake.
text_zh: 玛拉把她的轿车倒出车道，然后发现了空荡荡的路边。她的喉咙发紧。她明明把车停在自己家的碎石带上，一寸都没有越线。邻居的访客以前就这么干过，抱怨那辆旧车的油渍。她在雨刮器下发现了一张拖车公司的卡片，就是那张红色字体的。她站在院子里，双拳抵在外套口袋里，盯着轮胎留下的车辙。她会给他们打电话，是的，但她也会向市政府正式投诉，而且不等到他们承认错误，她绝不会罢休。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: Priya set down her grocery bags and stared at the empty asphalt. Her hatchback was gone. She checked the driveway camera on her phone; a flatbed had hooked it at dawn. She called the city's non-emergency line, and a dispatcher told her the street-sweeping schedule had changed. She had parked legally, she insisted, but the dispatcher was bored and unhelpful. Priya hung up and slammed her palm on the counter. She drove to the impound lot, her lips pressed thin, already planning to demand a written apology and a refund.
text_zh: 普里亚放下购物袋，盯着空荡荡的柏油路面。她的两厢车不见了。她查看了手机上的车道摄像头；一辆平板拖车在黎明时分钩走了她的车。她拨打了城市的非紧急热线，一位调度员告诉她街道清扫时间表改了。她坚持说自己是合法停车，但调度员态度敷衍，毫无帮助。普里亚挂了电话，手掌重重拍在柜台上。她开车去了扣押场，嘴唇紧抿，已经在计划要求书面道歉和退款。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: The space in front of the house was bare, and for a moment Dan thought he'd parked elsewhere. Then he remembered the car was right there this morning. He found the citation under the wiper of a neighbor's car, stuck there by the wind. It said his tags were expired, but he had renewed them online. Dan called the tow company, and the man on the phone laughed and said, 'Not my problem.' Dan's face burned. He got in his wife's car and followed the directions, gripping the wheel, muttering about incompetence and hidden fees.
text_zh: 房子前面的空地空着，有那么一瞬间，丹以为自己把车停在了别处。然后他想起今天早上车明明就在那里。他在邻居车的雨刮器下发现了罚单，是被风吹到那里的。罚单上说他的车牌过期了，但他明明在网上续过了。丹打电话给拖车公司，电话那头的男人笑着说：“不关我的事。”丹的脸涨得通红。他上了妻子的车，按照指示开过去，紧握方向盘，嘟囔着无能之辈和隐藏费用。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: Leah's kids were waiting for school pick-up. She ran out to the car, keys in hand, and found nothing. Just a bare patch of ground. She called her husband, who was already at work. He said he'd moved it, no, he hadn't. She called the school, said she'd be late. Then she started calling tow companies. The third one said, "Yeah, we got one from that address." She asked why. They cited a zoning violation, something about commercial vehicle registration. She drove a sedan. They must have made a mistakeKahenera. She told them, but the dispatcher was unmoved. She stood in the driveway, phone in one hand, keys in the other, vibrating with a frustration that had nowhere to go.
text_zh: 利亚的孩子们正等着放学接他们。她拿着钥匙跑出来，却发现什么都没有。只有一片光秃秃的地面。她打电话给已经上班的丈夫。他说他挪了车，不，他没有。她打电话给学校，说她会迟到。然后她开始给拖车公司打电话。第三家说：“是的，我们从那个地址拖了一辆车。”她问为什么。他们引用了分区违规，说是商用车辆注册的问题。她开的是轿车。他们一定搞错了。她告诉他们，但调度员不为所动。她站在车道上，一手拿着手机，一手拿着钥匙，满腹的挫败感无处发泄。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: Nina came out with her coffee, ready to leave for work, and found the driveway empty. Her old Civic was gone. She checked her phone for a parking app notification; nothing. She called the police non-emergency line, and they transferred her to the towing contractor. The woman said the car had been reported as a fire hazard. A fire hazard? Nina had parked it there for a decade. She set her mug down hard, cracking the ceramic. She asked for the address, then drove there, her jaw clenched, planning to speak to a supervisor.
text_zh: 尼娜端着咖啡出来，准备去上班，却发现车道空了。她那辆旧思域不见了。她查看手机上的停车应用通知；什么也没有。她拨打警方非紧急热线，被转接到拖车承包商。那个女人说这辆车被举报为火灾隐患。火灾隐患？尼娜在那里停了十年了。她重重地放下杯子，陶瓷裂了。她要了地址，然后开车过去，下巴紧绷，打算找主管谈谈。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: Elliot walked out to find a bare patch of gravel where his coupe should have been. He circled the house, then saw the notice nailed to his fence: vehicle impounded for expired registration. He had paid that bill, he was sure. He called the county office, and a recorded voice told him to leave a message. He hung up and called again, then again. Each time, the same recording. He paced the porch, kicking a loose board. He finally drove to the lot, rehearsing a speech about paperwork errors and demanding to see the original complaint.
text_zh: 埃利奥特走出去，发现本该停着他双门轿车的地方只剩一片光秃秃的碎石。他绕了房子一圈，然后看到钉在栅栏上的通知：车辆因注册过期被扣押。他确信自己付过那笔账单。他打电话给县办公室，一个录音声音让他留言。他挂了电话又打，一遍又一遍。每次都是同样的录音。他在门廊上踱步，踢着一块松动的木板。最后他开车去了停车场，排练着关于文书错误的演讲，并要求查看原始投诉。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: The driveway was empty, and Rosa's stomach dropped. She had just washed her car yesterday. She called her husband, who said he hadn't moved it. She called the neighbors; none had seen anything. Then she noticed a folded paper in the mailbox: a notice from the homeowners' association about a parking violation. She had a permit sticker on the windshield. Rosa crumpled the notice and threw it into the yard. She called the association office, and when the receptionist put her on hold, she hung up and dialed the city to file a complaint.
text_zh: 车道空了，罗莎的心猛地一沉。她昨天刚洗了车。她打电话给丈夫，他说他没挪车。她打电话给邻居；没人看到什么。然后她注意到邮箱里有一张折叠的纸：业主协会关于停车违规的通知。她的挡风玻璃上有许可证贴纸。罗莎把通知揉成一团，扔进院子里。她打电话给协会办公室，当接待员让她稍等时，她挂了电话，拨通了市政府的电话投诉。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: Tom came home from a short errand and found the driveway empty. His motorcycle was gone too. He ran inside, checked the security app, and saw a tow truck hooking up his bike at noon. He called the company, and the dispatcher said the bike was in a no-parking zone, which was wrong; it was on his own property. Tom's voice rose, and he caught himself, then spoke slower, colder. He asked for the lot address and drove there, his hands tight on the wheel, thinking about the damage to the kickstand.
text_zh: 汤姆出去办了点小事回来，发现车道空了。他的摩托车也不见了。他跑进屋，查看安全应用，看到中午有一辆拖车钩走了他的摩托车。他打电话给公司，调度员说摩托车停在禁停区，这是错的；那是他自己的财产。汤姆的声音提高了，他克制住自己，然后说得更慢、更冷。他要了停车场地址，开车过去，双手紧紧握着方向盘，想着脚架可能受到的损坏。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: Paul had just washed his car the day before. It shone under the porch light. This morning, the driveway was clean and bare. He felt a spike of adrenaline, then a dull thud in his chest. He called his son, who borrowed the car sometimes, but his son said no. He called his wife, no. Then he called the towing line posted on the neighborhood app. Yes, they had it. They said the vehicle was unregistered, but Paul knew the registration was in the glove compartment, up to date. He told them, but they wouldn't budge. He walked into his garage, opened a drawer, pulled out the registration paperwork, and held it in his hand, staring at the dates, then crumpled it in a fist before smoothing it out again.
text_zh: 保罗前一天刚洗了车。车在门廊灯下闪闪发光。今天早上，车道干净而空旷。他感到一阵肾上腺素飙升，随后胸口传来沉闷的一击。他打电话给有时借车的儿子，但儿子说没有。他打电话给妻子，也没有。然后他拨打了社区应用上张贴的拖车热线。是的，他们拖走了。他们说车辆未注册，但保罗知道注册文件就在手套箱里，而且是最新的。他告诉他们，但他们不肯让步。他走进车库，打开一个抽屉，拿出注册文件，握在手里，盯着日期看，然后攥成一团，又再抚平。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: Ramona was a freelancer. Her car was her office, her studio space, her getaway. She walked out to run errands and saw only a chalk outline of grease on the asphalt. Her heart dropped. She called the towing company she found via a quick internet search. They had it. She asked why, and they said it was because of a plumbing emergency, her driveway was blocking access to a nearby fire hydrant. She knew there was no hydrant anywhere near her house. She asked to speak to a supervisor, was put on hold, then given a quote for release. She hung up, leaned against the porch railing, and tapped her foot, feeling a growing pressure behind her eyes as she calculated the cost and the injustice.
text_zh: 拉莫娜是个自由职业者。她的车就是她的办公室、她的工作室、她的逃离之所。她出门办事，只看到沥青路面上一个粉笔画的油渍轮廓。她的心一沉。她通过快速网络搜索找到了一家拖车公司。他们拖走了。她问为什么，他们说是因为管道紧急情况，她的车道挡住了附近消防栓的通道。她知道她家附近根本没有消防栓。她要求与主管通话，被搁置等待，然后得到了放车报价。她挂断电话，靠在门廊栏杆上，跺着脚，计算着费用和不公，感到眼后压力越来越大。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: The driveway was bare where his truck had been. Leon checked the house keys again, as if that would change what he saw. He had left the vehicle behind his own fence, with the gate shut. The tow truck must have hooked it through the open side, or maybe the neighbor had called it in. He walked the perimeter, scanning for a note, a card, any scrap of paper. Nothing. He went inside, poured a glass of water, and set it down without drinking. He picked up the phone, then put it down. He would find the company, and he would make them explain why they had taken what was not theirs to touch.
text_zh: 车道空荡荡的，他的卡车不见了。利昂又检查了一遍房门钥匙，好像这样就能改变他所看到的一切。他把车停在自己围栏后面，门是关着的。拖车一定是通过敞开的侧面钩走的，或者也许是邻居举报的。他绕着周边走了一圈，寻找纸条、卡片或任何纸片。什么都没有。他走进屋里，倒了一杯水，又放下没喝。他拿起电话，又放下。他会找到那家公司，让他们解释为什么拖走了不属于他们的东西。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: Gloria came home late from visiting a friend. She parked in her driveway, locked the door, went to bed. The next morning, she opened the curtains and saw bare pavement. She felt a jolt, like a missed step. She found the tow company's number on the city's website. They confirmed they'd towed it. The reason? A snow zone. It was July. She laughed, a humorless laugh, then said, "It's July." The clerk said, "That's what the record says." Gloria hung up, sat on her bed, and stared at the wall, her jaw clenched, her hands pressed into the mattress, as she mentally composed a strongly worded letter to the city about their absurd records.
text_zh: 格洛丽亚拜访朋友后深夜回家。她把车停在车道上，锁好门，上床睡觉。第二天早上，她拉开窗帘，看到光秃秃的路面。她感到一阵震动，就像踩空了一步。她在市政府网站上找到了拖车公司的号码。他们确认拖走了。原因？雪区。现在是七月。她笑了，毫无笑意，然后说：“现在是七月。”职员说：“记录上是这么写的。”格洛丽亚挂断电话，坐在床上，盯着墙壁，下巴紧绷，双手按在床垫上，心里默默起草一封措辞强硬的信给市政府，质问他们荒谬的记录。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: Jim was a handyman. He liked routine. He woke up, walked outside, saw his van was gone. His tools were in the back. His livelihood. He felt a sharp pain in his gut. He called the towing company that was listed on the sign down the street. Yes, they had it. They said it was parked across a private driveway. Jim knew his own driveway was not private. He said so. The dispatcher said, "We go by the report." Jim asked who made the report. They wouldn't say. Jim ended the call, went back inside, grabbed his phone and keys again, and headed out to the lot to get his van back, a cold, steady pressure building in his chest the whole way.
text_zh: 吉姆是个杂工。他喜欢规律。他醒来，走出去，看到他的面包车不见了。他的工具在后面。他的生计。他感到腹部一阵剧痛。他拨打了街边标志牌上列出的拖车公司电话。是的，他们拖走了。他们说车停在了私人车道上。吉姆知道自己的车道不是私人的。他这么说了。调度员说：“我们按报告行事。”吉姆问是谁做的报告。他们不肯说。吉姆结束通话，回到屋里，又拿起手机和钥匙，出发去停车场取回他的面包车，一路上胸口都压着一股冰冷而稳定的压力。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: Clara had just moved in. Her boxes were still in the hall. She parked her car in the driveway, her first night in her new home. In the morning, she saw the empty space variable and felt a sinking feeling. She called the towing number on a Peoria sticker. They had it. They said the previous owner's permit had expiredaberration, and the system hadn't been updated. She explained she'd just bought the house, but they didn't care. She stood in the empty driveway, surrounded by unpacked boxes, and felt a wave of helplessness that turned quickly to a simmering frustration. She called her real estate agent, her voice tight, asking who was supposed to handle this, and in the meantime, she couldn't even go get coffees.
text_zh: 克拉拉刚搬进来。她的箱子还在门厅里。她把车停在车道上，这是她新家的第一晚。早上，她看到那个空位，感到一阵沮丧。她拨打了皮奥里亚贴纸上的拖车号码。他们拖走了。他们说前房主的许可证已过期，系统没有更新。她解释说她刚买了这栋房子，但他们不在乎。她站在空荡荡的车道上，周围是未拆封的箱子，感到一阵无助，很快变成了一股酝酿中的愤怒。她打电话给她的房地产经纪人，声音紧绷，问谁该负责处理这件事，而与此同时，她连咖啡都买不了。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: Miles was a teacher. He had a final exam to give. He walked to his car and found nothing. He checked his watch, pressed his hand against his forehead. He called the towing company. They had it. They said it had been left running, but he knew he had not left it running. He told them, but they said they had a video. He asked for proof. They said they'd mail it. He said he needed his car now. They said he could come pay the release fee. He walked back inside, called a colleague to cover his class, and stood in the kitchen, gripping the counter, thinking about all the bureaucratic steps ahead, his knuckles white.
text_zh: 迈尔斯是一名教师。他有一场期末考试要监考。他走向他的车，发现什么都没有。他看了看手表，用手按着额头。他打电话给拖车公司。他们拖走了。他们说车当时没熄火，但他知道自己没有让车保持运转。他告诉他们，但他们说他们有视频。他要求看证据。他们说会邮寄给他。他说他现在就需要车。他们说可以来付放车费。他走回屋里，打电话让同事代课，然后站在厨房里，紧紧抓着台面，想着前面所有官僚程序，指节发白。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: Aisha was an artist. She painted in her studio, which was in her garage. She went out to get more paint from her car and saw it was missing. She felt a cold grip around her stomach. She called the towing company that was listed on the building's bulletin board. They had it. They said it was on private property, but it was her property. They said the owner of the property had complained. She said she was the owner. They said they had a signature. She asked to see it. They said she could come look. She stood in the driveway, hands on her hips, then paced back and forth, her thoughts racing, picturing the confiscation of her belongings, and a hot, focused energy built up in her chest.
text_zh: 艾莎是一名艺术家。她在车库里画画，那是她的工作室。她出去从车里拿更多颜料，发现车不见了。她感到胃部一阵冰冷。她拨打了大楼公告栏上列出的拖车公司电话。他们拖走了。他们说车停在私人财产上，但那是她的财产。他们说财产所有者投诉了。她说她就是所有者。他们说他们有签名。她要求看。他们说可以过来看。她站在车道上，双手叉腰，然后来回踱步，思绪飞转，想象着自己的财物被没收，一股炽热而专注的能量在胸口积聚。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: Rosa stood on the porch, coffee cooling in her hand, watching the empty spot where her coupe had been. She had parked it there last night, under the carport, with the garage door shut behind it. Someone had opened the door, or perhaps the lock had failed. She walked to the street, checked the curb for chalk marks, checked the mailbox for a notice. Nothing. She called the non-emergency line, her voice flat, and asked for the tow records. When they told her to wait, she held the phone tight, jaw set. She would not let this slide. She would follow every procedure, every appeal, until the mistake was corrected.
text_zh: 罗莎站在门廊上，手中的咖啡渐渐变凉，看着她的双门轿车曾经停放的空白位置。她昨晚把车停在那里，在车棚下，车库门在后面关着。有人打开了门，或者也许锁坏了。她走到街上，检查路缘是否有粉笔标记，检查邮箱是否有通知。什么都没有。她拨打非紧急热线，声音平淡，要求查看拖车记录。当他们让她等待时，她紧紧握着电话，下巴紧绷。她不会让这件事就这么过去。她会遵循每一个程序，每一次申诉，直到错误被纠正。

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text_en: Lena stepped outside to water her plants and saw the empty driveway. Her compact car was gone. She checked her pockets for the keys; they were in her hand. She called the local police, and they gave her the number for a private towing company. The man on the line said the car was blocking a driveway, which was impossible; her driveway was the only one. Lena's face grew hot. She wrote down the address, then hung up and grabbed her jacket, her movements sharp, ready to argue with anyone who got in her way.
text_zh: 莉娜出门给植物浇水，看到空荡荡的车道。她的小型车不见了。她检查口袋找钥匙；钥匙在她手里。她打电话给当地警方，他们给了她一家私人拖车公司的号码。电话那头的男人说车挡住了车道，这不可能；她的车道是唯一的。莉娜的脸热了起来。她记下地址，然后挂断电话，抓起夹克，动作利落，准备和任何挡路的人争辩。

topic: A person finds out their article was published under someone else's name
text_en: Marta’s byline sat above the article she’d drafted over a month of late nights, the one about the harbor’s silent decline. She’d submitted it to the regional magazine, waited, and received only a polite rejection. Now, flipping through the new issue in the waiting room, she saw her own phrases, her interviews, even her odd metaphor about the rusted buoys—all under a man’s name she didn’t recognize. Her jaw tightened. She folded the magazine, slid it into her bag, and walked to the editor’s office. She knocked once, already planning her opening sentence, her hand steady on the handle.
text_zh: 玛尔塔的署名出现在她花了一个多月熬夜起草的文章上方，那篇关于港口悄然衰落的文章。她把它提交给了地区杂志，等待，只收到一封礼貌的拒绝信。现在，在候诊室里翻阅新一期杂志时，她看到了自己的措辞、她的采访，甚至她关于生锈浮标的奇特比喻——全都署在一个她不认识的男人名下。她的下巴绷紧了。她合上杂志，把它滑进包里，走向编辑办公室。她敲了一下门，已经在构思她的开场白，手稳稳地放在门把手上。

topic: A person finds out their article was published under someone else's name
text_en: Leo found out at the staff meeting when his colleague Clara was praised for the article he'd written about coastal erosion. He sat still, his hands folded on the table, while Clara smiled and accepted the congratulations. Afterward, he cornered her in the hallway. 'That piece about the tide gauges—where did you get your data?' he asked, his voice even. Clara looked away. Leo nodded slowly and walked to his desk, where he opened his original manuscript, comparing it line by line to the published version. He printed both and placed them side by side, then waited for the editor to arrive.
text_zh: 利奥在员工会议上发现，他写的关于海岸侵蚀的文章被同事克拉拉表扬了。他坐着不动，双手交叉放在桌上，而克拉拉微笑着接受祝贺。会后，他在走廊里拦住她。“那篇关于潮位计的文章——你的数据是从哪里来的？”他问道，声音平稳。克拉拉移开了目光。利奥慢慢点了点头，走回自己的办公桌，打开原始手稿，逐行与已发表版本进行比较。他打印了两份，并排放置，然后等待编辑到来。

topic: A person finds out their article was published under someone else's name
text_en: Priya's article on community gardens appeared online under the name of a senior writer, Raj. She read it on her phone during lunch, her stomach clenching at each familiar sentence. She put the phone face down on the table, then picked it up again. She emailed the web editor: 'There seems to be a mistake in the byline for the garden piece. I wrote that.' The reply came quickly: 'Raj edited it significantly.' Priya stared at the response. She had not seen any edits. She wrote back, attaching her original draft with timestamps, and asked for a correction. She then closed her laptop and walked outside, her hands still trembling slightly.
text_zh: 普里亚关于社区花园的文章在网上以资深作家拉吉的名义发表。她在午餐时用手机阅读，每看到熟悉的句子，胃就一阵紧缩。她把手机屏幕朝下放在桌上，然后又拿起来。她给网络编辑发邮件：“花园那篇文章的署名似乎有误。那是我写的。”回复很快：“拉吉大幅编辑过。”普里亚盯着回复。她没有看到任何编辑。她回信，附上带有时间戳的原始草稿，并要求更正。然后她合上笔记本电脑，走到外面，双手仍在微微颤抖。

topic: A person finds out their article was published under someone else's name
text_en: After months of pitching, Sam's essay on night-shift workers was finally accepted. When it came out, he saw the byline belonged to his former supervisor, who had once rejected the idea. Sam read the first few paragraphs, recognizing his own metaphors and even his closing line. He called the editor, who claimed the supervisor had submitted it 'as a collaborative piece.' Sam listened, his grip on the phone tightening. 'No,' he said, 'I wrote it alone. You can check my submission history.' He then wrote a formal complaint to the publication's ethics board, copying his original drafts to a folder, and sent it before he could second-guess himself.
text_zh: 经过数月的投稿，萨姆关于夜班工人的文章终于被接受了。文章发表时，他看到署名属于他的前主管，那位曾拒绝过这个想法的人。萨姆读了前几段，认出了自己的比喻，甚至他的结尾句。他打电话给编辑，编辑声称主管是“作为合作作品”提交的。萨姆听着，握紧电话的手越来越紧。“不，”他说，“是我独自写的。你可以查我的投稿记录。”然后他向出版物的道德委员会写了正式投诉，将原始草稿复制到一个文件夹中，并在自己犹豫之前发送了出去。

topic: A person finds out their article was published under someone else's name
text_en: Nina's feature on local food banks ran under the name of a staff writer, Tom. She saw it in the print edition at a café, and her coffee cup clinked against the saucer as she set it down. She read the whole article, noting where Tom had inserted a few generic transitions but left her interviews intact. She tore the page out, folded it, and put it in her bag. That evening, she called Tom. 'I saw the piece,' she said. 'I'm not sure how my name got left off.' Tom was silent. Nina waited, then said, 'I'd like a correction printed, or I'll take this to the union.' She hung up and sat in her kitchen, her jaw set.
text_zh: 尼娜关于当地食品银行的专题报道以员工作家汤姆的名义发表。她在咖啡馆看到印刷版，放下杯子时咖啡杯碰到碟子发出叮当声。她读了整篇文章，注意到汤姆插入了一些通用的过渡句，但保留了她的采访。她撕下那一页，折叠起来，放进包里。那天晚上，她打电话给汤姆。“我看到那篇文章了，”她说。“我不明白为什么我的名字被漏掉了。”汤姆沉默。尼娜等着，然后说：“我希望刊登更正，否则我会向工会投诉。”她挂断电话，坐在厨房里，下巴紧绷。

topic: A person finds out their article was published under someone else's name
text_en: For her first published piece, Elena had written about urban tree planting. When she saw the online article, the byline read 'Contributing Editor.' She clicked the author profile—a blank page. She scrolled to the comments, where people praised the anonymous writer. Elena refreshed the page, as if the name might change. She then wrote to the managing editor, demanding to know who had approved the change. The editor replied that it was a 'house style' decision. Elena typed a response, deleted it, then typed again: 'That's not acceptable. This is my work, and I want my name on it.' She saved the email as a draft, then reopened it and sent it.
text_zh: 埃琳娜的第一篇发表作品是关于城市植树。当她看到在线文章时，署名写着“特约编辑”。她点击作者简介——一个空白页。她滚动到评论区，人们称赞这位匿名作者。埃琳娜刷新了页面，好像名字可能会改变。然后她写信给责任编辑，要求知道是谁批准了更改。编辑回复说这是“内部风格”决定。埃琳娜打了一段回复，删掉，然后又打：“这不可接受。这是我的作品，我要我的名字在上面。”她将邮件保存为草稿，然后重新打开并发送。

topic: A person finds out their article was published under someone else's name
text_en: Marcus had written a personal history of his neighborhood for a local journal. His cousin called to congratulate him, but Marcus hadn't seen it yet. He opened the link and saw another author's name—a prominent historian. Marcus felt a hot wave pass through his chest. He read the article, finding his own anecdotes and even his father's stories. He called the journal's office, but the receptionist said the editor was out. Marcus left a message, his voice tight: 'This is about the byline on the neighborhood piece. I need to speak with someone now.' He then wrote an email, attaching his original submission, and sent it to every editor listed on the site.
text_zh: 马库斯为一家本地期刊写了一篇关于他所在社区的个人历史。他的表弟打电话祝贺他，但马库斯还没看到。他打开链接，看到另一个作者的名字——一位著名历史学家。马库斯感到一股热浪穿过胸膛。他读了文章，发现自己的轶事，甚至他父亲的故事。他打电话给期刊办公室，但接待员说编辑不在。马库斯留言，声音紧绷：“是关于社区那篇文章的署名。我需要现在就和某人谈谈。”然后他写了一封邮件，附上原始投稿，发送给网站上列出的每位编辑。

topic: A person finds out their article was published under someone else's name
text_en: Priya recognized the opening line the moment she saw it—her own careful phrasing about the old library’s renovation, published in the city blog under someone else’s credit. She’d pitched that piece weeks ago and heard nothing. Now here it was, slightly trimmed, but unmistakably hers. She set her coffee down with a clatter. Her pulse quickened as she reread the final paragraph, the one she’d rewritten until it felt true. She screenshot the page, then composed a message to the blog’s editor, attaching her original draft. Her fingers paused over the send button, then pressed it firmly.
text_zh: 普里亚一看到开头就认出来了——她自己关于老图书馆翻新的精心措辞，发表在城市博客上，却署着别人的名字。她几周前投了那篇稿，毫无音讯。现在它在这里，略有删减，但毫无疑问是她的。她砰地放下咖啡。她重读最后一段，那段她反复改写直到感觉真实的话，心跳加速。她截屏页面，然后给博客编辑写了一条消息，附上原始草稿。她的手指在发送按钮上停顿了一下，然后坚定地按了下去。

topic: A person finds out their article was published under someone else's name
text_en: For a travel magazine, Dan had written a piece on desert hiking trails. When he saw the published version, the byline belonged to a woman he'd never met. He read the article, recognizing his descriptions of the canyon walls and his warning about flash floods. He felt a dull, persistent pressure behind his eyes. He called the magazine, and after being transferred, he was told the name had been changed 'for balance.' Dan laughed once, without humor. 'Balance?' he said. 'I wrote every word. I want my name on it, or I'll post the original online.' He hung up and immediately began preparing his evidence.
text_zh: 丹为一家旅游杂志写了一篇关于沙漠徒步路线的文章。当他看到已发表版本时，署名属于一个他从未见过的女人。他读了文章，认出了他对峡谷壁的描述和对山洪的警告。他感到眼睛后面有一种沉闷而持续的压力。他打电话给杂志，经过转接，他被告知名字被改是“为了平衡”。丹干笑了一声，没有幽默感。“平衡？”他说。“每个字都是我写的。我要我的名字在上面，否则我会把原文发到网上。”他挂断电话，立即开始准备证据。

topic: A person finds out their article was published under someone else's name
text_en: The article on volunteer firefighters was Helena's own story—she had ridden along for weeks. When it came out, the byline said 'Staff Writer.' She stared at the screen, her fingers hovering over the keyboard. She scrolled through, seeing her own notes, her own quotes. She then wrote an email to the editor, asking for a correction. The editor replied that the staff writer had 'polished' it. Helena wrote back: 'Polishing doesn't change the byline. I'm the author.' She then called the staff writer, who claimed he had been told to put his name on it. Helena listened, then said, 'Then we both need to talk to the editor.' She scheduled a meeting for the next morning.
text_zh: 关于志愿消防员的文章是海伦娜自己的故事——她跟随采访了好几周。文章发表时，署名写着“员工作家”。她盯着屏幕，手指悬在键盘上。她滚动浏览，看到自己的笔记、自己的引语。然后她给编辑写了一封邮件，要求更正。编辑回复说员工作家“润色”了它。海伦娜回信：“润色不会改变署名。我是作者。”然后她打电话给员工作家，他声称有人让他署上自己的名字。海伦娜听着，然后说：“那我们俩都需要和编辑谈谈。”她安排了第二天早上的会议。

topic: A person finds out their article was published under someone else's name
text_en: When his essay on urban wildlife appeared, Ben saw it was credited to a professor he'd once interviewed. Ben's hands tightened on the newspaper. He read the essay, recognizing his own observations about raccoons and his comparison to medieval scavengers. He then wrote a letter to the editor, but before sending it, he called the professor. 'Did you submit my essay?' Ben asked. The professor was quiet, then said he had 'adapted' it. Ben's voice was low: 'You didn't ask. You didn't credit me. I'm going to the paper.' He then emailed the editor, attaching his original draft, and requested a public correction.
text_zh: 当他的关于城市野生动物的文章发表时，本看到文章被署名给了他曾采访过的一位教授。本的手紧紧攥住了报纸。他读了那篇文章，认出了自己关于浣熊的观察以及他将其与中世纪清道夫的比较。随后他给编辑写了一封信，但在寄出之前，他给那位教授打了电话。“你提交了我的文章吗？”本问道。教授沉默了一会儿，然后说他“改编”了那篇文章。本的声音低沉：“你没有问过。你没有署我的名。我要去找报社。”然后他给编辑发了电子邮件，附上了他的原始草稿，并要求公开更正。

topic: A person finds out their article was published under someone else's name
text_en: The article about school lunch programs was based on months of fieldwork by Aisha. When it appeared, the byline was her supervisor's. Aisha read it in the faculty lounge, her coffee growing cold. She then walked to her supervisor's office and stood in the doorway. 'I saw the piece,' she said. 'My name isn't on it.' Her supervisor looked up, saying it was a 'joint effort.' Aisha shook her head. 'No. You didn't write it. I did.' She then went to the dean's office and filed a formal complaint, her voice clear and steady, though her hands were balled at her sides.
text_zh: 那篇关于学校午餐计划的文章是基于艾莎数月的实地调查。当文章发表时，署名是她的导师。艾莎在教师休息室里读了那篇文章，她的咖啡渐渐变凉。然后她走到导师的办公室，站在门口。“我看到那篇文章了，”她说。“上面没有我的名字。”她的导师抬起头，说那是“共同努力”的结果。艾莎摇了摇头。“不。你没有写。是我写的。”然后她去了院长办公室，正式提出投诉，她的声音清晰而平稳，尽管她的双手在身侧紧握成拳。

topic: A person finds out their article was published under someone else's name
text_en: For a history blog, Tomás had written a detailed piece on old mill towns. When he saw it online, the byline was his friend's name. Tomás felt a cold knot in his stomach. He read the piece, finding his own research and even his own typos. He called his friend, who said he had 'submitted it for him.' Tomás listened, then said, 'That's not what happened. You took my work.' He then wrote to the blog's administrator, explaining the situation, and attached his original files. He sent the email and then sat back, his jaw tight, waiting for a response.
text_zh: 为一个历史博客，托马斯写了一篇关于老磨坊镇的详细文章。当他在网上看到这篇文章时，署名是他朋友的名字。托马斯感到胃里打了个冷结。他读了那篇文章，发现了自己的研究，甚至还有自己的错别字。他打电话给朋友，朋友说他“替他提交了”。托马斯听着，然后说：“事实不是那样的。你拿走了我的作品。”然后他写信给博客管理员，解释了情况，并附上了他的原始文件。他发送了电子邮件，然后向后靠去，下巴紧绷，等待回复。

topic: A person finds out their article was published under someone else's name
text_en: The article on river restoration was the result of a grant project by Laura. When it was published in the project's newsletter, the byline was the project manager's. Laura read it, her eyes scanning the familiar sentences. She then walked to the manager's office and placed the newsletter on the desk. 'I wrote this,' she said. 'I'd like my name on it.' The manager said it was a 'team product.' Laura picked the newsletter back up. 'No. I wrote it. I have the drafts. I'll take this to the funder if I have to.' She left the office, her steps deliberate, and went to her computer to print her evidence.
text_zh: 那篇关于河流修复的文章是一个资助项目的成果，由劳拉完成。当文章在项目通讯中发表时，署名是项目经理。劳拉读了那篇文章，目光扫过熟悉的句子。然后她走到经理的办公室，把通讯放在桌上。“这是我写的，”她说。“我希望我的名字在上面。”经理说那是“团队产品”。劳拉把通讯拿了起来。“不。是我写的。我有草稿。如果有必要，我会把这件事告诉资助方。”她离开了办公室，步伐坚定，走到电脑前打印她的证据。

topic: A person finds out their article was published under someone else's name
text_en: When the article about community theater appeared, it was under the name of a board member, not the volunteer who had written it. That volunteer, Carla, saw it in the program. She read her own lines, her own anecdotes. She then approached the board member after a rehearsal. 'I wrote that piece,' she said. 'You didn't ask, and you didn't credit me.' The board member shrugged, saying it was 'for the good of the theater.' Carla shook her head. 'No. You'll issue a correction, or I'll send my version to the local paper.' She turned and walked away, her heart thumping, but her voice had been steady.
text_zh: 当那篇关于社区剧院的文章发表时，署名是一位董事会成员，而不是写这篇文章的志愿者。那位志愿者卡拉在节目单上看到了它。她读到了自己的文字，自己的轶事。然后她在一次排练后找到了那位董事会成员。“那篇文章是我写的，”她说。“你没有问过，也没有署我的名。”董事会成员耸了耸肩，说那是“为了剧院的利益”。卡拉摇了摇头。“不。你要发表更正，否则我就把我的版本发给当地报纸。”她转身走开了，心怦怦直跳，但她的声音一直很平稳。

topic: A person finds out their article was published under someone else's name
text_en: The article on local bird migrations was written by Yuki, a freelance writer. When it was published in a nature magazine, the byline was a staff photographer's. Yuki saw it online, and her shoulders stiffened. She read the piece, recognizing her own descriptions of the hawks. She then emailed the editor, asking for a correction. The editor said the photographer had 'provided the images and helped with text.' Yuki replied, 'The text is mine. I have the original. I need my name on it.' She then called the photographer, who claimed he had been told to write it. Yuki listened, then said, 'We'll see what the editor says.' She hung up, her grip on the phone still firm.
text_zh: 那篇关于当地鸟类迁徙的文章是由自由撰稿人由纪写的。当文章在一本自然杂志上发表时，署名是一位在职摄影师。由纪在网上看到了它，她的肩膀僵住了。她读了那篇文章，认出了自己关于鹰的描述。然后她给编辑发了电子邮件，要求更正。编辑说摄影师“提供了图片并帮助了文字”。由纪回复说：“文字是我的。我有原稿。我需要我的名字在上面。”然后她打电话给摄影师，摄影师声称他被告知要写这篇文章。由纪听着，然后说：“我们看看编辑怎么说。”她挂了电话，握着电话的手依然坚定。

topic: A person finds out their article was published under someone else's name
text_en: After a year of work, Omar's article on refugee resettlement was finally published—under the name of his organization's director. Omar read it on his laptop, his face heating. He then went to the director's office, closing the door behind him. 'I need to talk about the byline,' he said. The director said it was 'institutional branding.' Omar shook his head. 'That's my work. My interviews. My words. I want my name on it, or I'll publish the original myself.' He stood there, his arms crossed, waiting. The director promised to 'look into it.' Omar left, but he didn't wait. He emailed the journal, attaching his draft.
text_zh: 经过一年的工作，奥马尔关于难民安置的文章终于发表了——署名却是他所在组织的主任。奥马尔在笔记本电脑上读了那篇文章，脸热了起来。然后他去了主任的办公室，关上了身后的门。“我需要谈谈署名问题，”他说。主任说那是“机构品牌”。奥马尔摇了摇头。“那是我的工作。我的采访。我的文字。我要我的名字在上面，否则我自己发表原稿。”他站在那里，双臂交叉，等待着。主任答应“调查一下”。奥马尔离开了，但他没有等待。他给期刊发了电子邮件，附上了他的草稿。

topic: A person finds out their article was published under someone else's name
