topic: A student discovers their teacher follows them on social media
text_en: Maya scrolled through her feed and froze. There, among her classmates, was Mr. Ellison's profile, liking her post about a late-night study session. Her jaw tightened. She clicked his profile—public, full of personal photos. It felt like he was watching her every move outside class. The next day, she avoided his gaze, but he smiled and said, "Saw your post about the library. Good hustle." She nodded, but her hands clenched under the desk. She wanted to tell him it was none of his business, but she held back, silently fuming while she planned to block him that evening.
text_zh: Maya滚动浏览她的信息流，然后僵住了。在同学中间，有Ellison先生的个人资料，他点赞了她关于深夜学习小组的帖子。她的下巴绷紧了。她点击了他的个人资料——公开的，满是个人照片。感觉就像他在课堂之外监视她的每一个举动。第二天，她避开他的目光，但他微笑着说道：“看到你关于图书馆的帖子了。干得好。”她点了点头，但双手在桌子底下紧握着。她想告诉他这不关他的事，但她忍住了，默默地生着气，同时计划着当晚就屏蔽他。

topic: A student discovers their teacher follows them on social media
text_en: Tom noticed the new follower on his account: Mr. Davis, his science teacher. He clicked on the profile and saw that Mr. Davis had liked a post about a video game. Tom felt a hot flash of annoyance. He thought about his other posts, the ones about his favorite bands, the ones with inside jokes. He felt like his private life was being invaded. He changed his profile picture and made his posts visible only to close friends. When Mr. Davis asked him about his weekend project, Tom gave a vague answer and turned back to his lab work.
text_zh: Tom注意到他的账户上有了新粉丝：他的科学老师Davis先生。他点击了个人资料，看到Davis先生点赞了一篇关于电子游戏的帖子。Tom感到一阵恼怒。他想到了其他帖子，那些关于他最喜欢的乐队的，那些带有内部笑话的。他感觉自己的私生活被侵入了。他更换了个人资料图片，并将帖子设置为仅对密友可见。当Davis先生问起他周末的项目时，Tom含糊地回答，然后转身继续做实验。

topic: A student discovers their teacher follows them on social media
text_en: Nina was on her phone during lunch when she saw that Mr. Thompson had followed her. She almost choked on her sandwich. She scrolled through her feed, seeing his likes on her posts about her art and her favorite TV shows. She felt a surge of heat. She put her phone away, her appetite gone. In art class, when Mr. Thompson walked by her table and commented on her sketch, she gave a stiff nod and didn't look up, her hand moving quickly across the page, her strokes heavier than usual.
text_zh: Nina午餐时正在玩手机，这时她看到Thompson先生关注了她。她差点被三明治噎住。她滚动浏览信息流，看到他对她关于艺术和她最喜欢的电视节目的帖子的点赞。她感到一阵燥热。她放下手机，胃口全无。在艺术课上，当Thompson先生走过她的桌子，评论她的素描时，她僵硬地点了点头，没有抬头，手在纸上快速移动，笔触比平时更重。

topic: A student discovers their teacher follows them on social media
text_en: Alex saw the notification on his phone: Ms. Park, his math teacher, had followed him. He felt his stomach clench. He opened his profile and saw she had liked a post from last week, a picture of him and his friends at a movie. He felt a flash of heat. He thought about his private messages, his comments on other people's posts. He felt watched. He blocked her. The next day in class, when she asked him a question, he answered with a single word, his eyes fixed on the board, his hands clenched under his desk.
text_zh: Alex看到手机上的通知：他的数学老师Park女士关注了他。他感到胃部一阵紧缩。他打开个人资料，看到她点赞了上周的一篇帖子，一张他和朋友们看电影的照片。他感到一阵燥热。他想到了他的私信，他在别人帖子下的评论。他感觉被监视了。他屏蔽了她。第二天在课堂上，当她问他问题时，他只回答了一个词，眼睛盯着黑板，双手在桌子底下紧握着。

topic: A student discovers their teacher follows them on social media
text_en: Grace saw the notification that Mr. Donovan, her civics teacher, had followed her. She felt a wave of heat. She'd posted a rant about a school policy that he had defended. She felt a burning need to delete it, but she also wanted to stand her ground. She left it, but she felt a knot in her stomach. She wanted to send him a message explaining her view, but she knew it would come out as an accusation. She just stared at the screen, her jaw tight, her eyes fixed on his name.
text_zh: Grace看到通知，她的公民课老师Donovan先生关注了她。她感到一阵热浪。她发过一篇关于学校政策的抱怨帖子，而这项政策正是他辩护过的。她感到一种强烈的删除冲动，但她也想坚持自己的立场。她留下了帖子，但心里七上八下。她想给他发条信息解释自己的观点，但她知道那会变成指责。她只是盯着屏幕，下巴紧绷，目光锁定在他的名字上。

topic: A student discovers their teacher follows them on social media
text_en: Isaac was about to post a meme about his least favorite subject when he saw that Ms. Tran, his literature teacher, had followed him. He felt a flash of annoyance. He had a post about hating reading. He quickly deleted it, but he felt a sense of violation. He wanted to block her, but he knew that would be rude. He just sat there, his foot tapping, and he thought about all the things he'd said online. He felt a growing sense of resentment. He decided to post a quote about privacy, but it felt hollow.
text_zh: Isaac正要发一个关于他最不喜欢的科目的梗图，这时他看到他的文学老师Tran女士关注了他。他感到一阵恼怒。他有一篇关于讨厌阅读的帖子。他迅速删除了它，但他感到一种被侵犯的感觉。他想屏蔽她，但他知道那会显得无礼。他只是坐在那里，脚不停地敲着地面，想着他在网上说过的所有事情。他感到一种越来越强烈的怨恨。他决定发一条关于隐私的引言，但那感觉空洞。

topic: A student discovers their teacher follows them on social media
text_en: Jordan was scrolling through their feed when they saw a familiar name: Dr. Lee, their sociology teacher, had followed them. Jordan felt a jolt. They clicked on the profile and saw that Dr. Lee had liked a post about a protest downtown. Jordan felt a tightness in their chest. They thought about their other posts, the ones about their personal life, the ones with their friends. They felt like their privacy had been violated. They made their account private. In class, when Dr. Lee mentioned the protest, Jordan stayed silent, their jaw set, their gaze fixed on their notebook.
text_zh: Jordan正在滚动浏览他们的信息流，这时他们看到一个熟悉的名字：他们的社会学老师Lee博士关注了他们。Jordan感到一阵震动。他们点击了个人资料，看到Lee博士点赞了一篇关于市中心抗议活动的帖子。Jordan感到胸口一阵发紧。他们想到了其他帖子，那些关于个人生活的，那些和朋友在一起的。他们感觉自己的隐私被侵犯了。他们把账户设为私密。在课堂上，当Lee博士提到那次抗议时，Jordan保持沉默，下巴紧绷，目光盯着笔记本。

topic: A student discovers their teacher follows them on social media
text_en: Nathan saw that Ms. Silva, his French teacher, had liked his post about a party. He felt a cold wave of discomfort. He had a photo of him holding a drink. He quickly untagged himself, but the feeling remained. He wanted to send her a message: 'This is not your space.' But he held back. He just sat there, his fingers gripping the phone, his eyes narrowed. He thought about all his future posts, and he felt a heavy sense of being watched. He decided to post a meme about teachers being creepy, but he knew it would cause trouble.
text_zh: Nathan看到他的法语老师Silva女士点赞了他关于一个派对的帖子。他感到一阵寒意和不适。他有一张拿着饮料的照片。他迅速取消了对自己的标记，但那种感觉依然存在。他想给她发一条信息：“这不是你的地盘。”但他忍住了。他只是坐在那里，手指紧握着手机，眼睛眯了起来。他想到了未来所有的帖子，他感到一种沉重的被监视感。他决定发一个关于老师令人毛骨悚然的梗图，但他知道那会惹麻烦。

topic: An employee discovers the company is being sold
text_en: Mara tapped her pen against the memo, reading it again. The company, her home for years, was being absorbed by a conglomerate known for gutting departments. Her jaw tightened. She thought of the projects she'd nurtured, the team she'd built. She walked to her manager's office, the memo crumpled in her fist. "This can't be right," she said, her voice low. Her manager shrugged, citing board decisions. Mara stood there, her knuckles white. She didn't shout, but her posture was rigid, her gaze unyielding. She would fight this, she decided, even if it meant making herself a problem.
text_zh: 玛拉用笔敲着备忘录，又读了一遍。这家公司，她多年的家，正被一家以裁员闻名的集团收购。她的下巴绷紧了。她想到了自己培育的项目，建立的团队。她走到经理办公室，备忘录在她拳头里被揉皱了。“这不可能是真的，”她说，声音低沉。经理耸耸肩，引用了董事会的决定。玛拉站在那里，指节发白。她没有喊叫，但她的姿态僵硬，目光坚定。她决定要抗争，即使这意味着让自己成为一个麻烦。

topic: An employee discovers the company is being sold
text_en: The news came via a leaked press release that Tom's colleague found online. The company was being bought by a rival he had spent years outperforming. Tom sat at his desk, his fingers drumming a fast, uneven rhythm on the keyboard. He had been promised a promotion, had worked weekends, and now this. He felt a hot surge that made his ears ring. He closed the browser and opened his personal email. He typed a message to his wife: 'They sold us. I need to get out.' He hit send, then immediately started updating his resume, his movements sharp and deliberate, refusing to let the betrayal sit quietly.
text_zh: 消息是通过汤姆的同事在网上找到的一份泄露的新闻稿传来的。公司正被一个他多年来一直超越的竞争对手收购。汤姆坐在办公桌前，手指在键盘上敲出快速而不均匀的节奏。他曾被承诺升职，周末加班，现在却这样。他感到一阵热浪涌上心头，耳朵嗡嗡作响。他关闭了浏览器，打开个人邮箱。他给妻子打了一条消息：“他们把我们卖了。我需要离开。”他按下发送键，然后立刻开始更新简历，动作干脆利落，拒绝让背叛悄无声息地过去。

topic: An employee discovers the company is being sold
text_en: Priya was in a team meeting when the manager casually mentioned that the acquisition talks were 'almost done.' She sat up, her spine stiff. No one had consulted the employees, not even the senior engineers. She felt a cold, hard knot form in her stomach. She thought of the project she had pitched, the one they had all praised. It would likely be shelved. She looked around the table, at the smiling faces, and felt a sudden urge to speak, to demand an explanation. But she held her tongue, her lips pressed into a thin line. After the meeting, she lingered, waiting to corner the manager alone.
text_zh: 普里亚正在参加团队会议，经理随口提到收购谈判“几乎完成了”。她坐直了身子，脊椎僵硬。没有人咨询过员工，甚至没有咨询过高级工程师。她感到胃里形成了一个冰冷而坚硬的结。她想到了自己提出的项目，那个大家都称赞的项目。它很可能会被搁置。她环顾桌子四周，看着那些微笑的面孔，突然有一种想说话的冲动，想要求一个解释。但她忍住了，嘴唇抿成一条细线。会议结束后，她逗留着，等着单独拦住经理。

topic: An employee discovers the company is being sold
text_en: Jake had just returned from lunch to find a notice on the bulletin board: 'Merger Announcement.' He ripped it down, reading it in disbelief. The company he had helped grow from a startup was being absorbed by a giant. He crumpled the paper and shoved it in his pocket. He walked to his cubicle, his steps heavy. He remembered the early days, the pizza dinners, the shared vision. Now it was just a transaction. He sat down and stared at his screen, but saw nothing. He began to compose an email to the founder, his words sharp, asking how he could have done this to them.
text_zh: 杰克刚吃完午饭回来，就在公告栏上看到一张通知：“合并公告”。他把它撕下来，难以置信地读着。他帮助从初创公司发展起来的公司正被一家巨头吸收。他把纸揉成一团，塞进口袋。他走向自己的隔间，脚步沉重。他记得早期那些日子，披萨晚餐，共同的愿景。现在这只是一笔交易。他坐下来，盯着屏幕，却什么也看不见。他开始给创始人写一封邮件，言辞尖锐，问他怎么能这样对待他们。

topic: An employee discovers the company is being sold
text_en: Elena heard the rumor from a friend in HR: the sale was signed. She felt a flush of heat rise from her chest to her neck. She had declined other offers, loyal to a company that now saw her as a liability. She slammed her locker door, the sound echoing in the break room. She had given them her best years, and they had given her a stock option that would be worthless. She walked to her desk, her mind racing. She started to plan her exit, but also to think about what she could do to make sure her voice was heard before she left. She would not go quietly.
text_zh: 埃琳娜从人力资源部的一个朋友那里听到谣言：交易已经签署。她感到一阵热浪从胸口升到脖子。她拒绝了其他工作机会，忠于一家现在视她为负担的公司。她砰地关上储物柜门，声音在休息室里回荡。她把自己最好的年华给了他们，而他们给她的股票期权将一文不值。她走向办公桌，思绪飞速运转。她开始计划离开，但也思考着在离开前如何确保自己的声音被听到。她不会悄无声息地离开。

topic: An employee discovers the company is being sold
text_en: Marcus was on a video call with the regional director when the director casually mentioned the 'transition plan.' Marcus's smile froze. He had been the one to open the office in this city, had built the client base. He felt a surge of disbelief, then a burning sense of injustice. He cut the call short, citing a conflict. He stood up, his hands shaking slightly. He walked to the window and looked out at the city he had conquered. He would not let them just hand it over. He began to think of the clients he could take with him, and he felt a grim satisfaction.
text_zh: 马库斯正在与区域总监进行视频通话，总监随口提到了“过渡计划”。马库斯的笑容僵住了。他是这个城市办公室的开拓者，建立了客户群。他感到一阵难以置信，然后是灼热的不公感。他以时间冲突为由，匆匆结束了通话。他站起来，双手微微颤抖。他走到窗前，望着他征服过的城市。他不会让他们就这样交出去。他开始思考可以带走的客户，感到一种冷酷的满足感。

topic: An employee discovers the company is being sold
text_en: The memo about the acquisition was terse, a single page. Nina read it twice, then a third time. She felt a growing pressure in her chest, as if something was being squeezed. She had been the one to design the product that made the company attractive. Now they were cashing in, and she would get a pittance. She deleted the email, but the words stayed. She walked to the break room and poured a cup of coffee, but didn't drink it. She just stared at the dark liquid, thinking about how to confront the CEO. She would demand to know what this meant for her team.
text_zh: 关于收购的备忘录很简短，只有一页。妮娜读了两遍，又读了第三遍。她感到胸口压力越来越大，仿佛有什么东西被挤压。是她设计了让公司具有吸引力的产品。现在他们正在兑现，而她只会得到微薄的报酬。她删除了邮件，但那些话留在了心里。她走到休息室，倒了一杯咖啡，但没有喝。她只是盯着黑色的液体，思考着如何面对首席执行官。她要问清楚这对她的团队意味着什么。

topic: An employee discovers the company is being sold
text_en: Omar had just finished a late shift when he saw the news on his phone. The company was being sold to a conglomerate he had once publicly criticized. He felt a wave of disgust, but also a sharp, focused resentment. He had been promised a stake, a future. He threw his phone onto the couch. He paced his small apartment, his mind churning. He thought of the years of low pay, the promises of 'sweat equity.' Now it was all for nothing. He sat down and began to write a long, detailed post for an industry forum, exposing the deal, his fingers moving fast.
text_zh: 奥马尔刚下晚班，就在手机上看到了新闻。公司被卖给了他曾经公开批评过的一家集团。他感到一阵厌恶，但也有一种尖锐而集中的怨恨。他曾被承诺有股份，有未来。他把手机扔到沙发上。他在小公寓里踱步，思绪翻腾。他想到了那些低薪的岁月，那些“汗水股权”的承诺。现在一切都白费了。他坐下来，开始为行业论坛写一篇长而详细的帖子，揭露这笔交易，手指飞快地移动。

topic: An employee discovers the company is being sold
text_en: Lena was in the middle of a code review when the CEO walked by and said, 'Good news, we're being acquired.' He said it as if it were a triumph. Lena stared at her screen, her face hot. She had just spent a month optimizing a system that the new owners would likely discard. She felt a surge of frustration, a desire to protest. She turned to her colleague, but said nothing. She closed her laptop and walked out, her steps quick. She went to the stairwell and leaned against the wall, her hands clenched. She would not let them see her break, but she would plan her next move.
text_zh: 莉娜正在做代码审查，首席执行官走过来说：“好消息，我们被收购了。”他说得好像这是一场胜利。莉娜盯着屏幕，脸发烫。她刚刚花了一个月优化一个新老板很可能会丢弃的系统。她感到一阵沮丧，想要抗议。她转向同事，但什么也没说。她合上笔记本电脑，快步走了出去。她走到楼梯间，靠在墙上，双手紧握。她不会让他们看到她崩溃，但她会计划下一步行动。

topic: An employee discovers the company is being sold
text_en: The email subject line was stark: "Company Sale Announced." Leo stared at the screen, his stomach dropping. He had just finalized a major client deal, a victory that now felt hollow. He slammed his palm on the desk, the sound sharp in the quiet office. He thought of his daughter's tuition, the mortgage, the years of loyalty. He found his supervisor in the breakroom. "You knew about this?" he demanded, his voice tight. The supervisor looked away. Leo turned, his steps heavy, his mind already racing with the betrayal. He wasn't sad, not yet. He was coiled, ready to demand answers from anyone who would listen.
text_zh: 邮件主题行很刺眼：“公司出售公告”。利奥盯着屏幕，胃往下沉。他刚刚敲定了一笔大客户交易，这个胜利现在显得空洞。他猛地拍了一下桌子，声音在安静的办公室里显得尖锐。他想到了女儿的学费、房贷，以及多年的忠诚。他在休息室找到了主管。“你知道这件事吗？”他质问道，声音紧绷。主管移开了视线。利奥转过身，脚步沉重，脑海里已经充满了背叛感。他并不悲伤，至少现在不是。他蜷缩着，准备向任何愿意听的人要求答案。

topic: An employee discovers the company is being sold
text_en: Priya read the notice on the bulletin board, her coffee growing cold in her hand. The parent company was selling the division. She had poured her life into this place, turning down other offers. She crumpled the paper, her heart pounding. She found her friend in the next cubicle. "They're just discarding us," she said, her voice shaking with a controlled intensity. Her friend tried to console her, but Priya cut her off. "No, this is wrong. They can't just do this." She sat down, her fingers flying across the keyboard, drafting a letter to the board, her face set in grim determination.
text_zh: 普里亚看着公告栏上的通知，手中的咖啡渐渐变凉。母公司要卖掉这个部门了。她曾把一生都倾注在这个地方，拒绝了其他工作机会。她揉皱了那张纸，心跳加速。她在隔壁工位找到了朋友。“他们就这样抛弃我们了，”她说，声音因压抑的强烈情绪而颤抖。朋友试图安慰她，但普里亚打断了她。“不，这是错的。他们不能就这样做。”她坐下来，手指飞快地在键盘上敲击，起草一封致董事会的信，脸上带着严峻的决心。

topic: An employee discovers the company is being sold
text_en: The rumor had been swirling, but the official announcement still landed like a blow. Jonas stared at the screen, his hands trembling slightly. He had been promised a promotion, a future. He stood abruptly, his chair scraping the floor. He walked to the CEO's office, his steps deliberate. The door was open. "Is it true?" he asked, his voice flat. The CEO nodded. Jonas took a breath, his jaw clenched. "After everything," he said, his voice low and strained. He didn't wait for a response. He turned and walked out, his mind already cataloging his options, his resolve hardening into a cold, silent opposition.
text_zh: 谣言一直在流传，但官方公告仍然像一记重击。乔纳斯盯着屏幕，双手微微颤抖。他曾被承诺升职，承诺未来。他突然站起来，椅子刮过地板。他走向CEO的办公室，步伐坚定。门开着。“是真的吗？”他问，声音平淡。CEO点了点头。乔纳斯深吸一口气，下巴紧绷。“经历了这一切之后，”他说，声音低沉而紧张。他没有等待回应。他转身走了出去，脑海中已经在盘算自己的选择，决心化为冰冷而沉默的对抗。

topic: An employee discovers the company is being sold
text_en: Grace had just finished a presentation to the board when the chairman announced the sale, as if it were an afterthought. She felt a flash of heat, then a cold resolve. She had prepared that presentation for weeks, and now it was meaningless. She looked at the smiling faces around the table and felt a surge of contempt. She gathered her notes slowly, deliberately, making them wait. She said nothing, but her silence was loud. As she left the room, she didn't look back. She went to her office and began to draft a letter of resignation, her pen pressing hard into the paper.
text_zh: 格蕾丝刚向董事会做完演示，董事长就宣布了出售的消息，仿佛这只是顺带一提。她感到一阵热浪，然后是冰冷的决心。她为那个演示准备了数周，现在一切都毫无意义。她看着桌旁那些微笑的面孔，涌起一阵轻蔑。她慢慢地、故意地收拾着笔记，让他们等着。她什么也没说，但她的沉默震耳欲聋。离开房间时，她没有回头。她回到办公室，开始起草辞职信，笔重重地压在纸上。

topic: An employee discovers the company is being sold
text_en: The news came through an internal chat message, a link to a press release. David clicked it and felt his stomach drop. The company was being sold to a private equity firm. He knew what that meant: layoffs, cost-cutting, and the end of the culture he had helped build. He felt a surge of protectiveness for his colleagues, then a burning resentment toward the owners. He typed a response in the chat, a single question: 'Is this a joke?' The silence that followed was his answer. He stood up and walked to the window, his hands in his pockets, his jaw set.
text_zh: 消息通过内部聊天消息传来，是一个新闻稿的链接。大卫点击了它，感到胃部一沉。公司要被卖给一家私募股权公司。他知道这意味着什么：裁员、削减成本，以及他帮助建立的文化终结。他对同事们涌起一阵保护欲，然后是对所有者的强烈怨恨。他在聊天中打了一条回复，只有一个问题：“这是个玩笑吗？”随之而来的沉默就是他的答案。他站起来，走到窗边，双手插在口袋里，下巴紧绷。

topic: An employee discovers the company is being sold
text_en: The company-wide email was short, clinical. Elena felt a hot flash of disbelief, then a slow burn. She had turned down a competitor's offer to stay. She closed the email and reopened it, as if the words would change. They didn't. She stood up, her movements stiff. She walked to the window, staring out at the city. Her reflection showed a tightness around her eyes. She thought of the new owner's reputation for layoffs. She wouldn't let them take her work without a fight. She returned to her desk, her fingers poised over the keyboard, her plan already forming, a quiet resistance brewing.
text_zh: 全公司范围的电子邮件简短而冷静。埃琳娜感到一阵难以置信的热潮，然后是缓慢的燃烧。她曾拒绝竞争对手的邀请而留下来。她关闭邮件又重新打开，仿佛文字会改变。它们没有。她站起来，动作僵硬。她走到窗边，凝视着城市。她的倒影显示眼睛周围紧绷。她想到了新东家裁员的声誉。她不会让他们不战而夺走她的工作。她回到办公桌前，手指悬在键盘上，计划已经成形，一场无声的抵抗正在酝酿。

topic: An employee discovers the company is being sold
text_en: The notice was posted on the intranet, a simple statement of intent. Marcus read it, his face flushing. He had been with the firm since its early days, building it from the ground up. He felt a surge of something hot and protective. He went to the breakroom, where a few colleagues were murmuring. "This is a betrayal," he said, his voice loud and clear. They looked at him, startled. He didn't soften his gaze. "We're not just assets to be sold off." He slammed his mug on the counter, the coffee sloshing. He was ready to make his displeasure known, to anyone who would listen.
text_zh: 通知发布在内网上，是一份简单的意向声明。马库斯读着它，脸涨得通红。他从公司成立初期就在这里，从零开始建设。他感到一阵炽热而保护性的冲动。他去了休息室，那里几个同事正在低声议论。“这是背叛，”他说，声音响亮而清晰。他们惊讶地看着他。他没有软化目光。“我们不是可以随便卖掉的资产。”他把杯子重重地砸在柜台上，咖啡溅了出来。他准备让任何人知道他的不满，只要有人愿意听。

topic: An employee discovers the company is being sold
text_en: Mara set down her coffee when the email from the CEO landed. The subject line said 'Important Company Update.' She read the first sentence twice, then a third time, the words 'acquisition' and 'strategic partnership' blurring. Her hands began to tremble, knuckles whitening around the mug. She had poured years into this place, built the client relationships from scratch, turned down other offers to stay loyal. Now they were selling it out from under her, no warning, no consultation. She forwarded the email to her team with a single line: 'We need to talk.' Her jaw clenched as she drafted a reply to the CEO, her cursor hovering over send.
text_zh: 玛拉放下咖啡，这时CEO的邮件到了。主题行写着“重要公司更新”。她把第一句话读了两遍，然后第三遍，“收购”和“战略合作”这些词变得模糊。她的双手开始颤抖，指节在杯子周围变白。她在这里投入了多年，从零开始建立客户关系，为了忠诚拒绝了其他工作机会。现在他们要在她不知情的情况下卖掉公司，没有警告，没有协商。她把邮件转发给团队，附上一句话：“我们需要谈谈。”她起草给CEO的回复时下巴紧绷，光标悬停在发送键上。

topic: An employee discovers the company is being sold
text_en: The news came via a leaked email that was forwarded to Raj. He read it, his heart sinking. The company was being sold, and the new owners planned to 'streamline operations.' He knew what that meant for his department. He felt a surge of injustice, a sense that his hard work had been for nothing. He slammed his hand on the desk, then immediately regretted it, the pain sharp in his palm. He took a deep breath. He would not let them see him lose control. He would channel this into action. He began to update his LinkedIn, his jaw tight.
text_zh: 消息通过一封泄露的邮件传来，被转发给了拉杰。他读着，心沉了下去。公司要被卖掉，新东家计划“精简运营”。他知道这对他的部门意味着什么。他感到一阵不公，觉得自己的辛勤工作都白费了。他用手猛拍桌子，但立刻后悔了，手掌传来尖锐的疼痛。他深吸一口气。他不会让他们看到他失控。他会把这种情绪转化为行动。他开始更新领英，下巴紧绷。

topic: An employee discovers the company is being sold
text_en: Tina had just come back from a client meeting when she saw the email subject: 'Company Update.' She opened it, and the words 'sale' and 'finalized' seemed to jump off the screen. She felt a hot, prickly sensation on her skin. She had been the one to reassure the client, to promise stability. Now she felt like a liar. She closed the email and sat back, her mind racing. She thought of the promises made to her, the career path that was now a dead end. She picked up her phone and texted her husband: 'They sold us.' Then she began to draft a letter to the CEO, her words sharp and unyielding.
text_zh: 蒂娜刚从客户会议回来，就看到了邮件主题：“公司更新”。她打开它，“出售”和“已完成”这些词似乎从屏幕上跳出来。她感到皮肤上一阵灼热刺痛。她曾是那个安抚客户、承诺稳定的人。现在她觉得自己像个骗子。她关闭邮件，靠回椅背，思绪飞速运转。她想到了对她做出的承诺，那条现在已成死胡同的职业道路。她拿起手机给丈夫发短信：“他们把我们卖了。”然后她开始起草给CEO的信，言辞尖锐而不妥协。

topic: An employee discovers the company is being sold
text_en: The quarterly meeting was ending when the CEO dropped the news. The company was being sold. A collective gasp, then silence. Daniel felt his face go hot. He had just signed a new lease on an apartment near the office, based on assurances of stability. He stood up, his chair scraping. "You gave us your word," he said, his voice cutting through the room. The CEO started to speak, but Daniel held up a hand. "No. I want to know what this means for our projects, our teams." His voice was controlled, but his eyes were hard. He wasn't going to let this slide. He would hold them accountable.
text_zh: 季度会议即将结束时，CEO抛出了这个消息。公司要被卖掉。众人倒吸一口气，然后一片寂静。丹尼尔感到脸上一阵发热。他刚刚在办公室附近签了一份新公寓的租约，基于稳定性的保证。他站起来，椅子刮过地面。“你给过我们承诺，”他说，声音划破房间。CEO开始说话，但丹尼尔举起一只手。“不。我想知道这对我们的项目、我们的团队意味着什么。”他的声音克制，但眼神坚定。他不会让这件事就这么过去。他要让他们负责。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: Marta tapped out a quick message to her husband about the neighbor's dog barking all night, but the contact list had shifted, and it went to the neighbor herself. Within minutes, a reply came: 'We'll try to keep him quieter.' Marta stared at the screen, her jaw tight. She had not wanted to complain directly, and now she'd have to face this person at the fence. She typed a hasty apology, but her thumb hovered over send. The thought of the neighbor's smug tone made her delete it and shove the phone in her pocket, her shoulders rigid as she paced the kitchen.
text_zh: 玛尔塔给丈夫快速发了一条消息，抱怨邻居家的狗整夜叫个不停，但联系人列表发生了错位，消息发到了邻居本人那里。几分钟后，回复来了：“我们会尽量让它安静些。”玛尔塔盯着屏幕，下巴紧绷。她本不想直接抱怨，现在却不得不在栅栏边面对这个人。她匆忙打了一封道歉信，但拇指悬在发送键上。想到邻居那得意的语气，她删掉了消息，把手机塞进口袋，肩膀僵硬地在厨房里踱步。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: Leo meant to text his sister about their mother's forgotten prescription, but the message landed on his ex-girlfriend's phone. She replied with a string of laughing emojis and a passive-aggressive 'Hope you're more careful with other things.' Leo felt heat climb his neck. He had ended things cleanly, and this was none of her business. He wanted to fire back a sharp retort, but instead he locked the screen, then unlocked it and typed a curt 'Wrong number.' His finger pressed send with more force than necessary, and he set the phone down, still glaring at it as if it had betrayed him.
text_zh: 利奥本想给姐姐发短信，说母亲忘了取药的事，但消息却发到了前女友的手机上。她回复了一串大笑的表情符号，还有一句阴阳怪气的话：“希望你其他事情上能更小心点。”利奥感到脖子发热。他当初是干净利落地分手的，这根本不关她的事。他想狠狠回击一句，但最终锁了屏，又解锁，打了一句简短的“发错了”。他的手指用力按下发送键，然后把手机放下，仍然怒视着它，仿佛手机背叛了他。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: Mara had typed a sharp complaint about her supervisor's decision to her coworker, but the message landed in the supervisor's inbox. She stared at the screen, her jaw tightening as she read her own words sent to the wrong person. Her fingers hovered over the keyboard, but she knew deleting it wouldn't undo the damage. She imagined his smug face reading it, and a hot flush spread up her neck. She stood abruptly, knocking her chair back, and paced the small office. She wanted to confront him, to demand he disregard it, but she knew that would only make things worse. She sat back down, hands clenched in her lap.
text_zh: 玛拉给同事打了一段尖锐的抱怨，内容是针对主管的决定，但消息却发到了主管的收件箱。她盯着屏幕，读着自己发错人的文字，下巴收紧。她的手指悬在键盘上，但她知道删除也无法挽回损失。她想象着他得意地读着消息的样子，一股热流涌上脖子。她猛地站起来，椅子被撞得向后倒，她在小办公室里踱步。她想当面质问他，要求他忽略这条消息，但她知道那只会让事情更糟。她重新坐下，双手紧握在膝上。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: Jamal was complaining to his brother about their father's stubbornness, writing 'He never listens to anyone.' But the message went to their father. The reply came: 'I listen when people make sense.' Jamal's chest tightened. He had been careful to keep his frustration private, and now it was out in the open. He considered apologizing, but the more he thought about it, the more he felt justified. His father's response was exactly the kind of dismissive comment that had sparked the complaint. Jamal put the phone in his pocket and went for a walk, his steps brisk and heavy, rehearsing a defense that he knew he'd never deliver.
text_zh: 贾马尔正在向哥哥抱怨父亲的固执，写道：“他从来不听任何人的话。”但消息发到了父亲那里。回复来了：“当人们说得有道理时，我会听。”贾马尔胸口一紧。他一直小心地把自己的沮丧藏在心里，现在却公开了。他考虑道歉，但越想越觉得自己有理。父亲的回应正是引发抱怨的那种轻蔑评论。贾马尔把手机放进口袋，出去散步，脚步急促而沉重，心里排练着一套他明知永远不会说出口的辩解。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: Elena's text about her landlord's neglect—'He'd let the pipes rot before fixing them'—went to the landlord himself. He replied, 'I'll schedule a plumber for next week.' Elena's face flushed. She had meant to vent to a friend, not to the man who held her security deposit. His polite response felt like a trap, a reminder that she was at his mercy. She wanted to point out that this was the first time he'd responded so quickly, but she knew it would only make things worse. She deleted the thread, but her jaw stayed clenched, and she spent the next hour drafting a letter she never sent.
text_zh: 埃琳娜的短信抱怨房东的疏忽——“他宁愿让管道烂掉也不修”——发到了房东本人那里。他回复说：“我下周安排水管工来。”埃琳娜脸红了。她本想向朋友倾诉，而不是发给那个攥着她押金的人。他礼貌的回复感觉像个陷阱，提醒她自己是任人摆布的。她想指出这是他第一次回复得这么快，但她知道那只会让事情更糟。她删除了对话，但下巴依然紧咬，接下来一个小时她都在起草一封从未寄出的信。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: Leo had been texting his brother about their mother's stubborn refusal to consider assisted living, calling her impossible and childish. He hit send, then realized the message had gone to his mother's phone. His stomach dropped, then hardened into a tight knot. He re-read the message, his pulse thumping in his ears, and felt a surge of defensive heat. She would see his frustration, his disrespect. He wanted to call her and explain, to spin it as concern, but the words were already out there, raw and honest. He threw his phone onto the couch and stared at it, his breathing shallow, his mind already rehearsing the argument he knew was coming.
text_zh: 利奥一直在给哥哥发短信，抱怨母亲固执地拒绝考虑辅助生活，说她不可理喻、像孩子一样。他按下发送键，然后意识到消息发到了母亲的手机上。他的胃猛地一沉，然后紧紧拧成一个结。他重读消息，脉搏在耳边砰砰作响，一股防御性的热流涌上心头。她会看到他的沮丧，他的不敬。他想打电话解释，把它说成是关心，但话已经说出去了，赤裸裸的，诚实的。他把手机扔到沙发上，盯着它，呼吸急促，脑子里已经在排练他知道即将到来的争吵。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: Owen's text about his boss's micromanaging—'I can't breathe without his approval'—went to his boss. The reply came: 'Let's talk about your workload tomorrow.' Owen's hands went cold. He had been careful to keep his complaints private, and now he'd have to sit in a meeting and pretend he hadn't said anything. He considered lying, saying he'd been hacked, but that felt weak. He stared at the screen, his jaw tight. He imagined the conversation, the boss's condescending tone, and he felt a surge of defiance. He decided he would not back down. He'd say exactly what he'd written, and let the chips fall.
text_zh: 欧文的短信抱怨老板的微观管理——“没有他的批准我连气都喘不过来”——发到了老板那里。回复来了：“明天我们谈谈你的工作量。”欧文的手变得冰凉。他一直小心地把抱怨藏在心里，现在却不得不在会议上坐着，假装什么都没说过。他考虑撒谎，说自己被黑客攻击了，但那感觉太软弱。他盯着屏幕，下巴紧绷。他想象着对话，老板居高临下的语气，一股反抗的情绪涌上心头。他决定不退缩。他会原原本本地说出自己写的话，让结果顺其自然。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: Tara's text about her mother-in-law's intrusive advice—'She treats me like a child'—went to her mother-in-law. The reply came: 'Because you act like one sometimes.' Tara's face burned. She had been venting to her sister, and now this woman had read her private thoughts. Tara wanted to scream, but she took a breath. She typed a long, heated response, then deleted it. She typed a short, polite apology, but that felt like surrender. She finally wrote, 'That was meant for someone else,' and hit send. But she knew the damage was done. She spent the rest of the evening avoiding her phone, her resentment simmering.
text_zh: 塔拉的短信抱怨婆婆的干涉性建议——“她把我当小孩对待”——发到了婆婆那里。回复来了：“因为你有时候表现得就像个小孩。”塔拉的脸烧了起来。她本来在向姐姐倾诉，现在这个女人读到了她的私密想法。塔拉想尖叫，但她深吸一口气。她打了一段长长的、激烈的回复，然后删掉了。她打了一段简短、礼貌的道歉，但那感觉像是投降。她最后写道：“那是发给别人的。”然后按下发送。但她知道伤害已经造成。她整个晚上都避开手机，怨恨在心头翻腾。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: Miles's text about his friend's habit of borrowing money—'He never pays me back'—went to that friend. The reply came: 'I'm good for it, just tight this month.' Miles's jaw tightened. He had meant to complain to his brother, not to the debtor. Now the friend was justifying himself, and Miles felt cornered. He wanted to say, 'That's what you always say,' but he held back. He typed a neutral reply: 'No worries.' But his thumb pressed the screen hard, and he felt a knot in his stomach. He knew he'd never see the money, and now the awkwardness was worse. He put the phone away, but his mind kept replaying the exchange.
text_zh: 迈尔斯的短信抱怨朋友借钱的习惯——“他从来不还我钱”——发到了那个朋友那里。回复来了：“我肯定能还，只是这个月手头紧。”迈尔斯下巴收紧。他本想向哥哥抱怨，而不是发给债务人。现在朋友在为自己辩解，迈尔斯感到被逼到了墙角。他想说：“你总是这么说。”但他忍住了。他打了一条中性的回复：“没事。”但他的拇指用力按在屏幕上，胃里打了个结。他知道自己永远拿不回那笔钱，而现在尴尬更甚。他把手机收起来，但脑子里不断回放这段对话。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: Rosa's text about her neighbor's loud parties—'I can't sleep with that racket'—went to the neighbor. The reply came: 'Sorry, I'll keep it down.' Rosa's pulse quickened. She had been venting to a friend, not to the source of her sleepless nights. The neighbor's apology felt hollow, as if he were just saying what she wanted to hear. She thought about all the times she'd lain awake, staring at the ceiling, and now he was being polite. She wanted to reply, 'You've said that before,' but she didn't. She just stared at the screen, her hands trembling slightly, and then she put the phone down and walked to the window, looking at his house with narrowed eyes.
text_zh: 罗莎的短信抱怨邻居的吵闹派对——“那噪音吵得我睡不着”——发到了邻居那里。回复来了：“抱歉，我会小声点。”罗莎心跳加速。她本在向朋友倾诉，而不是发给让她失眠的源头。邻居的道歉听起来很空洞，好像他只是说她想听的话。她想起自己无数次躺在床上盯着天花板，而现在他却彬彬有礼。她想回复：“你以前也这么说过。”但她没有。她只是盯着屏幕，双手微微颤抖，然后放下手机，走到窗边，眯着眼睛看着他的房子。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: Derek's text about his teammate's laziness—'He never pulls his weight'—went to that teammate. The reply came: 'I do my share.' Derek's chest tightened. He had been complaining to a mutual friend, and now the person in question was defending himself. Derek felt a surge of indignation. He listed in his head all the times he'd covered for this guy, all the late nights he'd stayed to finish the project. He wanted to type a scathing reply, but he knew it would only escalate. He deleted the message and put the phone down, but his mind was racing. He could feel his pulse in his temples, and he spent the rest of the day avoiding eye contact.
text_zh: 德里克关于队友懒惰的短信——‘他从不尽本分’——发给了那个队友。回复来了：‘我做了我该做的。’德里克胸口一紧。他一直在向一个共同的朋友抱怨，现在当事人正在为自己辩护。德里克感到一阵愤慨。他在脑子里列出了所有他为这家伙兜底的时候，所有他熬夜完成项目的夜晚。他想打一条尖刻的回复，但他知道那只会让事情升级。他删除了消息，放下手机，但他的思绪飞速运转。他能感觉到太阳穴处的脉搏，那天剩下的时间里他都在避免眼神接触。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: Fiona's text about her brother's messy apartment—'It's a biohazard'—went to her brother. He replied with a photo of a sink full of dishes and a caption: 'Your room isn't much better.' Fiona's face flushed. She had been venting to a friend, and now her brother had turned it around on her. She wanted to fire back, but she knew he had a point about her own clutter. Still, that didn't excuse his defensiveness. She typed a sharp retort, then deleted it. She felt a hot, stubborn resistance. She decided she would not let him have the last word, so she wrote, 'At least I don't have mold,' and hit send, her heart pounding.
text_zh: 菲奥娜关于她哥哥凌乱公寓的短信——‘那是生物危害’——发给了她哥哥。他回复了一张满是盘子的水槽照片，配文：‘你的房间也好不到哪去。’菲奥娜脸红了。她一直在向朋友发泄，现在她哥哥把矛头转向了她。她想反击，但她知道他关于她自己杂乱的说法有道理。尽管如此，这并不能成为他防御态度的理由。她打了一条尖锐的反驳，然后删掉了。她感到一种强烈的、固执的抵触。她决定不让他占上风，于是她写道：‘至少我没有霉菌，’然后按下发送，心怦怦直跳。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: Priya meant to vent to her sister about a friend who kept borrowing money without repaying, calling her careless and thoughtless. Instead, the text went to that friend. She saw the read receipt appear and her face went hot. She sat frozen, the phone heavy in her hand, a bitter taste rising in her throat. She thought about apologizing, about claiming it was a joke, but the words felt like a lie she couldn't swallow. She pictured her friend's hurt face and felt a wave of resentment that she had to deal with this at all. She typed a quick, clipped apology, but she knew it wouldn't fix the crack in their friendship, and she felt a stubborn refusal to grovel further.
text_zh: 普里亚本想向姐姐发泄，说一个朋友总是借钱不还，说她粗心大意、不为别人着想。结果，短信发给了那个朋友。她看到已读回执出现，脸一下子热了起来。她僵坐着，手机沉甸甸地握在手里，喉咙里涌起一股苦涩。她想道歉，想说是开玩笑，但那些话感觉像是她咽不下去的谎言。她想象着朋友受伤的脸，感到一阵怨恨，因为她不得不处理这件事。她打了一条简短而生硬的道歉，但她知道这无法修复她们友谊中的裂痕，她感到一种固执的拒绝，不愿再低声下气。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: Hannah's text about her colleague's constant interruptions—'I can't get a word in edgewise'—went to that colleague. The reply came: 'Sorry, I didn't realize I was so annoying.' Hannah's face went hot. She had been venting to a friend, and now the woman was being sarcastic. Hannah wanted to say, 'You are,' but she held back. She typed a diplomatic reply: 'It's fine, just a bad day.' But she didn't mean it. She felt a simmering resentment as she thought about all the meetings where she'd been cut off. She put the phone away, but her hands were clenched, and she spent the next hour rehearsing what she should have said.
text_zh: 汉娜关于同事不断打断她说话的短信——‘我一句话都插不上’——发给了那个同事。回复来了：‘对不起，我没意识到我这么烦人。’汉娜的脸热了起来。她一直在向朋友发泄，现在那个女人在讽刺她。汉娜想说：‘你就是，’但她忍住了。她打了一条圆滑的回复：‘没事，只是今天不顺。’但她不是那个意思。她感到一种压抑的怨恨，想着那些她被打断的会议。她把手机收起来，但双手紧握，接下来一个小时她都在排练她本应该说的话。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: After a long shift, Ben texted his wife about his coworker, calling him lazy and incompetent, but the message went to the coworker's number. He saw the mistake immediately and cursed under his breath. His shoulders tensed as he imagined the coworker showing the message to the whole team. He felt a hot surge of frustration at his own carelessness, and at the coworker for making him feel this way. He considered calling him, but he didn't want to give him the satisfaction. He just sat in his car, gripping the steering wheel, replaying the words he'd written, his jaw set, already planning how he'd handle the awkward silence at work tomorrow.
text_zh: 长时间轮班后，本给妻子发短信说他的同事，说他懒惰无能，但消息发到了同事的号码上。他立刻看到了错误，低声咒骂。他的肩膀绷紧了，想象着同事把消息给整个团队看。他感到一阵强烈的挫败感，既对自己的粗心，也对那个让他有这种感觉的同事。他考虑过给他打电话，但他不想让他得意。他只是坐在车里，紧握方向盘，回想着自己写的话，下巴紧绷，已经在计划明天如何处理工作中的尴尬沉默。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: Jenna's text about her roommate's eating habits—'She finishes all my snacks'—went to her roommate. The reply came: 'I'll buy you more.' Jenna's face burned. She had been venting to a mutual friend, and now the roommate was being condescending. Jenna didn't want her snacks replaced; she wanted her privacy and her food respected. She typed a sharp reply, then deleted it. She felt a knot of resentment. She thought about all the other little things she'd tolerated, and this felt like the last straw. She wrote, 'No need,' and hit send, but she knew she'd be checking the pantry every day now, her jaw tight every time she saw a missing bag.
text_zh: 珍娜关于室友饮食习惯的短信——‘她吃光了我所有的零食’——发给了室友。回复来了：‘我会给你买更多的。’珍娜的脸发烫。她一直在向共同的朋友发泄，现在室友在居高临下。珍娜不想让零食被替换；她想要的是她的隐私和食物得到尊重。她打了一条尖锐的回复，然后删掉了。她感到一阵怨恨的疙瘩。她想着所有她容忍过的其他小事，这感觉像是最后一根稻草。她写道：‘不用了，’然后按下发送，但她知道从现在起她每天都会检查食品柜，每次看到少了一袋，她的下巴都会绷紧。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: Kyle's text about his cousin's bragging—'He acts like he's the only one who's ever succeeded'—went to his cousin. The reply came: 'Just sharing my good news.' Kyle's stomach clenched. He had been venting to his brother, and now his cousin was playing the victim. Kyle felt a surge of frustration. He thought about all the times his cousin had overshadowed his own achievements, and this was just one more example. He wanted to point out the pattern, but he knew it would start a family feud. He typed a neutral 'Congrats again,' and hit send, but his jaw was tight, and he spent the rest of the evening stewing over the exchange.
text_zh: 凯尔关于表哥吹嘘的短信——‘他表现得好像只有他成功过’——发给了表哥。回复来了：‘只是分享我的好消息。’凯尔的胃紧缩了。他一直在向哥哥发泄，现在表哥在装受害者。凯尔感到一阵沮丧。他想着表哥多少次盖过他的成就，这只是又一个例子。他想指出这个模式，但他知道那会引发家庭争执。他打了一条中性的‘再次恭喜，’然后按下发送，但他的下巴紧绷，那天晚上剩下的时间他都在为这次交流而闷闷不乐。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: Elena had written a sarcastic remark about her neighbor's loud music to a friend, but she sent it to the neighbor's number by mistake. She watched the message deliver and felt a flash of heated defensiveness. The neighbor had been blasting music all week, and now she had to deal with this on top of it. She thought about knocking on his door and telling him exactly what she thought, but she held back, her hands trembling slightly. She typed a quick follow-up saying it was meant for someone else, but she felt a stubborn refusal to apologize for her honest opinion. She set the phone down, her chest tight, waiting for his reply.
text_zh: 埃琳娜给朋友写了一条关于邻居大声放音乐的讽刺评论，但她误发到了邻居的号码上。她看着消息送达，感到一阵强烈的防御性。邻居这周一直在大声放音乐，现在她还得处理这件事。她想过敲他的门，告诉他她的真实想法，但她忍住了，双手微微颤抖。她打了一条快速的后续消息，说那是发给别人的，但她感到一种固执的拒绝，不愿为她的诚实意见道歉。她放下手机，胸口发紧，等待他的回复。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: Marco's text about his neighbor's unkempt lawn—'It's an eyesore'—went to the neighbor. The reply came: 'Mind your own business.' Marco's jaw tightened. He had been complaining to his wife, and now the neighbor was telling him to back off. Marco felt a surge of indignation. He had been polite about it, just a private comment, and now he was being told to mind his own business. He wanted to reply, 'It's my business when it brings down the street,' but he knew it would escalate. He deleted the message and put the phone down, but his hands were clenched, and he spent the rest of the day avoiding looking out the window.
text_zh: 马可关于邻居草坪不整洁的短信——‘真是碍眼’——发给了邻居。回复来了：‘管好你自己的事。’马可的下巴绷紧了。他一直在向妻子抱怨，现在邻居让他别多管闲事。马可感到一阵愤慨。他一直很礼貌，只是私下评论，现在却被告知别管闲事。他想回复：‘当它拉低整条街的价值时，这就是我的事，’但他知道那会升级。他删除了消息，放下手机，但双手紧握，那天剩下的时间他都避免看向窗外。

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text_en: Nora's text about her sister's new boyfriend—'He's so full of himself'—went to that boyfriend. He replied: 'Nice to know what you think of me.' Nora's stomach dropped. She had been venting to a friend, and now the guy had read her honest opinion. She felt a mix of embarrassment and defiance. She wanted to take it back, but she also didn't want to lie. She typed a quick apology, but then she stopped. She thought about how he'd been bragging at dinner, and she felt justified. She wrote, 'If the shoe fits,' and hit send, her heart pounding. She knew it would cause drama, but she didn't care. She set the phone down, her jaw set.
text_zh: 诺拉关于姐姐新男友的短信——‘他太自以为是了’——发给了那个男友。他回复：‘很高兴知道你对我的看法。’诺拉的胃沉了下去。她一直在向朋友发泄，现在那个家伙读到了她的真实意见。她感到尴尬和反抗的混合情绪。她想收回，但她也不想撒谎。她打了一条快速的道歉，然后她停住了。她想着他在晚餐时如何吹嘘，她觉得自己有道理。她写道：‘如果合适的话，’然后按下发送，心怦怦直跳。她知道这会引起风波，但她不在乎。她放下手机，下巴紧绷。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: Marco had spent years restoring vintage fishing reels, his workbench a shrine to brass and steel. His daughter, Lena, now claimed that space as her own. She had dismantled his prized Hardy, its parts scattered like a metallic puzzle. When he asked her to help him reassemble it, she laughed, saying she was improving the drag system. He watched her fingers, so confident, and felt a hot knot tighten in his chest. This was his patient craft, not her playground. He wanted to snatch the spool from her grip, to demand she respect the hours he had poured into that reel. Instead, he stood silent, jaw clenched, as she made another unauthorized alteration.
text_zh: 马可花了很多年修复古董渔线轮，他的工作台是黄铜和钢铁的圣殿。他的女儿莉娜现在把那个空间据为己有。她拆散了他珍贵的哈迪渔线轮，零件散落一地，像金属拼图。当他请她帮忙重新组装时，她笑了，说她正在改进拖曳系统。他看着她自信的手指，感到胸口一阵灼热的结。这是他耐心的手艺，不是她的游乐场。他想从她手中夺回线轴，要求她尊重他为那个渔线轮倾注的时光。相反，他沉默地站着，下巴紧绷，看着她做了又一次未经授权的改动。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: Elena's stamp collection was her quiet sanctuary, each tiny square a window to distant lands. Her son, Theo, became fascinated and demanded to help. She let him sort duplicates, but soon he was rearranging her entire album, placing a rare misprint upside down. When she corrected him, he insisted his way was better. She felt a hot flush spread through her as she gently but firmly moved the stamp back. 'This is not a game,' she said, her hands trembling slightly, and she locked the album in her drawer, his defiant frown burning in her mind.
text_zh: 埃琳娜的邮票收藏是她安静的避难所，每一小方都是通往遥远国度的窗口。她的儿子西奥变得着迷，要求帮忙。她让他整理重复的邮票，但很快他就重新排列了她整个集邮册，把一张珍贵的错版票倒置。当她纠正他时，他坚持他的方式更好。她感到一阵热流蔓延全身，她轻柔但坚定地把邮票移回原位。“这不是游戏，”她说，双手微微颤抖，她把集邮册锁进抽屉，他挑衅的皱眉在她脑海中燃烧。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: For decades, Harold had whittled wooden birds, his shed smelling of cedar and patience. His grandson, Jake, now wanted to carve his own. Harold gave him a soft piece of pine and a blunt knife, but Jake grew impatient and grabbed Harold's favorite gouge. Harold saw him forcing it into the wood, and a sharp pang shot through him. He rushed over, gripping Jake's wrist. 'That tool is not for you,' he said, his voice strained. He took the gouge and held it close, his heart pounding as he examined the nicked edge.
text_zh: 几十年来，哈罗德一直在雕刻木鸟，他的小屋弥漫着雪松和耐心的气味。他的孙子杰克现在想自己雕刻。哈罗德给了他一块软松木和一把钝刀，但杰克不耐烦，抓起哈罗德最喜欢的凿子。哈罗德看到他用力把它压进木头，一阵尖锐的刺痛穿过他。他冲过去，抓住杰克的手腕。“那工具不是给你用的，”他说，声音紧绷。他拿起凿子，紧紧握着，检查着有缺口的边缘，心怦怦直跳。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: Nina's quilt collection was a testament to her grandmother's art, each stitch a memory. Her daughter, Ava, now wanted to make her own quilt using Nina's antique fabrics. Nina tried to steer her to new cloth, but Ava insisted on cutting up a Civil War–era square. Nina saw the scissors poised over the fragile fabric and felt a surge of protectiveness. She grabbed the fabric, her voice cracking, 'No, this is not for cutting.' Ava's eyes welled, but Nina held firm, her own hands shaking as she tucked the fabric away.
text_zh: 尼娜的拼布被收藏是她祖母艺术的见证，每一针都是回忆。她的女儿艾娃现在想用尼娜的古董布料做自己的拼布被。尼娜试图引导她用新布，但艾娃坚持要剪一块内战时期的方块。尼娜看到剪刀悬在脆弱的布料上，感到一阵保护欲涌起。她抓住布料，声音嘶哑，“不，这不是用来剪的。”艾娃的眼睛湿润了，但尼娜坚持着，她自己的手颤抖着把布料收起来。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: Dana had knitted sweaters for years, her patterns intricate and personal. Her daughter, June, began borrowing her yarn without asking, then her needles. One evening, Dana found June unraveling a finished cardigan to reuse the wool for a doll's dress. Dana's hands went cold. "That took me months," she said, snatching the sweater back. June shrugged. "It's just yarn, Mom." Dana held the ruined fabric, the loose threads dangling, and felt a hot pressure build behind her eyes. She turned away, clutching the garment, unable to speak without her voice shaking.
text_zh: 达娜多年来一直织毛衣，她的图案复杂而个人化。她的女儿琼开始不问自取她的毛线，然后是她的织针。一天晚上，达娜发现琼在拆一件织好的开衫，想用羊毛给娃娃做裙子。达娜的手变冷了。“那花了我几个月，”她说，把毛衣抢回来。琼耸耸肩。“只是毛线，妈妈。”达娜拿着毁坏的织物，松散的线头垂着，感到一阵灼热的压力在眼眶后积聚。她转过身，紧紧抓着衣服，说不出话，声音颤抖。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: Priya's garden was her sanctuary, a mosaic of heirloom tomatoes and fragrant basil. Her son, Arjun, had turned it into his own experiment. He had uprooted her prized seedlings, replacing them with his chaotic, cross-pollinated hybrids. She found him labeling his creations with a marker, his hands dirty with her soil. A surge of heat rose from her stomach. This wasn't collaboration; it was a takeover. She had nurtured those seeds from fragile sprouts, and he had discarded them without a word. She wanted to demand he restore every plant, to remind him of the years of careful tending. But he looked so proud, so oblivious to the violation, that her protest died in her throat, leaving only a bitter taste.
text_zh: 普里亚的花园是她的避难所，传家宝番茄和芬芳罗勒的马赛克。她的儿子阿琼把它变成了他自己的实验。他拔掉了她珍贵的幼苗，用他混乱的、异花授粉的杂交品种取而代之。她发现他在用记号笔给他的作品贴标签，手上沾着她的泥土。一股热浪从她胃里升起。这不是合作；这是接管。她曾从脆弱的嫩芽培育那些种子，而他一句话没说就丢弃了它们。她想要求他恢复每一株植物，提醒他多年精心照料。但他看起来那么自豪，对这种侵犯浑然不觉，她的抗议卡在喉咙里，只留下苦涩的味道。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: Nora's herb garden was her sanctuary, each plant labeled and tended. Her son, Liam, now claimed the patch as his own science project, digging up her prized rosemary to test soil acidity. She found the plant wilted on the patio, roots exposed. "What were you thinking?" she demanded. He explained his experiment, eyes bright. She listened, then picked up the rosemary and walked to the compost bin. "My garden is not your lab," she said, dropping it. He protested, but she turned her back, her jaw set. She would not let his enthusiasm erase her years of care.
text_zh: 诺拉的香草园是她的避难所，每株植物都有标签并得到照料。她的儿子利亚姆现在把这块地据为己有，作为他的科学项目，挖出她珍贵的迷迭香来测试土壤酸度。她发现那株植物在露台上枯萎，根暴露在外。“你在想什么？”她质问。他解释了他的实验，眼睛明亮。她听着，然后拿起迷迭香走向堆肥箱。“我的花园不是你的实验室，”她说，把它扔进去。他抗议，但她转过身，下巴紧绷。她不会让他的热情抹去她多年的照料。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: Pete's woodworking shop smelled of cedar and sawdust. His daughter, Ava, now spent hours there, using his tools without permission. He found his favorite chisel dulled, its edge gouged from prying apart boards. Ava grinned, holding up a crooked birdhouse. "Look what I made!" He ran his thumb along the damaged blade, feeling the rough metal. "You don't use my tools without asking," he said, his voice flat. She shrank back. He set the chisel on the bench and walked out, the birdhouse still in her hands, his workshop suddenly feeling like a place he no longer owned.
text_zh: 皮特的木工店弥漫着雪松和锯末的气味。他的女儿艾娃现在在那里待上几个小时，未经允许使用他的工具。他发现他最喜欢的凿子变钝了，边缘因撬开木板而出现缺口。艾娃咧嘴笑着，举起一个歪歪扭扭的鸟屋。“看我做了什么！”他用拇指沿着受损的刀刃划过，感觉粗糙的金属。“你不问就用我的工具，”他说，声音平淡。她退缩了。他把凿子放在工作台上，走了出去，鸟屋还在她手里，他的工作室突然感觉像他不再拥有的地方。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: Rosa's pottery wheel sat in the garage, her bowls and vases drying on racks. Her son, Mateo, had started throwing his own pieces, but he never cleaned up. Clay crusted on the wheel, splatters on the floor. One day she found her favorite kiln-fired vase shattered, knocked over by his carelessness. He stood there, guilty. "I'll fix it," he said. "You can't fix this," she replied, picking up a shard. Her voice was steady but cold. She swept the pieces into a dustpan, each scrape of the broom a small protest against his intrusion into her sacred space.
text_zh: 罗莎的陶轮放在车库里，她的碗和花瓶在架子上晾干。她的儿子马特奥开始自己拉坯，但他从不清理。陶土在轮子上结壳，地板上溅满泥点。一天她发现她最喜欢的窑烧花瓶碎了，被他的粗心撞倒。他站在那里，内疚。“我会修好它，”他说。“你修不好这个，”她回答，捡起一块碎片。她的声音平稳但冰冷。她把碎片扫进簸箕，扫帚的每一声刮擦都是对他侵入她神圣空间的小小抗议。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: For years, Helen had tended her koi pond, each fish a jewel. Her nephew, Liam, wanted to feed them, and she gave him a small pinch of food. But Liam threw the whole container in, and the water clouded. Helen saw her prized butterfly koi gasping, and a hot wave of indignation washed over her. She grabbed the net and began scooping out the excess food, her voice tight, 'You have to be careful.' Liam shrugged, and Helen felt her hands shake as she worked to restore the water's clarity.
text_zh: 多年来，海伦照料着她的锦鲤池，每条鱼都是宝石。她的侄子利亚姆想喂它们，她给了他一小撮食物。但利亚姆把整个容器都扔了进去，水变得浑浊。海伦看到她珍贵的蝴蝶锦鲤在喘气，一阵灼热的愤慨涌上心头。她抓起网开始捞出多余的食物，声音紧绷，“你必须小心。”利亚姆耸耸肩，海伦感到她的手在颤抖，她努力恢复水的清澈。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: Greta's birdwatching binoculars hung by the door, her field guide dog-eared. Her nephew, Felix, now tagged along, but he never followed her quiet rules. He clapped at sightings, scared off a rare warbler, and once threw a stone at a heron. She grabbed his wrist. "We watch, we don't disturb," she hissed. He pulled free, sulking. She walked ahead, her strides long and fast, the binoculars bouncing against her chest. Her hobby had become a source of tension, and she resented every moment he turned her peaceful pastime into a chaotic game.
text_zh: 格蕾塔的观鸟双筒望远镜挂在门边，她的野外指南书页卷了角。她的侄子费利克斯如今也跟着一起去，但他从来不遵守她安静的规矩。他看到鸟就拍手，吓跑了一只稀有林莺，还曾向一只苍鹭扔石头。她抓住他的手腕。"我们只观察，不打扰，"她低声怒道。他挣脱开来，闷闷不乐。她走在前面，步子又长又快，双筒望远镜在她胸前晃动。她的爱好成了紧张的源头，她恨他的每一个把她的宁静消遣变成混乱游戏的动作。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: Iris's jigsaw puzzles covered the dining table for weeks. Her son, Owen, now joined her, but he forced pieces into wrong spots, bending edges. She came in to find him hammering a piece with his fist. "Stop," she said, removing his hands. He pointed at the picture. "It goes there." She saw the misaligned piece, the cardboard creased. "No, it doesn't," she said, pulling it out. He stomped away. She sat alone, smoothing the damaged piece with her thumb, her breath shallow. Her quiet ritual had become a tug-of-war, and she wanted the table back.
text_zh: 艾里斯的拼图游戏在餐桌上摆了几个星期。她的儿子欧文如今也加入进来，但他把拼图块硬塞进错误的位置，折弯了边缘。她进来时发现他正用拳头敲打一块拼图。"停下，"她说，拿开他的手。他指着图片。"它放那里。"她看到那块错位的拼图，纸板都皱了起来。"不，不是那里，"她说，把它抽了出来。他跺脚走开。她独自坐着，用拇指抚平损坏的拼图块，呼吸浅浅的。她安静的仪式变成了一场拔河，她想要回那张桌子。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: Hank's vintage camera collection lined the bookshelf, each lens pristine. His daughter, Zoe, now borrowed his Leica for school projects, returning it with smudges and scratches. He found dust inside the lens cap. "You need to be careful," he said, holding the camera up to the light. She rolled her eyes. "It's just a camera." He set it down slowly, his hand trembling slightly. "It's not just a camera," he said, his voice tight. She shrugged and left. He wiped the lens with a cloth, his movements deliberate, his jaw clenched against the urge to yell.
text_zh: 汉克的复古相机收藏陈列在书架上，每支镜头都完好无损。他的女儿佐伊如今借他的徕卡相机做学校项目，还回来时总带着污迹和划痕。他在镜头盖里发现了灰尘。"你要小心一点，"他说，把相机举到光下查看。她翻了个白眼。"不就是一个相机。"他慢慢地放下相机，手微微颤抖。"不只是相机，"他说，声音紧绷。她耸耸肩离开了。他用布擦拭镜头，动作刻意，下巴紧咬，压住想喊叫的冲动。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: Leah's calligraphy set sat on her desk, her nibs and inks organized. Her son, Evan, had started practicing, but he used her finest nib to draw comics, bending the tip. She found it discarded on the floor, the point twisted. "This is ruined," she said, holding it up. He looked at it blankly. "Sorry, I didn't think." She placed it in a small box labeled 'damaged' and turned to her desk. He hovered, waiting. She didn't look at him. She dipped another nib in ink and began writing, her letters sharp and precise, shutting him out of her world.
text_zh: 莉亚的书法用具摆在书桌上，笔尖和墨水都整整齐齐。她的儿子埃文开始练习书法，但他用她最细的笔尖画漫画，把笔尖弄弯了。她发现它被丢弃在地板上，笔尖扭歪了。"这个毁了，"她说，把它拿起来。他茫然地看着它。"对不起，我没想那么多。"她把笔尖放进一个标着"损坏"的小盒子里，转而面向书桌。他在旁边徘徊，等着。她没有看他。她蘸了另一个笔尖的墨水开始写字，字母尖锐而精准，把他挡在了她的世界之外。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: Frank's hand-carved walking sticks were his signature craft, each one unique. His daughter, Emma, wanted to make her own, and Frank gave her a piece of ash. But Emma grew frustrated and grabbed his favorite oak stick, trying to carve it with a chisel. Frank saw her gouging the grain and felt a sharp stab of protectiveness. He took the stick from her, his voice firm, 'That one is not for you.' He examined the cut, his hands shaking, and he set the stick aside, his back to her, his jaw tight.
text_zh: 弗兰克的手工雕刻手杖是他的招牌手艺，每一根都是独一无二的。他的女儿艾玛想自己做一根，弗兰克给了她一块白蜡木。但艾玛很快失去耐心，抓住他最心爱的橡木手杖，想用凿子雕刻它。弗兰克看到她刮伤了纹理，感到一阵强烈的保护欲。他从她手中拿过手杖，语气坚定："那根不是给你的。"他检查那道刻痕，双手颤抖，把手杖放在一旁，背对着她，下巴紧绷。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: Miles's fly-fishing gear hung in the garage, his rods and reels carefully maintained. His son, Theo, now wanted to join every trip, but he cast recklessly, tangling lines and losing flies. One day Miles found his favorite bamboo rod snapped, the tip floating in the creek. Theo stood on the bank, guilty. "It slipped," he said. Miles picked up the broken pieces, water dripping from the cork handle. "This rod was my father's," he said, his voice low. He turned and walked back to the car, leaving Theo behind, the river carrying away his patience.
text_zh: 迈尔斯的飞钓装备挂在车库里，鱼竿和渔轮都精心保养。他的儿子西奥如今想参加每一次出行，但他抛线很鲁莽，缠住线，丢鱼饵。有一天迈尔斯发现他最爱的竹子钓竿折了，竿尖漂浮在小溪里。西奥站在岸上，满脸愧疚。"手滑了，"他说。迈尔斯捡起断裂的竿身，水从软木手柄上滴落。"这根钓竿是我父亲的，"他说，声音低沉。他转身走回车里，留下西奥，河水带走了他的耐心。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: Phyllis's quilting frame occupied the spare room, her fabric stacks color-coded. Her granddaughter, Emma, now cut her own patches, but she used Phyllis's best silks without asking. Phyllis found a square of vintage kimono silk sliced into uneven strips. "This was irreplaceable," she said, holding the remnants. Emma frowned. "I thought you'd like me to use it." Phyllis set the strips down carefully, her hands steady but her heart pounding. "You should have asked," she said, turning back to her machine. The whir of the needle filled the silence, a barrier between them.
text_zh: 菲利斯的绗缝架占了备用房间，布料堆按颜色分类。她的孙女艾玛如今自己剪补丁，但她没问就用菲利斯最好的丝绸。菲利斯发现一块复古和服丝绸被剪成了参差不齐的条状。"这是独一无二的，"她说，拿着残片。艾玛皱眉。"我以为你会喜欢我用它。"菲利斯小心地放下那些布条，手稳稳的但心在狂跳。"你应该先问问，"她说，转身回到机器前。针线的嗡嗡声充满了寂静，成了她们之间的一道屏障。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: Marta's garden was her sanctuary, each rosebush tended with quiet devotion. When her nephew Theo moved in, he developed a sudden passion for gardening—specifically, for digging up her bulbs to "see how they grow." She found him in the flowerbed, holding a tulip bulb like a trophy. "Theo, those need to stay in the ground," she said, her voice low. He looked up, confused. "But I want to see." She knelt, brushing dirt from the bulb, and placed it back carefully. "This is not a toy." He frowned, reaching for another. She caught his wrist, her grip firm, and felt a tight knot in her stomach as she fought to keep her tone gentle.
text_zh: 玛尔塔的花园是她的避难所，每一丛玫瑰都得到悉心照料。当她的侄子西奥搬进来后，他突然对园艺产生了热情——特别是挖出她的花球茎来"看看它们怎么长"。她发现他在花坛里，手里像捧着奖杯一样举着一个郁金香球茎。"西奥，那些需要留在土里，"她说，声音很低。他抬头看她，困惑不解。"可是我想看看。"她跪下，拂去球茎上的泥土，小心地放回去。"这不是玩具。"他皱眉，伸手去拿另一个。她抓住他的手腕，握得很紧，努力保持语气温和时，胃里打了个紧密的结。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: Tessa's collection of pressed flowers filled a scrapbook, each specimen labeled with date and location. Her son, Caleb, now gathered his own, but he picked rare blooms, leaving stems broken. She found a protected orchid crushed in his backpack. "This is endangered," she said, her voice rising. He looked confused. "It was pretty." She pulled out the wilted petals, her hands shaking. "You don't take things without understanding them," she said, closing the backpack. He started to cry, but she didn't comfort him. She sat on the floor, sorting the damaged flower, her lips pressed thin.
text_zh: 特莎的压花收藏填满了一本剪贴簿，每一件标本都标着日期和地点。她的儿子凯勒如今也收集自己的，但他采摘珍稀花卉，留下断茎。她发现一朵受保护的兰花被压在他的背包里。"这是濒危物种，"她说，声音提高。他一脸困惑。"它很漂亮。"她抽出枯萎的花瓣，双手颤抖。"你不能在不了解的情况下摘走东西，"她说，拉上背包拉链。他哭了起来，但她没有安慰他。她坐在地板上整理损坏的花，嘴唇抿得紧紧的。

topic: A person's longtime hobby becomes their child's obsession
text_en: Walter's chess set, carved from rosewood, sat on the sideboard. His son, Aaron, now challenged him daily, but he moved pieces randomly, knocking over the board when he lost. One evening, Walter found a knight snapped at the base. "How did this happen?" he asked. Aaron shrugged. "It fell." Walter picked up the broken piece, the smooth wood splintered. "This set is older than you," he said, his voice quiet but firm. Aaron looked away. Walter placed the knight in a velvet pouch and locked the set in a drawer. He wouldn't let his son's carelessness ruin what he treasured.
text_zh: 沃尔特的国际象棋棋盘由红木雕刻而成，放在餐边柜上。他的儿子亚伦如今每天都挑战他，但亚伦乱走棋子，输的时候就推翻棋盘。一天晚上，沃尔特发现一个马棋底部折断了。"这是怎么回事？"他问。亚伦耸耸肩。"它摔倒了。"沃尔特捡起断掉的棋子，光滑的木头上裂开了口子。"这套棋比你岁数还大，"他说，声音轻而坚定。亚伦看向别处。沃尔特把马棋放进一个天鹅绒袋子里，并把整套棋锁在抽屉里。他不能让儿子的粗心毁掉他珍视的东西。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: Marta found the letter in her father's old desk, tucked under a pile of receipts. It was addressed to the company he'd worked for all his life, dated decades ago. He'd written that he could no longer accept the way they treated the night shift, the broken promises about safety, the way they ignored his reports. He never sent it. He stayed, and came home gray-faced each day. Marta read it twice, then carefully put it back, her jaw tight. She saw his quiet surrender differently now, and it burned in her chest.
text_zh: 玛尔塔在她父亲旧书桌的一堆收据下发现了那封信。信是写给他工作了一辈子的公司的，日期是几十年前。他写道，他再也无法接受他们对待夜班的方式、关于安全的食言，以及他们对他报告的忽视。他从未寄出这封信。他留了下来，每天灰着脸回家。玛尔塔读了两遍，然后小心地把它放回去，下巴紧绷。她现在以不同的眼光看待他无声的屈服，这在她胸中燃烧。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: Leo was sorting through his father's desk when he found it. A typed letter, crisp and formal, addressed to the company's regional manager. His father had resigned from his position as shift supervisor, citing personal reasons. Leo knew the real reason. His father had been passed over for a transfer he desperately wanted. He had never said a word about it. Leo crumpled the letter in his fist, then smoothed it out again. He thought of his father's quiet evenings, the unspoken disappointment. He felt a hot surge of resentment toward the company, toward the manager, toward his father for not fighting back. He slammed the desk drawer shut.
text_zh: 利奥在整理父亲的书桌时发现了它。一封打印的信，清晰而正式，写给公司的区域经理。他的父亲辞去了轮班主管的职位，理由是个人原因。利奥知道真正的原因。他的父亲被拒绝了他非常想要的调动。他从未对此说过一个字。利奥把信在拳头里揉皱，然后又抚平。他想起了父亲安静的夜晚，那未说出口的失望。他对公司、对经理、对父亲没有反抗感到一阵强烈的怨恨。他砰地关上了书桌抽屉。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: Nina's mother had always been a homemaker, or so she claimed. But in a box of old sewing patterns, Nina found a letter of resignation from a law firm. The letter was dated a year before Nina was born. Her mother had been a paralegal, on the verge of becoming an attorney. She had given it all up. Nina stared at the letter, her heart pounding. She thought of her mother's advice to always be independent, to never rely on a man. The hypocrisy burned her. She wanted to confront her, to ask why she had abandoned her career. She held the letter tightly, her knuckles white, a bitter taste in her mouth.
text_zh: 尼娜的母亲一直自称是家庭主妇。但在一个装满旧缝纫图案的盒子里，尼娜发现了一封来自一家律师事务所的辞职信。信的日期是尼娜出生前一年。她的母亲曾是一名律师助理，即将成为一名律师。她放弃了一切。尼娜盯着信，心跳加速。她想起了母亲关于要永远独立、永远不要依赖男人的建议。这种虚伪让她感到灼烧。她想质问母亲，问她为什么放弃了自己的事业。她紧紧握着信，指节发白，嘴里泛起苦涩。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: Ethan found the letter tucked inside an old dictionary. His father's resignation from the volunteer fire department. The reason stated was a scheduling conflict. Ethan knew better. His father had been passed over for chief, a position he had earned through years of service. He had never complained, just quietly stepped down. Ethan read the letter, his face flushed. He remembered his father's stories about the department, the pride in his voice. Now it all felt like a lie. He wanted to go to the firehouse and demand they acknowledge his father's sacrifice. He shoved the letter back, his chest tight with a simmering, righteous indignation.
text_zh: 伊桑在一本旧词典里发现了那封信。他父亲从志愿消防队的辞职信。理由是时间安排冲突。伊桑更清楚。他的父亲被拒绝担任队长，而他通过多年的服务赢得了这个职位。他从未抱怨过，只是悄悄地退出了。伊桑读了信，脸涨得通红。他记得父亲关于消防队的故事，以及他声音中的自豪。现在这一切都感觉像谎言。他想去消防站，要求他们承认父亲的牺牲。他把信塞回去，胸口因一种酝酿中的、义愤填膺的情绪而紧绷。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: In a box of his mother's things, Leo found a typewritten page, folded small. It was a resignation letter, unsent, from when she worked at the bank. She'd written about being passed over for promotion, about a supervisor who took credit for her work. She'd called it a 'pattern of disregard.' Leo remembered her coming home tired, never complaining. Now he knew she'd had words for it once, and swallowed them. He folded the paper carefully, but his hands were tight, and he thought of her silent dinners with a new, sharp feeling.
text_zh: 在母亲的一箱物品中，利奥发现了一张折叠得很小的打字纸。那是一封未寄出的辞职信，来自她在银行工作的时候。她写了关于被拒绝晋升的事，以及一个把她的工作成果据为己有的主管。她称之为“一种漠视的模式”。利奥记得她回家时疲惫不堪，从不抱怨。现在他知道她曾经对此有话要说，却咽了回去。他小心地折好纸，但双手紧绷，他带着一种新的、尖锐的感觉想起了她沉默的晚餐。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: Jake's father had a letter of resignation from the church choir. The reason was a change in his work schedule. Jake knew the real story. The choir director had given the solo parts to a new member, someone with connections. His father had been humiliated. He had never said a word. Jake found the letter in a box of old Christmas decorations. He read it, his hands shaking. He thought of his father's beautiful voice, now silent. He felt a burning resentment toward the choir director, toward the church, toward his father for accepting it. He wanted to confront them all, to make them hear his father's voice again.
text_zh: 杰克的父亲有一封来自教堂唱诗班的辞职信。理由是工作日程的变化。杰克知道真实的故事。唱诗班指挥把独唱部分给了一个新成员，一个有背景的人。他的父亲受到了羞辱。他从未说过一个字。杰克在一盒旧圣诞装饰品中发现了这封信。他读了信，双手颤抖。他想起了父亲美妙的嗓音，如今已沉默。他对唱诗班指挥、对教堂、对父亲接受这一切感到一种燃烧的怨恨。他想去质问他们所有人，让他们再次听到父亲的声音。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: Meg found the folder wedged behind her father's old desk, a relic of paper and rusted clips. Inside, a typed letter, crisp despite its age, addressed to the school board. It was his resignation from teaching, dated the spring he'd taken the mill job instead. Her jaw tightened as she read his neat words about 'pursuing a more practical path.' She saw the sentence he'd crossed out, fierce and dark: 'I cannot in good conscience teach children who are not permitted to question.' She folded it, hands shaking slightly. He'd chosen obligation, and the town had chosen to let him.
text_zh: 梅格在她父亲旧书桌后面发现了一个文件夹，一个纸和生锈回形针的遗物。里面是一封打印的信，尽管年代久远却依然清晰，写给学校董事会。那是他的辞职信，日期是他转而接受工厂工作的那个春天。她读到他那整洁的字迹，写着“追求更实际的道路”，下巴紧绷起来。她看到了他划掉的那句话，笔迹强烈而黑暗：“我不能凭良心教导那些不被允许提问的孩子。”她折起信，双手微微颤抖。他选择了责任，而小镇选择了让他离开。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: While cleaning out his father's garage, Tom found a folder. Inside was a resignation letter from the factory, typed and signed, but never mailed. His father had written about the foreman's favoritism, the way he'd been blamed for another man's mistake, the unfair write-up. Tom remembered his father coming home with a tight smile, saying 'that's the way it goes.' He never knew his father had put it into words. Tom put the letter in his own drawer, and for a long time, he couldn't shake the feeling of a slow, simmering heat.
text_zh: 在清理父亲的车库时，汤姆发现了一个文件夹。里面是一封来自工厂的辞职信，打印并签了名，但从未寄出。他的父亲写了关于工头偏袒的事，以及他如何因另一个人的错误而受到指责，还有不公平的书面警告。汤姆记得父亲带着勉强的微笑回家，说“事情就是这样”。他从不知道父亲曾把这些话付诸文字。汤姆把信放进自己的抽屉，很长一段时间，他无法摆脱一种缓慢而酝酿的热度。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: In the garage, Marcus found a shoebox of his father's old papers. Beneath the faded receipts was a typed letter, crisp and formal, addressed to the city council. It was a resignation from a volunteer board, citing a broken promise about the community center's funding. Marcus remembered his father talking about that project with such pride. Now, seeing the letter, he felt a cold knot in his stomach. His father had never mentioned quitting. Marcus folded the letter carefully, not to keep, but to confront his father later, demanding to know what had really happened all those years ago.
text_zh: 在车库里，马库斯发现了一个装满父亲旧文件的鞋盒。在褪色的收据下面是一封打印的信，清晰而正式，写给市议会。那是一封来自志愿者委员会的辞职信，理由是社区中心资金承诺的食言。马库斯记得父亲曾带着那样的自豪谈论那个项目。现在，看到这封信，他感到胃里一阵冰冷的结。他的父亲从未提到过退出。马库斯小心地折起信，不是为了保留，而是为了以后质问父亲，要求知道那些年前到底发生了什么。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: Rummaging through her mother's desk, Lila uncovered a sealed envelope. Inside, a resignation letter from the hospital where her mother had worked as a nurse. The letter described a supervisor who dismissed her concerns about patient safety, and a policy that forced overtime. Lila's hands trembled as she read. Her mother had always spoken of that job with quiet endurance. Now, Lila felt a surge of protective heat. She imagined her mother, younger, facing that injustice alone. Lila slipped the letter into her bag, determined to ask her mother why she had stayed, and what it had cost her.
text_zh: 翻找母亲的书桌时，莉拉发现了一个密封的信封。里面是一封来自她母亲曾工作过的医院的辞职信。信中描述了一位无视她对病人安全担忧的主管，以及一项强制加班的政策。莉拉读信时双手颤抖。她的母亲总是以安静的忍耐谈论那份工作。现在，莉拉感到一阵保护性的热浪。她想象着母亲，更年轻的时候，独自面对那不公。莉拉把信塞进包里，决心要问母亲为什么留下来，以及这让她付出了什么代价。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: While sorting through his father's study, Tom found a letter tucked inside an old dictionary. It was a resignation from the law firm, written in his father's neat hand, citing a partner who had lied about a case and blamed him for the error. Tom's throat tightened. His father had never mentioned this, always saying he left for a better opportunity. Tom sat down, the letter heavy in his hands. He felt a slow, burning resentment toward that unnamed partner, and a deeper ache for his father, who had swallowed the injustice and moved on. Tom decided he would not let it rest.
text_zh: 在整理父亲的书房时，汤姆在一本旧词典里发现了一封信。那是一封律师事务所的辞职信，用父亲工整的笔迹写成，信中提到一位合伙人就案件撒谎，却把错误归咎于他。汤姆的喉咙发紧。父亲从未提起过这件事，总是说他是为了更好的机会才离开的。汤姆坐下来，信在手中沉甸甸的。他对那个无名的合伙人感到一股缓慢燃烧的怨恨，也为父亲感到更深的痛楚——父亲默默咽下不公，继续前行。汤姆决定，他不会让这件事就此了结。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: In a box of her father's keepsakes, Maya found a draft of a resignation letter to the school board. It was dated the year he had been denied a promotion. The letter was blunt, listing instances where his ideas were ignored and his contributions overlooked. Maya's face grew warm as she read. Her father had never complained, always saying the job was just a job. Now, she felt a stubborn, rising protest. She wanted to march to that school and demand answers, to make someone acknowledge what her father had endured. She clutched the letter, her resolve hardening.
text_zh: 在父亲的一盒遗物中，玛雅发现了一封写给学校董事会的辞职信草稿。日期是他被拒绝晋升的那一年。信写得直白，列举了他的想法被忽视、贡献被忽略的事例。玛雅读着读着，脸上发烫。父亲从未抱怨过，总是说工作只是工作。现在，她感到一股倔强的、不断升腾的抗议。她想冲到那所学校去要个说法，想让人承认父亲所承受的一切。她紧握着信，决心更加坚定。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: While sorting through his father's desk, Sam found a letter, crumpled and smoothed out. It was a resignation from the construction company, written in his father's hand. He'd written about being cheated out of pay, about a supervisor who lied about his hours, about 'a theft of my labor.' He'd never sent it. He'd kept working, and grumbled at dinner. Sam read it and felt a sharp, clear feeling cut through him. He thought of his father's worn hands, and the letter he never sent, and he wanted to shake him.
text_zh: 在整理父亲的办公桌时，萨姆发现了一封信，被揉皱后又抚平了。那是一封建筑公司的辞职信，是父亲的笔迹。他写到自己被克扣工资，写到有个工头谎报他的工时，写到“我的劳动被偷窃”。他从未寄出这封信。他继续工作，只在晚饭时嘟囔几句。萨姆读着信，感到一股锐利而清晰的感受穿透了他。他想起父亲粗糙的双手，和那封从未寄出的信，他想摇晃父亲。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: Behind a stack of old photo albums, Elena discovered a manila folder. Inside, a resignation letter from the bank where her mother had worked for years. The letter detailed a manager who had passed her over for a promotion, giving it instead to a less qualified man. Elena's stomach churned. Her mother had always said she left to spend more time at home. Now, Elena saw the lie, and the truth beneath it. She felt a fierce, protective indignation. She imagined her mother, young and capable, being denied what she deserved. Elena pressed the letter to her chest, vowing to never let such a thing go unspoken.
text_zh: 在一叠旧相册后面，埃琳娜发现了一个牛皮纸文件夹。里面是母亲工作多年的那家银行的辞职信。信中详细描述了一位经理在晋升时越过了她，把机会给了一个资历较浅的男人。埃琳娜的胃里翻江倒海。母亲总是说她离开是为了有更多时间待在家里。现在，埃琳娜看到了谎言，以及谎言之下的真相。她感到一阵强烈的、保护性的愤慨。她想象着母亲，年轻能干，却被剥夺了应得的东西。埃琳娜把信按在胸口，发誓绝不让这种事被埋没。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: In his mother's old briefcase, Daniel found a handwritten letter, not yet signed. It was a resignation from the publishing house, complaining about a colleague who had stolen her manuscript ideas and presented them as his own. Daniel's hands curled into fists as he read. His mother had never talked about that job, only saying it was a good place to learn. Now, he understood the silence. He felt a hot, bitter taste in his mouth, a desire to find that colleague and demand a reckoning, even though decades had passed. The letter was a testament to a wrong that had never been righted.
text_zh: 在母亲的旧公文包里，丹尼尔发现了一封手写的信，尚未签名。那是一封出版社的辞职信，抱怨一位同事窃取了她的手稿创意，并据为己有。丹尼尔读着读着，双手握成了拳头。母亲从未提起过那份工作，只说是学习的好地方。现在，他明白了那份沉默。他感到嘴里一阵苦涩，想要找到那位同事讨个说法，尽管几十年已经过去。这封信是一桩从未被纠正的错误的见证。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: While cleaning the garage, Sarah found a crumpled letter in her father's tool chest. It was a resignation from the construction company, citing a foreman who had sabotaged his work and spread rumors about him. Sarah's eyes stung as she read. Her father had always said he left because the commute was too long. Now, she felt a deep, grinding frustration. She thought of her father coming home tired, never saying a word about the unfairness. Sarah smoothed the letter on her knee, her jaw set. She would keep it, not as a relic, but as a reminder of what her father had quietly endured.
text_zh: 在打扫车库时，莎拉在父亲的工具箱里发现了一封揉皱的信。那是一封建筑公司的辞职信，提到一位工头破坏他的工作，并散布关于他的谣言。莎拉读着读着，眼睛刺痛。父亲总是说他离开是因为通勤时间太长。现在，她感到一种深沉的、磨人的挫败感。她想起父亲疲惫地回到家，对不公之事只字不提。莎拉把信在膝盖上抚平，下巴紧绷。她会留着它，不是作为遗物，而是作为父亲默默承受之事的提醒。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: In a stack of her mother's old papers, Rachel found a letter to the airline where she had worked as a flight attendant. It was a resignation, complaining about a supervisor who had assigned her to the worst routes and docked her pay for minor infractions. Rachel's heart pounded as she read. Her mother had always said she quit to raise a family. Now, Rachel felt a sharp, piercing sense of injustice. She remembered her mother's tired eyes after long trips. Rachel folded the letter, her own jaw tight. She wanted to call that airline and tell them what she thought of their treatment of her mother.
text_zh: 在母亲的一叠旧文件中，瑞秋发现了一封写给她曾担任空乘的航空公司的信。那是一封辞职信，抱怨一位主管总是给她安排最差的航线，并因小过失克扣她的工资。瑞秋读着读着，心怦怦直跳。母亲总是说她辞职是为了照顾家庭。现在，瑞秋感到一种尖锐刺骨的不公感。她想起母亲长途飞行后疲惫的眼神。瑞秋折起信，自己的下巴也绷紧了。她想给那家航空公司打电话，告诉他们她对那家公司对待母亲方式的看法。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: While cleaning out his mother's closet, Paul found a letter in a coat pocket. It was a resignation from the airline, where she'd been a flight attendant. She'd written about being forced to wear a 'friendly smile' while being harassed, about a supervisor who told her to 'ignore it,' about 'a policy of silence.' She'd never sent it. She'd quit a year later, and never flew again. Paul read it and felt a hot, simmering feeling in his gut. He thought of her fear of flying, and knew it was this.
text_zh: 在清理母亲的衣橱时，保罗在一件外套口袋里发现了一封信。那是一封航空公司的辞职信，她曾是那里的空乘。她写到被迫在遭受骚扰时保持“友好的微笑”，写到一位主管叫她“别理它”，写到“沉默的政策”。她从未寄出这封信。她一年后辞了职，从此再也没坐过飞机。保罗读着信，感到腹中一股灼热的、翻腾的情绪。他想起她对飞行的恐惧，知道原因就是这个。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: Behind a loose board in the closet, Alex found a letter from his father, addressed to the fire department. It was a resignation, citing a chief who had blamed him for a mistake another firefighter had made. Alex's chest tightened as he read. His father had never mentioned this, always saying he left for a safer job. Now, Alex felt a slow, simmering heat. He thought of his father, brave and dedicated, being unfairly blamed. Alex placed the letter back, but not before memorizing the chief's name. He wouldn't let it go; he would ask his father about it, and he would not accept a vague answer.
text_zh: 在衣橱里一块松动的木板后面，亚历克斯发现了父亲写给消防局的一封信。那是一封辞职信，提到一位队长把另一名消防员犯的错归咎于他。亚历克斯读着读着，胸口发紧。父亲从未提起过这件事，总是说他离开是为了找一份更安全的工作。现在，亚历克斯感到一股缓慢燃烧的热度。他想起父亲，勇敢而敬业，却受到不公的指责。亚历克斯把信放回原处，但记住了队长的名字。他不会就此罢休；他会去问父亲这件事，而且不会接受含糊其辞的回答。

topic: Someone finds their parent's draft letter of resignation from decades ago
text_en: The letter was in a box of her mother's old uniforms, written on a napkin. It was a resignation from the diner, where she'd been a waitress. Her mother had written about a customer who'd been 'disrespectful,' about a manager who'd told her to 'smile and take it,' about 'a dignity I won't give up.' She'd never sent it. She'd stayed, and never complained. Anna read it and felt a hot, sharp pang in her chest. She thought of her mother's tired feet, and the letter she never sent, and it made her want to fight.
text_zh: 这封信在母亲的一盒旧制服里，写在一张餐巾纸上。那是一封餐厅的辞职信，她曾是那里的服务员。母亲写到一位“无礼的”顾客，写到一位经理叫她“笑着忍下去”，写到“我不愿放弃的尊严”。她从未寄出这封信。她留了下来，从未抱怨过。安娜读着信，感到胸口一阵灼热的刺痛。她想起母亲疲惫的双脚，和那封从未寄出的信，这让她想要去抗争。

topic: Someone receives an apology letter years after the incident
text_en: Nora found the envelope in her mother's old desk, addressed in a handwriting she hadn't seen in a decade. The letter was from the man who had spread lies about her at her first job, costing her the promotion. She read his apology, his careful words about youth and mistakes. Her jaw tightened as she remembered the way her colleagues had looked at her, the whispered rumors. She thought of the years she'd spent proving herself elsewhere. She folded the letter, not into a neat square, but into a tight, uneven wad. She dropped it into the kitchen trash, under the coffee grounds, and pressed the lid down firmly.
text_zh: 诺拉在她母亲旧书桌里发现了那个信封，上面的笔迹她已经十年没见过了。信来自那个在她第一份工作时散布关于她的谎言、让她失去晋升机会的男人。她读着他的道歉，那些关于年轻和错误的谨慎措辞。她下巴紧绷，想起同事们看她的眼神，那些窃窃私语的谣言。她想到自己在别处花费多年证明自己的岁月。她把信折起来，不是折成整齐的方块，而是折成紧紧的不均匀的一团。她把它丢进厨房垃圾桶，压在咖啡渣下面，然后用力按紧盖子。

topic: Someone receives an apology letter years after the incident
text_en: Mara found the envelope wedged behind the radiator, the handwriting unmistakable. Years ago, Lena had promised to back her during the board review, then sat silent while Mara took the blame. Now Lena wrote that she had been afraid, that she was sorry. Mara's jaw tightened. She read the letter again, then folded it into precise squares. She did not respond. Instead, she placed it in the drawer where she kept the old meeting notes, the ones that showed her side of the story. She left it there, unacknowledged, a reminder of what she no longer owed.
text_zh: 玛拉在散热器后面发现了那个信封，笔迹清晰可辨。多年前，莉娜曾承诺在董事会审查时支持她，却在玛拉承担责任时保持沉默。现在莉娜写信说她当时害怕了，她很抱歉。玛拉下巴紧绷。她又读了一遍信，然后把它折成精确的方块。她没有回复。相反，她把它放在抽屉里，那里放着她保留的旧会议记录，那些显示她立场的东西。她把它留在那里，无人理会，作为她不再亏欠什么的提醒。

topic: Someone receives an apology letter years after the incident
text_en: Marco was sorting through boxes of his late father's belongings when he found it. A letter from his old business partner, the one who'd walked away with their client list. The apology was detailed, explaining how his own fear had driven him to it. Marco's hands stilled on a stack of old blueprints. He saw the empty office, the phone that never rang, the loan he had to take out. He didn't finish reading. He placed the letter back in the box, taped the box shut, and wrote 'Misc.' on the side with a black marker.
text_zh: 马可正在整理他已故父亲的箱子时发现了它。一封来自他老合伙人的信，那个带着他们客户名单离开的人。道歉很详细，解释了他自己的恐惧如何驱使他那样做。马可的手在一叠旧蓝图上停了下来。他看到了空荡荡的办公室，从未响过的电话，他不得不借的贷款。他没有读完。他把信放回箱子里，用胶带封好箱子，用黑色记号笔在侧面写上“杂项”。

topic: Someone receives an apology letter years after the incident
text_en: Elena was on the bus when she saw the name on the email preview. It was from her college roommate, who had stolen her research notes and published them as her own. The apology was brief, a single sentence about being young and desperate. Elena's face grew warm. She remembered the sleepless nights, the professor's disappointment, the academic probation. She deleted the email without opening it, then went to her sent folder and wrote a short, factual reply: 'Received.' She did not ask for details. She pressed send and put the phone away.
text_zh: 埃琳娜在公交车上看到了邮件预览上的名字。那是她大学室友发来的，那个偷了她的研究笔记并以自己的名义发表的人。道歉很简短，只有一句关于年轻和绝望的话。埃琳娜的脸热了起来。她想起了那些不眠之夜，教授的失望，留校察看。她没有打开就删除了邮件，然后去了发件箱，写了一封简短、事实性的回复：“收到。”她没有询问细节。她按下发送键，把手机收了起来。

topic: Someone receives an apology letter years after the incident
text_en: The letter arrived on a Tuesday, postmarked from a town he had fled long ago. Adrian recognized the handwriting of his former mentor, the man who had accused him of stealing research data and ruined his academic career. The apology said the real culprit had confessed. Adrian's hands trembled as he set the page down. He thought of the years of odd jobs, the explanations he had given that no one believed. He took the letter outside and burned it in the grill, watching the paper curl. He did not feel relief, only the old weight pressing harder.
text_zh: 信在星期二到达，邮戳来自一个他很久以前逃离的小镇。阿德里安认出了他前导师的笔迹，那个曾指控他窃取研究数据并毁了他学术生涯的人。道歉信说真正的罪魁祸首已经承认了。阿德里安放下信纸时双手颤抖。他想起了那些打零工的岁月，那些他给出却无人相信的解释。他把信拿到外面，在烤架上烧了，看着纸卷曲起来。他没有感到解脱，只有旧日的重担压得更紧。

topic: Someone receives an apology letter years after the incident
text_en: Nora had almost forgotten the accusation, until the letter surfaced in a pile of old mail forwarded from her childhood home. The neighbor who had blamed her for the broken fence finally admitted it had been his son. Nora read the apology twice, then crumpled it. She remembered the summer she had spent mowing lawns to pay for the repair, the way her parents had grounded her. She smoothed the paper out, folded it neatly, and mailed it back with no note. She wanted him to know she had not forgiven him, only stopped waiting.
text_zh: 诺拉几乎忘记了那次指控，直到那封信从她童年老家转寄来的一堆旧邮件中浮现。那个曾因篱笆坏了而责怪她的邻居终于承认是他儿子干的。诺拉读了两遍道歉信，然后把它揉成一团。她想起了那个夏天，她为了支付修理费而修剪草坪，以及父母如何禁足她。她把纸抚平，整齐地折好，然后没有附任何便条就寄了回去。她想让他知道她没有原谅他，只是不再等待了。

topic: Someone receives an apology letter years after the incident
text_en: When the envelope appeared, Theo recognized the return address of his old bandmate, the one who had sold their demo to a rival group and claimed credit.
