Brian, who had thrown her notebook into a puddle, ruining her project. Olivia's eyes narrowed. She clicked his profile, reading about his 'integrative approach.' Olivia remembered the soggy pages, the tears. She felt a surge of heat in her chest. She closed the portal, then opened it again, searching for his name to see if it was still there. It was. She felt a stubborn resistance, a refusal to let him into her life, but she couldn't stop looking at his face.
text_zh: 奥利维亚的新员工福利门户网站列出了心理健康服务提供者目录。她搜索了附近的心理治疗师，一个名字跳了出来：“布莱恩·李博士。”布莱恩，那个把她的笔记本扔进水坑，毁了她项目的人。奥利维亚眯起眼睛。她点击了他的个人资料，阅读了他“整合疗法”的介绍。奥利维亚想起湿透的页面和泪水。她感到胸口一阵热浪。她关闭了门户，然后又打开，搜索他的名字，看是否还在。是的。她感到一种倔强的抵抗，拒绝让他进入她的生活，但她无法停止看他的脸。

topic: A person learns their childhood bully became a therapist
text_en: David was at a community event, and someone introduced him to a friendly man named 'Dr. Peter Hall.' Peter, who had called David 'dummy' throughout elementary school. David shook his hand, but his smile was stiff. He recognized Peter's face instantly. David made an excuse to leave, then went to his car and looked up Peter's practice. He saw a website full of glowing testimonials. David felt a cold knot in his stomach. He thought about Peter's taunts, the name-calling. David sat in his car, gripping the wheel, his knuckles white. He knew he'd never see Peter as a client, but he couldn't let go of the image.
text_zh: 大卫在一个社区活动中，有人把他介绍给一个友善的男人，名叫“彼得·霍尔博士”。彼得，那个在整个小学期间都叫大卫“笨蛋”的人。大卫和他握手，但笑容僵硬。他立刻认出了彼得的脸。大卫找了个借口离开，然后走到他的车里，查找彼得的诊所。他看到一个充满好评的网站。大卫感到胃里一阵冰冷的结。他想起彼得的嘲弄和辱骂。大卫坐在车里，紧握方向盘，指节发白。他知道自己永远不会成为彼得的客户，但他无法摆脱那个形象。

topic: A person learns their childhood bully became a therapist
text_en: Rachel's friend mentioned that her therapist was a man named 'Dr. Chris Martin.' Rachel froze. Chris, who had stolen her lunch money every day for a semester, leaving her hungry. Rachel's stomach churned. She asked her friend for more details, and the friend happily gave the website. Rachel looked it up later, seeing Chris's kind smile. She remembered the hunger pangs, the shame of having nothing to eat. Rachel felt a hot flush of something she couldn't name. She wrote a long email to her friend, warning her about Chris's past, but she deleted it. She kept the website open, staring at it, her jaw set, a stubborn need to remember.
text_zh: 瑞秋的朋友提到她的治疗师是一个叫“克里斯·马丁博士”的男人。瑞秋僵住了。克里斯，那个在一个学期里每天偷她的午餐钱，让她挨饿的人。瑞秋的胃翻腾起来。她向朋友询问更多细节，朋友愉快地给了网站。瑞秋后来查看了，看到克里斯和善的微笑。她想起饥饿的疼痛和没有东西吃的羞耻。瑞秋感到一阵无法名状的热潮。她给朋友写了一封长邮件，警告她克里斯的过去，但删除了。她让网站保持打开状态，盯着它，下巴紧绷，有一种倔强的记忆需求。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: Marta flipped through the binder on the conference table, her fingers pausing on the schematic. It was her own design, down to the color-coded wiring. She'd spent every weekend for months on it. Across the room, Leo adjusted his glasses. He'd presented it as his brainchild, and the committee was nodding. She cleared her throat. 'That's my work.' Leo blinked. 'I developed this independently.' Marta's jaw tightened. She'd documented every step, and he knew it. Her voice stayed level, but her hand trembled as she closed the binder. 'Then you'll have no problem showing me your drafts.' She wanted to see him squirm, to prove he'd taken what was hers.
text_zh: 玛尔塔翻着会议桌上的活页夹，手指在其中一张示意图上停住了。那是她自己的设计，连颜色编码的接线都一模一样。她为此花了数月，每个周末都在忙。房间另一头，利奥扶了扶眼镜。他把这说成是自己的心血之作，委员会的人纷纷点头。她清了清嗓子。“那是我的作品。”利奥眨了眨眼。“我是独立完成的。”玛尔塔的下颌绷紧了。她记录了每一步，而他心知肚明。她的声音保持平稳，但合上活页夹时手在发抖。“那你肯定不介意让我看看你的草稿。”她想看他难堪，想证明他拿走了属于她的东西。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: Nadia set her coffee down, staring at the whiteboard in the shared workspace. The algorithm was identical to the one she'd been refining for her thesis. Same variable names, same edge cases. Across the table, Priya was explaining it to a visiting professor. Nadia's chest tightened. She'd mentioned her work to Priya weeks ago, casually, over lunch. Priya had nodded, asked a few questions. Now it was all here, polished and presented as her own. Nadia stood, walked over, and picked up a marker. She drew a circle around a specific loop. 'This part has a flaw,' she said, her voice steady. 'You might want to check your sources.' Priya's smile faltered.
text_zh: 纳迪亚放下咖啡，盯着共享工作区的白板。那个算法和她为论文一直在完善的完全一样。相同的变量名，相同的边界情况。桌子对面，普里亚正在向一位来访教授讲解。纳迪亚胸口发紧。她几周前曾在午餐时随口向普里亚提过自己的工作。普里亚当时点了点头，问了几个问题。现在这一切都在这里，被润色后当作她自己的成果展示出来。纳迪亚站起身，走过去，拿起一支马克笔。她在一个特定循环上画了个圈。“这部分有缺陷，”她说，声音平稳。“你也许该查查你的来源。”普里亚的笑容僵住了。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: Marta unrolled the schematic, and her hand froze. The layout, the color-coded nodes, the odd little spiral in the corner—it was hers, down to the pencil smudge. She looked across the table at Leo, who was grinning. "Great minds," he said. She didn't answer. Her jaw tightened as she traced the line she'd spent a month perfecting. He'd presented it to the client yesterday, she remembered. She'd been in the hospital with her mother. He'd never mentioned it. Now he was waiting for her to congratulate him. She rolled the paper back up, slowly, and placed it in her bag.
text_zh: 玛尔塔展开示意图，手僵住了。布局、颜色编码的节点、角落里那个奇怪的小螺旋——都是她的，连铅笔的污迹都一样。她抬头看向桌子对面的利奥，他正咧嘴笑着。“英雄所见略同，”他说。她没有回答。她一边描着那条她花了一个月才完善的线条，一边绷紧了下颌。她记得，他昨天已经向客户展示了这个。她当时正陪母亲在医院。他从未提起过。现在他在等她祝贺他。她慢慢地把纸卷起来，放进了包里。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: Jules scrolled through the presentation slides, her stomach clenching. The marketing campaign was hers. The tagline, the color palette, even the quirky mascot she'd sketched in a notebook. Her coworker, Dana, was presenting it to the client, smiling as if she'd dreamed it up herself. Jules remembered mentioning the idea to Dana in the break room, watching her nod thoughtfully. Now it was being sold as Dana's vision. Jules stood up, interrupting the meeting. 'Dana, I think you forgot to mention the collaborative process.' Dana's eyes widened. Jules's voice was calm but clipped. 'I'd like to walk the client through my original notes.' She held up her sketchbook.
text_zh: 朱尔斯快速浏览着演示文稿，胃里一阵翻腾。这个营销活动是她的。标语、配色方案，甚至她在笔记本上画的那个古怪吉祥物。她的同事达娜正在向客户展示，微笑着，仿佛是她自己想出来的。朱尔斯记得自己在休息室里向达娜提过这个想法，看着她若有所思地点头。现在这被当作达娜的创意在推销。朱尔斯站起来，打断了会议。“达娜，我想你忘了提协作过程。”达娜瞪大了眼睛。朱尔斯的声音平静但干脆。“我想带客户看看我的原始笔记。”她举起了自己的速写本。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: Marcus stared at the code on his screen, then at the commit log. The repository showed that his colleague, Sarah, had pushed a module that was nearly identical to the one he'd written weeks ago. He'd shared his work-in-progress with her, asking for feedback. She'd said it was promising, then suggested some minor changes. Now it was in the main branch, credited to her. Marcus's pulse quickened. He walked to her desk. 'Sarah, this is my code.' Sarah looked up, surprised. 'I refactored it significantly.' Marcus pointed at the screen. 'The logic is the same, line for line.' He felt his jaw tighten. He turned and went back to his desk, already drafting a message to their manager.
text_zh: 马库斯盯着屏幕上的代码，又看了看提交日志。代码库显示，他的同事莎拉推送了一个模块，和他几周前写的那个几乎一模一样。他把自己正在进行的工作分享给她，征求反馈。她说这很有前景，然后建议了一些小改动。现在它出现在主分支上，功劳记在了她名下。马库斯心跳加速。他走到她桌前。“莎拉，这是我的代码。”莎拉抬起头，一脸惊讶。“我做了大幅重构。”马库斯指着屏幕。“逻辑是一样的，逐行相同。”他感到下颌绷紧。他转身回到自己桌前，已经开始起草给经理的消息。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: Leah pushed open the door to the studio, her breath catching. The sculpture on the pedestal was unmistakable. The same twisted metal form, the same polished surface. Her roommate, Jess, was standing next to it, talking to a gallery owner. Leah had been working on that piece for months, in the corner of their shared space. She'd mentioned it, but never showed it fully. Jess had seen the sketches, the maquette. Leah's hands curled into fists at her sides. She stepped forward. 'Jess, that's my design.' Jess tilted her head. 'It's inspired by our shared aesthetic.' Leah's voice was tight. 'It's my work.' She walked to her corner and began gathering her tools.
text_zh: 莉亚推开门走进工作室，屏住了呼吸。基座上的雕塑不容错认。同样的扭曲金属造型，同样的抛光表面。她的室友杰丝正站在旁边，和一位画廊老板说话。莉亚那件作品已经做了好几个月，就在她们共享空间的一角。她提过它，但从没完整展示过。杰丝看过草图和小样。莉亚的双手在身侧握成了拳头。她走上前。“杰丝，那是我的设计。”杰丝歪了歪头。“这是受我们共同美学启发的。”莉亚的声音发紧。“那是我的作品。”她走到自己的角落，开始收拾工具。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: Ravi looked at the grant proposal on the table, his heart hammering. The research plan was his. The same hypotheses, the same methodology, even the same participant pool he'd discussed with his colleague, Nina. He'd been open about his ideas, trusting her. Now she was submitting them as her own. Ravi's throat tightened. He approached her in the hallway. 'Nina, this is my project.' Nina smiled, a little too brightly. 'We're colleagues, Ravi. It's a natural evolution.' Ravi's voice was low. 'You copied my proposal.' He felt a hot wave of resentment. He turned and walked away, his mind already racing with how to reclaim his work.
text_zh: 拉维看着桌上的经费申请，心怦怦直跳。研究计划是他的。同样的假设，同样的方法，甚至他之前和同事尼娜讨论过的同一个受试者库。他向来坦诚自己的观点，信任她。现在她要把这些当作自己的来提交。拉维喉咙发紧。他在走廊里走到她面前。“尼娜，这是我的项目。”尼娜笑了，笑得有点过于灿烂。“我们是同事，拉维。这是自然的演进。”拉维压低声音。“你抄了我的提案。”他感到一阵强烈的怨恨涌上来。他转身走开，脑子里已经飞速转着要如何夺回自己的成果。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: Marta stared at the whiteboard in the shared lab, her own neat diagrams mirrored in someone else's handwriting. She had spent months on this approach, sketching every variable, testing each assumption. Now, a junior researcher was presenting the same framework as if it were brand new. Marta's jaw tightened. She set down her marker with deliberate care, the click echoing in the quiet room. She stepped closer, blocking the view of her own notes. "Interesting," she said, her voice flat. "Where did you get this idea?" The question hung in the air, her crossed arms and steady gaze making the challenge unmistakable.
text_zh: 玛尔塔盯着共享实验室里的白板，自己整洁的图表被别人的笔迹复制了。她在这个方法上花了几个月，画出每个变量，测试每个假设。现在，一个初级研究员把这个框架当作全新的东西在展示。玛尔塔的下颌绷紧了。她刻意小心地放下马克笔，咔嗒声在安静的房间里回响。她走近几步，挡住了自己笔记的视线。“有意思，”她说，声音平淡。“你从哪儿得到这个想法的？”问题悬在半空，她双臂交叉，目光平稳，让这挑战意味不言自明。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: Carlos stared at the business plan on his laptop, his stomach churning. The product idea, the market analysis, even the name he'd brainstormed with his friend, Diego. Diego had listened, asked questions, offered suggestions. Now he was pitching it to investors as his own startup. Carlos's hands shook slightly as he typed a message to Diego. 'We need to talk.' Diego replied with a thumbs-up. Carlos felt a hot pressure behind his eyes. He'd trusted Diego, shared his dreams. Now it felt like a betrayal. He took a deep breath and drafted a cease-and-desist letter, his jaw set. He wouldn't let Diego steal his future without a fight.
text_zh: 卡洛斯盯着笔记本电脑上的商业计划书，胃里翻江倒海。产品创意、市场分析，甚至他和朋友迭戈一起头脑风暴出来的名字。迭戈当时听着，问问题，提建议。现在他把它当作自己的创业项目在向投资人推销。卡洛斯的手微微颤抖着给迭戈发了条消息。“我们得谈谈。”迭戈回了个竖大拇指的表情。卡洛斯感到眼睛后面一阵灼热。他信任迭戈，分享了自己的梦想。现在这感觉像是一种背叛。他深吸一口气，起草了一封停止侵权函，下颌紧绷。他不会让迭戈不战而胜，偷走他的未来。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: For a hackathon, Priya had built a food-sharing app with a unique matching algorithm. She'd only shared her code with her team. When the winners were announced, another team took first place with an app that looked identical—same interface, same logic. Priya confronted them at the award ceremony. 'Your code is the same as mine,' she said, her voice low. The team leader, a man in a hoodie, shrugged. 'We had a similar idea.' Priya's nostrils flared. 'No, you copied my repo.' She pulled out her laptop, showing her git history. The man's face went pale. Priya felt a hot surge of vindication as she called the organizers, demanding a review. She didn't care about the prize anymore; she just wanted acknowledgment that her work had been stolen.
text_zh: 为了黑客马拉松，普里亚构建了一个带有独特匹配算法的食品分享应用。她只和团队分享过代码。当获奖名单公布时，另一个团队凭借一个看起来一模一样的应用拿了第一名——相同的界面，相同的逻辑。普里亚在颁奖典礼上质问他们。“你们的代码和我的一样，”她压低声音说。团队负责人，一个穿连帽衫的男人，耸了耸肩。“我们也有类似的想法。”普里亚的鼻孔翕动。“不，你抄了我的代码库。”她拿出笔记本电脑，展示她的 git 历史。那个男人的脸变得苍白。普里亚感到一阵强烈的快意，她叫来组织者，要求审查。她不在乎奖品了；她只想要自己的作品被偷这件事得到承认。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: Aisha walked into the lab, her eyes narrowing at the poster on the wall. The research was hers. The same experimental design, the same data visualization, even the same phrasing in the abstract. Her colleague, Mark, had been in the lab when she'd discussed her findings. He'd nodded, asked a few questions. Now he was presenting it at a conference. Aisha felt a surge of heat. She walked up to Mark. 'This is my work.' Mark looked up, surprised. 'I built on it.' Aisha shook her head. 'You copied it.' Her voice was steady but firm. She pointed to a specific figure. 'This is from my dataset.' Mark's face paled. Aisha crossed her arms, waiting for an explanation that wouldn't come.
text_zh: 艾莎走进实验室，看到墙上的海报时眯起了眼睛。这项研究是她的。相同的实验设计，相同的数据可视化，甚至摘要中的措辞也一模一样。她的同事马克，在她讨论研究结果时就在实验室里。他当时点了点头，问了几个问题。现在他却在会议上展示它。艾莎感到一阵热血上涌。她走向马克。“这是我的工作。”马克抬起头，显得很惊讶。“我在它的基础上做了扩展。”艾莎摇了摇头。“你抄袭了它。”她的声音平稳而坚定。她指着一个具体的图表。“这是来自我的数据集。”马克的脸色变得苍白。艾莎双臂交叉，等待着那个不会到来的解释。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: Aisha had been working on a language-learning game for children, using a reward system she'd invented. When she saw a demo at a tech conference, she recognized her own mechanics—the same star levels, the same encouragement phrases. She approached the developer, a young man named Ben. 'That's an interesting game,' she said. 'I made something similar.' Ben smiled. 'Great minds think alike.' Aisha's heart pounded. 'No, I have the design documents,' she said. She pulled out her tablet, showing her wireframes from months earlier. Ben's smile faded. 'I don't know what to say.' Aisha felt a surge of heat as she realized he was likely a former colleague who'd seen her work. She turned and walked away, already drafting a legal notice, her mind racing with accusations.
text_zh: 艾莎一直在开发一款儿童语言学习游戏，使用了她自己发明的奖励系统。当她在一次科技会议上看到一个演示时，她认出了自己的机制——相同的星级，相同的鼓励语。她走向开发者，一个叫本的年轻人。“那是个有趣的游戏，”她说。“我做过类似的东西。”本笑了笑。“英雄所见略同。”艾莎的心怦怦直跳。“不，我有设计文档，”她说。她拿出平板电脑，展示她几个月前的线框图。本的笑容消失了。“我不知道该说什么。”艾莎感到一阵热血上涌，她意识到他很可能是一个见过她作品的前同事。她转身走开，已经在起草法律通知，脑海中思绪万千，充满了指控。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: Priya flipped through the proposal on the conference table. Her heart hammered. The same market analysis, the same phrasing, even the same quirky title she'd drafted last spring. She glanced at Raj, who was beaming at the board. "I thought this was dead," he said. She had shared it with him as a draft, asking for feedback. He'd said it was too risky. Now it was his signature project. She set the document down, her hands steady but cold. "You never mentioned you were working on this again," she said. He shrugged. She didn't stay for the rest of the meeting.
text_zh: 普里亚翻阅着会议桌上的提案，心怦怦直跳。相同的市场分析，相同的措辞，甚至还有她去年春天起草的那个古怪的标题。她瞥了一眼拉杰，他正对着董事会笑容满面。“我以为这个项目已经死了，”他说。她曾把草稿分享给他，征求反馈。他说这风险太大。现在这成了他的标志性项目。她放下文件，双手平稳但冰冷。“你从没提过你又开始做这个了，”她说。他耸了耸肩。她没有留下来参加剩下的会议。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: The sketchbook lay open on the studio table. Ben stared at the charcoal drawing—the same bridge, the same bent railing, the same shadow under the arch he'd been perfecting for weeks. He looked at his colleague, Sam, who was cleaning brushes. "Did you see my notebook?" Ben asked. "No, why?" Sam's voice was calm. Ben turned the page. There was his second drawing, the one with the boats. Sam had drawn it too. Ben closed the book, his jaw working. He picked up his own sketchbook and left the room without another word, walking to the far end of the studio.
text_zh: 速写本摊开在工作室的桌子上。本盯着那幅炭笔画——同一座桥，同一根弯曲的栏杆，同一个他几周来一直在完善的拱门下阴影。他看着他的同事山姆，他正在清洗画笔。“你看到我的笔记本了吗？”本问道。“没有，怎么了？”山姆的声音很平静。本翻过一页。那里有他的第二幅画，画着船的那幅。山姆也画了它。本合上书，下巴紧绷。他拿起自己的速写本，一言不发地离开了房间，走到工作室的另一端。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: Omar looked at the syllabus on the shared drive, his breath catching. The course design was his. The readings, the assignments, even the quirky weekly prompts he'd created. His colleague, Lisa, had been in his office when he'd shown her his draft. She'd suggested a few tweaks. Now she was teaching the same course, with his syllabus. Omar's chest tightened. He found Lisa in the faculty lounge. 'Lisa, that's my syllabus.' Lisa looked up, surprised. 'I adapted it.' Omar's voice was low. 'You copied it.' He felt a surge of resentment. He turned and walked away, already composing an email to the dean, his hands shaking.
text_zh: 奥马尔看着共享驱动器上的教学大纲，屏住了呼吸。课程设计是他的。阅读材料、作业，甚至他创作的古怪的每周提示。他的同事丽莎，在他给她看草稿时就在他的办公室里。她当时提了一些小建议。现在她在教同样的课程，用的是他的教学大纲。奥马尔的胸口发紧。他在教师休息室找到了丽莎。“丽莎，那是我的教学大纲。”丽莎抬起头，显得很惊讶。“我改编了它。”奥马尔的声音很低。“你抄袭了它。”他感到一阵怨恨涌上心头。他转身走开，已经在起草给院长的邮件，双手颤抖。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: Maya had been writing a cookbook, with her own twist on traditional recipes. When she saw a new cookbook at the store, she flipped through it and found her exact recipe for lentil stew—same spices, same notes. The author was a celebrity chef. Maya's hands trembled as she bought the book, then went home and compared it to her manuscript. She felt a surge of indignation as she realized the chef had likely used a recipe she'd shared online. She wrote a blog post, detailing the similarities, and posted it. The response was mixed; some believed her, others accused her of copying. Maya's frustration grew as she watched the chef's book continue to sell. She decided to pursue a legal case, her jaw set, determined to get some acknowledgment.
text_zh: 玛雅一直在写一本烹饪书，对传统食谱有自己的改良。当她在书店看到一本新烹饪书时，她翻阅了一下，发现了她那道扁豆炖菜的精确食谱——相同的香料，相同的注释。作者是一位名厨。玛雅双手颤抖着买了这本书，然后回家与她的手稿进行了比较。她感到一阵愤慨，意识到这位厨师很可能使用了她在网上分享的食谱。她写了一篇博客文章，详细说明了相似之处，并发布了。反应不一；有些人相信她，其他人则指责她抄袭。看着那位厨师的书继续畅销，玛雅的挫败感越来越强烈。她决定提起法律诉讼，下巴紧绷，决心得到某种承认。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: Sara stared at the app on her phone, her thumb hovering over the screen. The interface was hers. The layout, the icons, even the color scheme she'd chosen. Her friend, Dave, had seen her prototype during their hackathon. He'd offered suggestions. Now he'd released it as his own. Sara's pulse quickened. She called Dave, her voice tight. 'Dave, this is my app.' Dave was silent for a moment. 'I built on your idea.' Sara felt a hot wave. 'You copied my code.' She hung up, her hands trembling. She wrote a scathing review, then deleted it. She'd pursue it legally, she decided. She wasn't going to let him steal her work.
text_zh: 萨拉盯着手机上的应用，拇指悬停在屏幕上。界面是她的。布局、图标，甚至她选择的配色方案。她的朋友戴夫，在黑客马拉松期间看过她的原型。他当时提过建议。现在他把它作为自己的作品发布了。萨拉的脉搏加快了。她打电话给戴夫，声音紧绷。“戴夫，这是我的应用。”戴夫沉默了一会儿。“我在你的想法基础上做了扩展。”萨拉感到一阵热浪。“你抄袭了我的代码。”她挂断了电话，双手颤抖。她写了一篇尖刻的评论，然后删掉了。她决定要通过法律途径解决。她不会让他窃取她的工作成果。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: The grant application was on the screen, and Alina felt her stomach drop. The research question, the methodology, the exact wording of the hypothesis—it was her draft, the one she'd emailed to Dr. Chen for feedback. She scrolled down. Her name was listed as a collaborator, but Dr. Chen was the principal investigator. She'd been planning to submit this as her own project. She walked to his office, the printout in her hand. "I saw this," she said, holding it up. He smiled. "Great synergy, isn't it?" She didn't smile back, just stood there, the paper trembling slightly.
text_zh: 拨款申请在屏幕上，阿丽娜感到胃部一沉。研究问题、方法论、假设的确切措辞——这是她的草稿，她通过电子邮件发给陈博士征求意见的那份。她向下滚动。她的名字被列为合作者，但陈博士是首席研究员。她本来计划将其作为自己的项目提交。她走到他的办公室，手里拿着打印件。“我看到了这个，”她说，举了起来。他笑了笑。“很好的协同效应，不是吗？”她没有回以微笑，只是站在那里，纸张微微颤抖。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: Iris pushed her glasses up, her gaze fixed on the whiteboard. The lesson plan was hers. The activities, the examples, even the joke she used to explain the concept. Her teaching assistant, Ben, had been in her classroom, had seen her materials. Now he was using them in his own section. Iris's chest tightened. She approached Ben after class. 'Ben, those are my materials.' Ben shrugged. 'I adapted them.' Iris's voice was steady but firm. 'You copied them.' She felt a wave of indignation. She walked away, her mind already drafting an email to the department head. She wouldn't let him undermine her work.
text_zh: 艾里斯推了推眼镜，目光盯着白板。教案是她的。活动、例子，甚至她用来解释概念的那个笑话。她的助教本，在她的教室里待过，看过她的材料。现在他在他自己的课上使用它们。艾里斯的胸口发紧。下课后她走向本。“本，那些是我的材料。”本耸了耸肩。“我改编了它们。”艾里斯的声音平稳而坚定。“你抄袭了它们。”她感到一阵愤慨。她走开了，脑海中已经在起草给系主任的邮件。她不会让他破坏她的工作。

topic: Two people discover they've been working on identical projects
text_en: Zara looked at the patent application on her desk, her hands shaking. The invention was hers. The mechanism, the materials, the specific design. Her former business partner, Leo, had access to all her notes. Now he was filing it under his name. Zara felt a hot surge of betrayal. She called Leo, her voice cold. 'Leo, that's my patent.' Leo was silent. 'We were partners.' Zara's jaw tightened. 'You're taking credit for my work.' She hung up, her heart pounding. She gathered her evidence, the dated sketches, the emails, the prototypes. She would fight this, she decided, feeling a grim determination.
text_zh: 扎拉看着桌上的专利申请，双手颤抖。这项发明是她的。机制、材料、具体设计。她以前的事业伙伴利奥，可以接触到她的所有笔记。现在他以自己的名义提交申请。扎拉感到一阵强烈的背叛感。她打电话给利奥，声音冰冷。“利奥，那是我的专利。”利奥沉默了。“我们曾是合伙人。”扎拉的下巴紧绷。“你在把功劳归于自己，抢走我的工作。”她挂断了电话，心怦怦直跳。她收集她的证据，那些注明日期的草图、电子邮件和原型。她决定要抗争到底，感到一种冷酷的决心。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: Mara found her watercolor of the old pier hanging in the café's front window, a small price tag beneath it. She hadn't sold it, hadn't even lent it. Her hands tightened on her coffee cup. She approached the counter, the barista's cheerful greeting dying as she spoke. 'Who put that there?' The barista shrugged, mentioning a new hire who'd found it in the back room. Mara's jaw clenched. She didn't raise her voice, but her words were clipped and precise as she demanded it be taken down immediately. She watched the barista fumble with the frame, her pulse hammering, the violation of her private work burning in her chest.
text_zh: 玛拉发现她画的老码头水彩画挂在咖啡馆的临街橱窗里，下面还贴着一张小价签。她没有卖过这幅画，甚至没有借出去过。她的双手紧紧握住咖啡杯。她走向柜台，随着她开口说话，咖啡师那欢快的问候声戛然而止。“谁把那幅画挂在那儿的？”咖啡师耸耸肩，提到是一个新来的员工在后面的房间里发现的。玛拉的下颌绷紧了。她没有提高声音，但言辞简短而犀利，要求立刻把画取下来。她看着咖啡师笨手笨脚地摆弄画框，心跳如擂鼓，自己的私人作品被侵犯的感觉在她胸中燃烧。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: Leo scrolled through the gallery's online feed and froze. There was his charcoal sketch of the old library—the one he'd left with a friend for safekeeping. The post announced it as part of a 'community showcase.' His throat tightened. He called the gallery, his voice steady but sharp. 'I never gave permission for that piece.' The curator apologized, claiming a mix-up with submissions. Leo hung up, then typed a long, precise email demanding removal and an apology. He stared at the screen, his knuckles white on the mouse, the sense of his work being stolen simmering beneath his calm exterior.
text_zh: 利奥浏览着画廊的在线动态，突然愣住了。那是他画的老图书馆的木炭素描——那幅他托付给朋友保管的画。帖子宣称它是“社区展览”的一部分。他的喉咙发紧。他打电话给画廊，声音平稳而尖锐。“我从未允许展出那幅作品。”策展人道歉了，声称是投稿时出了差错。利奥挂了电话，然后打了一封长而措辞严谨的电子邮件，要求撤下作品并道歉。他盯着屏幕，握着鼠标的指节发白，作品被偷走的感觉在他平静的外表下暗暗翻涌。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: Nina walked into the community center for her pottery class and saw her raku vase on the display shelf, a ribbon around its neck. She hadn't entered any contest. She approached the coordinator, her voice low and strained. 'That's mine. I didn't agree to this.' The coordinator smiled, saying they thought it would be a nice surprise. Nina's eyes narrowed. She carefully lifted the vase, cradling it against her chest. 'It's not a surprise. It's my work.' She turned and left, her steps quick and deliberate, the cool clay in her hands the only thing grounding her from the hot wave rising inside.
text_zh: 尼娜走进社区中心上陶艺课，看到她的乐烧花瓶放在展示架上，瓶颈上系着一条丝带。她没有参加任何比赛。她走向协调员，声音低沉而紧绷。“那是我的。我没有同意这样做。”协调员微笑着，说他们以为这会是个惊喜。尼娜眯起眼睛。她小心地拿起花瓶，抱在胸前。“这不是惊喜。这是我的作品。”她转身离开了，步伐快速而坚定，手中冰凉的陶器是她唯一能从体内升腾的热浪中保持镇定的东西。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: Tom's phone buzzed with a notification: his photograph of the old mill had been featured in a local travel blog. He'd never submitted it. He clicked the link, his jaw dropping as he saw his image credited to 'Anonymous.' He found the blogger's contact and called, his voice tight. 'You used my photo without asking. I want it removed and a correction posted.' The blogger stammered an apology about sourcing. Tom hung up, then spent an hour drafting a cease-and-desist email, his hands shaking slightly as he typed, the feeling of being trampled on refusing to ease.
text_zh: 汤姆的手机收到一条通知：他拍的老磨坊的照片被一个本地旅游博客刊登了。他从没投稿过。他点开链接，看到自己的照片被标注为“匿名”时，惊得下巴都掉了下来。他找到博主的联系方式，打电话过去，声音发紧。“你未经允许就用了我的照片。我要你撤下它并发布更正。”博主结结巴巴地道了歉，说是来源问题。汤姆挂断电话，然后花了一个小时起草了一封停止侵权函，打字时手微微颤抖，那种被践踏的感觉久久无法平息。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: Priya discovered her digital painting of a monsoon scene projected on the wall of a local tech startup's lobby during a tour. Her friend, an employee, had shared it on a whim. Priya's face flushed. She marched to the front desk, her voice controlled but firm. 'That artwork is mine. I never gave permission for this.' The receptionist called a manager, who apologized profusely. Priya stood there, arms crossed, watching them take down the projection. Even as they apologized, she felt a cold knot in her stomach, the unauthorized display feeling like a personal invasion that a simple sorry couldn't undo.
text_zh: 普丽娅在一次参观中，发现她画的季风雨景数字画被投影在一家本地科技初创公司的大厅墙上。她的一个朋友在那里工作，一时兴起就分享了这幅画。普丽娅的脸涨得通红。她大步走到前台，声音受控而坚定。“那件作品是我的。我从没允许过这样使用。”接待员叫来了经理，经理连连道歉。普丽娅站在那里，双臂交叉，看着他们撤下投影。即使他们道歉了，她仍感到胃里打了个冷结，这种未经授权的展示感觉像是一种个人侵犯，一句简单的对不起无法抹去。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: Ethan saw his mixed-media collage of a cityscape in a dentist's office waiting room, framed and hung without a word. He recognized the torn magazine edges. He approached the receptionist, his voice flat. 'Who put that up?' The dentist came out, explaining he'd found it in a pile of donations. Ethan's hands were in his pockets, fists clenched. 'It wasn't a donation. It was mine.' He insisted on taking it down, standing there while the dentist fumbled with the frame. He left with the collage under his arm, but the bitter taste of having his work treated as public property lingered.
text_zh: 伊桑在牙科诊所的候诊室里看到了他的混合媒介拼贴画——一幅城市风景——被裱起来挂在那里，却没人跟他说一声。他认出了那些撕下来的杂志边缘。他走向接待员，声音平淡。“谁把那幅画挂上去的？”牙医走了出来，解释说他在一堆捐赠物品中发现了它。伊桑的手插在口袋里，拳头紧握。“那不是捐赠。那是我的。”他坚持要求把画取下来，站在那里看着牙医笨拙地摆弄画框。他离开时胳膊下夹着那幅拼贴画，但他的作品被当作公共财产对待的苦涩滋味久久不散。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: Ava opened the local newspaper and saw her linocut print of the harbor reproduced on the arts page, credited to 'A local artist.' She hadn't submitted it. She called the editor, her voice strained. 'That's my print. I never gave permission.' The editor said they'd received it via email. Ava's pulse raced. She demanded a retraction and an apology in the next issue. The editor hemmed and hawed, but Ava's tone was unyielding. She hung up, staring at the newspaper, the ink of her creation feeling like a brand of theft, her sense of ownership bruised and raw.
text_zh: 艾娃打开本地报纸，看到她的港口亚麻油毡版画被刊登在艺术版面上，署名为“一位本地艺术家”。她没有投稿过。她打电话给编辑，声音紧绷。“那是我的版画。我从未允许使用。”编辑说他们是通过电子邮件收到的。艾娃的心跳加速。她要求下一期发布撤回声明和道歉。编辑支支吾吾，但艾娃的语气毫不妥协。她挂了电话，盯着报纸，她创作的墨水感觉像是被烙上了偷窃的印记，她的所有权感受到重创，变得愤怒而伤感。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: Marta pushed through the gallery's glass doors, her portfolio case swinging at her side. There, on the far wall, hung her watercolor of the old bridge—her signature, her style, unmistakable. She hadn't sent it anywhere; it had vanished from her studio last month. The curator approached with a practiced smile. 'Lovely piece, isn't it?' Marta's jaw tightened. She stepped closer, studying the frame, the lighting, the small placard with another artist's name. Her hands trembled as she turned, voice low and steady. 'Take it down. Now.' She didn't wait for an answer, already pulling her phone to call her lawyer.
text_zh: 玛尔塔推开画廊的玻璃门，作品集画筒在身侧晃动。在那边的墙上，挂着她的老桥水彩画——她的签名，她的风格，一目了然。她没有把画寄到任何地方；这幅画上个月从她的工作室消失了。策展人带着职业性的微笑走近。“很好看的一件作品，不是吗？”玛尔塔的下颌绷紧了。她走近几步，仔细看着画框、灯光，还有那个写着另一位艺术家名字的小标牌。她转身时双手微微颤抖，声音低沉而平稳。“把它取下来。现在。”她没有等回答，已经掏出手机给律师打电话了。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: Hannah saw her embroidered textile art on a mannequin in a boutique window, tagged with a price. She hadn't sold it. She pushed the door open, the bell jangling. The shopkeeper smiled, but Hannah's face was set. 'That's my work. You have no right to sell it.' The shopkeeper claimed she'd bought it from a flea market. Hannah's hands were trembling. 'It was stolen from my studio.' She demanded it be removed, her voice shaking with the effort to stay composed. She watched the shopkeeper take the mannequin down, but the violation left a bitter residue she couldn't shake.
text_zh: 汉娜看到了她的刺绣纺织艺术品，它被穿在精品店橱窗里的人体模特身上，挂着价签。她没有卖过它。她推开店门，铃铛叮当作响。店主微笑着，但汉娜的表情是坚定的。“那是我的作品。你没有权利出售它。”店主声称她是从跳蚤市场买的。汉娜的双手在颤抖。“那是从我工作室偷来的。”她要求把它取下，声音因努力保持镇定而颤抖。她看着店主把人体模特取下来，但这种侵犯留下了她无法摆脱的苦涩余味。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: Diego's phone buzzed with a message from his cousin: 'Saw your painting at the hotel!' Diego hadn't given it to any hotel. He called his cousin, his voice tight. 'Which hotel?' He drove over, his jaw set. In the lobby, his abstract canvas hung behind the reception desk. He approached the manager, his words clipped. 'That's my work. It was taken without permission.' The manager apologized, saying a decorator had found it. Diego insisted on its immediate removal, his arms crossed, his gaze unwavering. He watched them take it down, but the sense of his creation being used as decoration rankled long after.
text_zh: 迭戈的手机收到一条来自表弟的消息：“在酒店看到你的画了！”迭戈没有把画给任何酒店。他打电话给表弟，声音发紧。“哪家酒店？”他开车过去，下颌紧绷。在大厅里，他的抽象画布挂在接待台后面。他走向经理，言语简短有力。“那是我的作品。是未经允许被拿走的。”经理道了歉，说是一位装饰师发现了它。迭戈坚持要求立刻撤下，双臂交叉，目光坚定。他看着他们把它取下来，但他的作品被用作装饰品的感觉在很久之后仍然让他感到恼怒。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: Sofia found a photo of her street mural on a city tourism website, credited to 'Unknown.' She hadn't submitted it. She called the city's tourism office, her voice strained. 'That mural is mine. I need it credited or removed.' The person on the line was dismissive, saying it was public art. Sofia's grip on the phone tightened. 'It's not public domain. It's my work.' She demanded to speak to a supervisor, her tone leaving no room for argument. Even after they agreed to update the credit, she felt a hot, slow burn that the initial dismissal had triggered, her rights brushed aside too easily.
text_zh: 索菲亚在城市旅游网站上找到了她街头壁画的照片，署名是“未知”。她并没有提交过这张照片。她打电话给市旅游办公室，声音紧绷。“那幅壁画是我的。我需要它署名或删除。”电话那头的人不以为意，说这是公共艺术。索菲亚握紧了电话。“这不是公共领域。这是我的作品。”她要求与主管通话，语气不容置疑。即使他们同意更新署名，她仍然感到一阵灼热的怒火，因为最初的轻蔑态度触发了她的愤怒，她的权利被轻易地忽视了。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: Liam walked into his doctor's waiting room and saw his pencil drawing of a mountain landscape on the wall, framed. He recognized the paper's faint crease. He approached the receptionist, his voice low. 'Who put that there?' The doctor came out, explaining a patient had left it. Liam's eyes narrowed. 'That was mine. It was in my sketchbook.' He demanded it be taken down, his hands in his pockets, fists tight. The doctor apologized, but Liam's gaze was cold as he watched them remove it. He left with the drawing, but the casual appropriation of his work left a sour taste in his mouth.
text_zh: 利亚姆走进医生的候诊室，看到墙上挂着他那幅铅笔画的山水风景，已经装裱好了。他认出了纸上淡淡的折痕。他走近接待员，压低声音说：“谁把那幅画挂在那儿的？”医生走出来，解释说是一位病人留下的。利亚姆眯起眼睛。“那是我的。它在我速写本里。”他要求把它取下来，双手插在口袋里，拳头紧握。医生道了歉，但利亚姆看着他们取下画时，目光冰冷。他带着画离开了，但对他作品随意的挪用让他嘴里留下了一股酸涩的味道。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: Zara saw her digital illustration of a night sky on a friend's social media post, with a caption 'Look what I found in a thrift store!' She hadn't sold it. She messaged her friend, her words sharp. 'That's my work. I never gave it away.' Her friend replied with a shrug emoji. Zara's jaw clenched. She typed a long, precise message about copyright and permission, her fingers tapping hard on the keyboard. Even after her friend agreed to take it down, Zara's pulse was still quick, the casual theft of her art feeling like a personal slight that lingered in her chest.
text_zh: 扎拉在一个朋友的社交媒体帖子上看到了她画的夜空数字插画，配文是“看看我在旧货店发现了什么！”她并没有卖掉它。她给朋友发信息，言辞尖锐。“那是我的作品。我从未给过任何人。”她的朋友回复了一个耸肩的表情符号。扎拉咬紧了牙关。她打了一长段关于版权和许可的精确信息，手指重重地敲击键盘。即使朋友同意删除，扎拉的脉搏仍然很快，对她艺术的随意窃取感觉像是一种个人冒犯，在她心中挥之不去。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: Omar found his ceramic bowl in a display case at a local craft fair, a price tag on it. He hadn't entered. He approached the booth owner, his voice flat. 'That's mine. It was in my studio.' The owner looked surprised, saying they'd bought it from a supplier. Omar's hands were at his sides, fingers twitching. 'It was stolen. I want it back.' The owner hesitated, but Omar's stare was unwavering. He watched the owner unlock the case and hand over the bowl, his grip on it tight. Even as he walked away, the sense of violation made his steps heavy.
text_zh: 奥马尔在当地一个手工艺博览会的展示柜里发现了他做的陶瓷碗，上面贴着价格标签。他并没有参展。他走近摊位主人，声音平淡。“那是我的。它在我工作室里。”主人看起来很惊讶，说他们是从供应商那里买来的。奥马尔双手垂在身侧，手指微微抽动。“它是被偷的。我要拿回来。”主人犹豫了一下，但奥马尔的目光坚定不移。他看着主人打开柜子，把碗递给他，他紧紧抓住碗。即使走开了，被侵犯的感觉让他的脚步变得沉重。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: Chloe saw her photograph of a child playing in a fountain on a local nonprofit's brochure. She'd never given it to them. She called the organization, her voice tight. 'That photo is mine. I never consented to its use.' The director apologized, saying a volunteer had found it online. Chloe's pulse hammered. She demanded they stop printing the brochure and issue a public apology. The director agreed, but Chloe's tone remained clipped. She hung up, staring at the brochure in her hand, the image of her work used for someone else's cause feeling like a deep betrayal of her trust.
text_zh: 克洛伊在当地一家非营利组织的宣传册上看到了她拍摄的一个孩子在喷泉里玩耍的照片。她从未给过他们。她打电话给该组织，声音紧绷。“那张照片是我的。我从未同意使用它。”主任道歉说，是一名志愿者在网上找到的。克洛伊的心跳加速。她要求他们停止印刷宣传册并公开道歉。主任同意了，但克洛伊的语气仍然生硬。她挂了电话，盯着手中的宣传册，她的作品被用于别人的事业，感觉像是对她信任的深深背叛。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: Elena walked into her favorite bookstore and saw her ink drawing of a raven on a tote bag for sale. She hadn't licensed it. She approached the cashier, her voice strained. 'Who made these?' The manager came out, explaining a local artist had provided designs. Elena's eyes widened. 'That's my drawing. I never gave permission.' The manager looked flustered. Elena demanded they remove all the bags and contact the artist. She stood there, arms crossed, while the manager made calls, her gaze fixed on the bags, the sight of her work commodified without her consent fueling a cold, simmering resolve.
text_zh: 埃琳娜走进她最喜欢的书店，看到她的乌鸦水墨画印在出售的帆布包上。她并没有授权。她走近收银员，声音紧绷。“这些是谁做的？”经理出来解释说，是一位当地艺术家提供的设计。埃琳娜睁大了眼睛。“那是我的画。我从未允许过。”经理显得很慌乱。埃琳娜要求他们撤下所有袋子并联系那位艺术家。她站在那里，双臂交叉，经理打着电话，她的目光盯着那些袋子，看到自己的作品未经同意就被商品化，燃起一股冰冷的、酝酿中的决心。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: Mateo found his mosaic tile piece on the wall of a new restaurant, a plaque with his name but no attribution to him. He'd never been contacted. He approached the host, his voice low. 'Who commissioned this?' The owner came out, saying a designer had sourced it. Mateo's jaw tightened. 'That's my work. It was taken from my studio.' He demanded it be removed, his words precise and unyielding. The owner hesitated, but Mateo's stare was unblinking. He watched them take it down, but the fact that his name was there without his consent felt like a slap, his work co-opted for someone else's gain.
text_zh: 马特奥在一家新餐厅的墙上发现了他做的马赛克瓷砖作品，上面有一块铭牌写着他的名字，但没有注明出处。他从未被联系过。他走近接待员，压低声音说：“这是谁委托的？”老板出来说是一位设计师采购的。马特奥咬紧了牙关。“那是我的作品。它是从我工作室拿走的。”他要求将其移除，言辞精确而坚定。老板犹豫了一下，但马特奥的目光一眨不眨。他看着他们把它取下来，但未经他同意就出现他的名字，感觉像是一记耳光，他的作品被挪用为他人谋利。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: Isla saw her watercolor of a lighthouse on a greeting card display at a stationery shop. She hadn't sold the rights. She picked up a card, her hands trembling. She approached the clerk, her voice shaking. 'These cards are using my art without permission.' The clerk looked confused, saying they came from a distributor. Isla demanded to speak to the manager, her tone rising. 'This is theft.' She left her number and demanded a call back, her steps quick as she exited. Even outside, her heart raced, the image of her work mass-produced without her consent burning in her mind.
text_zh: 艾拉在一家文具店的贺卡展示架上看到了她的灯塔水彩画。她并没有出售版权。她拿起一张卡片，双手颤抖。她走近店员，声音颤抖。“这些卡片未经许可使用了我的艺术。”店员看起来很困惑，说它们来自分销商。艾拉要求见经理，声音提高。“这是盗窃。”她留下了电话号码，要求回电，然后快步走了出去。即使在门外，她的心仍在狂跳，她的作品未经同意就被大量复制的画面在她脑海中燃烧。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: Noah found his woodcut print of a fox on a local brewery's beer label. He'd never given them the image. He called the brewery, his voice tight. 'That's my print. I want it removed from your label.' The owner laughed, saying they'd found it online. Noah's grip on the phone tightened. 'It's not a free image. It's mine.' He demanded they stop production and issue a recall. The owner's tone turned dismissive, but Noah's voice was unyielding. He hung up, his jaw set, already drafting a legal letter, the thought of his art being used to sell beer making his blood run hot.
text_zh: 诺亚在当地一家啤酒厂的啤酒标签上发现了他刻的狐狸木刻版画。他从未给过他们这幅图像。他打电话给啤酒厂，声音紧绷。“那是我的版画。我要你把它从标签上拿下来。”老板笑了，说他们是在网上找到的。诺亚握紧了电话。“这不是免费图片。这是我的。”他要求他们停止生产并召回产品。老板的语气变得轻蔑，但诺亚的声音毫不退让。他挂了电话，下巴紧绷，已经在起草法律信函，想到他的艺术被用来卖啤酒，他的血液就沸腾了。

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
text_en: Grace walked into her gym and saw her charcoal portrait of a boxer on the wall, framed. She hadn't given it to them. She approached the front desk, her voice flat. 'Who hung that?' The manager came out, saying a member had donated it. Grace's eyes narrowed. 'That's my work. It was in my studio.' She demanded it be taken down immediately, her arms crossed, her stance firm. The manager apologized, but Grace's gaze was cold as they removed it. She took the portrait, but the casual theft of her art from her own space left a lingering burn, her trust in the place shattered.
text_zh: 格蕾丝走进她的健身房，看到墙上挂着她画的拳击手炭笔画，已经装裱好了。她并没有给过他们。她走近前台，声音平淡。“谁挂的？”经理出来说是一位会员捐赠的。格蕾丝眯起眼睛。“那是我的作品。它在我工作室里。”她要求立即将其取下，双臂交叉，立场坚定。经理道了歉，但格蕾丝看着他们取下画时，目光冰冷。她拿走了画，但从她自己的空间里随意窃取她的艺术，留下了一种挥之不去的灼烧感，她对这个地方的信任破碎了。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: Marta gripped the campus map so hard the creases deepened. The email said the college would close by summer, just as she'd finally lined up lab access for her research. She'd spent years building this project, and now the administration called it 'a strategic realignment.' She walked to the registrar's office, jaw tight, and asked for a printed copy of the closure timeline. The clerk shrugged. Marta set the paper on the counter and spoke slowly, each word deliberate: 'You should have told us before we signed our leases.' She didn't raise her voice, but her hand trembled as she folded the notice.
text_zh: 玛尔塔紧紧抓着校园地图，折痕更深了。邮件说学院将在夏季前关闭，而就在她终于为自己的研究争取到实验室使用权时。她花了多年时间建立这个项目，现在管理部门称之为“战略性调整”。她走到注册办公室，下巴紧绷，要求打印一份关闭时间表。职员耸了耸肩。玛尔塔把纸放在柜台上，缓慢而字斟句酌地说：“你们应该在我们签租约之前告诉我们。”她没有提高声音，但折叠通知时手在颤抖。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: Jonah stood in the registrar's office, the printed notice crumpled in his fist. The clerk offered a rehearsed apology, mentioning consolidation with a larger university. Jonah's jaw worked silently. He had chosen this place for its small classes, for the professor who mentored his thesis. Now that mentor would be scattered to the winds. He spread the paper flat on the counter, smoothing the creases with deliberate care. 'I want the names of everyone who voted on this,' he said, his voice low and steady. 'And I want them to explain it to the students, face to face.'
text_zh: 乔纳站在注册办公室，手里攥着皱巴巴的打印通知。职员提供了一个排练过的道歉，提到与一所更大的大学合并。乔纳的下巴无声地动了动。他选择这个地方是因为小班教学，因为那位指导他论文的教授。现在那位导师将各奔东西。他把纸平铺在柜台上，刻意地抚平褶皱。“我要所有投票决定此事的人的名字，”他说，声音低沉而平稳。“我要他们向学生们当面解释。”

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: Leah had just paid her spring tuition, a significant chunk of her savings. The announcement came via a mass text, a sterile notification that the college would cease operations after the current term. She stared at the screen, her chest tightening. She had turned down a job offer to enroll here, trusting the catalog's promises of accreditation and career support. Now the provost's email talked about 'teach-out agreements' as if that solved everything. Leah began composing a response, her thumbs moving rapidly, demanding a refund for the unused portion of her fees and a clear plan for her credits.
text_zh: 利亚刚刚支付了春季学费，这是她积蓄的一大笔。公告通过群发短信传来，一条冷冰冰的通知，说学院将在本学期结束后停止运营。她盯着屏幕，胸口发紧。她为了入学拒绝了工作机会，相信了目录上关于认证和职业支持的承诺。现在教务长的邮件谈论“教学协议”，好像这能解决一切。利亚开始起草回复，拇指快速移动，要求退还她未使用部分的费用，并为她的学分制定明确计划。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: Damon stood in the empty lecture hall, the projector still humming. The dean's announcement echoed in his head: 'Enrollment decline necessitates consolidation.' His thesis committee had just approved his proposal, and now the archive would be shipped to another state. He walked to the department office, where a staffer was already boxing syllabi. 'Hold on,' Damon said, stepping in front of the cart. 'You're not taking these until I've copied everything I need.' He pulled out his phone and started photographing the course files, his shoulders rigid, ignoring the staffer's protests. His breath came in short, controlled bursts as he worked.
text_zh: 达蒙站在空荡荡的演讲厅里，投影仪还在嗡嗡作响。院长的公告在他脑海中回响：“入学人数下降需要合并。”他的论文委员会刚刚批准了他的提案，现在档案将被运往另一个州。他走到系办公室，一名工作人员已经在装箱教学大纲。“等等，”达蒙说，挡在手推车前。“在我复制完我需要的一切之前，你们不能拿走这些。”他掏出手机开始拍摄课程文件，肩膀僵硬，无视工作人员的抗议。他工作时呼吸短促而克制。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: Priya was in the middle of a lab experiment when her phone buzzed with the news. She read the brief announcement, then set the phone down and continued her pipetting, her movements precise. After a minute, she stopped and stared at the sample. She had chosen this university for its renowned research facility, a chance to work with a specific professor. Now the whole endeavor was being scrapped. She removed her gloves, threw them in the bin, and walked to the dean's office, not to plead, but to demand a written explanation of how this decision had been reached without student consultation.
text_zh: 普里亚正在做实验，手机嗡嗡作响，传来了消息。她读了简短的公告，然后放下手机继续移液，动作精准。一分钟后，她停下来，盯着样本。她选择这所大学是因为其著名的研究设施，有机会与一位特定的教授合作。现在整个事业都要被取消了。她摘下手套，扔进垃圾桶，走到院长办公室，不是去恳求，而是要求书面解释这个决定是如何在没有咨询学生的情况下做出的。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: The town hall meeting was packed. Elena stood near the back, listening to the president's smooth reassurances about 'phased transitions.' She had grown up in this town, watched the college anchor the community. Now it was leaving a void. She waited for the Q&A, then raised her hand. 'What about the scholarships promised to local students?' she asked, her voice carrying. 'What about the programs we helped design?' The president's vague answer made her fists clench at her sides. She did not shout, but she took the microphone when it was offered and listed every broken commitment she could recall.
text_zh: 市政厅会议座无虚席。埃琳娜站在后面，听着校长关于“分阶段过渡”的圆滑保证。她在这个小镇长大，看着这所学院成为社区的支柱。现在它要留下一个空缺。她等到问答环节，然后举手。“那些承诺给当地学生的奖学金呢？”她问道，声音传开。“我们帮助设计的项目呢？”校长含糊的回答让她双拳紧握。她没有喊叫，但当麦克风递过来时，她接过并列举了她能记得的每一个被打破的承诺。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: After the announcement, Ben walked out of the lecture hall and found a bench. He sat there, staring at the old brick buildings, the ivy-covered walls. He had transferred here after a rough year elsewhere, finally feeling a sense of belonging. Now the place was a ghost in the making. He pulled out his phone and started a group chat with his classmates, proposing a petition. He typed quickly, his words sharp: 'We need to make noise. They can't just erase our education.' He sent the message, then began drafting the petition text, his focus sharp and determined.
text_zh: 公告发布后，本走出演讲厅，找到一条长椅。他坐在那里，盯着古老的砖砌建筑，爬满常春藤的墙壁。他在别处度过艰难的一年后转学到这里，终于感到一种归属感。现在这个地方正在变成鬼城。他掏出手机，开始和同学建群聊，提议发起请愿。他快速打字，言辞尖锐：“我们需要制造噪音。他们不能就这样抹去我们的教育。”他发了消息，然后开始起草请愿书，专注而坚定。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: Chloe had been saving for years, working double shifts to afford this private college. The news came in a glossy brochure, a 'special announcement' about merging with a larger institution. She read it on the bus, her stomach dropping. The tuition she had paid would not guarantee the intimate seminars she had been promised. She crumpled the brochure in her bag and, once home, wrote a formal letter of complaint to the state accreditation board. Her handwriting was neat, but the pressure of the pen left grooves in the paper. She listed every discrepancy between the catalog and the new reality.
text_zh: 克洛伊多年来一直在存钱，为了负担这所私立学院，她打了两份工。消息来自一本光鲜的小册子，关于与一所更大的机构合并的“特别公告”。她在公交车上读到，心沉了下去。她支付的学费并不能保证她所被承诺的小型研讨会。她把小册子揉进包里，回家后，给州认证委员会写了一封正式的投诉信。她的字迹整洁，但笔的压力在纸上留下了凹痕。她列出了目录与新现实之间的每一个差异。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: Priya read the notice on the bulletin board while holding her coffee. The college would merge with a larger institution, and her program would be phased out. She'd turned down a job offer to stay here, trusting the promise of a new faculty mentor. Now that mentor had already left, and the board cited 'fiscal prudence.' Priya tore the notice down and carried it to the faculty lounge, where she set it on the table. 'Read this,' she told a colleague, tapping the paper. 'Then tell me why we should keep prepping our classes.' She crossed her arms and waited, her gaze fixed, refusing to look away.
text_zh: 普里亚端着咖啡读着公告栏上的通知。学院将与一所更大的机构合并，她的项目将被逐步取消。她为了留在这里拒绝了工作机会，相信了新导师的承诺。现在那位导师已经离开，董事会引用了“财政审慎”。普里亚撕下通知，拿到教师休息室，放在桌子上。“读读这个，”她对一位同事说，敲着纸。“然后告诉我为什么我们应该继续备课。”她双臂交叉等着，目光坚定，拒绝移开。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: Sofia had just finished her junior year, her capstone project underway. The email arrived with a subject line: 'Important Update.' She opened it, expecting a schedule change. Instead, she read about the permanent closure. She stared at the screen, then reread the message, searching for a loophole. There was none. She closed the laptop and went for a long walk, her steps quick and purposeful. When she returned, she had a list of questions written on a scrap of paper, ready to take to the faculty senate meeting she had just learned about.
text_zh: 索菲亚刚刚完成大三，毕业设计正在进行中。邮件到达，主题是：“重要更新。”她打开，期待是日程变更。相反，她读到了永久关闭的消息。她盯着屏幕，然后重读消息，寻找漏洞。没有。她合上笔记本电脑，去散了很长时间的步，步伐快速而坚定。当她回来时，她在一张废纸上写下了一系列问题，准备带到她刚听说的教师参议院会议上。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: The news broke during a faculty meeting, but Liam was a student representative. He sat in the back, listening to the trustees explain the financial shortfall. He had been an advocate for student services, pushing for better mental health resources. Now the entire institution was dissolving. When the floor opened for questions, Liam stood. 'You've been planning this for months, haven't you?' he asked, his tone flat. 'While we were paying tuition and planning our futures.' He did not wait for an answer, but walked out, his mind already racing with ways to organize a student protest.
text_zh: 消息在教职工会议上传开，但利亚姆是学生代表。他坐在后排，听着董事会解释资金短缺的问题。他一直倡导学生服务，推动改善心理健康资源。现在整个机构即将解散。当进入提问环节时，利亚姆站了起来。“你们已经计划了好几个月了，不是吗？”他问道，语气平淡。“而我们在支付学费，规划未来。”他没有等待回答，就走了出去，脑海中已经在飞速思考如何组织学生抗议。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: Nadia was in the library when she saw the post on the school's official account. She put down the book she was holding, a rare edition she had reserved for her research. The closure notice was brief, almost clinical. She felt a hot flush rise to her cheeks. She had chosen this college specifically for its special collections. She marched to the reference desk and asked the librarian if she knew anything. The librarian's sad nod was enough. Nadia left the library, but not before taking a photo of the notice, intending to share it widely.
text_zh: 纳迪亚在图书馆时看到了学校官方账号上的帖子。她放下手中的书，那是一本她为研究而预留的珍稀版本。关闭通知简短，几乎不带感情。她感到一阵热流涌上脸颊。她选择这所学院正是为了它的特藏。她走到咨询台，问图书管理员是否知道什么。图书管理员悲伤地点了点头，这就足够了。纳迪亚离开了图书馆，但离开前拍下了通知的照片，打算广泛传播。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: Tommy had been a first-generation student, proud to be the first in his family to attend college. The announcement came as a recorded video message, the president's face solemn. Tommy watched it twice, then paused the video at the president's face. He wanted to see if there was any hint of regret. There wasn't. He texted his mother, who had sacrificed so much for his tuition. Then he called the admissions office, demanding to know if there was any way to transfer his credits without loss. The long hold music made his grip on the phone tighten.
text_zh: 汤米是家中第一代大学生，为自己是家里第一个上大学的人而自豪。公告是以录制的视频消息形式发布的，校长的表情严肃。汤米看了两遍，然后暂停视频，定格在校长的脸上。他想看看是否有任何悔意。没有。他给母亲发了短信，母亲为他的学费牺牲了很多。然后他打电话给招生办公室，要求知道是否有办法无损转学分。漫长的等待音乐让他握紧了手机。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: Ava was a senior, weeks away from graduation. The news of the closure hit her like a physical blow. She had already lined up a job, but the degree's validity was now in question. She sat in the student union, watching others react with shock or tears. She felt something different, a cold resolve. She pulled out her laptop and started a spreadsheet, tracking every course she had taken, every credit earned, and the corresponding accreditation requirements. She planned to present this evidence to the university's board, to hold them accountable for her wasted years.
text_zh: 艾娃是大四学生，离毕业还有几周。关闭的消息像一记重击。她已经找到了一份工作，但学位的有效性现在成了问题。她坐在学生会里，看着其他人震惊或流泪。她感到一种不同的东西，一种冷静的决心。她拿出笔记本电脑，开始制作电子表格，记录她上过的每一门课、获得的每一个学分，以及相应的认证要求。她计划将这些证据提交给大学董事会，让他们为她浪费的岁月负责。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: Ethan had just signed a lease on an apartment near campus, planning for his final year. The closure notice came with a PDF attachment detailing 'teach-out' options at other schools. He read it on his phone, standing in his new, empty living room. The room felt like a mockery. He had uprooted his life for this. He called his landlord, but the lease was binding. Then he called the registrar, his voice strained, asking how the school intended to help students with housing costs. The vague answer made him slam his fist against the wall, a rare outburst.
text_zh: 伊桑刚签了一份校园附近公寓的租约，为最后一学年做准备。关闭通知附带了一个PDF附件，详细说明了其他学校的“完成学业”选项。他站在新租的空荡荡的客厅里，用手机阅读。房间感觉像是一种嘲弄。他为此改变了生活。他打电话给房东，但租约是有约束力的。然后他打电话给注册主任，声音紧张，问学校打算如何帮助学生解决住房费用。模糊的回答让他一拳砸在墙上，这是罕见的爆发。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: Leo's phone buzzed with the university alert while he was shelving books in the library. The building would close, and the collection would be dispersed. He'd spent a semester organizing the rare poetry section, and now the donor's family was reclaiming everything. Leo set down the book he was holding and walked to the circulation desk. 'Who decided this?' he asked the librarian, who shrugged. Leo pulled out his notebook and began listing the titles he'd cataloged. 'I'm documenting what's here,' he said, his pen pressing hard. 'If they're going to dismantle this, someone should have a record.' He didn't look up, but his jaw was set.
text_zh: 利奥在图书馆整理书架时，手机收到了大学警报。大楼将关闭，藏书将被分散。他花了一个学期整理珍稀诗歌区，现在捐赠者的家人要收回一切。利奥放下手中的书，走到借阅台。“谁决定的？”他问图书管理员，管理员耸了耸肩。利奥掏出笔记本，开始列出他编目的书名。“我在记录这里有什么，”他说，笔尖用力。“如果他们要拆毁这里，应该有人留下记录。”他没有抬头，但下巴紧绷。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: The closure was announced on the same day the college sent out a fundraising appeal. Sarah saw the juxtaposition and felt a surge of something hot and bitter. She had donated to the annual fund, trusting the institution's future. Now they were asking for more money while shutting down. She opened the email and composed a reply, her words polite but pointed, asking for a full refund of her donations and an explanation of how the funds had been used. She hit send, then immediately started drafting a letter to the local newspaper.
text_zh: 关闭的消息与学院发出筹款呼吁在同一天公布。莎拉看到这种并置，感到一阵灼热的苦涩。她曾向年度基金捐款，信任学校的未来。现在他们却在关闭的同时要求更多钱。她打开邮件，写了一封回复，措辞礼貌但尖锐，要求全额退还她的捐款，并解释资金的使用情况。她点击发送，然后立即开始起草一封给当地报纸的信。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: Diego was a commuter student, balancing a full-time job and night classes. The news reached him via a voicemail from his advisor, left during his shift. He listened to it in the break room, his face expressionless. He had been taking one class per semester, inching toward his degree. Now the finish line had moved. He called his advisor back, but the line was busy. He left a message, his voice controlled but firm, asking for a meeting to discuss his options. After hanging up, he stared at his work schedule, wondering how he would ever finish now.
text_zh: 迭戈是一名走读生，兼顾全职工作和夜校课程。消息是通过顾问的语音邮件传来的，是在他上班时留下的。他在休息室听了，面无表情。他一直每学期修一门课，慢慢接近学位。现在终点线移动了。他回电给顾问，但线路繁忙。他留了言，声音克制但坚定，要求开会讨论他的选择。挂断后，他盯着自己的工作日程，想知道现在怎样才能完成学业。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: Nadia sat in the student union, staring at the official letter. The college would cease operations after the current term, and her teaching assistantship would end early. She'd already planned her fall courses, bought the textbooks, and scheduled office hours. Now she crumpled the letter, then smoothed it out again. She went to the provost's office and stood in the doorway until the provost looked up. 'This isn't a decision,' Nadia said, holding up the paper. 'This is an announcement after the fact.' She placed the letter on the desk, her palm flat on it. 'I expect a meeting with the board.' She waited, unmoving, until the provost agreed.
text_zh: 纳迪亚坐在学生会里，盯着官方信函。学院将在本学期结束后停止运营，她的助教职位将提前结束。她已经计划好了秋季课程，买了教科书，安排了办公时间。现在她揉皱了信，然后又抚平。她去了教务长办公室，站在门口，直到教务长抬起头。“这不是一个决定，”纳迪亚举起纸说。“这是事后通知。”她把信放在桌上，手掌平放在上面。“我期待与董事会会面。”她一动不动地等着，直到教务长同意。

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text_en: The news came from a friend's text, a link to a news article. Leo clicked it, reading about the college's 'financial restructuring' and 'planned closure.' He was a sophomore, his tuition paid through a combination of scholarships and loans. He felt a dull throb in his temples. He had chosen this school for its reputation in environmental science, a field he cared deeply about. He called the financial aid office, but the line was busy. He left a message, his tone clipped, asking how the closure would affect his loans. Then he started a list of all the administrators to contact.
text_zh: 消息来自朋友的短信，一个新闻文章的链接。利奥点击了，阅读了关于学院“财务重组”和“计划关闭”的内容。他是大二学生，学费通过奖学金和贷款的组合支付。他感到太阳穴隐隐作痛。他选择这所学校是因为它在环境科学方面的声誉，这是他深感兴趣的领域。他打电话给财务援助办公室，但线路繁忙。他留了言，语气简短，问关闭将如何影响他的贷款。然后他开始列出所有需要联系的管理人员。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: When the new neighbor knocked and asked to cut the old maple on the boundary, Mara folded her arms. She’d watched that tree shade her vegetable patch for a decade. She said no, but he returned with a surveyor’s flag and a chainsaw. As he revved the engine, she stood on her side, hands on hips, jaw tight. She didn’t shout, but her voice was steel: “That tree is half mine. You’ll pay for its removal, and I’ll call the city if you touch it without a permit.” He backed off, but she stayed by the window, watching, ready.
text_zh: 当新邻居敲门，要求砍掉边界上的老枫树时，玛拉双臂交叉。她看着那棵树为她的菜园遮荫已有十年。她说不，但他带着测量旗和电锯回来了。当他发动引擎时，她站在自己这边，双手叉腰，下巴紧绷。她没有喊叫，但她的声音像钢铁一样：“那棵树有一半是我的。你要为砍掉它付钱，如果你没有许可证碰它，我会打电话给市政府。”他退让了，但她守在窗边，注视着，准备着。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: Elliot’s pulse quickened when the neighbor, a man he barely knew, proposed cutting the spruce that had stood between their yards for years. “It’s dropping needles on my lawn,” the man said. Elliot felt a hot tightness in his chest. He’d built a birdhouse in that tree. He spoke slowly, each word deliberate: “That tree is the reason my kids have shade. You want it gone, you’ll have to go through me and the property line law.” He didn’t raise his voice, but his hands trembled as he gestured for the man to leave.
text_zh: 当邻居，一个他几乎不认识的男人，提议砍掉多年来矗立在他们院子之间的云杉时，埃利奥特的心跳加快了。“它把针叶掉在我的草坪上，”那人说。埃利奥特感到胸口一阵灼热。他在那棵树上建了一个鸟屋。他慢慢地说，每个字都经过深思：“那棵树是我孩子们有阴凉的原因。你想让它消失，你得先过我这一关和地产线法律。”他没有提高声音，但当他示意那人离开时，他的手在颤抖。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: Marta watched from her kitchen window as the neighbor, Pete, circled the old oak with a chainsaw. She had planted that tree with her late husband. When she stepped outside, Pete said the roots were lifting his driveway. Marta crossed her arms. "That tree stays," she said, her voice flat. Pete shrugged and mentioned the city ordinance. Marta's jaw tightened. She walked back inside and called the city office, then the tree service, then her lawyer. She spent the afternoon on the porch, arms crossed, staring at Pete's side of the line. The saw stayed silent.
text_zh: 玛尔塔从厨房窗户看着邻居皮特用电锯绕着老橡树转。那棵树是她和已故丈夫一起种的。当她走出去时，皮特说树根顶起了他的车道。玛尔塔双臂交叉。“那棵树留着，”她说，声音平淡。皮特耸耸肩，提到了城市条例。玛尔塔的下巴绷紧了。她走回屋里，打电话给市政办公室，然后打给树木服务公司，然后打给她的律师。她整个下午都坐在门廊上，双臂交叉，盯着皮特那边。电锯一直沉默着。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: The maple had been there since before the houses were built. When the new neighbor, a young man named Cole, knocked on her door and asked to cut it down, Ruth felt a cold knot in her stomach. "It's on the property line," he said, "so I have a right." Ruth stared at him. "You have a right to ask," she said. "I have a right to refuse." Cole's face tightened. Ruth closed the door, then stood at the window, watching him pace. She didn't move until he went inside. Then she called the county surveyor and made an appointment.
text_zh: 枫树在房子建成之前就存在了。当新邻居，一个叫科尔的年轻人，敲她的门，要求砍掉它时，露丝感到胃里一阵冰冷的结。“它在房产线上，”他说，“所以我有权利。”露丝盯着他。“你有权利问，”她说。“我有权利拒绝。”科尔的脸绷紧了。露丝关上门，然后站在窗边，看着他踱步。她一动不动，直到他进屋。然后她打电话给县测量员，预约了时间。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: The willow's branches hung over both yards, but the trunk stood squarely on the line. When the neighbor, a woman named Priya, proposed cutting it down, Tom felt his chest tighten. "It's a hazard," Priya said, pointing at a cracked limb. Tom shook his head. "I've had it checked. It's fine." Priya insisted, her voice rising. Tom stepped closer, his hands clenched at his sides. "You're not touching that tree," he said. Priya opened her mouth, but Tom turned and walked into his garage, slamming the door. He spent the evening sharpening his saw, though he had no intention of using it.
text_zh: 柳树的枝条垂过两个院子，但树干正好立在边界线上。当邻居，一个叫普里亚的女人，提议砍掉它时，汤姆感到胸口一紧。“它是个危险，”普里亚指着一根裂开的树枝说。汤姆摇了摇头。“我让人检查过。它没问题。”普里亚坚持，声音提高了。汤姆走近一步，双手在身侧握紧。“你别碰那棵树，”他说。普里亚张开嘴，但汤姆转身走进车库，砰地关上门。他整个晚上都在磨他的锯子，尽管他无意使用它。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: The pine was the only thing blocking the view of the new condo complex. When the neighbor, a man named Greg, asked to cut it down, Ellen felt a surge of heat. "It's on the line," Greg said, "so I'll pay for half." Ellen shook her head. "It's not for sale." Greg laughed, a short, dismissive sound. Ellen's face went still. "I said no," she repeated. Greg shrugged and said he'd check with the city. Ellen watched him walk away, her hands trembling slightly. She went inside and wrote a long letter to the zoning board, her pen pressing hard into the paper.
text_zh: 松树是唯一挡住新公寓楼视野的东西。当邻居，一个叫格雷格的男人，要求砍掉它时，艾伦感到一阵热浪。“它在线上，”格雷格说，“所以我付一半钱。”艾伦摇了摇头。“它不卖。”格雷格笑了，一声短促、轻蔑的笑。艾伦的脸变得平静。“我说了不，”她重复道。格雷格耸耸肩，说他会去和市政府核实。艾伦看着他走开，双手微微颤抖。她走进屋里，给分区委员会写了一封长信，笔重重地压在纸上。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: The old elm had survived a storm that took down half the street. When the neighbor, a man named Dave, asked to cut it down because it dropped leaves on his lawn, Sam felt a hot flash of disbelief. "You want to kill a healthy tree for leaves?" Sam said. Dave shrugged. "It's a nuisance." Sam's jaw worked. "No," he said. Dave started to argue, but Sam held up a hand. "I said no. That's final." Dave's face reddened, but he turned and left. Sam stood on the porch, arms crossed, watching Dave's back. He didn't move until Dave was out of sight.
text_zh: 老榆树在一场摧毁了半条街的风暴中幸存下来。当邻居，一个叫戴夫的男人，因为树叶掉在他的草坪上而要求砍掉它时，萨姆感到一阵难以置信的热浪。“你想为了一片叶子杀死一棵健康的树？”萨姆说。戴夫耸耸肩。“它是个麻烦。”萨姆的下巴动了动。“不，”他说。戴夫开始争辩，但萨姆举起一只手。“我说了不。就这样。”戴夫的脸涨红了，但他转身离开了。萨姆站在门廊上，双臂交叉，看着戴夫的背影。他一动不动，直到戴夫消失在视线之外。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: Marta watched the neighbor's chainsaw bite into the oak that shaded her kitchen window. He'd claimed the tree was half his, so he could do as he pleased. She stepped outside, arms crossed. "You're cutting the branches that hang over my roof," she said. He shrugged and revved the saw. Marta stood there, jaw tight, counting the years she'd watered that tree's roots. She didn't move when sawdust sprayed her shoes. She just memorized his face, thinking of the call she'd make to the zoning office the moment he finished.
text_zh: 玛尔塔看着邻居的电锯咬进遮蔽她厨房窗户的橡树。他声称那棵树有一半是他的，所以他可以为所欲为。她走出去，双臂交叉。“你在砍我屋顶上方的树枝，”她说。他耸耸肩，发动了锯子。玛尔塔站在那里，下巴紧绷，数着她给那棵树根浇水的年数。锯末溅到她的鞋子上，她一动不动。她只是记住他的脸，想着他一完工她就要给分区办公室打的电话。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: The oak was the only shade on the block. When the neighbor, a woman named Carol, asked to cut it down because it blocked her solar panels, Frank felt a hot surge of resentment. "You knew about the tree when you bought the house," he said. Carol shrugged. "I didn't think it would be this big." Frank's hands clenched. "It's not coming down," he said. Carol's eyes narrowed. "We'll see," she said, and turned away. Frank watched her go, his heart pounding. He went inside and called the city, then the tree board, then his lawyer. He spent the afternoon on the phone, his voice tight.
text_zh: 橡树是街区唯一的阴凉。当邻居，一个叫卡罗尔的女人，因为挡住了她的太阳能电池板而要求砍掉它时，弗兰克感到一阵强烈的怨恨。“你买房子的时候就知道有这棵树，”他说。卡罗尔耸耸肩。“我没想到它会这么大。”弗兰克的手握紧了。“它不会倒，”他说。卡罗尔眯起眼睛。“走着瞧，”她说，然后转身离开。弗兰克看着她走，心跳加速。他走进屋里，打电话给市政府，然后打给树木委员会，然后打给他的律师。他整个下午都在打电话，声音紧绷。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: The birch was the last thing his daughter had planted before she left for college. When the neighbor, a man named Rick, asked to cut it down because it was too close to his fence, Paul felt a cold knot in his stomach. "That tree stays," Paul said. Rick frowned. "It's on the line." Paul shook his head. "It's on my side." Rick pulled out a survey map. Paul didn't look at it. "I don't care what that says," Paul said. "You're not touching it." Rick's face hardened. Paul stepped forward, his hands at his sides. Rick backed up, then turned and walked away. Paul stood there, breathing hard, until Rick was gone.
text_zh: 白桦树是他女儿去上大学前种的最后一件事。当邻居，一个叫里克的男人，因为太靠近他的栅栏而要求砍掉它时，保罗感到胃里一阵冰冷的结。“那棵树留着，”保罗说。里克皱起眉头。“它在线上。”保罗摇了摇头。“它在我这边。”里克拿出一张测量图。保罗没有看。“我不在乎那上面说什么，”保罗说。“你别碰它。”里克的脸硬了起来。保罗向前一步，双手放在身侧。里克后退，然后转身走开。保罗站在那里，喘着粗气，直到里克消失。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: The surveyor's stakes were still in the ground when Roland saw the fresh cut on the maple's trunk. His neighbor had started without a word, claiming the property line ran through the tree's middle. Roland walked over, hands in his pockets. "We agreed to talk first." The man wiped his brow. "Talk's over." Roland stared at the gash, then at his own house, where his kids had hung a swing from that branch. He turned and went inside, but he didn't unpack the boxes. He sat by the window, watching, his knuckles white on the armrest.
text_zh: 罗纳德看到枫树树干上的新切口时，测量员的木桩还插在地上。他的邻居一声不吭就动了手，声称地界线正好穿过树的正中间。罗纳德双手插在口袋里走过去。“我们说好先谈的。”那人擦了擦额头。“谈完了。”罗纳德盯着那道切口，又看看自己的房子，孩子们曾在那个树枝上挂过秋千。他转身进了屋，但没有打开那些箱子。他坐在窗边，望着外面，指节在扶手上攥得发白。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: The willow had been there for decades, its branches a haven for birds. When the neighbor, a man named Tom, asked to cut it down because it was blocking his view, Alice felt a surge of protectiveness. "That tree is older than both of us," she said. Tom shrugged. "It's on the line." Alice shook her head. "It's not coming down." Tom's jaw tightened. "I'll pay for it." Alice's voice was cold. "It's not for sale." Tom stared at her, then turned and walked away. Alice stood on the porch, her arms crossed, watching him go. She didn't move until he was inside his house.
text_zh: 那棵柳树已经立了几十年，枝条是鸟儿的庇护所。当邻居，一个叫汤姆的男人，因为树挡住了他的视线而要求砍掉它时，爱丽丝感到一阵强烈的保护欲。“那棵树比我们俩都老，”她说。汤姆耸耸肩。“它在界线上。”爱丽丝摇摇头。“它不能砍。”汤姆的下巴绷紧了。“我会付钱。”爱丽丝的声音冰冷。“它不卖。”汤姆盯着她，然后转身走开了。爱丽丝站在门廊上，双臂交叉，看着他离去。她一动不动，直到他进了自己的房子。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: Priya found the note taped to her door: "Tree coming down Saturday." No signature, no discussion. The elm stood exactly on the line, its roots lifting both their sidewalks. She knocked on his door. He opened it, beer in hand. "It drops leaves in my gutters." She said, "It also shades my bedroom." He shrugged. "Not my problem." Priya went back inside and pulled out the property deed, tracing the old map with her finger. She underlined the shared-ownership clause, then set the paper on the table, staring at it until the words blurred.
text_zh: 普里亚发现门上贴着一张纸条：“周六砍树。”没有署名，没有商量。那棵榆树正好长在界线上，树根把两边的人行道都拱了起来。她敲了他的门。他开了门，手里拿着啤酒。“它的叶子掉进我的排水沟里。”她说：“它也给我的卧室遮阴。”他耸耸肩。“那不是我的问题。”普里亚回到屋里，拿出地契，用手指描着旧地图。她在共同所有权条款下划了线，然后把纸放在桌上，盯着它，直到字迹模糊。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: The thud of the axe woke Dana before sunrise. She pulled on her robe and found her neighbor halfway up the oak, sawing a limb that hung over her fence. "Hey!" she called. He didn't stop. "This tree is on both sides." He grunted, "I'm just trimming." Dana watched a heavy branch crash onto her rose bushes. She stood very still, her breath short, then walked back inside and called the city arborist. When she hung up, she sat on the floor by the window, arms wrapped around her knees, waiting for the inspector's truck.
text_zh: 斧头的闷响在天亮前就把达娜吵醒了。她披上睡袍，发现邻居正爬到橡树半腰，锯着一根伸过她栅栏的树枝。“嘿！”她喊道。他没有停。“这棵树两边都有。”他咕哝道：“我只是修剪一下。”达娜看着一根粗大的树枝砸在她的玫瑰花丛上。她站着一动不动，呼吸急促，然后走回屋里，给市里的树木管理员打了电话。挂断电话后，她靠着窗户坐在地板上，双臂抱住膝盖，等着检查员的车来。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: The cherry tree was the first thing she'd planted when she moved in. When the neighbor, a woman named Lisa, asked to cut it down because it was attracting birds, Mark felt a hot surge of resentment. "Birds are good," he said. Lisa shook her head. "They're noisy." Mark's voice was tight. "You're in a neighborhood." Lisa crossed her arms. "I want it gone." Mark's jaw worked. "No." Lisa's eyes narrowed. "I'll talk to the city." Mark stepped forward. "Go ahead," he said. "I'll be there." Lisa turned and walked away. Mark watched her go, his hands shaking. He went inside and started writing a letter, his pen pressing hard.
text_zh: 那棵樱桃树是她搬来时种下的第一样东西。当邻居，一个叫丽莎的女人，因为树招鸟而要求砍掉它时，马克感到一阵强烈的怨恨。“鸟是好的，”他说。丽莎摇摇头。“它们很吵。”马克的声音紧绷。“你住在社区里。”丽莎双臂交叉。“我要它消失。”马克的下巴动了动。“不行。”丽莎眯起眼睛。“我会去找市里。”马克上前一步。“去吧，”他说。“我会到场。”丽莎转身走了。马克看着她离去，双手颤抖。他进屋开始写信，笔压得很重。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: The elm was the only thing that kept the afternoon sun from baking the living room. When the neighbor, a man named Ray, asked to cut it down because it was blocking his satellite signal, Tina felt a cold knot in her stomach. "You can move the dish," she said. Ray shook his head. "It's easier to cut the tree." Tina's voice was flat. "It's not easier for me." Ray's face tightened. "It's on the line." Tina crossed her arms. "It's staying." Ray stared at her, then turned and walked away. Tina stood on the porch, her heart pounding, watching him go. She didn't move until he was inside his house.
text_zh: 那棵榆树是唯一能让午后的阳光不把客厅烤得滚烫的东西。当邻居，一个叫雷的男人，因为树挡住了他的卫星信号而要求砍掉它时，蒂娜感到胃里一阵发紧。“你可以移动天线，”她说。雷摇摇头。“砍树更容易。”蒂娜的声音平淡。“对我来说不容易。”雷的脸绷紧了。“它在界线上。”蒂娜双臂交叉。“它得留着。”雷盯着她，然后转身走了。蒂娜站在门廊上，心怦怦直跳，看着他离去。她一动不动，直到他进了自己的房子。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: Eli's neighbor had hired a crew without a permit, or so Eli assumed, because no one had asked. The crew leader pointed at the pine. "Owner says it's a hazard." Eli crossed the yard. "I own half of that tree." The man shrugged. "Talk to him." Eli found his neighbor on the porch. "You can't just—" "I can," the neighbor said, and went inside. Eli stood there, hands shaking slightly, then walked to the tree and placed his palm flat against the bark. He stayed there, ignoring the crew's stares, until they shut off the saw.
text_zh: 伊莱的邻居雇了一队人，没有许可证，至少伊莱是这么认为的，因为没人问过。领队指着那棵松树。“主人说它是个隐患。”伊莱穿过院子。“那棵树我有一半。”那人耸耸肩。“跟他谈。”伊莱在门廊上找到了邻居。“你不能就这么——”“我能，”邻居说着，进了屋。伊莱站在那里，双手微微颤抖，然后走到树前，把手掌平贴在树皮上。他待在那里，无视工人们的目光，直到他们关掉了锯子。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: The letter from the city arrived, but Lena already knew. Her neighbor had filed a complaint about the willow's roots, and the inspector had sided with him. She read the notice twice, then folded it neatly. She went outside and found him watering his lawn. "You didn't tell me you filed." He smiled. "Didn't think I needed to." Lena looked at the willow, then at him. "I'll fight it." He laughed. She turned away, but not before she'd memorized every detail of his face. Back inside, she began writing her appeal, her pen pressing hard enough to leave grooves in the paper.
text_zh: 市里的信到了，但莉娜已经知道了。她的邻居就柳树的树根提出了投诉，检查员站在了他那边。她把通知读了两遍，然后整齐地折好。她走出去，发现他在给草坪浇水。“你没告诉我你投诉了。”他笑了。“我觉得没必要。”莉娜看了看柳树，又看了看他。“我会抗争的。”他大笑。她转过身去，但在此之前，她已经记住了他脸上的每一个细节。回到屋里，她开始写申诉书，笔压得很重，在纸上留下了凹痕。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: The oak was the only thing that kept the yard from being a dust bowl. When the neighbor, a woman named Pat, asked to cut it down because it was blocking her view of the street, Jim felt a hot surge of protectiveness. "That tree is the best thing on this block," he said. Pat shook her head. "I can't see the traffic." Jim's voice was tight. "You can look around it." Pat crossed her arms. "I want it gone." Jim's jaw worked. "No." Pat's eyes narrowed. "I'll get a survey." Jim stepped forward. "Go ahead," he said. "I'll get my own." Pat turned and walked away. Jim watched her go, his hands shaking. He spent the afternoon on the phone, his voice low and hard.
text_zh: 那棵橡树是唯一能让院子不变成尘土飞扬的空地的东西。当邻居，一个叫帕特的女人，因为树挡住了她看街道的视线而要求砍掉它时，吉姆感到一阵强烈的保护欲。“那棵树是这条街上最好的东西，”他说。帕特摇摇头。“我看不见车流。”吉姆的声音紧绷。“你可以绕过它看。”帕特双臂交叉。“我要它消失。”吉姆的下巴动了动。“不行。”帕特眯起眼睛。“我会找人测量。”吉姆上前一步。“去吧，”他说。“我也会找人。”帕特转身走了。吉姆看着她离去，双手颤抖。他整个下午都在打电话，声音低沉而强硬。

topic: A neighbor asks to cut down a tree on the property line
text_en: The birch was the only thing that reminded her of her childhood home. When the neighbor, a man named Ed, asked to cut it down because it was dropping bark on his lawn, Rosa felt a cold knot in her stomach. "That tree is not coming down," she said. Ed frowned. "It's a mess." Rosa's voice was flat. "It's a tree." Ed stepped closer. "I'll pay for it." Rosa shook her head. "It's not for sale." Ed's face hardened. "You're being unreasonable." Rosa's jaw tightened. "No, I'm being clear." Ed stared at her, then turned and walked away. Rosa stood on the porch, her arms crossed, watching him go. She didn't move until he was inside his house.
text_zh: 那棵白桦树是唯一能让她想起童年家园的东西。当邻居，一个叫埃德的男人，因为树皮掉在他的草坪上而要求砍掉它时，罗莎感到胃里一阵发紧。“那棵树不能砍，”她说。埃德皱起眉头。“它一团糟。”罗莎的声音平淡。“它是一棵树。”埃德走近一步。“我会付钱。”罗莎摇摇头。“它不卖。”埃德的脸色变得僵硬。“你不可理喻。”罗莎的下巴绷紧。“不，我说得很清楚。”埃德盯着她，然后转身走了。罗莎站在门廊上，双臂交叉，看着他离去。她一动不动，直到他进了自己的房子。

topic: Someone discovers their partner has been writing a novel about them
text_en: Nadia found the manuscript tucked between Leo's tax folders. Her own name, years, and the apartment's quirks were all there—the chipped mug, the way she hummed off-key. She read about a version of herself who couldn't stop talking about her mother, and who cried at commercials. Leo had never asked her about any of it. He'd just watched, taken notes, and made her a character. She set the pages down. Her hands were steady as she pulled out her suitcase, but her jaw was set. She packed only her things, leaving his notes untouched on the desk.
text_zh: 娜迪亚在利奥的税务文件夹之间发现了那份手稿。她自己的名字、那些年份，还有公寓里的种种怪癖都在里面——那个有缺口的马克杯，她跑调哼歌的样子。她读到另一个版本的自己，那个版本的她不停地谈论母亲，还会因为广告而哭泣。利奥从未问过她任何关于这些的事。他只是观察、做笔记，然后把她变成了一个角色。她放下那些纸页。她拉出行李箱时双手很稳，但下巴紧绷着。她只收拾了自己的东西，把他的笔记原封不动地留在书桌上。

topic: Someone discovers their partner has been writing a novel about them
text_en: Maya found the manuscript in Leo's desk drawer, a stack of pages titled *The Quiet Hours*. She read until her hands trembled. It was her—her habit of biting her lip, the way she folded laundry, even the scar on her knee. He had written her as fragile, needing his steadying hand. Every line was a small theft. She slammed the drawer shut, then opened it again, rereading the passage where his fictional self calmed her fictional panic. Her jaw clenched. She copied the file to her drive, deleted his draft, and left a single printed page on his pillow: "Write your own life."
text_zh: 玛雅在利奥的书桌抽屉里发现了那份手稿，一叠标题为《安静时光》的纸页。她读着读着，双手开始颤抖。那就是她——她咬嘴唇的习惯，她叠衣服的方式，甚至她膝盖上的伤疤。他把她写成一个脆弱的人，需要他稳定的手来扶持。每一行都是小小的偷窃。她砰地关上抽屉，然后又打开，重读那段他虚构的自我安抚她虚构的恐慌的段落。她咬紧牙关。她把文件复制到自己的硬盘，删除了他的草稿，并在他的枕头上留下一张打印的纸页：“写你自己的人生吧。”

topic: Someone discovers their partner has been writing a novel about them
text_en: Jules came home early from a canceled meeting to find Priya's notebook open on the sofa cushion. The handwriting was looped and careful, describing a person who 'sulked like a child when dinner was late.' Jules recognized the specific complaint they'd made last Tuesday. They flipped to the next page, finding themselves portrayed as petty and needy. Jules felt the heat climb up their neck. They closed the notebook with a sharp tap and placed it on Priya's pillow, then sat down to wait, tapping their foot until they heard the key in the lock.
text_zh: 朱尔斯因会议取消而提前回家，发现普里娅的笔记本摊开放在沙发垫上。笔迹是圆润而仔细的，描述着一个人“晚餐迟到时就像孩子一样生闷气”。朱尔斯认出了上周二他们提出的那个具体抱怨。他们翻到下一页，发现自己被描绘成小气和粘人。朱尔斯感到热度从脖子上升起来。他们啪的一声合上笔记本，把它放在普里娅的枕头上，然后坐下来等待，脚一直敲着地面，直到听到钥匙插进锁孔的声音。

topic: Someone discovers their partner has been writing a novel about them
text_en: Ethan discovered the document on the shared cloud drive, a file named 'Anchorage.' His own childhood town, his father's boat, the scar on his knee—all present. The protagonist, however, was a coward who ran from the sea after a minor storm. Ethan read his own life reduced to a cautionary tale. His fingers tightened on the mouse, knuckles whitening. He deleted the file from the trash, then restored it, then deleted it again. When his roommate came in, Ethan stood up, jaw tight, and pointed at the screen. 'Explain this.'
text_zh: 伊桑在共享云盘上发现了那份文档，文件名是“安克雷奇”。他自己童年的小镇，他父亲的船，他膝盖上的伤疤——都在里面。然而，主角是个懦夫，在一场小风暴后就逃离了大海。伊桑读到自己的人生被简化成一个警示故事。他的手指在鼠标上收紧，指节发白。他从回收站删除了文件，然后又恢复，然后又删除。当室友进来时，伊桑站起来，下巴紧绷，指着屏幕。“解释一下这个。”

topic: Someone discovers their partner has been writing a novel about them
text_en: Lena found the printed pages in the recycling bin, half-torn. Her nickname, 'Lulu,' was there. The story described a woman who laughed at everything, who was afraid of silence, who used noise to fill a void. Lena had only told Marcus about her fear of quiet rooms. She smoothed out the sheet, reading the insulting lines again. Her pulse thumped in her ears. She took the torn pages and placed them on Marcus's pillow, then stood in the doorway with her arms crossed, waiting for him to come home, her mouth a thin line.
text_zh: 莉娜在回收站里发现了那些打印的纸页，已经撕了一半。她的昵称“露露”就在上面。故事描述了一个对什么都笑的女人，一个害怕沉默、用噪音填补空虚的女人。莉娜只告诉过马库斯她害怕安静的房间。她抚平那张纸，又读了一遍那些侮辱性的句子。她的脉搏在耳边砰砰作响。她拿起那些撕碎的纸页，放在马库斯的枕头上，然后双臂交叉站在门口，等着他回家，嘴唇抿成一条细线。

topic: Someone discovers their partner has been writing a novel about them
text_en: Omar was looking for a stamp in the desk drawer and found a thick binder labeled 'Draft.' He opened it, reading about a fellow who 'always lost his keys but pretended it was a strategy.' That was Omar's exact joke. He flipped further, finding himself described as oblivious, always missing the obvious. Omar shut the binder. He felt a cold wave wash over him, then a heat that made him want to smash something. Instead, he carried the binder to the kitchen and set it beside the coffee maker, then woke his partner with a sharp nudge.
text_zh: 奥马尔在书桌抽屉里找邮票时，发现了一个厚厚的活页夹，标签写着“草稿”。他打开它，读到一个家伙“总是丢钥匙，却假装那是一种策略”。这正是奥马尔的原话玩笑。他继续翻，发现自己被描述成迟钝，总是错过显而易见的东西。奥马尔合上活页夹。一股冷意席卷了他，接着是一股让他想砸东西的热气。但他没有，而是把活页夹拿到厨房，放在咖啡机旁边，然后用力推了推伴侣，把他叫醒。

topic: Someone discovers their partner has been writing a novel about them
text_en: Sadie saw the manuscript on the coffee table, its corners curled. The main character had her habit of repeating herself when anxious, and her tendency to check locks. But in the story, those traits were signs of a controlling mind. Sadie had never once told Diego about her anxiety rituals. She read the ending, where the character was left alone. She put the pages down and walked out onto the balcony. Diego found her there, gripping the railing. She didn't turn around. 'I need you to be honest about what you wrote.' Her back was a rigid line.
text_zh: 萨迪看到茶几上的手稿，边角都卷起来了。主角有她焦虑时重复说话的习惯，还有检查门锁的倾向。但在故事里，这些特质是控制欲强的表现。萨迪从未告诉过迭戈她的焦虑仪式。她读到结尾，那个角色被独自留下。她放下纸页，走到阳台上。迭戈在那里找到了她，她紧抓着栏杆。她没有转身。“我需要你对你写的东西诚实。”她的背挺成一条僵硬的直线。

topic: Someone discovers their partner has been writing a novel about them
text_en: Ben found the file on the desktop: 'The Boy Who Couldn't Decide.' It was about his own indecisiveness, but recounted as a series of failures—jobs, relationships, even a stray cat he'd left outside. Ben slammed the laptop shut. A hot pulse beat in his temple. He paced the room, then pulled out a red pen and started marking up the margins of the printed copy. His partner came in, and Ben held up the crimson-penned pages. 'Let's talk about the editorial process,' he said, his voice tight and controlled.
text_zh: 本在桌面上发现了那个文件：“无法决定的孩子”。那是关于他自己的优柔寡断，但被叙述成一系列失败——工作、感情，甚至一只被他留在外面的流浪猫。本啪地合上笔记本电脑。太阳穴上热脉跳动。他在房间里踱步，然后拿出一支红笔，开始在打印副本的页边空白处做标记。他的伴侣走进来，本举起那些被红笔划满的纸页。“我们来谈谈编辑流程吧，”他说，声音紧绷而克制。

topic: Someone discovers their partner has been writing a novel about them
text_en: Ruth discovered the notebook while looking for her wallet. The story began with 'She always thought she was right, even when she was wrong.' The character shared Ruth's profession, her love of chess, her habit of biting her lip during arguments. Ruth read how this character alienated every friend. Her stomach churned. She put the notebook back where she found it and waited for Alex to come home. At dinner, she ate in silence, then said, 'I read your work. I want an explanation for your character's behavior.' Her fork stayed pointed at him across the table.
text_zh: 露丝在找钱包时发现了那个笔记本。故事以“她总以为自己是对的，即使她错了”开头。这个角色和露丝有相同的职业，热爱国际象棋，争论时咬嘴唇的习惯。露丝读到这个角色如何疏远了每一个朋友。她的胃翻腾起来。她把笔记本放回原处，等着亚历克斯回家。晚餐时，她沉默地吃着，然后说：“我读了你的作品。我想让你解释一下你角色的行为。”她的叉子隔着桌子一直指着他。

topic: Someone discovers their partner has been writing a novel about them
text_en: Ivan found the book on the nightstand, a title 'The Late Comer.' He skimmed the first page and saw his own chronic lateness, but described as a deliberate act of disrespect. The character's father shook his head, and Ivan felt tears of indignation sting his eyes. He wasn't forgetful; he was cruel. He shut the book with a loud thump. His partner stirred in the bed. Ivan stood over them. 'Is this how you see me?' He held the book up, his hand shaking slightly. 'Because I see this as a betrayal of trust.'
text_zh: 伊万在床头柜上发现了那本书，标题是《迟到者》。他浏览了第一页，看到了自己长期迟到的习惯，但被描述成一种蓄意的不尊重行为。角色的父亲摇了摇头，伊万感到愤慨的泪水刺痛了眼睛。他不是健忘；他是残忍。他砰的一声合上书。他的伴侣在床上动了动。伊万站在他们面前。“你就是这么看我的吗？”他举起书，手微微颤抖。“因为在我看来，这是对信任的背叛。”
