topic: Someone discovers their partner has been writing a novel about them
text_en: Mia was searching for her phone charger and found a stack of printed sheets under Hannah's laptop. The first line: 'She thought her laughter was a sign of intelligence, but it was just a shriek.' Mia read about a woman who dominated conversations, who talked over people, who never listened. There was a scene about an argument at a restaurant that had happened exactly as written, but with Mia's dialogue altered to make her look foolish. Mia scrunched the pages into a ball, then smoothed them out again. She stood in the doorway as Hannah entered, her chest heaving. 'We need to talk about what you wrote about me.'
text_zh: 米娅正在找她的手机充电器，却在汉娜的笔记本电脑下发现了一叠打印稿。第一行写着：“她以为自己的笑声是智慧的标志，但那只是一声尖叫。”米娅读到一个女人主导着对话，打断别人，从不倾听。有一个场景是关于餐厅里的一场争执，和发生过的完全一样，但米娅的对话被改写，让她看起来很愚蠢。米娅把纸揉成一团，然后又抚平了。她站在门口，汉娜走了进来，她的胸口起伏着。“我们需要谈谈你写我的那些东西。”

topic: Someone discovers their partner has been writing a novel about them
text_en: Diego found the story on his e-reader, a shared library. The protagonist had his baking habit, his flour-dusted apron, his stubborn pride in his sourdough. But the character was pathetic, baking to win affection that never came. Diego had shared his feelings about his mother's approval in confidence. He read the scene where the character's bread fails and everyone laughs. He closed the device. In the kitchen, he threw his apron into the trash. When his partner asked what was wrong, he just pointed at the e-reader, his lips pressed so tight they were white.
text_zh: 迭戈在他的电子阅读器上发现了这个故事，是一个共享图书馆。主角有他烘焙的习惯，他沾满面粉的围裙，他对自己酸面团固执的骄傲。但那个角色很可悲，为了赢得从未到来的爱而烘焙。迭戈曾私下告诉过他对母亲认可的渴望。他读到那个角色面包失败、大家都笑的场景。他合上了设备。在厨房里，他把围裙扔进了垃圾桶。当他的伴侣问怎么了时，他只是指着电子阅读器，嘴唇抿得发白。

topic: Someone discovers their partner has been writing a novel about them
text_en: Priya found the handwritten pages in Arjun's jacket pocket. The story described a woman who 'embraced every trend, thinking she was modern, but was just a follower.' Priya recognized her new glasses, her playlist, her yoga mat. She also recognized the description of her childhood home, which she'd told Arjun about in a whisper. She felt a jolt, then a steady burn. She folded the pages neatly and slid them back into the pocket. At dinner, she asked, 'Did you have anything to tell me?' Her gaze fixed on his face, unmoving, as he stammered.
text_zh: 普里娅在阿琼的夹克口袋里发现了手写稿。故事描述了一个女人，“拥抱每一个潮流，以为自己很现代，但只是个跟风者。”普里娅认出了她的新眼镜，她的播放列表，她的瑜伽垫。她还认出了她童年家的描述，那是她曾低声告诉阿琼的。她感到一阵刺痛，然后是持续的灼烧。她把纸叠整齐，滑回口袋。晚餐时，她问：“你有什么想告诉我的吗？”她的目光紧盯着他的脸，一动不动，而他结结巴巴。

topic: Someone discovers their partner has been writing a novel about them
text_en: Tom found the manuscript in the attic while looking for holiday decorations. The main character, 'Ted,' had his habit of whistling out of tune, his fear of heights, his secret love of bubblegum. But Ted was a coward who backed down from every challenge. Tom had once told his wife about his fear of heights after a nightmare. He read the climax where Ted hides under a table. Tom tore out the final page and folded it into his pocket. Downstairs, he put his hand on his wife's shoulder, squeezing a bit too hard. 'Let's talk about your recordings of our life.'
text_zh: 汤姆在阁楼找节日装饰品时发现了手稿。主角“泰德”有他跑调吹口哨的习惯，他怕高，他偷偷爱嚼泡泡糖。但泰德是个懦夫，面对每一个挑战都退缩。汤姆曾在噩梦后告诉过妻子他怕高。他读到泰德躲在桌子底下的高潮场景。汤姆撕下最后一页，折进口袋。楼下，他把手放在妻子肩膀上，捏得有点太紧。“让我们谈谈你对我们的生活记录。”

topic: Someone discovers their partner has been writing a novel about them
text_en: Aisha found the USB drive in the center console of the car. The novel was about 'a woman who always needed the last word.' Aisha recognized her own arguments about philosophy, her insistence on precise definitions. The character was shrill, insufferable, alone at the end. Aisha had never shown that side to Samir, except in one heated debate about free will. She turned the drive over and over in her hand, her pulse steady and hard. When she got home, she placed the drive on the kitchen counter. 'I found this,' she said, her voice flat. 'I'm waiting for your apology for misrepresenting my character.'
text_zh: 艾莎在汽车的中央控制台里发现了U盘。小说是关于“一个总是需要说最后一句话的女人”。艾莎认出了她自己关于哲学的争论，她对精确定义的坚持。这个角色尖声刺耳，令人难以忍受，最后独自一人。艾莎从未向萨米尔展现过那一面，除了一次关于自由意志的激烈辩论。她把U盘在手里翻来覆去，脉搏平稳而有力。回到家后，她把U盘放在厨房台面上。“我发现了这个，”她说，声音平淡。“我在等你就歪曲我的性格道歉。”

topic: Someone discovers their partner has been writing a novel about them
text_en: Marcus discovered the journal in the study, under a pile of bills. The entry was dated months ago, describing 'his habit of finishing other people's sentences, always wrong, always annoying.' Marcus recognized the exact anecdote about his sister's wedding. He read more, finding himself mocked for his careful planning, his list-making, his fear of dust. His neck tightened. He took the journal and placed it open to that page on the breakfast table. When his partner came down, Marcus just pointed at the page, his finger tapping the ink, his jaw set, refusing to speak first.
text_zh: 马库斯在书房的一堆账单下发现了那本日记。条目日期是几个月前，描述“他打断别人说话的习惯，总是说错，总是烦人。”马库斯认出了关于他姐姐婚礼的确切轶事。他读得更多，发现自己因精心计划、列清单、怕灰尘而被嘲笑。他的脖子紧绷。他拿起日记，翻到那一页，放在早餐桌上。当他的伴侣下楼时，马库斯只是指着那一页，手指敲着墨水，下巴绷紧，拒绝先开口。

topic: Someone discovers their partner has been writing a novel about them
text_en: Nina recognized herself in the opening chapter. The character wore her coat, quoted her mother, even shared her fear of tunnels. Sam had typed it all down, turned her into a plot device—the anxious wife who needed saving. She stood in the doorway of his study, watching him type. He smiled. "It's not you, it's fiction." She picked up the coffee mug he'd left on the stack of pages, felt the heat through the ceramic, and set it down hard, watching the liquid slosh over the manuscript. "Then delete my name from your notes," she said, her voice flat. She didn't wait for an answer.
text_zh: 妮娜在开头章节中认出了自己。这个角色穿着她的外套，引用她母亲的话，甚至有她怕隧道的特点。萨姆把所有都打了出来，把她变成了情节装置——一个需要拯救的焦虑妻子。她站在他书房门口，看着他打字。他微笑着说：“那不是你，那是虚构。”她拿起他留在纸堆上的咖啡杯，感受到透过陶瓷的热度，然后重重地放下，看着液体溅到手稿上。“那把你的笔记里我的名字删掉，”她说，声音平淡。她没有等回答。

topic: Someone discovers their partner has been writing a novel about them
text_en: Victor found the cloud document open on the shared tablet. The story was about 'a man who thought he was calm but was just suppressed,' someone whose emotions leaked out at the wrong times. The character had Victor's habit of humming when tense, and his fear of crowds. The narrative painted him as a time bomb waiting to explode. Victor read the scene where the character breaks a glass. Victor had once told his partner about his father's drinking, and his own fear of becoming a rager. He closed the tablet. He stood up and walked to the window, his back to the room. 'I need you to explain what you think you know about me,' he said, his voice tight.
text_zh: 维克多在共享平板电脑上发现了打开的云文档。故事是关于“一个以为自己冷静实则压抑的男人”，一个情绪在错误时间泄露的人。这个角色有维克多紧张时哼歌的习惯，还有他怕人群。叙述把他描绘成一个随时会爆炸的定时炸弹。维克多读到角色打碎玻璃的场景。维克多曾告诉过伴侣他父亲的酗酒，以及他自己害怕变成暴怒者的恐惧。他合上平板电脑。他站起来，走到窗边，背对着房间。“我需要你解释你认为你了解我的什么，”他说，声音紧绷。

topic: Someone discovers their partner has been writing a novel about them
text_en: Yuki found the manuscript in the printer tray. The main character, 'Y,' had her love of quiet mornings, her habit of reading the same book repeatedly, her dislike of surprise guests. But Y was antisocial, a recluse, someone who hated people not just preferred solitude. Yuki had shared her anxiety about social expectations once. She watched the character lose all her friends. Yuki picked up the pages and carefully folded each one, creating a paper crane. She set it on her partner's desk. He came in, and she looked up, her eyes hard, her voice controlled. 'I made you a symbol. Now, let's talk about your narrative.'
text_zh: 由纪在打印机托盘里发现了手稿。主角“Y”有她喜欢安静的早晨、重复读同一本书的习惯，不喜欢惊喜客人。但Y是反社会的，是个隐居者，一个讨厌人而不只是喜欢独处的人。由纪曾分享过她对社交期望的焦虑。她看着角色失去了所有朋友。由纪拿起纸，小心地折叠每一张，折成一只纸鹤。她把它放在伴侣的桌上。他进来时，她抬起头，眼神坚定，声音控制。“我为你做了一个象征。现在，让我们谈谈你的叙事。”

topic: Someone discovers their partner has been writing a novel about them
text_en: Zach found the handwritten letter in the mail stack, addressed to 'My Protagonist.' It described a man who 'always needed to be the smartest in the room,' who corrected others relentlessly, who was tolerated rather than loved. Zach had a habit of explaining facts at parties. He also had a memory of his own father, a man who was wrong but never admitted it. The letter was a confession of how the writer was tired of his character. Zach's hands were cold. He folded the letter back into its envelope. As his partner walked through the door, Zach held it out. 'This is your fiction, and it's a false accusation. I want you to retract it.' His voice was flat, but his knuckles were white.
text_zh: 扎克在邮件堆里发现了手写信，收件人是“我的主角”。信描述了一个男人，“总是需要成为房间里最聪明的人”，无情地纠正别人，被容忍而不是被爱。扎克有在聚会上解释事实的习惯。他还有一个父亲记忆，一个错了但从不承认的男人。这封信是写作者承认自己厌倦了他的角色。扎克的手冰凉。他把信折回信封。当他的伴侣走进门时，扎克把信递出去。“这是你的小说，也是虚假指控。我希望你撤回它。”他的声音平淡，但指节发白。

topic: Someone finds a time capsule they don't remember burying
text_en: Marta's trowel hit metal beneath the rose bush. She dug it out, a rusted cookie tin. Inside, a child's scrawl: a drawing of a dog with wings, a lock of hair, a note promising to return. She didn't remember burying this. But the handwriting was unmistakably hers, from a summer she'd tried to forget. He'd taken her dog, and she'd buried the memory. Now, seeing it, she felt a hot surge, not of grief, but of blame. He'd made her bury this. She slammed the lid shut, the tin denting under her palm.
text_zh: 玛尔塔的泥刀在玫瑰丛下碰到了金属。她把它挖了出来，是一个生锈的饼干盒。里面有一张孩子的涂鸦：一只长着翅膀的狗的画，一缕头发，还有一张承诺会回来的纸条。她不记得埋过这个。但笔迹毫无疑问是她的，来自一个她试图忘记的夏天。他带走了她的狗，而她埋葬了这段记忆。现在，看到它，她感到一阵强烈的涌动，不是悲伤，而是责备。他让她埋葬了这一切。她砰地关上盖子，铁盒在她的手掌下凹陷下去。

topic: Someone finds a time capsule they don't remember burying
text_en: Under the loose floorboard, Leon found a cigar box. Inside, a faded train ticket, a pressed flower, and a letter addressed to him. The letter was in his own hand, but he had no memory of writing it. It spoke of a promise to leave town with someone. He had never left. Someone had made him stay. He read the letter again, the words now a bitter accusation. He felt a tight knot in his chest, a resolve to find who had kept him from that train. He folded the letter, sharp crease, and pocketed it.
text_zh: 在松动的地板下，莱昂发现了一个雪茄盒。里面有一张褪色的火车票、一朵压花，还有一封写给他的信。信是他自己的笔迹，但他不记得写过。信中提到一个要和某人一起离开小镇的承诺。他从未离开过。有人让他留了下来。他又读了一遍信，那些话现在成了痛苦的指责。他感到胸口一阵紧绷，下定决心要找出是谁阻止了他登上那列火车。他把信折好，折痕锐利，然后放进了口袋。

topic: Someone finds a time capsule they don't remember burying
text_en: The mason jar was buried near the old oak. Priya pulled it out, wiping off the dirt. Inside, a silver ring and a note: "For when you come back." She didn't remember putting it there. But the ring was her mother's, the one she'd claimed was lost. A cold realization spread through her. She hadn't lost it; she'd hidden it, and forgotten. She felt a flare of injustice at her own mind for erasing this, for making her doubt her own history. She gripped the jar, the glass cool and unyielding, and walked inside, determined to set the record straight.
text_zh: 梅森罐被埋在老橡树附近。普里亚把它拔出来，擦掉泥土。里面有一枚银戒指和一张纸条：“等你回来的时候。”她不记得把它放在那里。但那枚戒指是她母亲的，她曾声称丢失的那枚。一个冰冷的认知在她心中蔓延。她没有丢，而是把它藏了起来，然后忘记了。她感到一阵不公的怒火，针对的是自己的大脑，因为它抹去了这一切，让她怀疑自己的历史。她紧紧抓住罐子，玻璃冰凉而坚硬，然后走进屋里，决心把事情弄清楚。

topic: Someone finds a time capsule they don't remember burying
text_en: Digging for potatoes, Tom unearthed a leather pouch. Inside, a folded map and a small key. The map was to a spot by the creek, marked with an X. He didn't remember burying it, but the ink was his. He followed the map, found a lockbox. The key fit. Inside, a stack of letters, all from a woman he'd loved. He'd never sent them. He felt a dull, persistent burn. He'd been a coward, but now he knew it. He shoved the letters back, the paper crinkling. He'd find her, and this time, he'd speak his piece.
text_zh: 汤姆挖土豆时，挖出了一个皮袋。里面有一张折叠的地图和一把小钥匙。地图指向小溪边的一个地方，标着一个X。他不记得埋过它，但墨水是他的。他沿着地图走，找到了一个锁箱。钥匙正好能打开。里面是一叠信，都来自他爱过的一个女人。他从未寄出过这些信。他感到一种沉闷而持续的灼烧感。他一直是个懦夫，但现在他知道了。他把信塞回去，纸张发出沙沙声。他会找到她，而这一次，他会说出自己的想法。

topic: Someone finds a time capsule they don't remember burying
text_en: The old coffee can surfaced when Sara weeded the garden. Inside, a child's drawing of a family, but with a figure crossed out. She recognized her own art. She didn't remember drawing this, but she knew the crossed-out figure was her father. He'd left when she was small. She'd buried this, a silent protest. Now, she felt a renewed, sharp sense of betrayal. He'd made her do this. She took the drawing, marched to the compost bin, and tore it into pieces, each shred a small act of defiance against the past.
text_zh: 萨拉在花园除草时，旧咖啡罐露了出来。里面有一张孩子的家庭画，但有一个被划掉的人物。她认出了自己的画作。她不记得画过这个，但她知道被划掉的是她的父亲。他在她很小的时候就离开了。她埋了这幅画，作为一种无声的抗议。现在，她感到一种重新燃起的、尖锐的背叛感。是他让她这么做的。她拿起画，大步走到堆肥箱前，把它撕成碎片，每一片碎纸都是对过去的一次小小的反抗。

topic: Someone finds a time capsule they don't remember burying
text_en: Nina's basement flooded, and while mopping, she found a small copper box in a corner she'd never noticed. Inside was a keychain with a tiny brass key and a note: 'For the lock on the old shed. Don't tell Mom.' She had no memory of this. She was an only child, and her mother had died years ago. She went to the shed—it had no lock, just a rusty latch. She stood there, key in hand, feeling a surge of heat. Someone had planted this, and for what? To make her think she was losing her mind? She threw the key into the weeds, but she couldn't stop thinking about it, and she went back to search for it, her jaw set.
text_zh: 妮娜的地下室被水淹了，拖地时，她在从未注意过的角落里发现了一个小铜盒。里面有一个带小黄铜钥匙的钥匙链和一张纸条：“旧棚屋锁的钥匙。别告诉妈妈。”她不记得这件事。她是独生女，母亲多年前就去世了。她去了棚屋——那里没有锁，只有一个生锈的门闩。她站在那里，手里拿着钥匙，感到一阵热浪涌来。有人把这个放在这里，为了什么？为了让她以为自己疯了？她把钥匙扔进了杂草丛，但她无法停止思考这件事，于是又回去找，下巴紧绷着。

topic: Someone finds a time capsule they don't remember burying
text_en: While renovating the bathroom, Tom found a small tin behind the medicine cabinet. Inside was a matchbox car, a marble, and a folded note: 'Tom's treasure, do not open.' He recognized the handwriting—it was his own, but he'd never written this. He'd never even had a matchbox car. He sat on the bathroom floor, turning the note over. The ink was smudged, but it looked fresh. He felt a hot prickling at the back of his neck. Someone was messing with his head. He threw the tin into the dumpster, but he couldn't stop thinking about it. He went back to the dumpster, but it was already gone. He spent the rest of the day in a foul mood, snapping at his wife.
text_zh: 翻新浴室时，汤姆在药柜后面发现了一个小铁盒。里面有一辆火柴盒小车、一颗弹珠和一张折叠的纸条：“汤姆的宝藏，不要打开。”他认出了笔迹——是他自己的，但他从未写过这个。他甚至从未有过火柴盒小车。他坐在浴室地板上，翻来覆去地看着纸条。墨水有点模糊，但看起来是新的。他感到脖子后面一阵灼热。有人在耍他。他把铁盒扔进了垃圾箱，但他无法停止思考这件事。他回到垃圾箱，但已经不见了。他余下的一整天都心情恶劣，对妻子发脾气。

topic: Someone finds a time capsule they don't remember burying
text_en: While installing a fence post, Owen struck a metal box. Inside, a cassette tape and a photo of him with his brother, both smiling. He didn't remember burying it. He found a player, inserted the tape. His own voice, young, promising to always help his brother. But he hadn't. His brother had moved away, and Owen had let him go. Now, hearing that promise, he felt a hot, bitter resentment at his own neglect. He snapped the tape in half, the plastic cracking, and threw the pieces into the trash.
text_zh: 安装栅栏柱时，欧文撞到了一个金属盒子。里面有一盘盒式磁带和一张他和哥哥的照片，两人都笑着。他不记得埋过它。他找到一个播放器，插入磁带。是他自己的声音，年轻的声音，承诺永远帮助哥哥。但他没有。哥哥搬走了，欧文让他走了。现在，听到那个承诺，他感到一阵强烈的、苦涩的怨恨，针对的是自己的疏忽。他把磁带掰成两半，塑料裂开，把碎片扔进了垃圾桶。

topic: Someone finds a time capsule they don't remember burying
text_en: While cleaning out the attic, Carl found a shoebox taped shut, addressed to him in his own handwriting. He opened it to find a collection of bottle caps and a note: 'For when I grow up.' He was grown up, and he'd never collected bottle caps. He stared at the box, his throat tight. He felt a wave of frustration—not at the box, but at the mystery. Who would do this? He turned the box over, looking for a date, a stamp, anything. Nothing. He slammed the box onto the attic floor, scattering the caps. He left them there, but he couldn't stop thinking about it. He went back up later and picked them up, one by one, his jaw clenched.
text_zh: 清理阁楼时，卡尔发现了一个用胶带封住的鞋盒，上面用他自己的笔迹写着他的名字。他打开它，发现里面有一堆瓶盖和一张纸条：“等我长大了。”他已经长大了，而且他从未收集过瓶盖。他盯着盒子，喉咙发紧。他感到一阵沮丧——不是针对盒子，而是针对这个谜团。谁会这么做？他把盒子翻过来，想找日期、邮票或任何东西。什么都没有。他把盒子摔在阁楼地板上，瓶盖散落一地。他把它们留在那里，但他无法停止思考这件事。他后来回到楼上，一个一个地捡起它们，下巴紧咬着。

topic: Someone finds a time capsule they don't remember burying
text_en: Sofia was weeding the flower bed when she found a small glass vial with a rolled paper inside. The paper said, 'Sofia, you're too slow.' She didn't recognize the handwriting. She'd never seen this vial before. She sat back on her heels, staring at it. The words stung—she'd always been self-conscious about her pace. She felt a hot flash of resentment. Someone had deliberately chosen those words to hurt her. She uncorked the vial, read the note again, then crushed it in her fist. She didn't cry, but she felt a burning in her chest that made her want to find out who'd done this. She started asking neighbors, but no one knew anything.
text_zh: 索菲亚在花坛除草时，发现了一个小玻璃瓶，里面有一张卷起来的纸。纸上写着：“索菲亚，你太慢了。”她不认识这个笔迹。她以前从未见过这个小瓶。她坐回脚跟上，盯着它。这些话刺痛了她——她一直对自己的速度感到自卑。她感到一阵强烈的怨恨。有人故意选择这些话来伤害她。她拔掉瓶塞，又读了一遍纸条，然后把它攥在手里捏碎。她没有哭，但她感到胸口一阵灼烧，让她想找出是谁干的。她开始询问邻居，但没人知道。

topic: Someone finds a time capsule they don't remember burying
text_en: Cleaning out the attic, Nora found a shoebox under the insulation. Inside, a set of house keys and a note: "To start over." She didn't remember hiding them. But the keys were to her old apartment, the one she'd fled after the breakup. She'd buried this, a symbol of escape. Now, she felt a surge of protest at her past self, at the fear that had made her hide. She picked up the keys, the metal cold. She'd go there, stand in the empty rooms, and reclaim what was hers.
text_zh: 在清理阁楼时，诺拉在隔热层下发现了一个鞋盒。里面有一串房门钥匙和一张纸条：“重新开始。”她不记得自己藏过这些东西。但钥匙是她旧公寓的，就是她分手后逃离的那个地方。她曾埋下这个象征逃离的东西。现在，她感到一阵对过去的自己的抗议，对那个让她躲藏起来的恐惧的抗议。她拿起钥匙，金属冰冷。她会去那里，站在空荡荡的房间里，夺回属于她的一切。

topic: Someone finds a time capsule they don't remember burying
text_en: Marta pried the rusted tin from the garden soil, her trowel scraping against a corner she had never seen before. Inside, a child's handwriting covered folded paper: promises to a friend she had long forgotten. But the date, scrawled in crayon, was unmistakable—a year she had spent far away. Someone had buried this here, not her. She turned the tin over, finding a small charm that belonged to her sister. Her jaw tightened. She threw the tin against the fence, watching it dent, and kicked the dirt back into the hole.
text_zh: 玛尔塔从花园的泥土里撬出那个生锈的铁皮罐，她的泥铲刮到了一个她从未见过的角落。里面，折叠的纸上覆盖着孩子的笔迹：写给一个她早已忘记的朋友的承诺。但用蜡笔潦草写下的日期是确凿无疑的——那是她在远方度过的一年。是有人把这个埋在这里的，不是她。她把罐子翻过来，发现了一个属于她姐姐的小护身符。她的下巴绷紧了。她把罐子扔向栅栏，看着它被撞凹，然后把泥土踢回坑里。

topic: Someone finds a time capsule they don't remember burying
text_en: Leo found the metal box under the porch while fixing a broken step. The latch gave easily, revealing a map and a note in his own handwriting, but the words were wrong. It described a treasure hunt in a park he had never visited, with clues about a red bicycle he never owned. He read it twice, then crumpled it, his knuckles white. Someone had made this to look like his work. He shoved the box into the trash bin, then pulled it out again, slamming it onto the workbench, unwilling to let it go unanswered.
text_zh: 利奥在修理一块破损的台阶时，在门廊下发现了那个金属盒子。锁扣很容易就打开了，里面是一张地图和一张用他自己的笔迹写的纸条，但上面的字是错的。它描述了一个他从未去过的公园里的寻宝活动，线索涉及一辆他从未拥有过的红色自行车。他读了两遍，然后把它揉成一团，指节发白。有人做了这个来模仿他的作品。他把盒子扔进垃圾桶，然后又把它拉出来，砰地一声砸在工作台上，不愿就此罢休。

topic: Someone finds a time capsule they don't remember burying
text_en: Nadia uncovered the ceramic jar while planting tulips, its lid sealed with wax. Inside lay a photograph of a street she didn't recognize, and a letter signed with her initials. The letter mentioned a promise to meet someone at a corner café, a promise she never made. She stared at the handwriting, so close to hers but not quite. Her chest tightened. She ripped the letter in half, then in quarters, and threw the pieces into the compost bin, her hands shaking as she stomped the jar back into the ground.
text_zh: 纳迪亚在种郁金香时挖出了那个陶瓷罐，罐口用蜡封着。里面放着一张她不认识的街道的照片，还有一封签着她名字首字母的信。信中提到一个承诺，要在街角咖啡馆见一个人，而她从未做过这样的承诺。她盯着那笔迹，和她的如此相似，但又不太一样。她的胸口发紧。她把信撕成两半，再撕成四份，把碎片扔进堆肥箱，双手颤抖着把罐子踩回土里。

topic: Someone finds a time capsule they don't remember burying
text_en: Evan found the old lunchbox buried beneath the oak tree, its paint faded but intact. Inside, a series of drawings depicted a family camping trip, complete with a lake and a tent. But Evan had never camped as a child; his family had stayed in hotels. The drawings showed a boy with his exact hair color, his exact freckles. He slammed the lid shut, then reopened it, pulling out each page and tearing them into strips. He kicked the lunchbox across the yard, then retrieved it, not wanting anyone else to see the lie.
text_zh: 埃文在橡树下发现了那个旧午餐盒，油漆褪色但完好无损。里面有一系列画作，描绘了一次家庭露营旅行，有湖和帐篷。但埃文小时候从未露营过；他的家人总是住酒店。画中有一个男孩，发色和他一模一样，雀斑也一模一样。他砰地关上盖子，然后又打开，把每一页都抽出来撕成条。他把午餐盒踢过院子，然后又捡回来，不想让任何人看到这个谎言。

topic: Someone finds a time capsule they don't remember burying
text_en: Marta dug through the overgrown corner of her garden, clearing weeds for a new flower bed. Her trowel struck metal. She unearthed a rusted cookie tin, sealed with tape. Inside, wrapped in oilcloth, lay a childish drawing of a house with a crooked chimney, and a note in her own handwriting: 'For future me, don't forget the secret under the porch.' She had no memory of this. A hot wave rose in her chest. She had been so careful, so present, for years. How had she missed this? She slammed the lid shut, shoved the tin into her bag, and stalked inside, muttering about her own carelessness.
text_zh: 玛尔塔在她花园杂草丛生的角落挖土，为新的花坛清除杂草。她的泥铲碰到了金属。她挖出一个生锈的饼干罐，用胶带封着。里面，用油布包着的，是一幅幼稚的画，画着一座烟囱歪斜的房子，还有一张她自己的笔迹写的纸条：“给未来的我，别忘了门廊下的秘密。”她对此毫无记忆。一股热浪涌上她的胸口。多年来她一直如此小心，如此专注。她怎么会错过这个？她砰地关上盖子，把罐子塞进包里，大步走进屋里，嘟囔着自己粗心大意。

topic: Someone finds a time capsule they don't remember burying
text_en: While fixing a leaky pipe under the sink, Victor found a small plastic bag tied to the pipe. Inside was a note: 'You'll never find the real one.' He didn't know what that meant. He'd never hidden anything. He felt a cold knot in his stomach, then a flare of heat. Someone had been in his apartment, in his plumbing. He felt violated. He cut the bag loose, read the note again, then crumpled it. He threw it in the trash, but he couldn't stop thinking about it. He checked his locks, his windows, his closets. He found nothing else. He spent the rest of the day in a foul mood, snapping at his roommate. He kept going back to the trash can, but he didn't know why.
text_zh: 在修理水槽下漏水的管道时，维克多发现了一个系在管道上的小塑料袋。里面有一张纸条：“你永远找不到真正的那个。”他不知道那是什么意思。他从未藏过任何东西。他感到胃里一阵冰冷的紧缩，然后是一阵灼热。有人进过他的公寓，动过他的管道。他感到被侵犯了。他剪断袋子，又读了一遍纸条，然后把它揉成一团。他把它扔进垃圾桶，但他无法停止想这件事。他检查了门锁、窗户、壁橱。他没有发现其他东西。他余下的一天都心情恶劣，对室友发脾气。他不断回到垃圾桶旁，但他不知道为什么。

topic: Someone finds a time capsule they don't remember burying
text_en: During spring cleaning, Leo found a glass jar tucked behind old paint cans in the garage. Inside was a folded map and a key. The map marked a spot in the backyard, but he'd never seen it before. His handwriting, though—he recognized the looped 'L'. He followed the map, dug, and found a small box with a note: 'For when you need a reminder of what matters.' It held a smooth stone and a ticket stub. He stood, fists clenched, jaw tight. Someone had played a trick on him, or he'd forgotten something vital. He shoved the box into his jacket, refusing to be fooled.
text_zh: 春季大扫除时，利奥在车库的旧油漆罐后面发现了一个玻璃罐。里面有一张折叠的地图和一把钥匙。地图标记了后院的一个地点，但他以前从未见过。不过，那是他的笔迹——他认出了那个带圈的“L”。他按照地图走，挖开土，发现了一个小盒子，里面有一张纸条：“当你需要提醒自己什么才是重要的时，打开它。”里面有一块光滑的石头和一张票根。他站在那里，双拳紧握，下巴紧绷。有人跟他开了个玩笑，或者他忘记了什么至关重要的事。他把盒子塞进夹克里，拒绝被愚弄。

topic: Someone finds a time capsule they don't remember burying
text_en: Sofia dug up a tin can while planting a rose bush, its label faded. Inside, a note in her mother's handwriting described a family vacation to the mountains, with details about a cabin and a stream. But Sofia's family had never gone to the mountains; they had stayed home. The note was dated a year after her mother's death. Sofia read it twice, her eyes narrowing. She folded the note carefully, then tore it into small pieces, dropping them into the can. She buried the can deeper than she found it.
text_zh: 索菲亚在种玫瑰丛时挖出一个铁皮罐，标签已经褪色。里面有一张她母亲笔迹的纸条，描述了一次去山里的家庭度假，提到了小屋和小溪的细节。但索菲亚的家人从未去过山里；他们一直待在家里。纸条的日期是她母亲去世后一年。索菲亚读了两遍，眯起了眼睛。她小心地折起纸条，然后把它撕成小碎片，扔进罐子里。她把罐子埋得比发现时更深。

topic: Someone finds a time capsule they don't remember burying
text_en: Marcus found the old ammunition box while clearing brush, its hinges rusted. Inside, a stack of letters, all addressed to him, all in his own handwriting, but describing events he had never experienced: a road trip with a friend he didn't know, a job he had never held. The dates spanned a year he had spent abroad, but the letters were postmarked from his hometown. He read one, then another, his grip tightening. He threw the box into the fire pit, watching the flames catch, and turned away without looking back.
text_zh: 马库斯在清理灌木丛时发现了那个旧弹药箱，铰链生锈了。里面有一叠信，都是写给他的，都是他自己的笔迹，但描述的事件他从未经历过：和一个他不认识的朋友的公路旅行，一份他从未做过的工作。日期跨越了他在国外度过的一年，但邮戳却是他家乡的。他读了一封，又读了一封，手越握越紧。他把盒子扔进火坑，看着火焰燃起，然后转身离开，没有回头。

topic: Someone finds their partner's bucket list
text_en: Marta found the crumpled list in his jacket pocket while looking for change. She smoothed it out on the kitchen counter, her eyes scanning the items. 'Swim with sharks,' 'Learn to tango,' 'Kiss a stranger in Paris.' The last one made her fingers tighten around the paper. She thought of their quiet anniversaries, the dinners he never planned, the trips he always postponed. He was home now, calling out her name. She folded the list neatly and slipped it back, but her jaw was set. She would not mention it. Yet she placed his coffee mug on the floor, just to see him bend.
text_zh: 玛尔塔在找零钱时，在他夹克口袋里发现了那张皱巴巴的清单。她在厨房台面上把它抚平，目光扫过那些项目。“与鲨鱼同游”，“学跳探戈”，“在巴黎亲吻一个陌生人”。最后一项让她的手指攥紧了纸张。她想起他们安静的结婚纪念日，他从未计划过的晚餐，他总是推迟的旅行。他现在回家了，喊着她的名字。她把清单整齐地叠好，塞了回去，但她的下巴绷紧了。她不会提起这件事。然而，她把他的咖啡杯放在地板上，只是为了看他弯腰去捡。

topic: Someone finds their partner's bucket list
text_en: Maya found the crumpled list in his jacket pocket while doing laundry. It read: 'kayak the river, learn guitar, see the auroras.' She recognized her own handwriting from a scrapbook she'd made years ago, before they moved. He had crossed off every item without ever telling her. He'd gone on those adventures with his friends, never once inviting her, never once mentioning the list she'd thought was lost. She stood in the kitchen, the paper trembling in her fist, staring at the crossed-out lines. He walked in, smiling, and she held it up without a word.
text_zh: 玛雅在洗衣服时，在他夹克口袋里发现了那张皱巴巴的清单。上面写着：“划皮划艇，学吉他，看极光。”她认出了自己的笔迹，那是多年前他们搬家前她做的一本剪贴簿里的。他划掉了每一项，却从未告诉过她。他和朋友们一起去进行了那些冒险，从未邀请过她，也从未提起过那张她以为已经丢失的清单。她站在厨房里，纸在她拳头里颤抖，盯着那些被划掉的线条。他走进来，微笑着，她一言不发地举起那张纸。

topic: Someone finds their partner's bucket list
text_en: Priya found the list in the bedside drawer, tucked under his reading glasses. It was written on a napkin, the ink smudged. 'See the Northern Lights,' 'Learn to surf,' 'Reconnect with an old flame.' The last item had a small checkmark beside it, dated last summer, when he'd claimed to be on a business trip. She put the napkin back, her hands trembling slightly. She walked to the living room where he sat watching TV. She stood in front of the screen, blocking his view. 'What did you do last August?' she asked, her voice flat, her gaze unwavering. He blinked, and she felt a cold satisfaction.
text_zh: 普里亚在床头柜抽屉里发现了那张清单，就塞在他的老花镜下面。它写在一张餐巾纸上，墨水已经模糊了。“看北极光”，“学冲浪”，“与旧情人重归于好”。最后一项旁边有一个小勾，日期是去年夏天，那时他声称在出差。她把餐巾纸放回去，双手微微颤抖。她走到客厅，他正坐在那里看电视。她站在屏幕前，挡住了他的视线。“去年八月你做了什么？”她问道，声音平淡，目光坚定。他眨了眨眼，她感到一种冰冷的满足感。

topic: Someone finds their partner's bucket list
text_en: Dana slid the folded paper from his bedside drawer, expecting a grocery note. It was a list, neatly printed: 'ride a horse, bake sourdough, hike the canyon.' She'd mentioned each of those dreams over dinner, and he'd nodded, saying he wasn't interested. Now she saw his checkmarks beside every line, dated with small stars. He had done them all, on weekends he claimed were for work. She put the list back, closed the drawer, and when he came home that evening, she asked him about his weekend—his answer was a lie. She felt her jaw tighten, her hands still.
text_zh: 达娜从他床头柜抽屉里抽出那张折叠的纸，以为是购物清单。那是一张清单，打印得整整齐齐：“骑马，烤酸面包，徒步峡谷。”她曾在晚餐时提到过这些梦想，他点点头，说自己不感兴趣。现在她看到每一项旁边都有他的勾，还标着小星星。他全都做了，在他声称是工作的周末。她把清单放回去，关上抽屉，那天晚上他回家时，她问他周末过得怎么样——他的回答是谎言。她感到下巴绷紧，双手静止。

topic: Someone finds their partner's bucket list
text_en: Elena found the list in his gym bag, a crumpled receipt with a scrawl on the back. 'Bungee jump,' 'Learn the guitar,' 'Sleep with someone else.' She stared at the last item, the ink slightly faded, but the intent clear. She folded the receipt into a tiny square and put it in her pocket. That night, she lay awake listening to his breathing. In the morning, she made his coffee, but she added salt instead of sugar. When he grimaced, she asked, 'Is something wrong?' Her tone was sweet, but her eyes were hard, watching him squirm as he tried to explain the taste.
text_zh: 埃琳娜在他的健身包里发现了那张清单，一张皱巴巴的收据，背面潦草地写着字。“蹦极”，“学吉他”，“和别人上床”。她盯着最后一项，墨水有点褪色，但意图清晰。她把收据折成一个小方块，放进口袋。那天晚上，她躺着听他的呼吸声。早上，她给他泡了咖啡，但她加了盐而不是糖。当他皱眉时，她问道：“有什么不对劲吗？”她的语气甜美，但眼神冷硬，看着他试图解释味道时的不自在。

topic: Someone finds their partner's bucket list
text_en: Sam found the list in the glove compartment, a torn page from a magazine. 'Skydive,' 'See the pyramids,' 'Have an affair.' The last one was circled, not checked, but the circle was dark, pressed hard. He put the page back, his jaw tight. He drove home in silence, gripping the wheel until his knuckles ached. He walked in and found her reading on the couch. He didn't say a word, just stood there, blocking the light. She looked up, startled. 'What?' she asked. He shook his head, but his hands were fists at his sides, and he didn't move for a long moment.
text_zh: 萨姆在手套箱里发现了那张清单，是从杂志上撕下来的一页。“跳伞”，“看金字塔”，“有外遇”。最后一项被圈了起来，不是打勾，但圆圈很深，用力压过。他把那页纸放回去，下巴紧绷。他沉默地开车回家，紧握方向盘，直到指关节发疼。他走进去，发现她正坐在沙发上看书。他一句话没说，只是站在那里，挡住了光线。她抬起头，吓了一跳。“怎么了？”她问。他摇了摇头，但双手在身侧握成拳头，好一会儿没有动。

topic: Someone finds their partner's bucket list
text_en: Priya found the list tucked inside his old notebook: 'learn to sail, visit the desert, write a song.' She remembered telling him she'd always wanted to sail, and he'd laughed, saying it was too expensive. Now the notebook showed photos, a map, even a lyric sheet. He'd done it all, with a friend she'd never met. She didn't cry. She closed the notebook, placed it on his desk, and when he asked about her day, she said it was fine. That night, she watched him sleep and thought about the desert, the sea, the song he never played for her.
text_zh: 普里亚在他的旧笔记本里发现了那张清单：“学帆船，去沙漠，写一首歌。”她记得告诉过他她一直想学帆船，他笑了，说那太贵了。现在笔记本里显示着照片、一张地图，甚至还有一张歌词页。他全都做了，和一个她从未见过的朋友。她没有哭。她合上笔记本，放在他的书桌上，当他问起她的一天时，她说很好。那天晚上，她看着他睡觉，想着沙漠、大海，以及他从未为她弹奏的那首歌。

topic: Someone finds their partner's bucket list
text_en: Tom found the list in her diary, hidden under a stack of novels. He knew he shouldn't read it, but he did. 'Learn to paint,' 'See the aurora,' 'Fall for someone unexpected.' The last one was underlined, with a small smiley face drawn next to it. He closed the diary, his heart pounding. He put it back exactly as it was. That evening, he watched her across the table, her head bent over a book. He asked, 'Who's unexpected?' She looked up, puzzled. 'What do you mean?' He shrugged, but his fork scraped the plate loudly, and he didn't look at her again.
text_zh: 汤姆在她的日记里发现了那张清单，藏在一堆小说下面。他知道自己不该读，但他还是读了。“学画画”，“看极光”，“爱上意想不到的人”。最后一项被划了线，旁边画了一个小小的笑脸。他合上日记，心跳加速。他把它放回原处。那天晚上，他隔着桌子看着她，她低头看书。他问道：“谁是那个意想不到的人？”她抬起头，困惑地说：“你什么意思？”他耸耸肩，但叉子刮盘子发出响亮的声音，他再也没有看她。

topic: Someone finds their partner's bucket list
text_en: Rosa found the list in his workshop, pinned to the corkboard above the workbench. 'Build a boat,' 'Play the saxophone,' 'Have a secret lover.' The last one was in a different ink, added later. She stared at it, her hands on her hips. She didn't touch it. She went back to the house and made a phone call to his sister, asking casually about his old friends. She hung up, her suspicions hardening. When he came in, covered in sawdust, she smiled. 'Dinner's ready,' she said, but she had set only one plate on the table.
text_zh: 罗莎在他的工作室里发现了那张清单，钉在工作台上方的软木板上。“造一艘船”，“吹萨克斯”，“有一个秘密情人”。最后一项是用不同的墨水写的，是后来加上去的。她盯着它，双手叉腰。她没有碰它。她回到屋里，给他的妹妹打了个电话，随口问起他的老朋友。她挂了电话，疑心更重了。当他进来时，浑身是木屑，她微笑着说：“晚饭好了。”但桌上只摆了一个盘子。

topic: Someone finds their partner's bucket list
text_en: Elena found the list in his gym bag: 'climb a mountain, learn French, adopt a dog.' She had a dog allergy, and he knew it. The list was old, but the checkmarks were fresh ink. He'd been taking French classes on Tuesday nights, the same nights he told her he was working late. She saw the certificate, the photos of a peak she'd never seen. When he came through the door, she held the list out, her voice flat. 'You learned French,' she said. He looked at the floor. She turned and walked to the bedroom, the paper still in her hand.
text_zh: 埃琳娜在他的健身包里发现了那张清单：“爬一座山，学法语，养一只狗。”她对狗过敏，他知道。清单是旧的，但勾是新墨。他一直在周二晚上上法语课，那些晚上他告诉她他在加班。她看到了证书，还有一张她从未见过的山峰照片。当他进门时，她举起清单，声音平淡：“你学了法语。”他看着地板。她转身走进卧室，纸还在她手里。

topic: Someone finds their partner's bucket list
text_en: Clara found the list in his nightstand, a piece of paper with a coffee stain. 'Write a screenplay,' 'Learn to fly,' 'Have a fling.' She read it, her lips pressed into a thin line. She left it there. That night, she wore her nicest dress, the one he always complimented. He didn't notice. She sat across from him, her fork moving slowly, her eyes on his face. She asked about his day, and he talked about work. She listened, but she was thinking about the fling, wondering if it had already happened or was still to come. Her grip on her fork tightened.
text_zh: 克拉拉在他的床头柜里发现了那张清单，一张有咖啡渍的纸。‘写个剧本，’‘学飞行，’‘来段风流韵事。’她读着，嘴唇抿成一条细线。她把它留在了原处。那天晚上，她穿上了自己最漂亮的裙子，那条他总夸的裙子。他没有注意到。她坐在他对面，叉子移动得很慢，眼睛看着他的脸。她问他今天过得怎么样，他说起了工作。她听着，但心里想着那段风流事，想着它是否已经发生，还是即将到来。她握叉子的手收紧了。

topic: Someone finds their partner's bucket list
text_en: Marco found the list in her sketchbook, tucked between drawings of flowers. 'Go to Venice,' 'Learn the cello,' 'Have a passionate affair.' The last one was written in pencil, faint, as if she'd hesitated. He closed the sketchbook, his throat tight. He went to the garden and began pulling weeds, yanking them out by the roots. His hands were black with dirt. When she came out to call him for lunch, he didn't look up. 'I'm not hungry,' he said, his voice low. He kept pulling, his movements sharp, the soil scattering around him.
text_zh: 马可在她的速写本里发现了那张清单，夹在花朵图画之间。‘去威尼斯，’‘学大提琴，’‘来一场热烈的婚外情。’最后一项是用铅笔写的，很淡，仿佛她曾犹豫过。他合上速写本，喉咙发紧。他去了花园，开始拔杂草，连根拔起。他的双手沾满泥土，黑乎乎的。当她出来喊他吃午饭时，他没有抬头。‘我不饿，’他说，声音低沉。他继续拔着，动作尖锐，泥土在他周围飞溅。

topic: Someone finds their partner's bucket list
text_en: Hannah found the list in his coat pocket, a receipt from a bar. 'Learn to dance,' 'Go to New York,' 'Meet someone new.' The last item was checked, with a date that coincided with his last conference. She put the receipt back, her face hot. She went to the bathroom and ran cold water over her wrists, watching the water swirl. She dried her hands and walked out. He was on the couch, scrolling through his phone. She sat down next to him, closer than usual. 'What are you looking at?' she asked, her voice light, but her eyes were fixed on his screen.
text_zh: 汉娜在他的外套口袋里发现了那张清单，一张酒吧的收据。‘学跳舞，’‘去纽约，’‘认识新的人。’最后一项被勾掉了，日期和他上次出差的时间一致。她把收据放回去，脸颊发热。她去了洗手间，用冷水冲手腕，看着水流旋转。她擦干手，走了出来。他靠在沙发上，翻着手机。她在他旁边坐下，比平时更近。‘你在看什么？’她问，声音轻快，但眼睛盯着他的屏幕。

topic: Someone finds their partner's bucket list
text_en: Oscar found the list in her desk, a page torn from a journal. 'Learn to ride a motorcycle,' 'See the Grand Canyon,' 'Kiss a stranger.' He read it, then read it again, the word 'stranger' burning into his mind. He put the page back, his jaw set. He went for a run, pushing himself harder than usual, his feet pounding the pavement. When he returned, she was in the kitchen, humming. He stood in the doorway, dripping with sweat. 'Where's my running shirt?' he asked, his voice tight. She pointed to the laundry room, and he walked away without another word.
text_zh: 奥斯卡在她的书桌里发现了那张清单，一页从日记本上撕下的纸。‘学骑摩托车，’‘看大峡谷，’‘亲吻一个陌生人。’他读了一遍，又读了一遍，‘陌生人’这个词灼烧着他的脑海。他把那页纸放回去，下巴绷紧。他去跑步，比平时更用力，双脚猛击路面。回来后，她在厨房里哼着歌。他站在门口，浑身是汗。‘我的跑步衫呢？’他问，声音紧绷。她指了指洗衣房，他再没说一句话，转身离开了。

topic: Someone finds their partner's bucket list
text_en: Rosa found the list in his coat pocket while searching for a tissue: 'write a novel, run a marathon, see the ocean.' She'd always dreamed of the ocean, but he'd said it was too far. Now she saw a race bib, a manuscript draft, and a photo of him on a beach. He'd done all of it, alone, never telling her. She sat on the couch, the list in her lap, and when he came in, she didn't look up. 'You ran a marathon,' she said. He started to explain, but she cut him off. 'You never once asked me to come.' Her hands were cold, but her voice was steady.
text_zh: 罗莎在他的外套口袋里找纸巾时发现了那张清单：‘写一本小说，跑一场马拉松，看一次大海。’她一直梦想着去看海，但他说那太远了。现在她看到一张比赛号码布、一份手稿草稿，还有一张他在海滩上的照片。他全都做到了，独自一人，从没告诉过她。她坐在沙发上，清单放在膝上，当他进来时，她没有抬头。‘你跑了马拉松，’她说。他正要解释，但她打断了他。‘你从没问过我一起去。’她的手冰凉，但声音平稳。

topic: Someone finds their partner's bucket list
text_en: Theo found the list in her jewelry box, under a tangle of necklaces. 'Learn to sail,' 'See the northern lights,' 'Have an adventure.' The last one was vague, but he knew. He closed the box, his fingers lingering on the lid. He went to the garage and started the car, then turned it off. He sat in the dark, gripping the wheel. When he went back inside, she was in the kitchen, making tea. He stood behind her, not touching her. 'What kind of adventure?' he asked, his voice quiet. She turned, surprised. 'What do you mean?' He shook his head, but his eyes were hard.
text_zh: 西奥在她的首饰盒里发现了那张清单，在一团项链下面。‘学航海，’‘看北极光，’‘来一次冒险。’最后一项含糊不清，但他明白。他合上盒子，手指在盖子上停留。他去了车库，发动了汽车，然后熄了火。他坐在黑暗中，紧握方向盘。回到屋里，她在厨房泡茶。他站在她身后，没有碰她。‘什么样的冒险？’他问，声音很轻。她转过身，很惊讶。‘你什么意思？’他摇了摇头，但眼神变得冷硬。

topic: Someone finds their partner's bucket list
text_en: Ava found the list in his old briefcase, a yellowed piece of paper. 'Run a farm,' 'Learn to play the piano,' 'Have a wild romance.' The last one was underlined twice. She put the paper back, her hands steady, but her heart was racing. She spent the afternoon cleaning the house, scrubbing the floors with more force than necessary. When he came home, she was on her knees, the scrub brush in her hand. 'The floor looks great,' he said. She looked up, her face flushed. 'It needed it,' she said, her voice clipped, and she went back to scrubbing.
text_zh: 艾娃在他的旧公文包里发现了那张清单，一张泛黄的纸。‘经营一个农场，’‘学弹钢琴，’‘有一段狂野的恋情。’最后一项被画了两道下划线。她把纸放回去，手很稳，但心跳加速。她花了整个下午打扫房子，擦地板时用力过猛。他回家时，她正跪在地上，手里拿着刷子。‘地板看起来很干净，’他说。她抬起头，满脸通红。‘早就该擦了，’她说，声音干脆，然后继续擦着。

topic: Someone finds their partner's bucket list
text_en: Milo found the list in her nightstand, a folded note. 'Learn to knit,' 'Visit a volcano,' 'Reconnect with a first love.' He read it, then put it back, his jaw tight. He went to the kitchen and made himself a sandwich, but he didn't eat it. He stared at the wall, his hands flat on the counter. When she came in, she asked, 'What's wrong?' He said, 'Nothing.' But his voice was flat, and he didn't turn to look at her. He picked up the sandwich and took a bite, chewing slowly, his eyes on the window.
text_zh: 米洛在她的床头柜里发现了那张清单，一张折叠的便条。‘学编织，’‘看火山，’‘与初恋重逢。’他读了一遍，然后放了回去，下巴紧绷。他走进厨房，给自己做了个三明治，但没有吃。他盯着墙，双手平放在台面上。她进来后，问：‘怎么了？’他说：‘没事。’但他的声音很平淡，也没有转身看她。他拿起三明治咬了一口，慢慢咀嚼，眼睛看着窗外。

topic: Someone finds their partner's bucket list
text_en: Tara found the list in his desk drawer, hidden under tax forms: 'grow a garden, learn to paint, visit the mountains.' She'd always wanted a garden, but he'd said the soil was bad. Now she saw photos of a lush vegetable patch, a set of watercolors, and a trail map. He'd done it all, on weekends he said he was fishing. She took the list, walked into the living room, and placed it on the coffee table in front of him. 'You grew a garden,' she said. He looked at the paper, then at her. She didn't wait for an answer. She turned and walked out the front door, leaving the list where it lay.
text_zh: 塔拉在他的书桌抽屉里发现了那份清单，藏在税单下面：‘种一个花园，学画画，游历山川。’她一直想要一个花园，但他说土壤不好。现在她看到了一张蔬菜郁郁葱葱的照片、一套水彩画和一个地图。他在他说是去钓鱼的周末里，全做到了。她拿起清单，走进客厅，放在他面前的咖啡桌上。‘你种了一个花园，’她说。他看了看那张纸，又看了看她。她没有等回答，转身走出前门，留下那份清单。

topic: Someone finds their partner's bucket list
text_en: Ethan found the list in her coat pocket, a receipt with a list on the back. 'Learn to tango,' 'See the Pacific Ocean,' 'Have a secret affair.' The last one was written in pencil, partially erased, but he could still read it. He put the receipt back, his face burning. He went for a drive, his hands gripping the wheel. He drove to the coast, watching the waves crash. When he returned, she was asleep on the couch. He stood over her, watching her breathe. He didn't wake her. He went to the bedroom and packed a bag, then sat on the edge of the bed, waiting for morning.
text_zh: 伊桑在她的外套口袋里发现了那张清单，一张背面是清单的收据。‘学探戈，’‘看太平洋，’‘有一场秘密婚外情。’最后一项是铅笔写的，部分被擦掉了，但他仍然能读出来。他把收据放回去，脸烧得发烫。他开车出去，双手紧握方向盘。他开到海边，看着海浪拍岸。回来后，她躺在沙发上睡着了。他站在她旁边，看着她的呼吸。他没有叫醒她。他走到卧室，收拾了一个包，然后坐在床边，等待早晨来临。

topic: A neighbor asks to use part of the yard for a garden
text_en: Lena watched from the kitchen window as her neighbor, Mr. Alvarez, dragged a hose across the strip of lawn she'd been nurturing for years. He'd asked to plant tomatoes there, and she'd said yes, thinking a few plants. But now he was staking out a plot twice the size she'd imagined, his boots crushing her newly seeded grass. She gripped the mug too hard, the heat searing her palm. She wanted to march out and demand he stop, but instead she stood frozen, jaw tight, planning exactly where she'd put a fence the next day.
text_zh: 莉娜从厨房窗户看着她的邻居阿尔瓦雷斯先生把一根水管拖过她多年来一直精心照料的草坪。他曾请求在那里种西红柿，她同意了，以为只是几株。但现在他正在圈出一块比她想象中大一倍的地，他的靴子踩坏了她新播的草籽。她握紧了杯子，热度灼烧着她的手掌。她想冲出去要求他停下，但她却僵立在那里，下巴紧绷，心里盘算着第二天该在哪里建一道篱笆。

topic: A neighbor asks to use part of the yard for a garden
text_en: When Priya saw the fresh mound of soil piled high against her prized rose bushes, she felt a hot knot twist in her stomach. Her neighbor, Dan, had promised to keep his vegetable patch to the far corner. Yet here he was, edging ever closer, his shovel slicing through the roots she'd babied for a decade. She stormed over, her voice sharp and clipped as she pointed at the damage. Dan shrugged, saying the soil was just temporary. Priya's hands trembled as she turned away, already drafting a formal complaint in her head.
text_zh: 当普里亚看到一堆新土高高堆在她珍爱的玫瑰丛旁时，她感到胃里一阵灼热的纠结。她的邻居丹曾答应把他的菜地保持在最远的角落。然而他却在不断靠近，他的铲子切过她精心照料了十年的根系。她怒气冲冲地走过去，指着损坏的地方，声音尖锐而急促。丹耸耸肩，说那些土只是临时的。普里亚转身离开时双手颤抖，心里已经在起草一份正式投诉。

topic: A neighbor asks to use part of the yard for a garden
text_en: Marcus had agreed to let the new neighbor, Mrs. Chen, use a narrow strip of his side yard for herbs. He hadn't expected her to dig up the entire border, uprooting the irises his late wife had planted. He stood on his porch, arms crossed, watching her work. Each shovelful of earth felt like a personal insult. He thought about all the times he'd watered those flowers, the memories tangled in their roots. He couldn't find the words to stop her, so he just stared, a bitter taste rising in his throat.
text_zh: 马库斯曾同意让新邻居陈太太使用他侧院的一条窄地种香草。他没想到她会把整个边界都挖开，连根拔起他已故妻子种下的鸢尾花。他站在门廊上，双臂交叉，看着她干活。每一铲土都像是对他个人的侮辱。他想起了自己无数次给那些花浇水，那些记忆缠绕在根须中。他找不到话来阻止她，只能盯着看，一股苦涩的味道涌上喉咙。

topic: A neighbor asks to use part of the yard for a garden
text_en: When the neighbor knocked, Maria expected a quick chat about the fence. Instead, he pointed to her sunny side yard, saying his tomatoes needed more light. She listened, arms crossed, as he proposed digging up her lawn. Her jaw tightened when he mentioned 'just a small patch.' She stepped back, saying, 'That's my space for the kids.' He laughed, waving it off. Maria's hand went to her hip, and she told him flatly, 'No.' He kept talking, but she turned and walked inside, shutting the door harder than she meant. She stood by the window, watching him linger.
text_zh: 当邻居敲门时，玛丽亚以为只是关于篱笆的简短交谈。相反，他指着她阳光充足的侧院，说他的西红柿需要更多光照。她双臂交叉听着他提议挖掉她的草坪。当他提到“只是一小块地”时，她的下巴绷紧了。她后退一步，说：“那是我孩子们的空间。”他笑了，挥手不以为意。玛丽亚把手放在腰上，直截了当地告诉他：“不行。”他还在继续说，但她转身走进屋里，关门的声音比她预想的要重。她站在窗边，看着他徘徊不去。

topic: A neighbor asks to use part of the yard for a garden
text_en: Ravi had always kept his backyard immaculate. So when his neighbor, Sarah, proposed a small garden plot, he'd set clear limits. Yet now, he saw her children trampling through his flower beds, chasing a ball, while Sarah watered her expanding rows of kale. Ravi's hands clenched into fists at his sides. He felt a surge of injustice, a violation of the unspoken agreement. He yelled at the kids to get out, his voice harsher than he intended, and then he turned to Sarah, his face hot, demanding she keep them on her side.
text_zh: 拉维一直把后院保持得一尘不染。所以当邻居莎拉提议要一小块菜地时，他设定了明确的界限。然而现在，他看到她的孩子们追着球踩过他的花坛，而莎拉则在给不断扩大的羽衣甘蓝行浇水。拉维的双手在身侧握成了拳头。他感到一阵不公，一种对默契协议的侵犯。他朝孩子们大喊让他们出去，声音比他预想的更严厉，然后他转向莎拉，脸涨得通红，要求她把孩子们管在她那边。

topic: A neighbor asks to use part of the yard for a garden
text_en: The neighbor's note was polite, but it sat on the counter like a challenge. He wanted to plant a garden in the strip along the driveway, the one she'd just reseeded. Leo read it twice, then crumpled it. He went outside and saw him already measuring, tape in hand. 'I haven't agreed to anything,' Leo said. The neighbor shrugged, 'It's just unused dirt.' Leo felt heat rise in his chest. He stood over the tape, blocking it. 'You'll need to find somewhere else.' The neighbor's smile faded. Leo didn't move until he packed up his tools, then he went inside, leaving the crumpled note on the counter.
text_zh: 邻居的纸条很客气，但它放在台面上就像一种挑战。他想在车道旁的那条地带上种菜，而那条地她刚刚重新播了种。利奥读了两遍，然后把它揉成一团。他走出去，看到他已经在量尺寸，手里拿着卷尺。“我还没同意任何事，”利奥说。邻居耸耸肩，“那只是没用的土。”利奥感到胸口一阵发热。他站在卷尺上，挡住它。“你得另找地方。”邻居的笑容消失了。利奥一直没动，直到他收拾好工具，然后他走进屋里，把揉皱的纸条留在台面上。

topic: A neighbor asks to use part of the yard for a garden
text_en: Priya had planned that corner for herbs, but the new neighbor saw it as a vegetable patch. He came over with a sketch, talking about carrots and beans. Priya shook her head, explaining her plans. He interrupted, saying she could use the back for herbs. She felt a sting of unfairness. He wasn't asking, he was rearranging her yard. Priya's voice turned flat. 'I've already bought seeds.' He waved a hand, 'They can go elsewhere.' She stared at him, then pointed to the property line. 'This is mine.' He started to argue, but she walked to her door. She paused, hand on the knob, her back stiff.
text_zh: 普里亚原本计划在那个角落种香草，但新邻居却把它看作菜地。他带着一张草图过来，谈论着胡萝卜和豆子。普里亚摇摇头，解释她的计划。他打断她，说可以用后面种香草。她感到一阵不公平的刺痛。他不是在询问，而是在重新安排她的院子。普里亚的声音变得平淡。“我已经买了种子。”他挥挥手，“它们可以种到别处。”她盯着他，然后指向地界。“这是我的。”他开始争辩，但她走向门口。她停下来，手放在门把手上，后背僵硬。

topic: A neighbor asks to use part of the yard for a garden
text_en: The request came as a text: 'Could we use your side yard for a garden? We'll split the veggies.' Tom read it while eating lunch. He put down his fork, stared at the screen, then typed, 'No, I use that space.' A reply came instantly: 'It's mostly weeds.' Tom felt his neck tighten. He went outside, seeing the neighbor already poking at the soil. 'I said no,' Tom called. The neighbor straightened, 'I thought you'd reconsider.' Tom shook his head, stepping closer. 'I don't want a garden there.' The neighbor sighed, 'Fine.' But he lingered, and Tom stayed by the fence until he left, then went back to his cold lunch.
text_zh: 请求以短信形式到来：“我们能用你的侧院种菜吗？我们会分你蔬菜。”汤姆吃午饭时读到了这条消息。他放下叉子，盯着屏幕，然后打字：“不行，我用那块地方。”回复立刻来了：“那里大多是杂草。”汤姆感到脖子发紧。他走出去，看到邻居已经在戳弄土壤。“我说了不行，”汤姆喊道。邻居直起身，“我以为你会重新考虑。”汤姆摇摇头，走近一步。“我不想在那里种菜。”邻居叹了口气，“好吧。”但他逗留着，汤姆一直待在篱笆旁直到他离开，然后回去吃他冷掉的午餐。

topic: A neighbor asks to use part of the yard for a garden
text_en: Elena found the stakes in her lawn before the knock came. The neighbor explained he was planning a community garden plot. She stared at the orange flags, then at him. 'You put these up without asking?' He smiled, 'I assumed you'd be fine with it.' Elena felt a flare of disbelief. She pulled up the nearest stake. 'You assumed wrong.' He looked hurt, but she didn't care. She told him to take his flags and his plan elsewhere. He started to say it was for everyone, but she cut him off, holding the stake out. He took it, and she watched him walk away, her hands still trembling slightly.
text_zh: 埃琳娜在敲门之前就发现了草坪上的木桩。邻居解释说他在规划一个社区菜园地块。她盯着那些橙色旗子，然后看着他。“你没问就插了这些？”他笑了，“我以为你会同意的。”埃琳娜感到一阵难以置信。她拔起最近的一根木桩。“你猜错了。”他看起来受伤了，但她不在乎。她告诉他带着他的旗子和计划去别处。他开始说这是为了大家，但她打断了他，把木桩递出去。他接过去，她看着他走开，双手还在微微颤抖。

topic: A neighbor asks to use part of the yard for a garden
text_en: Marta watched through the kitchen window as her neighbor, Dan, uncoiled a hose across her flower bed. She had agreed to let him use the strip by the fence, but he was now trampling her tulips, his boots leaving deep prints. She stepped outside, arms crossed. "Dan, the garden is on the other side of the path." He shrugged, not meeting her eyes. "It's just easier this way." Marta's jaw tightened. She picked up the hose and moved it back, her movements deliberate. "I said the other side," she repeated, her voice flat. She stood there until he relocated his supplies, her gaze fixed on his back.
text_zh: 玛尔塔透过厨房窗户看着邻居丹把水管展开横过她的花坛。她曾同意让他使用篱笆旁的那条地，但他现在正在踩踏她的郁金香，靴子留下深深的脚印。她走出去，双臂交叉。“丹，菜园在小路的另一边。”他耸耸肩，没有看她的眼睛。“这样更方便。”玛尔塔的下巴绷紧了。她拿起水管，把它移回去，动作刻意。“我说的是另一边，”她重复道，声音平淡。她站在那里，直到他把他的东西搬走，目光一直盯着他的背。

topic: A neighbor asks to use part of the yard for a garden
text_en: Sam saw the shovel leaning against the fence before he saw the neighbor. The man was already digging a trench along the boundary. 'What are you doing?' Sam asked. The neighbor wiped his brow, 'Putting in a border for a garden.' Sam looked at the hole, then at him. 'You didn't ask.' The neighbor shrugged, 'It's just a few feet.' Sam felt a hot surge of frustration. He stepped closer, looking at the exposed roots. 'That's my side.' The neighbor kept digging. Sam grabbed the shovel handle. 'Stop.' The neighbor looked up, surprised. Sam held his gaze until the man let go. 'We'll talk later,' Sam said, but he knew he wouldn't.
text_zh: 萨姆在看见邻居之前，先看到了靠在栅栏上的铁锹。那人已经在沿着边界挖沟了。“你在做什么？”萨姆问道。邻居擦了擦额头，“给花园修个边。”萨姆看了看坑，又看了看他。“你没问过。”邻居耸耸肩，“就几英尺。”萨姆感到一阵愤怒涌上心头。他走近了些，看着露出的树根。“那是我家那边。”邻居继续挖。萨姆抓住铁锹柄。“停下。”邻居抬起头，很惊讶。萨姆盯着他，直到那人松了手。“我们以后再说，”萨姆说，但他知道自己不会再说。

topic: A neighbor asks to use part of the yard for a garden
text_en: The email was forwarded to the whole block: 'Proposal: community garden in unused yard space.' Ana read it, seeing her own address listed. She walked next door, finding the neighbor at his computer. 'You can't volunteer my yard,' she said. He looked up, 'It's for the neighborhood.' Ana felt a cold knot in her stomach. She leaned on the doorframe. 'I don't want strangers in my yard.' He said she could have a plot too. Ana shook her head. 'You should have asked me first.' He shrugged, 'It's just a garden.' Ana turned and left, but she spent the afternoon drafting a reply to the list, her words sharp and precise.
text_zh: 那封邮件被转发给了整个街区：“提案：在闲置院落空间建社区花园。”安娜读着，看到自己的地址被列在上面。她走到隔壁，发现邻居在电脑前。“你不能擅自把我们家院子拿出来用，”她说。他抬起头，“这是为了街坊。”安娜感到胃里一阵发紧。她靠在门框上。“我不想让陌生人来我院子里。”他说她也可以有一块地。安娜摇了摇头。“你应该先问我。”他耸耸肩，“只是个花园。”安娜转身离开了，但她花了整个下午起草回复邮件，措辞尖锐而准确。

topic: A neighbor asks to use part of the yard for a garden
text_en: The neighbor came over with a bucket of seedlings, asking if she could plant them along the side path. Nadia looked at the tiny green shoots, then at the woman's hopeful face. 'I was going to pave that,' she lied. The woman's face fell. 'But it's perfect for tomatoes.' Nadia shook her head, feeling a twinge of guilt, but also a stronger sense of intrusion. 'I have plans.' The woman insisted, saying they'd be no trouble. Nadia's voice rose slightly. 'No means no.' She handed back the bucket. The woman took it, her lips pressed together. Nadia watched her walk away, then went inside, her jaw still set.
text_zh: 邻居提着一桶幼苗过来，问她能不能沿着旁边的小路种下。纳迪亚看了看那些小小的绿芽，又看了看那个女人充满希望的脸。“我打算把那里铺上，”她撒了个谎。女人的脸垮了下来。“但那里很适合种西红柿。”纳迪亚摇了摇头，感到一丝内疚，但更强烈的是一种被侵犯的感觉。“我有打算。”女人坚持说，说它们不会惹麻烦。纳迪亚的声音稍稍提高。“不行就是不行。”她把桶递了回去。女人接过去，嘴唇抿紧。纳迪亚看着她走开，然后进了屋，下巴仍然绷着。

topic: A neighbor asks to use part of the yard for a garden
text_en: The note was taped to her door: 'We'll start the garden next week. Hope that's okay.' Mei read it, then ripped it off. She marched over, finding the neighbor arranging tools. 'It's not okay,' she said. He looked up, surprised. 'I left a note.' Mei held it up. 'This isn't asking. It's telling.' He said he thought she wouldn't mind. Mei felt a surge of heat. 'You thought wrong.' She pointed to her yard. 'That's my space. You don't get to decide.' He started to apologize, but Mei cut him off. 'I don't want your garden.' She turned and walked away, leaving him standing there with his trowel.
text_zh: 纸条贴在她的门上：“我们下周开始种花园。希望这样没问题。”梅读了，然后撕了下来。她大步走过去，发现邻居正在整理工具。“有问题，”她说。他抬起头，很惊讶。“我留了纸条。”梅举起纸条。“这不叫问，这叫做告诉。”他说他以为她不会介意。梅感到一阵热气上涌。“你想错了。”她指着自己的院子。“那是我的地方。你无权决定。”他开始道歉，但梅打断了他。“我不想要你的花园。”她转身走开了，留下他拿着小铲子站在那里。

topic: A neighbor asks to use part of the yard for a garden
text_en: Carlos was weeding when the neighbor called over the fence, 'You should let me plant some squash there.' Carlos kept pulling weeds, not answering. The neighbor continued, 'It's a waste of dirt.' Carlos stood up, brushing his hands. 'It's not a waste. It's my yard.' The neighbor laughed, 'I'll do all the work.' Carlos felt his shoulders tense. He looked at the man's eager face, then at his own neat rows. 'I like it as is.' The neighbor said, 'You'll like fresh squash more.' Carlos shook his head, picking up his trowel. 'No.' He turned back to his weeds, but his hands were shaking, and he had to stop.
text_zh: 卡洛斯正在除草，邻居隔着栅栏喊道：“你应该让在那里种点南瓜。”卡洛斯继续拔草，没有回答。邻居继续说：“那是浪费土地。”卡洛斯站起来，拍了拍手。“不是浪费。那是我的院子。”邻居笑了，“所有活我都干。”卡洛斯感到肩膀绷紧了。他看着那人急切的脸，又看了看自己整齐的菜畦。“我喜欢现在这样。”邻居说：“你会更喜欢新鲜南瓜的。”卡洛斯摇了摇头，拿起他的小铲子。“不要。”他转身回到他的草前，但他的手在发抖，他不得不停下来。

topic: A neighbor asks to use part of the yard for a garden
text_en: The neighbor knocked, holding a map of the block with a section marked 'garden.' He spread it out, pointing to her corner. 'This spot gets the most sun.' Yuki stared at the map, then at him. 'You've already planned this.' He nodded, 'Just need your go-ahead.' Yuki felt a flash of resentment. 'And if I don't give it?' He looked surprised. 'Well, it's for the community.' Yuki folded her arms. 'My yard isn't a community project.' He started to talk about shared harvests, but Yuki shook her head. 'I'm not interested.' She stepped back, closing the door. Through the window, she saw him standing there, map in hand, and she felt a hot, stubborn defiance.
text_zh: 邻居敲门，手里拿着一张区块地图，上面标着“花园”的区域。他展开地图，指着她家的角落。“这个位置阳光最充足。”由纪盯着地图，又看着他。“你早就计划好了。”他点点头，“只需要你同意。”由纪感到一阵愤懑。“如果我不同意呢？”他显得很惊讶。“呃，这是为了社区。”由纪双臂交叉。“我的院子不是社区项目。”他开始谈论分享收成的事，但由纪摇了摇头。“我不感兴趣。”她后退一步，关上了门。透过窗户，她看到他站在那里，手里拿着地图，她感到一种强烈的、固执的反抗。

topic: A neighbor asks to use part of the yard for a garden
text_en: The neighbor had already started digging when Ben came out. Ben saw the overturned earth, the small flags marking rows. 'What is this?' he asked, though he knew. The neighbor straightened, 'A garden. I thought I'd surprise you.' Ben felt his jaw tighten. 'You thought wrong.' He walked over, looking at the hole. 'You're digging up my lawn.' The neighbor laughed, 'It's just grass.' Ben stepped closer, his voice low. 'It's my grass.' The neighbor stopped smiling. 'I can put it back.' Ben shook his head. 'You can't undo this.' He turned and went inside, but he stood at the window, watching the neighbor slowly fill the hole, his fists clenched.
text_zh: 本出来的时候，邻居已经开始挖了。本看到了翻起的泥土，还有标记着行的的小旗子。“这是什么？”他问道，尽管他已经知道了。邻居直起身来，“一个花园。我想给你个惊喜。”本感到下巴绷紧了。“你想错了。”他走过去，看了看那个坑。“你在挖我的草坪。”邻居笑了，“只是草而已。”本走近一步，压低声音。“那是我的草。”邻居收起了笑容。“我可以填回去。”本摇了摇头。“你无法挽回。”他转身进屋，但他站在窗前，看着邻居慢慢地填那个坑，他双拳紧握。

topic: A neighbor asks to use part of the yard for a garden
text_en: The request came through the homeowners' association: 'Resident proposes using your yard for a garden.' Hana read it, then called the neighbor. 'I got your proposal.' He said, 'Oh, great. I think it's a win-win.' Hana felt a spike of annoyance. 'It's not a win for me. I don't want a garden.' He said, 'You'll get free vegetables.' Hana's grip tightened on the phone. 'I don't want vegetables. I want my yard.' He started to argue, but Hana interrupted. 'I'm saying no. End of story.' She hung up, then sat there, her heart beating fast. She wrote a long email to the board, explaining, but she couldn't shake the feeling of being imposed upon.
text_zh: 请求通过业主协会传来：“住户提议使用您的院子建花园。”哈娜读完后，打电话给邻居。“我收到了你的提议。”他说：“哦，太好了。我认为这是双赢。”哈娜感到一阵恼怒。“对我来说不是胜利。我不想要花园。”他说：“你会得到免费的蔬菜。”哈娜握紧了电话。“我不想要蔬菜。我要我的院子。”他开始争辩，但哈娜打断了他。“我说不。到此为止。”她挂断了电话，然后坐在那里，心跳加速。她给委员会写了一封长邮件解释，但那种被强加的感觉挥之不去。

topic: A neighbor asks to use part of the yard for a garden
text_en: Ravi found the plot staked out in his side yard, wooden posts driven into the grass he'd just reseeded. His neighbor, Ellen, waved from her porch. "I figured this sunny corner was wasted on you," she called. Ravi walked over, counting the posts. "I didn't agree to this." Ellen laughed. "Oh, you won't even notice it's there." Ravi's chest tightened. He pulled up the first stake, the ground resisting. "I notice," he said, his voice low. He worked through the afternoon, removing each marker, leaving the yard bare. Ellen watched from her porch, her smile gone. Ravi didn't look up.
text_zh: 拉维发现他侧院里刚重新播种的草地上被打了木桩，圈出了一块地。他的邻居艾伦从她家的门廊朝他挥手。“我觉得这个向阳的角落对你来说是浪费，”她喊道。拉维走过去，数了数木桩。“我没同意这件事。”艾伦笑了。“哦，你不会注意到它在的。”拉维胸口一紧。他拔起第一个木桩，地面有些阻力。“我注意到了，”他说，声音很低。他干了一下午，把每根标记都拔了出来，让院子光秃秃的。艾伦从门廊看着，笑容消失了。拉维没有抬头。

topic: A neighbor asks to use part of the yard for a garden
text_en: The neighbor came over with a bag of compost, saying she wanted to start a 'shared garden' on the border. Mara looked at the bag, then at her. 'I have my own plans for that strip.' The neighbor smiled, 'We can work together.' Mara felt a knot of resistance. 'I don't want to share.' The neighbor's smile faltered. 'It's just a few feet.' Mara shook her head. 'It's my few feet.' She pointed to the bag. 'Take that back.' The neighbor stood there, holding the bag, looking hurt. Mara didn't soften. She turned and went inside, but she watched from the window, seeing the neighbor leave the bag on the path. She left it there, refusing to touch it.
text_zh: 邻居带着一袋堆肥过来，说她想在边界上建一个“共享花园”。玛拉看了看袋子，又看了看她。“我对那块地有自己的打算。”邻居笑了，“我们可以一起做。”玛拉感到一阵抵触。“我不想分享。”邻居的笑容僵住了。“就几英尺。”玛拉摇了摇头。“那是我的几英尺。”她指着袋子。“拿回去。”邻居站在那里，拿着袋子，看起来很受伤。玛拉没有心软。她转身进屋，但从窗户看着，看到邻居把袋子留在小路上。她任由它放在那里，拒绝去碰它。

topic: A person learns their apartment building is going condo
text_en: Marta traced the outline of her key fob, the one that no longer opened the front door after the new locks were installed. The notice had been slipped under her door at dawn, promising 'modernization' but demanding a buyout she couldn't dream of matching. She watched the superintendent patch a crack in the lobby wall, his radio playing cheerful tunes. She wanted to ask him if he knew what was happening, but her jaw was tight. Instead, she pressed her palm against the cold glass of the entryway, feeling the solidity of the buildings she could not afford to keep.
text_zh: 玛尔塔摩挲着钥匙扣的轮廓，自从换了新锁，这把钥匙再也打不开前门了。通知是在黎明时分从门缝下塞进来的，承诺着“现代化改造”，却要求一笔她做梦也凑不出的买断费。她看着管理员修补大厅墙上的裂缝，他的收音机里播放着欢快的曲子。她想问他是否知道发生了什么，但她的下巴绷得紧紧的。她转而将手掌按在门厅冰冷的玻璃上，感受着那些她无力保留的建筑的坚固。

topic: A person learns their apartment building is going condo
text_en: Marta gripped the notice so hard the paper creased. They had fixed the leaky roof, repainted the hallway, and now suddenly the building was too good for renters. She thought of her neighbor, old Mr. Chen, who had lived there for decades and could never afford this. She marched to the superintendent's door, not to ask, but to tell him exactly what she thought of his timing. When he shrugged and said it was out of his hands, she stepped closer, her voice low and sharp, daring him to look her in the eye and repeat it. He didn't.
text_zh: 玛尔塔紧紧攥着通知，纸张都皱了。他们修好了漏水的屋顶，重新粉刷了走廊，现在突然这栋楼对租户来说太好了。她想起邻居陈老先生，他在这里住了几十年，永远也付不起这笔钱。她大步走到管理员的门口，不是去问，而是去告诉他她对他挑的时机有何看法。当他耸耸肩说这不归他管时，她凑近一步，声音低沉而尖锐，激他敢不敢看着她的眼睛再说一遍。他没敢。

topic: A person learns their apartment building is going condo
text_en: Priya had planted the tulip bulbs by the entrance, each one a small defiance against the gray concrete. The new owner's agent stood there now, measuring the footprint for a sign. She approached and asked, 'Those flowers, will they stay?' The agent smiled, said, 'We'll likely redo the landscaping.' Priya's hands, buried in her sweater pockets, balled into fists. She watched the agent's pen scratch notes, and she felt the soil under her nails from this morning's weeding turn to something sharp. She said nothing, but she didn't move until the agent left.
text_zh: 普里娅在入口处种下了郁金香球茎，每一株都是对灰色混凝土的小小反抗。新业主的代理人此刻站在那里，为一块招牌测量占地面积。她走上前问：“那些花，会留下吗？”代理人笑了笑，说：“我们可能会重新做景观。”普里娅的手埋在毛衣口袋里，攥成了拳头。她看着代理人的笔在纸上划拉记录，她感到今早除草时留在指甲缝里的泥土变得尖锐起来。她什么也没说，但直到代理人离开，她才挪动脚步。

topic: A person learns their apartment building is going condo
text_en: The letter sat on the table for a full day before Andre picked it up. His father had bought this unit so he could go to school nearby, and now the new owners wanted him out. He calculated every Saturday he had spent painting the trim, fixing the wiring, hauling old furniture down those stairs. This was not a business deal to him. He dialed the number on the letter, and when a cheerful voice answered, he did not introduce himself. He demanded the name of the actual decision-maker, and then demanded again, louder, until the cheerfulness faltered into stammered reassurances he did not believe.
text_zh: 那封信在桌上放了一整天，安德烈才拿起来。他父亲买下这个单元是为了让他能在附近上学，现在新业主想让他搬走。他计算着每一个星期六，他用来油漆装饰线条、修理电线、把旧家具拖下楼梯。这对他来说不是一桩生意。他拨通了信上的号码，当一个欢快的声音接起电话时，他没有自我介绍。他要求知道真正做决定的人的名字，然后又要求了一遍，声音更大，直到那欢快变成了结结巴巴的保证，而他并不相信。

topic: A person learns their apartment building is going condo
text_en: The new management company's flyer had a smiling cartoon family in front of a clean, modern building. Julia tore it down from the stairwell bulletin board. Her apartment was on the top floor, the one with the sloped ceiling that she had to duck under by the window. She remembered the day she moved in, painting over the old water stains herself. Now they said she had first right of refusal, but at what price? She looked at the crack in the ceiling that snaked from the light fixture to the wall. She felt a knot in her stomach, but her hands were steady as she folded the flyer into a tight, small square.
text_zh: 新管理公司的传单上有一户微笑的卡通家庭，站在一栋干净现代的楼房前。朱莉娅把它从楼梯间的公告板上撕了下来。她的公寓在顶楼，窗户边有面斜顶，她得低着头才能过去。她记得搬进来的那天，自己动手粉刷遮盖旧水渍。现在他们说她有优先购买权，但价格是多少？她看着天花板上从灯座蜿蜒到墙壁的裂缝。她感到胃里打了个结，但当她把传单折成紧紧的小方块时，手很稳。

topic: A person learns their apartment building is going condo
text_en: Tom had always been the one to organize the building's potlucks in the courtyard. He knew everyone's names, their kids' names, their dog's names. The conversion notice was taped to the elevator door, and he read it twice, hoping he'd misunderstood. He hadn't. He found himself at the manager's office, his voice low and clipped. 'You can't just do this without telling us,' he said. The manager shrugged, said, 'It's business.' Tom walked out, past the courtyard where the chairs were still stacked from Sunday's gathering. He sat on one of the chairs, staring at the empty space where the grill usually stood.
text_zh: 汤姆一直是院子里楼里聚餐的组织者。他认识每个人的名字、他们孩子的名字、他们狗的名字。改造通知贴在电梯门上，他读了两遍，希望是自己理解错了。他没有。他来到经理办公室，声音低沉而简短。“你不能不告诉我们就这么做，”他说。经理耸耸肩，说：“这是生意。”汤姆走了出去，经过院子，那里星期天聚会用的椅子还堆着。他坐在其中一把椅子上，盯着通常放烤架的那块空地。

topic: A person learns their apartment building is going condo
text_en: Priya stood in the stairwell, the letter clutched behind her back. She had raised her daughter in this apartment; the rent was manageable, the school was close. Her husband had just lost his job. She imagined telling him they had to find a new place, then imagined the landlord's smug face as he talked about market value. Her jaw tightened. She walked straight to the leasing office, ignoring the receptionist's smile. She placed the paper on the counter and said, flatly, that this was not a fair move. When the manager tried to explain, she cut him off, her hand flat on the desk, and asked who had signed off on this.
text_zh: 普里娅站在楼梯间，信紧紧攥在背后。她在这间公寓里把女儿养大；租金可以承受，学校也近。她丈夫刚刚失业。她想象着告诉他他们得找个新地方，然后想象着房东谈论市场价值时那得意的脸。她的下巴绷紧了。她径直走进租赁办公室，无视接待员的微笑。她把纸放在柜台上，平淡地说，这不是公平的做法。当经理试图解释时，她打断了他，手平放在桌上，问是谁批准了这件事。

topic: A person learns their apartment building is going condo
text_en: Mr. Okonkwo had lived in this building for forty years, before the neighborhood was 'up-and-coming.' He had watched the grocery store become a coffee shop, the bookstore become a gym. Now, they wanted his building to become something else. He sat at his kitchen table, the notice propped against the salt shaker. He thought of the small garden he kept on the fire escape, tomatoes and peppers that he shared with the neighbors. He didn't need to read the fine print to know what it meant. He picked up the phone to call his daughter, but stopped. He didn't want to hear her tell him to be reasonable.
text_zh: 奥孔科沃先生在这栋楼里住了四十年，那时这个街区还没“崭露头角”。他看着杂货店变成了咖啡店，书店变成了健身房。现在，他们想让他的楼也变成别的东西。他坐在厨房桌旁，通知靠在盐瓶上。他想起了他在防火梯上打理的小花园，种的西红柿和辣椒，他常和邻居分享。他不需要读小字就知道这意味着什么。他拿起电话想打给女儿，但又停住了。他不想听她劝他要理智。

topic: A person learns their apartment building is going condo
text_en: The real estate agent was friendly, almost too friendly, as she showed a potential buyer around. Maya watched from her window, her dog barking at the stranger by the stoop. She saw the agent gesture toward the shared yard, the one where she'd built a small compost bin, the one the landlord had said she could use. Maya felt her face get hot. She pulled her curtains shut, but the voices drifted up. She let her dog out into the hall, then thought better of it and yanked him back, her grip tighter than she intended. The dog whimpered, and she softened, but the heat remained.
text_zh: 房地产经纪人很友好，几乎过于友好，她带着一位潜在买家四处参观。玛雅从窗户看着，她的狗对着门廊边的陌生人吠叫。她看到经纪人指向共用的院子，那个她建了小型堆肥箱的院子，那个房东说过她可以用的院子。玛雅感到脸发烫。她拉上窗帘，但声音还是飘了上来。她把狗放到走廊里，然后又改变了主意，把它拽了回来，抓得比预想的要紧。狗呜咽了一声，她放松了手，但那股热意仍在。

topic: A person learns their apartment building is going condo
text_en: Marisol had lived in the Peachtree for years, till the day the landlord's email announced the building would convert. She read it standing at her kitchen counter, coffee cooling. "First right of purchase," the message said, but her rent already chewed half her paycheck. She thought of the neighborhood market, the old oak by the door, her friend's laugh echoing in the stairwell. When the landlord called, she kept her voice flat. "I'm not moving," she said. She hung up and began writing a letter to every resident, listing what they'd lose, signing each one herself.
text_zh: 玛丽索尔在桃树公寓住了多年，直到有一天房东的邮件宣布大楼将改造。她站在厨房台子前读着，咖啡都凉了。“优先购买权，”消息说，但她的房租已经吃掉了一半的工资。她想起了街区的市场、门口的老橡树、朋友在楼梯间的笑声。当房东打来电话时，她保持声音平淡。“我不会搬，”她说。她挂了电话，开始给每位住户写信，列出他们会失去的东西，每封都亲自签名。

topic: A person learns their apartment building is going condo
text_en: Marta pressed the notice against the hallway wall, reading it again as if the words might rearrange themselves. The building she had called home for years was going condo, and the new owners wanted her out by spring. Her hands trembled slightly as she folded the paper, not from fear but from the injustice of it all. She had paid her rent on time, cared for the old radiators, and greeted every neighbor by name. Now they were treating her like a transient, a problem to be solved. She shoved the notice into her pocket and marched to the landlord's door, ready to demand answers.
text_zh: 玛尔塔把通知按在走廊的墙上，又读了一遍，仿佛那些字会自己重新排列似的。她住了多年的这栋楼要改成共管公寓，新业主想让她春天前搬走。她折起纸时双手微微颤抖，不是因为害怕，而是因为这一切的不公。她按时交租，照料那些旧暖气片，跟每个邻居都打招呼叫名字。现在他们却把她当成一个过客，一个需要解决的问题。她把通知塞进口袋，大步走向房东的门，准备去讨个说法。

topic: A person learns their apartment building is going condo
text_en: The building's super, a friendly man named Jorge, had been a fixture for a decade. He'd helped her carry groceries, jump-started her car, and kept the back door from jamming. When the new management came, he was replaced by a crew that wore uniforms and worked for an outside company. The conversion notice followed a week later. Anna saw Jorge packing his tools and went outside. 'I'm sorry,' she said. He just shook his head. She watched him drive away, and she felt a burning behind her eyes. She went back inside and slammed her apartment door, rattling the cheap drywall. She didn't care if the new owners heard.
text_zh: 这栋楼的物业管理员，一个叫豪尔赫的友善男人，十年来一直是这里的常驻人物。他帮她搬过杂货，给她的车搭过电，还修好了老是卡住的后门。新管理层来了以后，他被一个穿制服、为外部公司工作的团队取代了。一周后，改建通知就来了。安娜看到豪尔赫在收拾工具，就走了出去。“我很抱歉，”她说。他只是摇了摇头。她看着他开车离去，感到眼眶一阵灼热。她回到屋里，砰地关上公寓门，震得廉价的石膏板墙咯咯响。她不在乎新业主是否听到。

topic: A person learns their apartment building is going condo
text_en: Nadia found the flyer in her mailbox, wedged between bills: "Important Notice: Condo Conversion." She read it twice, then stood very still. The building was all she could afford, and she'd painted her bedroom a soft yellow. She went to the management office the same afternoon. "This isn't fair," she said, her voice low. The manager shrugged. She left and walked the hall, counting the familiar doors, the scuffed baseboards. Back in her apartment, she began drafting a letter to the city housing department, her handwriting growing heavier with each line.
text_zh: 娜迪亚在邮箱里发现了那张传单，夹在账单之间：“重要通知：共管公寓改建。”她读了两遍，然后一动不动地站着。这栋楼是她唯一负担得起的，她把自己的卧室刷成了柔和的黄色。当天下午她就去了管理办公室。“这不公平，”她压低声音说。经理耸了耸肩。她离开后，沿着走廊走着，数着那些熟悉的门，那些磨损的踢脚板。回到公寓，她开始起草一封给市住房部门的信，笔迹随着每一行变得越来越重。

topic: A person learns their apartment building is going condo
text_en: The building was old, with creaky floors and drafty windows, but it was home. The conversion notice came with a glossy cover photo of the building, modified to look brighter, cleaner. Rosa stood in her kitchen, the radiator hissing, and she stared at that fake picture. She wanted to tear it up, but she needed the paper for evidence. She took a photo of the notice with her phone, then another, then a video of the drafty window she'd taped with plastic last fall. She was collecting ammunition, but she didn't know where to fire. She felt a coiled tightness in her shoulders, and she kept taking photos, the click of the shutter a small defiance.
text_zh: 这栋楼很旧，地板吱吱作响，窗户漏风，但这里是家。改建通知附了一张光鲜的封面照片，照片里的楼被修饰得看起来更明亮、更干净。罗莎站在厨房里，暖气片嘶嘶作响，她盯着那张假照片。她想把它撕掉，但她需要这张纸作为证据。她用手机拍了一张通知的照片，又拍了一张，然后拍了一段视频，拍的是去年秋天她用塑料布封起来的漏风窗户。她在收集弹药，但她不知道该往哪里开火。她感到肩膀一阵紧绷，她不停地拍照，快门咔嗒声是一种小小的反抗。

topic: A person learns their apartment building is going condo
text_en: Owen found the notice folded under his windshield wiper. The building was going condo, and tenants had a month to decide. He remembered the year the heat broke in January and how he had boiled water for baths. He remembered the mice. And now they wanted to sell him the unit at a price he could never match. He crumpled the paper and shoved it in his pocket. At the tenants' meeting, he sat in the front row, arms crossed. When the investor finished his polished pitch, Owen was the first to ask, in a flat voice, how much profit they had already counted before telling anyone.
text_zh: 欧文在雨刷器下发现了折叠的通知。这栋楼要改成共管公寓，租户有一个月的时间决定。他记得那年一月暖气坏了，他是怎么烧水洗澡的。他记得那些老鼠。而现在他们想以他永远无法企及的价格把单元卖给他。他把纸揉成一团，塞进口袋。在租户会议上，他坐在前排，双臂交叉。当投资者结束他精心打磨的推销时，欧文是第一个发问的人，他用平淡的声音问，他们在告诉任何人之前，已经算好了多少利润。

topic: A person learns their apartment building is going condo
text_en: The email from the property company arrived while Derek was making dinner. He clicked it open, scanned the subject line, and set his spoon down slowly. Condo conversion. He thought of the single mother upstairs, the retired veteran next door. He typed a reply, deleted it, typed again. His hands were steady, but his stomach coiled. He went downstairs and knocked on every door he could, explaining what he'd found. "We have to act together," he said. In his living room that evening, he organized a meeting for the following week, his voice firm, his resolve unyielding.
text_zh: 德里克正在做晚饭时，物业公司的电子邮件到了。他点开邮件，扫了一眼主题行，然后慢慢放下勺子。共管公寓改建。他想到了楼上的单亲妈妈，隔壁的退伍老兵。他打了一封回信，又删掉，再打。他的手很稳，但胃里却一阵翻腾。他下楼，挨家挨户敲门，解释他发现的情况。“我们必须一起行动，”他说。那天晚上，他在自己的客厅里，为下周组织了一次会议，声音坚定，决心不屈。

topic: A person learns their apartment building is going condo
text_en: The property manager, a young woman with a clipboard, knocked on every door to explain the 'exciting opportunity.' Gina answered in her bathrobe, her morning coffee going cold. 'We'd love to have you stay as an owner,' the manager said with a rehearsed smile. Gina thought of her rent, which had never been late, and the maintenance requests that had always been ignored. 'No thanks,' she said, and closed the door, her hand trembling slightly. She leaned against the door and heard the manager knock next door. She finished her cold coffee, the bitter taste matching the resentment settling in her chest.
text_zh: 物业经理，一个拿着剪贴板的年轻女人，挨家挨户敲门解释这个“激动人心的机会”。吉娜穿着睡袍应了门，她的晨咖啡已经凉了。“我们很希望您能留下来成为业主，”经理带着排练过的微笑说。吉娜想到了她的房租，从来没有迟交过，还有那些总是被忽视的维修请求。“不了，谢谢，”她说，然后关上了门，手微微颤抖。她靠在门上，听到经理去敲隔壁的门。她喝完了凉咖啡，苦涩的味道与她心中沉淀的怨恨相称。

topic: A person learns their apartment building is going condo
text_en: The building's laundry room was a place of communal struggle, with washers that ate quarters and dryers that didn't dry. When the conversion notice went up, the tenant association formed. Malik, who had once complained about the laundry room most, now led the meetings. He stood by the dryer, his voice steady, listing the code violations, the deferred maintenance, the broken elevator that had trapped Mrs. Chen for an hour. The owners' eyes glazed over, but Malik kept going. He felt a quiet, grinding determination, like a stone being worn smooth. He knew they'd lose, but he wasn't going to make it easy.
text_zh: 这栋楼的洗衣房是一个共同奋斗的地方，洗衣机吞硬币，烘干机不烘干。改建通知贴出来后，租户协会成立了。马利克，曾经最抱怨洗衣房的人，现在领导着会议。他站在烘干机旁，声音平稳，列举着违反法规的地方、拖延的维修、以及困住陈太太一个小时的坏电梯。业主们的目光变得呆滞，但马利克继续说下去。他感到一种安静的、磨人的决心，就像一块石头被磨得光滑。他知道他们会输，但他不会让他们轻松。

topic: A person learns their apartment building is going condo
text_en: The view from the fifth floor was of a parking lot, but it was her parking lot, her view. When the conversion was announced, the new owners sent a survey asking what 'amenities' residents valued most. Carmen filled it out with sarcastic comments, 'A home I can afford,' 'A landlord who fixed the leaking roof,' 'A reason to stay.' She mailed it in, but she knew it was futile. She looked out her window at the parking lot, noticing for the first time the cracks in the asphalt. She felt a tired frustration, not a flash of heat, but a steady, low hum. She sat on her couch, not moving, the survey form's carbon copy still on the table.
text_zh: 五楼的景色是一个停车场，但那是她的停车场，她的景色。改建宣布后，新业主发来一份调查问卷，询问居民最看重哪些“便利设施”。卡门用讽刺的评论填了问卷，“一个我负担得起的家”，“一个修好漏雨屋顶的房东”，“一个留下来的理由”。她把它寄了出去，但她知道这是徒劳的。她看着窗外停车场，第一次注意到沥青上的裂缝。她感到一种疲惫的沮丧，不是一阵热浪，而是一种稳定的、低沉的嗡嗡声。她坐在沙发上，一动不动，调查表的复写副本还在桌上。

topic: A person learns their apartment building is going condo
text_en: Leah did not react at first. She set the letter down and made a cup of tea, then read it again. Her rent had always been on time. She had never complained when the pipes thumped. And now this. The developer's name was at the bottom, smooth and professional. She took a photo of the letter and sent it to every tenant she knew. Then she went to the lobby and scrawled the date of the next tenants' association meeting in big letters. She did not ask permission. When the building manager saw her and cleared his throat, she turned, looked at him, and said they would sort this out together, or they would sort it out without him.
text_zh: 利亚起初没有反应。她放下信，泡了一杯茶，然后又读了一遍。她的房租总是按时交的。水管砰砰响的时候她从未抱怨过。而现在却来了这个。开发商的签名在底部，光滑而专业。她给信拍了张照片，发给她认识的每个租户。然后她去了大厅，用大字写下了下次租户协会会议的日期。她没有征求许可。当楼管看到她，清了清嗓子时，她转过身，看着他，说他们会一起解决这件事，或者他们会绕过他解决。

topic: An artist discovers someone has tattooed their work
text_en: Elena traced the fine lines of the dragon inked on the barista's forearm as he handed her a latte. It was her design, the one she'd painted for her sister's memorial. She hadn't given permission. Her chest tightened, and she looked away, watching the rain slide down the window. She pulled her sleeves over her own bare wrists, feeling the absence of her sister's hand in hers. She wanted to ask how, why, but the words felt heavy and stuck in her throat. She paid without meeting his eyes and left her coffee steaming on the counter, the image of her private goodbye walking off with a stranger.
text_zh: 埃琳娜看着咖啡师把拿铁递给她时，描摹着他前臂上纹着的龙纹的细线。那是她的设计，是她为姐姐的纪念而创作的画。她没有允许任何人使用。她的胸口发紧，移开目光，望着雨水从窗户上滑落。她拉下袖子盖住自己裸露的手腕，心中空落落的，感受不到姐姐那只手曾握着的温暖。她想问怎么会、为什么，但话语沉重，卡在喉咙里。她没抬眼就付了钱，任由她的咖啡在吧台上冒着热气，而她那个私密的告别，就这样随着一个陌生人走远了。

topic: An artist discovers someone has tattooed their work
text_en: Marcus saw the phoenix on the jogger's shoulder as she stretched by the park bench. He recognized the exact curve of the wing, the way the tail feathers bled into flames—his own watercolor from years ago, before his gallery show flopped. He sat still, his sketchbook unopened on his lap. The jogger smiled at him, oblivious. He tried to smile back, but his mouth felt dry. text_zh: 马库斯看到那个慢跑者在公园长椅边伸展身体时，肩上的凤凰。他认出了那翅膀的曲线，尾羽燃成火焰的形态——那是他多年前的水彩画，在他个展失败之前。他坐在那里一动不动，素描本摊在腿上，没有打开。慢跑者朝他笑了笑，浑然不觉。他想回以微笑，却觉得口干舌燥。他看着她跑远了，凤凰随着她的步伐上下起伏。他合上素描本，里面的空白页面与那鲜活、被偷走的生命正沿路消失，形成鲜明对比。那一周他都没再画。

topic: An artist discovers someone has tattooed their work
text_en: Priya was at the flea market when she spotted the tattoo on the vendor's neck—a small constellation of her own design, the one she'd drawn for her late father, a map of the sky from their last camping trip. text_zh: 普里娅在跳蚤市场里，看到摊主脖子上的纹身——一个她亲手设计的星座图案，是她为已故的父亲画的，那是他们最后一次露营时夜空的地图。摊主正和顾客讨价还价，笑着。普里娅摸了摸自己的锁骨，那里她一直想纹这个图案，但从未纹过。一阵熟悉的隐痛在肋骨后蔓延。她转身走开了，集市的声音渐渐模糊成一片低沉的嗡嗡声。她游荡了几个小时，走过老书和旧物件的摊位，那个陌生人皮肤上星空的影像在她脑海里燃烧：一个私密的记忆变得公开而遥远。

topic: An artist discovers someone has tattooed their work
text_en: In the locker room after his swim, Ben noticed the lily on the man's calf. It was the exact flower he'd painted in the hospital, the one he'd given to his wife the day before she passed. text_zh: 游泳后，在更衣室里，本注意到那个男人小腿上的百合花。那正是他在医院里画的那朵花，是在妻子去世前一天他送她的。男人正在擦头发，百合随他的肌肉一起起伏。本感到胸口突然一紧，一股寒意涌上来，与空调无关。他迅速转开身，慌慌张张地拨弄着锁。他还记得那朵花在脑海中的样子，但现在它却在陌生人的腿上，成为别人故事的一部分。他重重地坐在长凳上，游泳包也忘了管，一直盯着地板，直到那个男人离开。

topic: An artist discovers someone has tattooed their work
text_en: Aria was sketching in the park when she saw the girl with the koi fish on her forearm. text_zh: 艾瑞亚在公园里速写时，看到了那个前臂上纹着锦鲤的女孩。鳞片闪闪发光，橙色和黑色的漩涡正如艾瑞亚为自己的论文所画的那样——那幅她称之为《放手》的作品。她记得画笔的重量，数个钟头的劳作。如今，它成了陌生人身上永久的印记。艾瑞亚自己的手僵住了，铅笔悬在纸上。女孩正和朋友笑着，指着远处什么东西。艾瑞亚看着她们，一种空洞的感觉在胃里蔓延。她合上素描本，里面那幅未完成的树的素描，像是一个提醒，提醒她失去了什么。她收拾好东西走了，锦鲤在她记忆中游着。

topic: An artist discovers someone has tattooed their work
text_en: Hiroshi was at the onsen, steam rising around him, when he saw the wave tattoo on the man's back. text_zh: 宏志在温泉中，蒸汽在四周升腾，这时他看到了那个男人背上的波浪纹身。那是他自己受浮世绘启发的作品，是他在导师去世后苦熬数月创作的，是对他们共同深爱的大海的致敬。男人正和别人说话，背随着他的比划起伏。宏志感到喉咙里起了个疙瘩。他更深的沉入水中，希望就此消失。他想起了导师的笔触，想起了他教宏志捕捉浪卷曲的笔法。如今，那教导却在一个陌生人的背上，成为公开展示的私密之物。他再看不下去了，闭上了眼睛，蒸汽令人窒息。

topic: An artist discovers someone has tattooed their work

text_zh: 在牙医诊所的候诊室里，克拉拉注意到前台手腕上的蜂鸟。那正是她为从未出版的童书画的插图，是在她等待会改变一切的检查结果时画的那幅。接待员正在打字，小小的蜂鸟随着每一次击键上下跳动。克拉拉的双手麻木。她记得自己倾注在那些色彩中的希望，以及她试图用画覆盖的恐惧。现在，它成了别人手臂上可爱的装饰。她移开目光，望着窗外灰蒙蒙的天空。她甚至不想看杂志了，就坐在那里，耳边充斥着荧光灯的嗡嗡声。

text_zh: 针尖描摹着她脊背的曲线，一只展翅飞翔的蓝鸟，那幅她多年前画在画布上的图案。她触了触墨迹，传来陌生人皮肤的温度。那是她精妙的笔触，翅膀的倾斜，下面的阴影。他微笑着，带着自豪。她想回以微笑，但手却沉重地垂在身侧。工作室里太亮了，画架太空了。她转身离开那个男人，盯着那面空白的墙——那幅画曾经挂在那儿，被卖给了别人。一种缓慢的痛在她胸口蔓延。

topic: An artist discovers someone has tattooed their work

topic: An artist discovers someone has tattooed their work
text_en: Lena was at the bus stop when she saw the crescent moon on the man's neck. It was the same moon she'd drawn for her twin brother, who had died in a car accident. The man was listening to music, his head bobbing, the moon tilting with each movement. Lena felt a cold shiver run down her spine. She remembered the night they'd stayed up to watch a meteor shower, her brother pointing at the moon. Now that image was a permanent part of a stranger's body. She got on the bus without looking back, but the moon stayed in her mind, a pale ghost of what she'd lost. She found a seat by the window and watched the world go by, the moon following her all the way home.
